  • lines 10-11: a POST with only the [password] parameter: state [212]. With the [-d] option, the parameters are posted as an HTML form does: the request body is the string [password=x] and the [Content-Type] header is [application/x-www-form-urlencoded];
  • lines 13-14: a POST with only the [user] parameter: state [214];
  • lines 16-26: a POST with incorrect credentials: state [221]. Note the status [401 Unauthorized] of the response (line 17);
  • lines 28-38: a POST with valid credentials: state [200] and status [200 OK] (line 29).

docs.title: 23.11.5. The [calculer-impot] action
docs.text:
The [calculer-impot] action is processed by the following [CalculerImpotController] controller:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// dépendances Symfony
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;
// dépendances Predis
use Predis\Client as RedisClient;
use Predis\PredisException;
// alias de classe : la couche [dao] de la version 9 est utilisée avec Redis
use Application\ServerDaoWithSession as ServerDaoWithRedis;

// action [calculer-impot] : calcul de l'impôt avec les paramètres postés [marié, enfants, salaire]
final class CalculerImpotController implements InterfaceController
{
    #[\Override]
    public function execute(array $config, Request $request, Session $session): ControllerResult
    {
        // on doit avoir un POST avec le seul paramètre [action] dans l'URL
        if ($request->getMethod() !== "POST" || $request->query->count() !== 1) {
            $message = "il faut utiliser la méthode [post] avec [action] dans l'URL"
                . " et les paramètres postés [marié, enfants, salaire]";
            return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_BAD_REQUEST, 301, $message);
        }
        // on vérifie les paramètres postés
        // chaque erreur ajoute une valeur différente à l'état : l'état final dit quelles erreurs se sont produites
        $erreurs = [];
        $état = 310;
        // statut marital
        if (!$request->request->has("marié")) {
            $état += 2;
            $erreurs[] = "paramètre [marié] manquant";
        } else {
            $marié = strtolower(trim($request->request->getString("marié")));
            if (!in_array($marié, ["oui", "non"], true)) {
                $état += 4;
                $erreurs[] = "valeur [$marié] invalide pour le paramètre [marié]";
            }
        }
        // nombre d'enfants et salaire annuel : des entiers >= 0
        $valeurs = [];
        foreach (["enfants" => [8, 9], "salaire" => [16, 17]] as $paramètre => [$manquant, $invalide]) {
            if (!$request->request->has($paramètre)) {
                $état += $manquant;
                $erreurs[] = "paramètre [$paramètre] manquant";
                continue;
            }
            $valeur = trim($request->request->getString($paramètre));
            if (preg_match('/^\d+$/', $valeur) !== 1) {
                $état += $invalide;
                $erreurs[] = "valeur [$valeur] invalide pour le paramètre [$paramètre]";
            } else {
                $valeurs[$paramètre] = (int) $valeur;
            }
        }
        // erreurs ?
        if ($erreurs !== []) {
            return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_BAD_REQUEST, $état, $erreurs);
        }
        [$enfants, $salaire] = [$valeurs["enfants"], $valeurs["salaire"]];

        // on a des paramètres valides - la mémoire de portée [application] : un serveur Redis
        try {
            $redis = new RedisClient($config["redis"]);
            // on se connecte tout de suite au serveur pour savoir s'il est là
            $redis->connect();
        } catch (PredisException $ex) {
            // erreur 500
            return new ControllerResult(
                Response::HTTP_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
                350,
                "[redis], " . self::utf8($ex->getMessage())
            );
        }
        // création de la couche [dao]
        try {
            $json = $redis->get("taxAdminData");
            if ($json === null) {
                // les données fiscales sont prises dans la base de données puis mises dans Redis
                $dao = new ServerDaoWithRedis(ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["databaseFilename"]);
                $redis->set("taxAdminData", (string) $dao->getTaxAdminData());
            } else {
                // les données fiscales sont prises dans Redis
                $taxAdminData = TaxAdminData::fromArray(json_decode($json, true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR));
                $dao = new ServerDaoWithRedis($taxAdminData);
            }
        } catch (ExceptionImpots $ex) {
            // erreur 500
            return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, 341, self::utf8($ex->getMessage()));
        } finally {
            // on n'a plus besoin du serveur Redis
            $redis->disconnect();
        }
        // création de la couche [métier] et calcul de l'impôt
        $résultat = (new ServerMetier($dao))->calculerImpot($marié, $enfants, $salaire);
        // la simulation : les clés du tableau [$résultat] deviennent des arguments nommés
        $simulation = new Simulation($marié, $enfants, $salaire, ...$résultat);
        // on l'ajoute à la liste des simulations de la session
        $session->set("simulations", [...$session->get("simulations", []), $simulation]);
        // réussite
        return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_OK, 300, $simulation);
    }

    // le message d'erreur d'un pilote de SGBD ou de Redis peut ne pas être codé en UTF-8
    // (Windows-1252 sous Windows) : il ne pourrait alors pas être mis dans une chaîne JSON
    private static function utf8(string $message): string
    {
        return mb_check_encoding($message, "UTF-8") ? $message : mb_convert_encoding($message, "UTF-8", "Windows-1252");
    }
}

Comments

  • the expected request is [POST main.php?action=calculer-impot] with three posted parameters [marié, enfants, salaire]:
    • [marié] must have its value in [oui, non];
    • [enfants, salaire] must be positive or zero integers;
  • lines 13-16: as in version 10, we use the [Predis] library and the [dao] layer of version 9, under the alias [ServerDaoWithRedis];
  • lines 25-29: we check that we indeed have a POST with a single parameter in the URL. If this is not the case, an error result is returned to the main controller, with state [301];
  • lines 32-33: we will accumulate the error messages in the [$erreurs] array. The state starts from the value 310 and each error adds a value to it;
  • lines 35-44: we check the presence of the [marié] parameter (+2 if it is missing) and then that its value is in [oui, non] (+4 otherwise);
  • lines 47-60: the [enfants] and [salaire] parameters are checked by the same loop. The array iterated over associates with each parameter the pair of values added to the state when the parameter is missing or invalid: (8, 9) for [enfants], (16, 17) for [salaire]. The destructuring [[$manquant, $invalide]] is done directly in the [foreach] statement. The PHP 7 script wrote the same code twice;
    • lines 48-52: the parameter is missing: the [continue] statement moves on to the next parameter;
    • lines 54-59: the value must be a sequence of at least one digit. If so, it is converted to an integer and stored in the [$valeurs] array;
  • lines 62-64: if there were errors, we return a result whose response is the list of errors;
  • line 65: we have valid parameters. We can calculate the tax. To do so, we must build the [dao] and [métier] layers that know how to perform this calculation;
  • lines 68-79: we create a [Redis] client and connect to the server right away. If we could not connect to the [Redis] server, we return a result with the status [500 Internal Server Error] and state [350];
  • lines 81-98: building the [dao] layer:
    • line 82: we check whether the [Redis] server has the [taxAdminData] key. This key represents the data of the tax administration. The [get] method of [Predis] returns [null] if the key does not exist;
    • line 85: the key does not exist: the tax data must be fetched from the database. The path of the database description file is relative to the application's root folder, known thanks to the [ROOT_DIRECTORY] constant defined by [main.php];
    • line 86: the data retrieved from the database is put in the [Redis] memory with the [taxAdminData] key, in the form of its JSON string;
    • lines 89-90: if the [taxAdminData] key exists in the [Redis] memory, the tax data is passed directly to the constructor of the [dao] layer;
  • lines 92-94: if the database lookup went wrong, we return a result with the status [500 Internal Server Error], state [341] and the message of the exception thrown by the [dao] layer. The listing of the PHP 7 course showed state 340 here, whereas its source code, its configuration (which associates state 341 with the tax calculation view) and its text used 341. We have kept 341: state 340 is already the state of a request whose three posted parameters are invalid (310 + 4 + 9 + 17);
  • lines 95-98: the [finally] clause is executed in all cases, whether or not there was an exception, and even if the [catch] block ends with a [return]. This is where we close the connection to the [Redis] server;
  • line 100: the [métier] layer is created and calculates the tax. The result is the array [impôt, surcôte, décôte, réduction, taux];
  • line 102: with the result of the calculation, a [Simulation] object is created. The first three arguments are positional. The [...] operator then unpacks the associative array [$résultat]: since PHP 8.1, its keys become named arguments, here [impôt, surcôte, décôte, réduction, taux], the names of the constructor's last parameters;
  • line 104: the simulation that has just been built is added to the list of simulations already calculated, which is in the session. The second parameter of the session's [get] method is the value returned if the key is absent: an empty list if no simulation has been performed yet. The new list is built by unpacking the old list, followed by the new simulation, and then put back into the session;
  • line 106: we return the simulation to the main controller, with state [300];
  • line 111: the error message of a DBMS driver may not be encoded in UTF-8 (see version 8). It could then not be put into a JSON string. The PHP 7 script used the [utf8_encode] function, deprecated since PHP 8.2; we use [mb_convert_encoding].

docs.title: 23.11.6. [curl] tests
docs.text:
We test the [CalculerImpotController] controller in JSON mode, with the user authenticated:

> curl -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=calculer-impot"
{"action":"calculer-impot","état":301,"réponse":"il faut utiliser la méthode [post] avec [action] dans l'URL et les paramètres postés [marié, enfants, salaire]"}

> curl -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=calculer-impot" --data-urlencode "marié=peut-être" -d "enfants=x&salaire=y"
{"action":"calculer-impot","état":340,"réponse":["valeur [peut-être] invalide pour le paramètre [marié]","valeur [x] invalide pour le paramètre [enfants]","valeur [y] invalide pour le paramètre [salaire]"]}

> curl -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=calculer-impot" -d "salaire=y"
{"action":"calculer-impot","état":337,"réponse":["paramètre [marié] manquant","paramètre [enfants] manquant","valeur [y] invalide pour le paramètre [salaire]"]}

> curl -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=calculer-impot" --data-urlencode "marié=oui" -d "enfants=2&salaire=55555"
{"action":"calculer-impot","état":300,"réponse":{"marié":"oui","enfants":2,"salaire":55555,"impôt":2814,"surcôte":0,"décôte":0,"réduction":0,"taux":0.14}}

> curl -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=calculer-impot" --data-urlencode "marié=non" -d "enfants=3&salaire=200000"
{"action":"calculer-impot","état":300,"réponse":{"marié":"non","enfants":3,"salaire":200000,"impôt":58006,"surcôte":26649,"décôte":0,"réduction":0,"taux":0.45}}
  • lines 1-2: we make a GET request instead of a POST: state [301];
  • lines 4-5: a POST request with the three parameters [marié, enfants, salaire] present and all invalid: state 310 + 4 + 9 + 17 = 340;
  • lines 7-8: only the [salaire] parameter is posted and, moreover, it is invalid: state 310 + 2 + 8 + 17 = 337;
  • lines 10-11: a tax calculation with valid parameters: state [300]. The response is the JSON object of the simulation. We find the tax of 2814 euros from the official 2019 example for a couple with two children and a salary of 55555 euros;
  • lines 13-14: a second tax calculation.

Note that the state does not always designate a unique combination of errors: 8 + 17 = 9 + 16. State 337 is also that of a request where [marié] and [salaire] are missing and [enfants] is invalid. It is the list of error messages that gives the precise description of the errors.

Let us now simulate a failure of the [Redis] server. Rather than stopping the server, we specify in [config.json] a port on which no server is listening: ["port": 6380]. After a new authentication, a calculation request gives the following response:

> curl -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=authentifier-utilisateur" -d "user=admin&password=admin"
{"action":"authentifier-utilisateur","état":200,"réponse":"Authentification réussie [admin]"}

> curl -i -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=calculer-impot" --data-urlencode "marié=oui" -d "enfants=2&salaire=55555"
HTTP/1.0 500 Internal Server Error
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 16:51:52 GMT
Server: Apache/2.4.58
X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.11
Cache-Control: max-age=0, private, must-revalidate
Cache-Control: no-cache, private
Connection: close
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"action":"calculer-impot","état":350,"réponse":"[redis], Connection refused [tcp://127.0.0.1:6380]"}
  • line 5: the status [500 Internal Server Error];
  • line 14: state [350] and the message of the exception thrown by [Predis].

An email has been sent to the application administrator: it can be seen in the web interface of [Mailpit] (URL [http://localhost:8025]). Its subject is [plantage du serveur de calcul d'impôts] (tax calculation server crash) and its text is the JSON response sent to the client. Let us not forget to restore port 6379.

docs.title: 23.11.7. The [lister-simulations] action
docs.text:
The [lister-simulations] action is processed by the following secondary controller [ListerSimulationsController]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// dépendances Symfony
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;

// action [lister-simulations] : rend la liste des simulations de la session
final class ListerSimulationsController implements InterfaceController
{
    #[\Override]
    public function execute(array $config, Request $request, Session $session): ControllerResult
    {
        // on doit avoir un GET avec le seul paramètre [action] dans l'URL
        if ($request->getMethod() !== "GET" || $request->query->count() !== 1) {
            $message = "GET requis, avec l'unique paramètre [action] dans l'URL";
            return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_BAD_REQUEST, 501, $message);
        }
        // la liste des simulations de la session (vide s'il n'y en a pas encore)
        return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_OK, 500, $session->get("simulations", []));
    }
}

Comments

  • request [GET main.php?action=lister-simulations];
  • lines 20-23: we check that we have a GET request with a single parameter. If this is not the case, an error result is returned to the main controller, with state [501];
  • line 25: we return to the main controller the list of simulations found in the session, or an empty list if the session contains none, with state [500]. The PHP 7 course declared the class without [implements InterfaceController]: an oversight, fixed here.

docs.title: 23.11.9. The [supprimer-simulation] action
docs.text:
The [supprimer-simulation] action is processed by the following secondary controller [SupprimerSimulationController]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// dépendances Symfony
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;

// action [supprimer-simulation] : supprime la simulation n° [numéro] de la liste des simulations
final class SupprimerSimulationController implements InterfaceController
{
    #[\Override]
    public function execute(array $config, Request $request, Session $session): ControllerResult
    {
        // on doit avoir un GET avec les seuls paramètres [action, numéro] dans l'URL
        if ($request->getMethod() !== "GET" || $request->query->count() !== 2) {
            return self::erreur(602, "GET requis, avec les paramètres [action, numéro]");
        }
        // le paramètre [numéro] doit exister
        if (!$request->query->has("numéro")) {
            return self::erreur(604, "paramètre [numéro] manquant");
        }
        // le paramètre [numéro] doit être un entier >= 0
        $numéro = trim($request->query->getString("numéro"));
        if (preg_match('/^\d+$/', $numéro) !== 1) {
            return self::erreur(612, "paramètre [$numéro] invalide");
        }
        // la simulation n° [numéro] doit exister : [numéro] dans l'intervalle [0, n-1]
        $numéro = (int) $numéro;
        $simulations = $session->get("simulations", []);
        if ($numéro >= count($simulations)) {
            return self::erreur(628, "la simulation n° [$numéro] n'existe pas");
        }
        // on supprime la simulation : [array_splice] renumérote les éléments suivants de la liste
        array_splice($simulations, $numéro, 1);
        // on remet les simulations dans la session
        $session->set("simulations", $simulations);
        // on rend la nouvelle liste des simulations
        return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_OK, 600, $simulations);
    }

    // un résultat d'erreur
    private static function erreur(int $état, string $message): ControllerResult
    {
        return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_BAD_REQUEST, $état, $message);
    }
}

Comments

  • request [GET main.php?action=supprimer-simulation&numéro=x];
  • lines 20-22: we check that we have a GET request with two parameters. Otherwise the state is [602];
  • lines 24-26: we check that the [numéro] parameter exists among the URL parameters. Otherwise the state is [604];
  • lines 28-31: we check that the value of the [numéro] parameter is syntactically correct: a positive or zero integer. Otherwise the state is [612];
  • lines 33-37: we check that simulation no. [numéro] does exist: the number must be in the interval [0, n-1] where n is the number of simulations in the session. Otherwise the state is [628]. Since the number cannot be negative, it is enough to check that it is less than n. If the session contains no simulations, n is 0;
  • line 39: simulation no. [numéro] is deleted by the [array_splice] function, which here deletes one element starting at position [$numéro] and renumbers the following elements. The PHP 7 script used [unset], which does not change the keys of the other elements, and then [array_values] to obtain a list with keys [0, n-2];
  • line 41: we put the new array of simulations back into the session;
  • line 43: we return the new list of simulations to the main controller, with state [600];
  • line 47: a utility method that builds an error result. The error states are those of the PHP 7 script, which calculated them by adding 2, 4, 8 and then 16 to state 600 as the checks proceeded.

docs.title: 23.11.11. The [fin-session] action
docs.text:
The [fin-session] action is processed by the following secondary controller [FinSessionController]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// dépendances Symfony
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;

// action [fin-session] : termine la session de simulations
final class FinSessionController implements InterfaceController
{
    #[\Override]
    public function execute(array $config, Request $request, Session $session): ControllerResult
    {
        // on doit avoir un GET avec le seul paramètre [action] dans l'URL
        if ($request->getMethod() !== "GET" || $request->query->count() !== 1) {
            $message = "GET requis avec le seul paramètre [action] dans l'URL";
            return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_BAD_REQUEST, 401, $message);
        }
        // on mémorise le type de la session
        $type = $session->get("type");
        // on invalide la session courante : ses données sont supprimées et une nouvelle session démarre
        $session->invalidate();
        // on remet le type dans la nouvelle session
        $session->set("type", $type);
        // réussite
        return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_OK, 400, "session supprimée");
    }
}

Comments

  • request [GET main.php?action=fin-session];
  • lines 20-23: we check that the action is a GET with the single parameter [action]. Otherwise the state is [401];
  • line 25: before the session ends, we store its type [json, xml, html];
  • line 27: we invalidate the current session. This deletes the data recorded in it and a new session is started, with a new identifier;
  • line 29: the type of the previous session is put back into the new session. In the end, we start again with a new session having the single key [type]: the user will have to authenticate again;
  • line 31: we return the result to the main controller, with state [400].

docs.title: 23.12.1. Introduction
docs.text:
Let us come back to the general architecture of the application:

We are going to present the possible response types [3a]. They are grouped together in the project's [Responses] folder. We have already presented the [InterfaceResponse] interface, the parent class [ParentResponse] and the [JsonResponse] class. The response type of a session is set by the [init-session] action, which places it in the session. It is represented by the [ResponseType] enumeration of the [Entities] folder:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// les types de réponse que le client peut demander avec l'action [init-session]
enum ResponseType: string
{
    case Json = "json";
    case Xml = "xml";
    case Html = "html";

    // l'objet chargé d'envoyer une réponse de ce type
    public function response(): InterfaceResponse
    {
        return match ($this) {
            self::Json => new JsonResponse(),
            self::Xml => new XmlResponse(),
            self::Html => new HtmlResponse(),
        };
    }
}

Comments

  • lines 11-13: the three response types. The value of each case is the value expected for the [type] parameter of the [init-session] action;
  • lines 16-23: the [response] method returns the object responsible for sending a response of this type. The return type is the [InterfaceResponse] interface: the calling code knows only the interface's [send] method. The PHP 7 course associated each type with a class name in the configuration file ([types] key) and instantiated it with [new $response()].

Let us recall the code of the main controller that requests the sending of the response to the client:

// le type de la réponse est dans la session - JSON par défaut s'il n'a pas encore été fixé
$type = ResponseType::tryFrom($session->get("type", "")) ?? ResponseType::Json;
// l'objet [InterfaceResponse] du type demandé envoie la réponse au client
$type->response()->send(
    $request,
    $session,
    $config,
    $résultat->statusCode,
    $content,
    $résultat->headers,
    $logger
);
  • line 107: we determine the response type;
  • line 109: we instantiate the appropriate response class and send the response to the client using its method [send($request, $session, $config, $statusCode, $content, $headers, $logger)].

docs.title: 23.12.2. The [JsonResponse] class
docs.text:
It has already been presented. We nevertheless show its code again to better highlight the uniformity of the three response classes:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// dépendances Symfony
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;

// une réponse JSON
final class JsonResponse extends ParentResponse
{
    #[\Override]
    public function send(
        Request $request,
        Session $session,
        array $config,
        int $statusCode,
        array $content,
        array $headers = [],
        ?Logger $logger = null
    ): void {
        // sérialisation JSON : [json_encode] sérialise aussi les attributs publics des objets [Simulation]
        $json = json_encode($content, self::JSON_OPTIONS);
        // envoi de la réponse par la classe parent
        $this->sendResponse($statusCode, $json, "application/json", $headers);
        // log
        $logger?->write("réponse=$json");
    }
}

docs.title: 23.12.3. The [XmlResponse] class
docs.text:
The [XmlResponse] class is as follows:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// dépendances Symfony
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;

// une réponse XML
final class XmlResponse extends ParentResponse
{
    #[\Override]
    public function send(
        Request $request,
        Session $session,
        array $config,
        int $statusCode,
        array $content,
        array $headers = [],
        ?Logger $logger = null
    ): void {
        // sérialisation XML avec la classe [XmlUtilitaires] de la version 11
        // les objets [Simulation] sont d'abord transformés en tableaux associatifs
        $xml = XmlUtilitaires::arrayToXml(self::toArray($content), "root");
        // envoi de la réponse par la classe parent
        $this->sendResponse($statusCode, $xml, "application/xml", $headers);
        // log en JSON, plus concis que le XML
        $this->log($logger, $content);
    }
}

Comments

  • line 27: the response [$content] is serialized to XML by the [arrayToXml] method of the [XmlUtilitaires] class of version 11. This method expects an array whose values are arrays or simple values: the [toArray] method of the parent class first replaces the [Simulation] objects with the array of their attributes. The root element of the document is called [root], as in the PHP 7 course;
  • line 29: the parent class sends the response to the client, with the type [application/xml];
  • line 31: the response is logged in JSON, which is more concise than XML.

The PHP 7 course used the XML encoder of the [Symfony / Serializer] library, and a second encoder, JSON, for the logs.

docs.title: 23.12.5. The [HtmlResponse] response
docs.text:
When the session type is [html], an object of type [HtmlResponse] is instantiated to send the response to the client. It will send the client an HTML document that depends on the state code returned by the secondary controller that processed the action. This [état => vue] mapping is written in the configuration file [config.json] as follows:

    "vues": {
        "vue-authentification.php": [700, 221, 400],
        "vue-calcul-impot.php": [200, 300, 341, 350, 800],
        "vue-liste-simulations.php": [500, 600]
    },
    "vue-erreurs": "vue-erreurs.php"

This configuration reads as follows: [‘view name' => ‘states associated with this view']:

  • line 56: if the secondary controller returned a state from the array [700, 221, 400], then the view [vue-authentification.php] must be displayed;
  • line 57: if the secondary controller returned a state from the array [200, 300, 341, 350, 800], then the view [vue-calcul-impot.php] must be displayed;
  • line 58: if the secondary controller returned a state from the array [500, 600], then the view [vue-liste-simulations.php] must be displayed;
  • line 60: if the secondary controller returned a state that is in none of the previous arrays, then the view [vue-erreurs.php] must be displayed.

The views are grouped together in the project's [Views] folder. The code of the [HtmlResponse] class is as follows:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// dépendances Symfony
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;

// une réponse HTML : une des vues du dossier [Views]
final class HtmlResponse extends ParentResponse
{
    #[\Override]
    public function send(
        Request $request,
        Session $session,
        array $config,
        int $statusCode,
        array $content,
        array $headers = [],
        ?Logger $logger = null
    ): void {
        // la réponse HTML dépend du code d'état rendu par le contrôleur
        $état = $content["état"];
        // à un état correspond une vue : on cherche la 1re vue dont la liste d'états contient [$état]
        // si aucune vue ne convient, c'est une erreur inattendue : on affiche la vue des erreurs
        $vue = array_find_key(
            $config["vues"],
            fn(array $états): bool => in_array($état, $états, true)
        ) ?? $config["vue-erreurs"];
        // on exécute la vue : ce qu'elle écrit est mis dans un tampon au lieu d'être envoyé au client
        // la vue a accès aux variables [$request, $session, $config, $content] de la méthode
        ob_start();
        require __DIR__ . "/../Views/$vue";
        // on récupère le contenu du tampon, le document HTML, et on vide le tampon
        $html = ob_get_clean();
        // envoi de la réponse par la classe parent
        $this->sendResponse($statusCode, $html, "text/html", $headers);
        // log en JSON de la réponse du contrôleur, sans le HTML
        $this->log($logger, $content);
    }
}

Comments

  • line 26: the view to be displayed depends on the state code returned by the controller that processed the action. This code is in [$content["état"]];
  • lines 29-32: we look in the application configuration for the view corresponding to this state. The [array_find_key] function (PHP 8.4) returns the key of the first element of the [$config["vues"]] array that satisfies the condition expressed by the arrow function, here the name of the first view whose list of states contains [$état]. If no element satisfies the condition, it returns [null]: we are then in a situation of an abnormal state code for the HTML application and we display the error view, thanks to the [??] operator. The PHP 7 script performed this search with a fifteen-line [while] loop;
  • lines 35-38: we execute the PHP code of the selected view and put the result in the [$html] variable. This code deserves some explanation. Let us imagine that the selected view is [vue-authentification.php], which presents a web authentication form:
    • line 35: the [ob_start] function starts what the documentation calls output buffering. Everything written by [print] and [echo] operations, by the HTML text of an included script... and which is normally sent immediately to the client, goes into an output buffer (ob = output buffer) without being sent to the client;
    • line 36: we load the view [vue-authentification.php], which is a dynamic HTML view containing PHP code. Two things then happen. First, the PHP code of the view is executed. The result is a page that contains only HTML, possibly CSS and JavaScript, but no more PHP. Then, this HTML code is normally sent to the client. This is in fact the case for any text encountered by the PHP interpreter that is not PHP code. Because of output buffering, this HTML code is put into the output buffer without being sent to the client;
    • line 38: the [ob_get_clean] function does two things: it returns the contents of the output buffer, hence the HTML page that was put into it; it empties the buffer and stops output buffering. For the client, everything happens as if nothing had occurred: it still has not received anything;
  • the view is included by the [send] method: the view's code therefore has access to the method's local variables, in particular its parameters [$request], [$session], [$config] and [$content]. This is how the view receives the data it must display;
  • [__DIR__] is the absolute path of the folder of the script being executed, here the [Responses] folder. To find the view, we therefore have to go up one level [..] and then into the [Views] folder;
  • line 40: the parent class sends the response to the client, with the type [text/html];
  • line 42: we log in JSON the response [$content] provided by the secondary controller that processed the current action, without the HTML.

docs.title: 23.12.6. [curl] tests
docs.text:
To really test the HTML mode of the session, we would need to go through all the views. We will do so later. We will simply check that a successful [init-session] action (state 700) in a new [html]-type session does produce an HTML response. According to the configuration file, it is the view [vue-authentification.php] that then constitutes the response:

> curl -D - -o vue.html -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=init-session&type=html"
HTTP/1.0 200 OK
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 16:51:53 GMT
Server: Apache/2.4.58
X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.11
Cache-Control: max-age=0, private, must-revalidate
Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID=60bf588b0873f085af3b33940c0d8417; path=/
Cache-Control: no-cache, private
Vary: Accept-Encoding
Connection: close
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
  • line 1: the [-D -] option asks [curl] to write the HTTP headers of the response to standard output (the file [-]), the [-o vue.html] option to write the body of the response to the file [vue.html];
  • line 11: the response is an HTML document.

Opened in a browser, the file [vue.html] displays the authentication view, which is presented now.

docs.title: 23.13.1. Presentation of the views
docs.text:
The HTML web application uses four views. The authentication view:

The tax calculation view:

The view of the list of simulations:

The view of unexpected errors:

The views use the CSS framework [Bootstrap], in its version 5.3. The PHP 7 course used version 4.1: some CSS classes have changed or disappeared, and we will point this out along the way. We are going to describe these views one after the other.

docs.title: 23.13.2.1. Presentation of the view
docs.text:
The authentication view is as follows:

The view is made up of three elements that we will call fragments:

  • the top banner, with the logo and the title, is generated by the script [v-bandeau.php];
  • the authentication form is generated by the script [v-authentification.php];
  • the pink error box, displayed only when there are errors, is generated by the script [v-erreurs.php].

The authentication view is generated by the following page [vue-authentification.php]:

<?php
// la vue d'authentification - états [700, 221, 400]
// on hérite des variables de la méthode [HtmlResponse::send] qui fait le [require] de cette vue :
// Request $request : la requête en cours
// Session $session : la session de l'application
// array $config : la configuration de l'application
// array $content : la réponse du contrôleur [action, état, réponse]

// dépendances Symfony
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;

// on calcule le modèle de la vue
$modèle = getModelForThisView($request, $content);

function getModelForThisView(Request $request, array $content): stdClass
{
    // le modèle dépend de l'état de l'application
    return match ($content["état"]) {
        // authentification ratée : on réaffiche l'identifiant saisi et un message d'erreur
        221 => (object) [
            "login" => $request->request->getString("user"),
            "titreErreurs" => "Les erreurs suivantes se sont produites :",
            "erreurs" => ["Echec de l'authentification"],
        ],
        // 700, 400 : formulaire vide, sans erreur
        default => (object) ["login" => "", "erreurs" => []],
    };
}
?>
<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
    <!-- document codé en UTF-8, affiché sur toute la largeur de l'écran -->
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
    <!-- Bootstrap 5.3 -->
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.8/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css"
          integrity="sha384-sRIl4kxILFvY47J16cr9ZwB07vP4J8+LH7qKQnuqkuIAvNWLzeN8tE5YBujZqJLB" crossorigin="anonymous">
    <title>Application impots</title>
</head>
<body>
<div class="container">
    <!-- bandeau -->
    <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-bandeau.php" ?>
    <!-- formulaire d'authentification sur 9 colonnes -->
    <div class="row">
        <div class="col-md-9">
            <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-authentification.php" ?>
        </div>
    </div>
    <!-- s'il y a des erreurs, on les affiche sous le formulaire -->
    <?php if ($modèle->erreurs !== []): ?>
        <div class="row">
            <div class="col-md-9">
                <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-erreurs.php" ?>
            </div>
        </div>
    <?php endif ?>
</div>
</body>
</html>

Comments

  • lines 2-7: the view is executed by the [require] statement of the [HtmlResponse::send] method. It inherits the variables of this method;
  • lines 13-28: the PHP part of the view calculates the view model. We will come back to this a little further on;
  • line 30: an HTML5 document begins with this line;
  • lines 31-61: the HTML page is encapsulated in the [<html>] and [</html>] tags. The [lang] attribute indicates the language of the document;
  • lines 32-40: the head of the HTML document:
    • line 34: the [<meta charset>] tag indicates that the document is encoded in UTF-8;
    • line 35: the [<meta name="viewport">] tag sets the initial display of the view: over the full width of the screen displaying it (width) at its initial size (initial-scale). The value [shrink-to-fit=no] of the PHP 7 version is no longer useful with current browsers;
    • lines 37-38: the [<link rel="stylesheet">] tag sets the CSS file that governs the appearance of the view. We use the CSS framework [Bootstrap] 5.3.8, downloaded from the [jsDelivr] distribution network ([https://getbootstrap.com/docs/5.3/getting-started/introduction/]). The [integrity] attribute contains the SHA-384 hash of the file: the browser rejects the downloaded file if it does not have this hash, which protects the page against a modification of the file on the distribution network;
    • line 39: the [<title>] tag sets the page title, displayed in the browser tab;
  • lines 41-60: the body of the web page is encapsulated in the [<body>] and [</body>] tags;
  • line 42: the [<div>] tag delimits a section of the displayed page. The [class] attributes used in the view all refer to the Bootstrap CSS framework. The [<div class="container">] tag delimits a Bootstrap container, centered in the page;
  • line 44: we include the fragment [v-bandeau.php], which generates the page banner. We will describe it shortly. The path is built with [__DIR__], the [Views] folder: a simple relative path such as ["v-bandeau.php"] would be looked up first in the folders of PHP's [include_path] directive, then in the folder of the calling script ([Responses]) and the current folder, which is a source of surprises;
  • lines 46-47: the [<div class="row">] tag delimits a Bootstrap row. These rows are made up of 12 columns. The [<div class="col-md-9">] tag delimits a 9-column section;
  • line 48: we include the fragment [v-authentification.php], which displays the authentication form;
  • lines 52-58: if the model's list of errors is not empty, we include the fragment [v-erreurs.php], which displays the errors in a new Bootstrap row. Here we use PHP's alternative syntax for control structures, [if (...):] ... [endif], which is more readable than braces in an HTML page. The PHP 7 script wrote the HTML code of the errors with the [heredoc] syntax ([print <<<EOT ... EOT;]).

From this code, let us note the dynamic elements to be defined:

  • [$modèle->erreurs]: the list of error messages, empty if there is no error;
  • [$modèle->titreErreurs]: the text preceding the list of errors.

docs.title: 23.13.2.2. The [v-bandeau.php] fragment
docs.text:
The [v-bandeau.php] fragment displays the top banner of all the views of the web application:

<?php
// fragment : le bandeau supérieur de toutes les vues
// modèle : [$modèle->logo] (facultatif) - l'URL du logo, relative à l'URL de la page affichée
?>
<!-- bandeau : un cadre gris clair aux coins arrondis -->
<div class="p-4 my-4 bg-body-tertiary rounded-3">
    <div class="row align-items-center">
        <div class="col-md-4">
            <img src="<?= htmlspecialchars($modèle->logo ?? "Views/logo.jpg") ?>" alt="Cerisier en fleurs">
        </div>
        <div class="col-md-8">
            <h1>Calculez votre impôt</h1>
        </div>
    </div>
</div>

Comments

  • line 6: the banner is encapsulated in a section whose Bootstrap classes give inner padding (p-4), vertical margins (my-4), a light gray background (bg-body-tertiary) and rounded corners (rounded-3). The PHP 7 course used the [jumbotron] class of Bootstrap 4, which no longer exists in Bootstrap 5: these four classes replace it;
  • line 7: a Bootstrap row. The [align-items-center] class vertically centers the contents of its columns;
  • lines 8-10: an image [<img>] is placed in the first four columns of the row;
  • line 9: the syntax [<?= expression ?>] is equivalent to [<?php echo expression ?>]. In other words, the value of the [src] attribute will be the value of the PHP expression. This expression is:
    • [$modèle->logo ?? "Views/logo.jpg"]: the URL of the logo, if the view model contains one; otherwise the relative URL [Views/logo.jpg]. All the application's URLs are of the form [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=…]: the relative URL [Views/logo.jpg] is completed by the browser with the path of the displayed page, which gives [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/Views/logo.jpg]. The PHP 7 fragment built the absolute URL of the logo from the server variables ([REQUEST_SCHEME], [SERVER_NAME], [SERVER_PORT], [REQUEST_URI]) and a regular expression: this was unnecessary;
    • [htmlspecialchars(...)]: the [htmlspecialchars] function replaces HTML special characters with their entities: [&] becomes [&], [<] becomes [<], [>] becomes [>], ["] becomes ["] and ['] becomes [']. Thus, the value written into the page can neither break the [src] attribute nor introduce tags into the page;
  • lines 11-13: the other 8 columns of the row (remember that there are 12 in total) are used to place text in large characters ([<h1>] tag).

Dynamic element: [$modèle->logo], the URL of the image displayed in the banner (optional).

Every dynamic value written into an HTML page must go through [htmlspecialchars]. This is the protection against XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) attacks: if a value entered by the user, or coming from an untrusted source, were written as is into the page, a malicious user could introduce JavaScript code into it, for example [<script>…</script>], which would be executed by the browser of those who display the page. The PHP 7 course escaped no value. Since PHP 8.1, the default options of [htmlspecialchars] ([ENT_QUOTES | ENT_SUBSTITUTE | ENT_HTML401]) also encode the apostrophe: the call [htmlspecialchars($valeur)] is enough, whether the value is written in text or in an attribute delimited by double or single quotes.

docs.title: 23.13.2.3. The [v-authentification.php] fragment
docs.text:
The [v-authentification.php] fragment displays the authentication form of the web application:

<?php
// fragment : le formulaire d'authentification
// modèle : [$modèle->login] - l'identifiant à afficher dans la zone de saisie [user]
?>
<!-- formulaire HTML - on poste ses valeurs avec l'action [authentifier-utilisateur] -->
<form method="post" action="main.php?action=authentifier-utilisateur">
    <!-- titre sur fond bleu -->
    <div class="alert alert-primary" role="alert">
        <h4>Veuillez vous authentifier</h4>
    </div>
    <!-- 1re ligne : l'identifiant -->
    <div class="row mb-3">
        <!-- libellé sur 3 colonnes -->
        <label for="user" class="col-md-3 col-form-label">Nom d'utilisateur</label>
        <!-- zone de saisie texte sur 4 colonnes -->
        <div class="col-md-4">
            <input type="text" class="form-control" id="user" name="user"
                   placeholder="Nom d'utilisateur" value="<?= htmlspecialchars($modèle->login) ?>">
        </div>
    </div>
    <!-- 2e ligne : le mot de passe -->
    <div class="row mb-3">
        <label for="password" class="col-md-3 col-form-label">Mot de passe</label>
        <!-- zone de saisie cachée -->
        <div class="col-md-4">
            <input type="password" class="form-control" id="password" name="password"
                   placeholder="Mot de passe">
        </div>
    </div>
    <!-- 3e ligne : bouton de type [submit] -->
    <div class="row mb-3">
        <div class="col-md-2">
            <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Valider</button>
        </div>
    </div>
</form>

Comments

  • lines 6-36: the [<form>] tag delimits an HTML form. A form generally has the following characteristics:
    • it defines input fields ([<input>] tags);
    • it has a [submit]-type button that sends the entered values to the URL indicated in the [action] attribute of the [<form>] tag. The HTTP method used to request this URL is specified in the [method] attribute of the [<form>] tag;
    • here, when the user clicks the [Valider] (Validate) button, the browser will post the values entered in the form to the URL [main.php?action=authentifier-utilisateur];
    • the posted values are the values entered by the user in the two input fields. They will be posted in the form [user=xx&password=yy]. The parameter names [user, password] are those of the [name] attributes of the input fields;
  • lines 8-10: a Bootstrap section to display a title on a blue background;
  • lines 12-20: the 1st row of the form. The [mb-3] class gives the row a bottom margin. Bootstrap 4 used the [form-group] class, which no longer exists in Bootstrap 5;
  • line 14: the label, over three columns. The [for] attribute of the [<label>] tag links the label to the [id] attribute of the input field: clicking the label places the cursor in the input field;
  • line 16: the input field is placed in a group of four columns;
  • lines 17-18: the HTML [<input>] tag describes an input field. It has several attributes:
    • [type="text"]: this is a text input field. Anything can be typed into it;
    • [class="form-control"]: Bootstrap style for the input field;
    • [id="user"]: identifier of the input field. This identifier is generally used by CSS and JavaScript code;
    • [name="user"]: name of the input field. It is under this name that the value entered by the user will be posted by the browser [user=xx];
    • [placeholder="invite"]: the text displayed in the input field when the user has not yet typed anything;
    • [value="valeur"]: the text displayed in the input field as soon as it is displayed, therefore before the user enters anything else. This mechanism is used in case of error to display the input that caused the error. Here this value will be the value of [$modèle->login], escaped by [htmlspecialchars]: an identifier entered containing a double quote cannot close the [value] attribute;
  • lines 22-29: similar code for entering the password. The attribute [type="password"] gives a text input field whose typed characters are hidden;
  • lines 31-35: a 3rd row for the [Valider] button;
  • line 33: because it has the attribute [type="submit"], clicking this button triggers the sending of the entered values to the server by the browser. The CSS classes [btn btn-primary] display a blue button.

One last thing remains to be explained. The attribute [action="main.php?action=authentifier-utilisateur"] of the [<form>] tag defines an incomplete URL (it does not start with http://machine:port/chemin). The authentication view will be obtained with various URLs:

  • [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=init-session&type=html];
  • [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=authentifier-utilisateur].

These URLs designate a document [main.php] in the path [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12]. This will be the case for all the URLs of this application. The URL [main.php?action=authentifier-utilisateur] will be prefixed with this path when the entered values are sent. They will therefore be posted to the URL [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=authentifier-utilisateur].

docs.title: 23.13.2.4. The [v-erreurs.php] fragment
docs.text:
The [v-erreurs.php] fragment displays a list of error messages. It is used by three of the application's four views:

<?php
// fragment : une liste de messages d'erreur dans un cadre rose
// modèle : [$modèle->titreErreurs] - le texte d'introduction, [$modèle->erreurs] - les messages
?>
<div class="alert alert-danger" role="alert">
    <?= htmlspecialchars($modèle->titreErreurs) ?>
    <ul class="mb-0">
        <?php foreach ($modèle->erreurs as $erreur): ?>
            <li><?= htmlspecialchars($erreur) ?></li>
        <?php endforeach ?>
    </ul>
</div>
  • line 5: the errors are displayed in a Bootstrap box with a pink background;
  • line 6: the text introducing the errors;
  • lines 7-11: the HTML [<ul>] tag (unordered list) displays a bulleted list. Each item of the list has the syntax [<li>élément</li>]. The [mb-0] class removes the list's bottom margin;
  • lines 8-10: the alternative syntax of the [foreach] loop. Each message is escaped by [htmlspecialchars]: the controllers' error messages contain the values sent by the client ([valeur [x] invalide pour le paramètre [enfants]]). In the PHP 7 course, the view model contained the HTML list of errors, built by concatenating [<li>$erreur</li>] strings: a posted value containing JavaScript code would have been executed by the browser.

Dynamic elements: [$modèle->titreErreurs] and [$modèle->erreurs].

docs.title: 23.13.2.5. Visual tests
docs.text:
Views can be tested well before they are integrated into the application. The aim here is to test their visual appearance. We group all the test views in the project's [Tests] folder. To test the view [vue-authentification.php], we need to create the data model it will display. The script [Tests/vue-authentification.php] is as follows:

<?php
// test visuel de la vue d'authentification : la vue est affichée avec un modèle de test

// on calcule le modèle de la vue
$modèle = getModelForThisView();

function getModelForThisView(): stdClass
{
    return (object) [
        // identifiant de l'utilisateur
        "login" => "albert",
        // liste d'erreurs - la 2e vérifie que les caractères spéciaux du HTML sont neutralisés
        "titreErreurs" => "Les erreurs suivantes se sont produites :",
        "erreurs" => ["erreur1", "<b>erreur2</b>"],
        // le logo du bandeau, relatif à l'URL de ce script
        "logo" => "../Views/logo.jpg",
    ];
}
?>
<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.8/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css"
          integrity="sha384-sRIl4kxILFvY47J16cr9ZwB07vP4J8+LH7qKQnuqkuIAvNWLzeN8tE5YBujZqJLB" crossorigin="anonymous">
    <title>Application impots</title>
</head>
<body>
<div class="container">
    <!-- bandeau -->
    <?php require __DIR__ . "/../Views/v-bandeau.php" ?>
    <!-- formulaire d'authentification sur 9 colonnes -->
    <div class="row">
        <div class="col-md-9">
            <?php require __DIR__ . "/../Views/v-authentification.php" ?>
        </div>
    </div>
    <!-- s'il y a des erreurs, on les affiche sous le formulaire -->
    <?php if ($modèle->erreurs !== []): ?>
        <div class="row">
            <div class="col-md-9">
                <?php require __DIR__ . "/../Views/v-erreurs.php" ?>
            </div>
        </div>
    <?php endif ?>
</div>
</body>
</html>

Comments

  • line 5: the authentication view has dynamic parts controlled by the [$modèle] object. This object is called the view model. According to one of the two definitions given for the acronym MVC, this is the M of MVC. It is calculated by the [getModelForThisView] function. A function defined at the top level of a script is known from the beginning of the script's execution: it can be called before its definition;
  • lines 9-17: the view model is an object of type [stdClass], PHP's generic class. It is obtained here by converting an associative array into an object with the [(object)] operator: the array's keys become the object's attributes. The [stdClass] type is the only object type to which undeclared attributes can still be added (see the chapter on classes). We could have chosen an associative array instead for the same result;
  • line 14: test values for the dynamic elements of the view. The 2nd error contains HTML tags: we will check that they are displayed as they are and not interpreted by the browser;
  • line 16: the URL of the logo is relative to the URL of the test script, located in the [Tests] folder;
  • line 32: the rest of the script is that of the view [Views/vue-authentification.php]. The included fragments are those of the [Views] folder: they are the ones being tested. The PHP 7 course copied a version of them into the [Tests] folder.

The visual test is done by requesting the URL [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/Tests/vue-authentification.php] in a browser:

Note that the [<b>] tag of the 2nd error has been displayed and not interpreted: the protection against XSS attacks works. We continue these visual tests until we are satisfied with the result. While fine-tuning, we modify the file in [VS Code] and then refresh the browser page (F5).

docs.title: 23.13.2.6. Calculating the view model
docs.text:
Once the visual appearance of the view has been determined, we can proceed to calculate the view model under real conditions. Let us recall the state codes that lead to this view. They are found in the configuration file:

    "vues": {
        "vue-authentification.php": [700, 221, 400],
        "vue-calcul-impot.php": [200, 300, 341, 350, 800],
        "vue-liste-simulations.php": [500, 600]
    },
    "vue-erreurs": "vue-erreurs.php"

It is therefore the state codes [700, 221, 400] that cause the authentication view to be displayed. To find the meaning of these codes, we can use the [curl] tests carried out on the JSON application:

  • 700 is the state code after a successful [init-session] action: we then present the empty authentication form;
  • 221 is the state code after a failed [authentifier-utilisateur] action (credentials not recognized): we then present the authentication form so that it can be corrected;
  • 400 is the state code after a successful [fin-session] action: we then present the empty authentication form.

Now that we know when the authentication form must be displayed, we can calculate its model in [vue-authentification.php]:

<?php
// la vue d'authentification - états [700, 221, 400]
// on hérite des variables de la méthode [HtmlResponse::send] qui fait le [require] de cette vue :
// Request $request : la requête en cours
// Session $session : la session de l'application
// array $config : la configuration de l'application
// array $content : la réponse du contrôleur [action, état, réponse]

// dépendances Symfony
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;

// on calcule le modèle de la vue
$modèle = getModelForThisView($request, $content);

function getModelForThisView(Request $request, array $content): stdClass
{
    // le modèle dépend de l'état de l'application
    return match ($content["état"]) {
        // authentification ratée : on réaffiche l'identifiant saisi et un message d'erreur
        221 => (object) [
            "login" => $request->request->getString("user"),
            "titreErreurs" => "Les erreurs suivantes se sont produites :",
            "erreurs" => ["Echec de l'authentification"],
        ],
        // 700, 400 : formulaire vide, sans erreur
        default => (object) ["login" => "", "erreurs" => []],
    };
}
?>

Comments

  • lines 3-7: we recall the variables inherited from the [HtmlResponse::send] method, which has the view displayed by a [require];
  • line 10: the Symfony class used in the view's code. The view has no namespace: without this statement, [Request] would designate the class [\Request], which does not exist;
  • lines 15-28: the [getModelForThisView] function calculates the view model. It receives the request and the controller's response, the only data it needs. The views have no [declare(strict_types=1)] declaration: they are HTML pages with a little PHP code;
  • lines 18-27: the model depends on the state code returned by the controller that processed the current action:
    • lines 20-23: the case of incorrect authentication: we redisplay the identifier entered by the user, found in the posted parameters [$request->request], and we display an error message. The user at the keyboard can then try another authentication;
    • line 26: states 700 and 400: a blank authentication form, without errors.

The PHP 7 script used a [switch] statement that modified a [stdClass] object created at the beginning of the function.

docs.title: 23.13.2.8. Conclusion
docs.text:
We were able to test the view [vue-authentification.php] without having written the other views. This was possible because:

  • all the controllers have been written;
  • [curl] allows us to send requests to the server without needing the views. When writing the controllers, you must be aware that anyone can do this. You must therefore be ready to handle requests that no view would allow. They are made by hand with [curl]. You must never tell yourself a priori "this request is impossible". You must check.

docs.title: 23.13.3.1. Presentation of the view
docs.text:
The tax calculation view is as follows:

The view has five parts:

  • the top banner is generated by the [v-bandeau.php] fragment already presented;
  • the tax calculation form is generated by the [v-calcul-impot.php] fragment;
  • a menu presenting two links is generated by the [v-menu.php] fragment;
  • the result of the calculation is displayed in a green box;
  • the errors are displayed in a pink box by the [v-erreurs.php] fragment.

The green and pink boxes are never displayed together in the application: the screenshot above is that of the visual test of the view, presented later. The tax calculation view is generated by the following script [vue-calcul-impot.php], of which we show only the HTML part for now:

We comment only on what is new:

  • line 57: inclusion of the view's top banner;
  • lines 60-62: inclusion of the menu, which will occupy three columns of the Bootstrap row following the banner;
  • lines 63-65: inclusion of the tax calculation form, which will occupy the other nine columns of this row;

docs.text:
The [v-calcul-impot.php] fragment displays the tax calculation form:

<?php
// fragment : le formulaire de calcul de l'impôt
// modèle : [$modèle->marié] (oui / non), [$modèle->enfants], [$modèle->salaire] - les valeurs affichées
?>
<!-- formulaire HTML posté avec l'action [calculer-impot] -->
<form method="post" action="main.php?action=calculer-impot">
    <!-- titre sur fond bleu -->
    <div class="alert alert-primary" role="alert">
        <h4>Remplissez le formulaire ci-dessous puis validez-le</h4>
    </div>
    <!-- 1re ligne : le statut marital, deux boutons radio du même groupe [marié] -->
    <fieldset class="row mb-3">
        <legend class="col-form-label col-md-4 pt-0">Etes-vous marié(e) ou pacsé(e) ?</legend>
        <div class="col-md-5">
            <div class="form-check">
                <input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="marié" id="mariéOui" value="oui"
                    <?= $modèle->marié === "oui" ? "checked" : "" ?>>
                <label class="form-check-label" for="mariéOui">Oui</label>
            </div>
            <div class="form-check">
                <input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="marié" id="mariéNon" value="non"
                    <?= $modèle->marié === "oui" ? "" : "checked" ?>>
                <label class="form-check-label" for="mariéNon">Non</label>
            </div>
        </div>
    </fieldset>
    <!-- 2e ligne : le nombre d'enfants, un entier >= 0 -->
    <div class="row mb-3">
        <label for="enfants" class="col-md-4 col-form-label">Nombre d'enfants à charge</label>
        <div class="col-md-5">
            <input type="number" min="0" step="1" class="form-control" id="enfants" name="enfants"
                   placeholder="Nombre d'enfants à charge" value="<?= htmlspecialchars($modèle->enfants) ?>">
        </div>
    </div>
    <!-- 3e ligne : le salaire annuel, un entier >= 0 -->
    <div class="row mb-3">
        <label for="salaire" class="col-md-4 col-form-label">Salaire annuel</label>
        <div class="col-md-5">
            <input type="number" min="0" step="1" class="form-control" id="salaire" name="salaire"
                   placeholder="Salaire annuel" aria-describedby="salaireHelp"
                   value="<?= htmlspecialchars($modèle->salaire) ?>">
            <div id="salaireHelp" class="form-text">Arrondissez à l'euro inférieur</div>
        </div>
    </div>
    <!-- 4e ligne : bouton de type [submit] -->
    <div class="row mb-3">
        <div class="col-md-5">
            <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Valider</button>
        </div>
    </div>
</form>

Comments

  • line 6: the HTML form will be posted ([method] attribute) to the URL [main.php?action=calculer-impot] ([action] attribute). The posted values will be the values of the input fields:
    • the value of the checked radio button in the form [marié=oui] if the [Oui] (Yes) radio button is checked, [marié=non] if the [Non] (No) radio button is checked. [marié] is the value of the [name] attribute of the two buttons, [oui] and [non] the values of their [value] attributes;
    • the value of the numeric input field [enfants] in the form [enfants=xx] where [xx] is the value typed by the user at the keyboard;
    • the value of the numeric input field [salaire] in the form [salaire=xx];
    • finally, the posted value will have the form [marié=xx&enfants=yy&salaire=zz];
  • the entered values will be posted when the user clicks the [submit]-type button line 48;
  • lines 12-26: the two radio buttons. The [<fieldset>] tag groups form elements together, the [<legend>] tag gives them a title;
  • lines 16-21: these are radio buttons because of the attribute [type="radio"]. The two radio buttons are part of the same group of radio buttons because they have the same [name] attribute. The browser ensures that in a group of radio buttons, only one is checked at any given time. So clicking on one unchecks the one that was checked before;
  • lines 17-22: when the form is displayed, one of the radio buttons must be checked: to do so, it is enough to add the [checked] attribute to the relevant [<input type="radio">] tag. The ternary operator writes this attribute on the [Oui] button if [$modèle->marié] is [oui], on the [Non] button otherwise. Since the value written is a constant, there is nothing to escape. The PHP 7 course put into the model two variables [checkedOui] and [checkedNon] containing the text [checked="checked"] or an empty string;
  • lines 31-32: a numeric input field ([type="number"]) with a minimum value of 0 ([min="0"]). In current browsers, this means that the user will only be able to enter a number >= 0. Input can also be done with a spinner that can be clicked up or down. The attribute [step="1"] indicates that the spinner operates in steps of 1 unit: the spinner will only take integer values progressing from 0 to n with a step of 1. For manual input, this means that numbers with decimals will not be accepted. For some displays, the children input field will have to be prefilled with the last input made in this field: this is the role of the [value] attribute, whose value is provided by [$modèle->enfants];
  • lines 39-42: the same explanations apply to entering the salary as to entering the children. The help text under the input field has the [form-text] class; Bootstrap 4 used a [<small>] tag.

Dynamic elements: [$modèle->marié], [$modèle->enfants], [$modèle->salaire].

docs.title: 23.13.3.3. The [v-menu.php] fragment
docs.text:
This fragment displays a menu to the left of the tax calculation form. Its code is as follows:

<?php
// fragment : le menu de l'application
// modèle : [$modèle->optionsMenu] - un tableau [texte du lien => URL cible]
?>
<!-- menu Bootstrap : une liste verticale de liens -->
<nav class="nav flex-column">
    <?php foreach ($modèle->optionsMenu as $texte => $url): ?>
        <a class="nav-link" href="<?= htmlspecialchars($url) ?>"><?= htmlspecialchars($texte) ?></a>
    <?php endforeach ?>
</nav>

Comments

  • lines 6-10: the HTML [<nav>] tag surrounds a portion of the document presenting navigation links to other documents. The classes [nav, flex-column, nav-link] are Bootstrap classes that give the menu its appearance: a vertical list of links;
  • line 7: the fragment's model [$modèle->optionsMenu] is an array of the form [["Liste des simulations" => "main.php?action=lister-simulations", "Fin de session" => "main.php?action=fin-session"]];
  • line 8: the HTML [<a>] tag introduces a navigation link. [$url] is the URL navigated to when the link [$texte] is clicked. The browser then performs a [GET $url] operation. If [$url] is a relative URL, then it is completed with the path of the URL currently displayed by the browser. Thus, while the browser's current URL is of the type [http://chemin/main.php?paramètres], the link [Liste des simulations] (List of simulations) leads to [http://chemin/main.php?action=lister-simulations]. The text and the URL are escaped by [htmlspecialchars]: in a URL, the [&] character that separates the parameters must be written [&] in an HTML document.

docs.title: 23.13.3.5. Calculating the view model
docs.text:
Once the visual appearance of the view has been determined, we can proceed to calculate the view model under real conditions. The state codes that lead to this view are the codes [200, 300, 341, 350, 800] of the configuration. To find the meaning of these codes, we can use the [curl] tests carried out on the JSON application:

  • 200 is the state code after a successful [authentifier-utilisateur] action: we then present the empty tax calculation form;
  • 300 is the state code after a successful [calculer-impot] action. We then display the calculation form with the data entered in it and the amount of the tax. The user can then perform another calculation;
  • 341 is the state code obtained for a tax calculation with valid parameters when the lack of a connection to the DBMS causes an error;
  • 350 is the state code obtained for a tax calculation with valid parameters when the lack of a connection to the [Redis] server causes an error;
  • state code 800 will be presented later. We have not encountered it yet;
  • we assume here that the user is using a recent browser. Thus, with the form studied, it is not possible to type negative numbers, non-numeric character strings or decimal numbers in the input fields [enfants, salaire]. If these errors occur nevertheless (hand-made request), we will treat them as unexpected errors: we will then display the view [vue-erreurs.php].

Now that we know when the tax calculation form must be displayed, we can calculate its model in [vue-calcul-impot.php]:

<?php
// la vue du calcul de l'impôt - états [200, 300, 341, 350, 800]
// on hérite des variables [$request, $session, $config, $content] de la méthode [HtmlResponse::send]

// dépendances Symfony
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;

// on calcule le modèle de la vue
$modèle = getModelForThisView($request, $content);

function getModelForThisView(Request $request, array $content): stdClass
{
    $modèle = new stdClass();
    // état de l'application
    $état = $content["état"];
    // le formulaire : vide (200, 800) ou rétabli avec les valeurs saisies (300, 341, 350)
    $saisie = in_array($état, [300, 341, 350], true);
    $modèle->marié = $saisie ? $request->request->getString("marié") : "non";
    $modèle->enfants = $saisie ? $request->request->getString("enfants") : "";
    $modèle->salaire = $saisie ? $request->request->getString("salaire") : "";
    // réussite du calcul (300) : la réponse du contrôleur est un objet [Simulation]
    $modèle->résultats = [];
    if ($état === 300) {
        $simulation = $content["réponse"];
        $modèle->résultats = [
            "Montant de l'impôt : $simulation->impôt euros",
            "Décôte : $simulation->décôte euros",
            "Réduction : $simulation->réduction euros",
            "Surcôte : $simulation->surcôte euros",
            "Taux d'imposition : " . $simulation->taux * 100 . " %",
        ];
    }
    // échec du calcul (341 : base de données indisponible, 350 : Redis indisponible)
    $modèle->titreErreurs = "L'erreur suivante s'est produite :";
    $modèle->erreurs = in_array($état, [341, 350], true) ? [$content["réponse"]] : [];
    // le menu
    $modèle->optionsMenu = [
        "Liste des simulations" => "main.php?action=lister-simulations",
        "Fin de session" => "main.php?action=fin-session",
    ];
    // on rend le modèle
    return $modèle;
}
?>

Comments

  • line 17: for states 300, 341 and 350, the form is redisplayed with the entered values;
  • lines 18-20: the entered values are found in the posted parameters [$request->request]. For states 200 and 800, the form is empty, with the [Non] button checked;
  • lines 23-32: the case of a successful tax calculation. The controller's response [$content["réponse"]] is a [Simulation] object: we build the lines of the result from its attributes. The rate is displayed as a percentage. Since a simulation is an object, [$simulation->impôt] is interpolated directly into a double-quoted string;
  • line 35: the case of the failure of the tax calculation because the database or the [Redis] server is unavailable. The controller's response is then the error message;
  • lines 37-40: the two menu options.

docs.title: 23.13.4.3. Calculating the view model
docs.text:
The state codes that lead to the simulations view are the codes [500, 600] of the configuration:

  • 500 is the state code after a successful [lister-simulations] action: we then present the list of simulations performed by the user;

In both cases, the controller's response is the list of simulations. The view model is calculated in [vue-liste-simulations.php]:

function getModelForThisView(array $content): stdClass
{

    ];

?>

The PHP 7 script transformed each object into an associative array using the getters of the [Simulation] class: with public attributes, this is unnecessary;

docs.title: 23.13.5. The view of unexpected errors
docs.text:
Here we call an unexpected error an error that should not have occurred during normal use of the web application. Let us take as an example the following request, in a JSON session:

> curl -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=calculer-impot" -d "salaire=y"
{"action":"calculer-impot","état":337,"réponse":["paramètre [marié] manquant","paramètre [enfants] manquant","valeur [y] invalide pour le paramètre [salaire]"]}

The [marié] and [enfants] parameters are missing, the [salaire] parameter is invalid. Yet in the HTML form of the web application, this case cannot occur:

  • all the parameters are present;
  • the [marié] parameter, which takes its value from the [value] attributes of two radio buttons, necessarily has one of the values [oui] or [non];
  • with a recent browser, the attributes [<input type="number" min="0" step="1" …>] ensure that the inputs for the children and the salary are necessarily integers >= 0.

However, nothing prevents a user from sending such a request to our server in an HTML session, with [curl] or with their browser's developer tools. We will call an unexpected error an error that should not occur within the HTML application. If it does occur, someone is probably trying to "hack" the application. For teaching purposes, we have decided to display an error view in these cases. In reality, we could redisplay the last page sent to the client. To do so, it is enough to record in the session the last HTML response sent. In the event of an unexpected error, we send this response again. The user will thus have the impression that the server does not respond to their errors since the displayed page does not change.

It is the state codes absent from the [vues] key of the configuration file that cause the view of unexpected errors to be displayed. The code calculating the model of the view [vue-erreurs.php] is as follows:

<?php

function getModelForThisView(array $content): stdClass
{

            "Fin de session" => "main.php?action=fin-session",
        ],
    ];
}
?>
