</div>
  • line 9: the URL of the logo is relative to the URL of the displayed page, which is always that of the main controller [.../version-13/public/main.php]. The browser will therefore request the URL [.../version-13/public/Resources/logo.jpg].

docs.title: 24.4. The application's [.htaccess] file
docs.text:
With [Laragon], the document root of the [Apache] server ([DocumentRoot] directive) is the [www] folder. Everything under [www] can therefore be requested through a URL, and in particular the whole [version-13] folder. To forbid access to everything that is not in the [public] folder, we use a single [.htaccess] file, placed at the root of the application, in the [version-13] folder. Recall that the directives of an [.htaccess] file apply to the folder containing it and to all its subfolders. [Laragon] configures [Apache] so that it reads these files (directive [AllowOverride All]):

# version 13 : seul le dossier [public] de l'application est accessible par le web
# (Apache 2.4 - le module [mod_rewrite] doit être actif, ce qui est le cas avec Laragon)

# pas de liste du contenu des dossiers
Options -Indexes

# réécriture des URL : les motifs sont comparés au chemin de l'URL relatif au dossier [version-13]
RewriteEngine On
# l'URL du dossier de l'application [.../version-13/] est redirigée vers le dossier [public]
# %1 : le chemin de l'URL demandée, sans le / final, capturé par la condition [RewriteCond]
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_URI} ^(.*)/$
RewriteRule ^$ %1/public/ [R=302,L]
# toute autre URL qui ne désigne pas le dossier [public] ou l'un de ses fichiers est refusée (403 Forbidden)
RewriteRule !^public(/|$) - [F]

Comments

  • line 5: when a URL designates a folder that has no default document ([index.php], [index.html]), [Apache] may display the list of the folder's files. The [Options -Indexes] directive forbids it to do so;
  • line 8: we use [Apache]'s [mod_rewrite] module, the URL rewriting module, enabled by default in [Laragon]. A [RewriteRule] rule has the form [RewriteRule pattern substitution [options]]. In an [.htaccess] file, the pattern, a regular expression, is compared with the path of the requested URL relative to the folder of the [.htaccess] file. For the URL [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-13/Config/config.json], this path is [Config/config.json];
  • lines 11-12: the 1st rule handles the URL of the application's folder [.../version-13/], whose relative path is empty (pattern [^$]). It redirects the browser (option [R=302]) to the [public] folder and stops processing the rules (option [L], for "last"). The substitution must be a full URL path: it is obtained from [Apache]'s [REQUEST_URI] variable, the path of the requested URL [/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-13/]. The [RewriteCond] condition preceding the rule compares this variable with the regular expression [^(.*)/$]: the part between parentheses, the path without the final /, is then available in the rule under the name [%1]. Thus, the [.htaccess] file does not depend on the location of the application within the [www] folder;
  • line 14: the 2nd rule applies to any URL whose relative path does not start with [public/] and is not exactly [public]: that is the meaning of the [!] placed before the pattern. The substitution [-] means "no substitution" and the [F] option (for "forbidden") makes [Apache] respond with the code [403 Forbidden]. The URL [.../version-13/public], without the final /, must remain allowed: [Apache] (module [mod_dir]) responds to it with a redirection to [.../version-13/public/].

This file also forbids access to itself: it is not in the [public] folder. Since the path of a URL is normalized by [Apache] before the rules are applied, a URL such as [.../version-13/public/../Config/config.json] is also refused.

The PHP 7 course placed in each of the folders to be protected an [.htaccess] file containing the two lines [order deny,allow] and [deny from all]. This is the [Apache] 2.2 syntax. [Apache] 2.4 only accepts it thanks to the compatibility module [mod_access_compat], which is destined to disappear. The [Apache] 2.4 syntax is [Require all denied], which we have been using since version 8.

If we do not want to use the [mod_rewrite] module, a possible variant uses two [.htaccess] files and the [Require] syntax:

  • in the [version-13] folder, an [.htaccess] file containing the single line [Require all denied]: everything is forbidden;
  • in the [public] folder, an [.htaccess] file containing the single line [Require all granted]: the authorization directives of a subfolder replace those of the parent folder, and the entire content of [public] is allowed.

This variant also works, but the URL [.../version-13/] is then refused instead of being redirected to the [public] folder.

docs.title: 24.4.1. [curl] tests
docs.text:
The application's files outside the [public] folder are refused:

> curl -I http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-13/Config/config.json
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Server: Apache/2.4.58
Content-Type: text/html; charset=iso-8859-1

> curl -I http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-13/Views/vue-calcul-impot.php
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Server: Apache/2.4.58
Content-Type: text/html; charset=iso-8859-1

> curl -I http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-13/Logs/logs.txt
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Server: Apache/2.4.58
Content-Type: text/html; charset=iso-8859-1

The [403 Forbidden] code is that of the 2nd rule. Note that the [vue-calcul-impot.php] view was not even executed. The files of the [public] folder are served:

> curl -i "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-13/public/main.php?action=init-session&type=json"
HTTP/1.0 200 OK
Server: Apache/2.4.58
X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.11
Cache-Control: max-age=0, private, must-revalidate
Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID=cf229e8b3c335cdf3e9e94f7919e8f9f; path=/
Cache-Control: no-cache, private
Connection: close
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"action":"init-session","état":700,"réponse":"session démarrée avec type [json]"}

> curl -I http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-13/public/Resources/logo.jpg
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: Apache/2.4.58
Last-Modified: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 16:39:23 GMT
ETag: "1410-65cca0eef010c"
Accept-Ranges: bytes
Content-Length: 5136
Content-Type: image/jpeg
  • lines 1-11: the main controller responds normally: the JSON session is started;
  • lines 13-20: the logo is served (type [image/jpeg]).

Finally, the application's URL is redirected to the [public] folder, whose [index.php] script in turn redirects to the main controller:

> curl -I http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-13/
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Server: Apache/2.4.58
Location: http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-13/public/
Content-Type: text/html; charset=iso-8859-1

> curl -I http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-13/public/
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Server: Apache/2.4.58
X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.11
Location: main.php?action=init-session&type=html
Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8
  • line 4: the redirection by the 1st rule of the [.htaccess] file;
  • line 11: the redirection by the [public/index.php] script.

In a browser, the start URL of the HTML application becomes [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-13/]. After the two redirections, we get the authentication view, with its logo:

The application works like that of version 12. Here is the tax calculation view after a simulation:

The URLs of the JSON and XML clients' requests change: the main controller is now [.../version-13/public/main.php]. To use the version 12 JSON client with the version 13 server, it is enough to change the [urlServer] key in its configuration file.

docs.title: 24.5. In production: the document root is the [public] folder
docs.text:
The [.htaccess] file is a solution suited to [Laragon], where a single folder, [www], contains many applications. On a production server, things are done differently: the [public] folder is made the document root of the site. The rest of the application is then outside the website's tree: no URL can reach it, and no rule is needed. This is the organization recommended by PHP frameworks.

With [Apache], this is done by defining a virtual host, i.e. an additional website served by the same [Apache] server. The [Config/vhost-impots-v13.conf] file gives an example:

# un hôte virtuel Apache dont la racine des documents est le dossier [public] de la version 13
# à placer dans le dossier [<laragon>/etc/apache2/sites-enabled] (chemins à adapter)
# l'application est alors accessible à l'URL [http://localhost:8013/]
Listen 8013
<VirtualHost *:8013>
    # la racine des documents : seul le contenu de [public] est accessible par le web
    DocumentRoot "C:/laragon/www/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-13/public"
    <Directory "C:/laragon/www/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-13/public">
        # pas de fichier [.htaccess] à lire : la configuration est ici
        AllowOverride None
        Options -Indexes
        Require all granted
    </Directory>
</VirtualHost>
  • line 4: [Apache] also listens on port 8013. A virtual host can be distinguished from the others by its port, as here, or by its name ([impots.test] for example). Using the port avoids having to declare a new machine name;
  • lines 5-14: the configuration of the virtual host that responds to requests received on port 8013;
  • line 7: the document root of this site is the [public] folder of version 13. The URL [http://localhost:8013/main.php] therefore designates the file [public/main.php];
  • lines 8-13: the access rights to the [public] folder. [AllowOverride None] tells [Apache] that it does not need to look for [.htaccess] files: the whole configuration is here, which is also faster.

In [Laragon], such a file is placed, with its paths adapted to [Laragon]'s installation folder, in the [<laragon>/etc/apache2/sites-enabled] folder, then [Apache] is restarted from the [Laragon] window ([Stop] then [Start All] buttons). We then get:

> curl -I http://localhost:8013/
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Server: Apache/2.4.58
X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.11
Location: main.php?action=init-session&type=html
Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8

> curl "http://localhost:8013/main.php?action=init-session&type=json"
{"action":"init-session","état":700,"réponse":"session démarrée avec type [json]"}

> curl -I http://localhost:8013/Resources/logo.jpg
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: Apache/2.4.58
Last-Modified: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 16:39:23 GMT
ETag: "1410-65cca0eef010c"
Accept-Ranges: bytes
Content-Length: 5136
Content-Type: image/jpeg

> curl -I http://localhost:8013/Config/config.json
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Server: Apache/2.4.58
Content-Type: text/html; charset=iso-8859-1
  • lines 1-6: the site's URL is served by the [public/index.php] script;
  • lines 8-9: the main controller responds normally;
  • lines 11-18: the logo is served;
  • lines 20-23: the configuration file is no longer refused, it simply does not exist for the web server: the response is [404 Not Found]. The [.htaccess] file in the [version-13] folder is not read, since it is outside the document root.

In both cases, [Laragon] with the [.htaccess] file or a virtual host whose root is the [public] folder, the application's code is the same. That is the benefit of the new folder structure: what is public is gathered in a single folder, and everything else is protected by default.

docs.title: 8. Application exercise – version 3
docs.text:
We return to the exercise already studied previously (versions 1 and 2) in order to solve it with PHP code using classes. We are going to put into practice what we learned in the three previous chapters:

  • a [readonly] (immutable) class to represent the tax administration data;
  • an interface, an abstract class that partially implements it and a derived class that completes it;
  • a single exception type, [ExceptionImpots], to report all the application's errors;
  • the [#[\Override]] attribute on all methods that implement an interface method or override a parent method.

docs.title: 8.1. The script tree
docs.text:
Version 3 is in the [scripts-console/impots/version-03] folder:

version-03
├── AbstractBaseImpots.php
├── errors.txt
├── ExceptionImpots.php
├── ImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile.php
├── InterfaceImpots.php
├── main.php
├── resultats.txt
├── taxadmindata.json
├── TaxAdminData.php
├── taxpayersdata.txt
├── test-taxadmindata.php
└── Utilitaires.php

Each class or interface is in a file bearing its name. This is a convention universally followed in PHP (it is even imposed by the PSR-4 autoloading standard that we will meet with [Composer]).

docs.title: 8.2. The [ExceptionImpots] exception
docs.text:
In version 3, when a class constructor or method encounters an error, it will throw an exception of type [ExceptionImpots]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// l'exception lancée par les classes de l'application de calcul de l'impôt
class ExceptionImpots extends \RuntimeException
{
    // pas de code : le constructeur hérité de [\RuntimeException] suffit
    // __construct(string $message = "", int $code = 0, ?\Throwable $previous = null)
}

Comments

  • line 6: the [ExceptionImpots] class is in the [Application] namespace. All the classes and interfaces of the tax calculation application will be in this namespace;
  • line 9: the [ExceptionImpots] class extends PHP's predefined [RuntimeException] class. As we saw in the chapter on exceptions, an exception is useful first of all through its type: it is the type that lets you catch it with a [catch (ExceptionImpots $ex)] clause;
  • lines 11-12: the PHP 7 course defined a constructor [__construct(string $message, int $code = 0)] that merely called the parent class's constructor. It is useless: the class inherits the constructor of [RuntimeException], which accepts a message, an error code and an optional previous exception. This last parameter will let us wrap a low-level exception (a [JsonException], for example) in an [ExceptionImpots].

docs.title: 8.3. The [TaxAdminData] class
docs.text:
In version 2, the tax administration data were gathered:

  • first in a JSON file;
  • then from this JSON file into an associative array.

We had noted the flaw of this solution: nothing guarantees that the associative array contains all the expected keys, nor that the associated values are numbers. In version 3, the tax administration data are still in the [taxadmindata.json] file but with different attribute names, written according to the camelCase convention for class property names:

{
    "limites": [9964, 27519, 73779, 156244, 0],
    "coeffR": [0, 0.14, 0.3, 0.41, 0.45],
    "coeffN": [0, 1394.96, 5798, 13913.69, 20163.45],
    "plafondQfDemiPart": 1551,
    "plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction": 21037,
    "plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction": 42074,
    "valeurReducDemiPart": 3797,
    "plafondDecoteCelibataire": 1196,
    "plafondDecoteCouple": 1970,
    "plafondImpotCouplePourDecote": 2627,
    "plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote": 1595,
    "abattementDixPourcentMax": 12502,
    "abattementDixPourcentMin": 437
}

In version 2, this file was used to initialize an associative array. In version 3, it will initialize an object of the following [TaxAdminData] class:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// les données de l'administration fiscale : un objet immuable
final readonly class TaxAdminData
{
    // les noms des tableaux et des constantes attendus dans les données
    private const array TABLEAUX = ["limites", "coeffR", "coeffN"];
    private const array CONSTANTES = [
        "plafondQfDemiPart",
        "plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction",
        "plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction",
        "valeurReducDemiPart",
        "plafondDecoteCelibataire",
        "plafondDecoteCouple",
        "plafondImpotCouplePourDecote",
        "plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote",
        "abattementDixPourcentMax",
        "abattementDixPourcentMin",
    ];

    // constructeur privé : on passe obligatoirement par les méthodes [from...]
    private function __construct(
        // tranches d'impôt
        public array $limites,
        public array $coeffR,
        public array $coeffN,
        // constantes de calcul de l'impôt
        public float $plafondQfDemiPart,
        public float $plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction,
        public float $plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction,
        public float $valeurReducDemiPart,
        public float $plafondDecoteCelibataire,
        public float $plafondDecoteCouple,
        public float $plafondImpotCouplePourDecote,
        public float $plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote,
        public float $abattementDixPourcentMax,
        public float $abattementDixPourcentMin,
    ) {
    }

    // construction à partir d'un fichier JSON
    public static function fromJsonFile(string $taxAdminDataFilename): self
    {
        // on récupère le contenu du fichier des données fiscales
        $fileContents = is_readable($taxAdminDataFilename) ? file_get_contents($taxAdminDataFilename) : false;
        // erreur ?
        if ($fileContents === false) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Le fichier des données [$taxAdminDataFilename] n'existe pas", 1);
        }
        // on décode le JSON dans un tableau associatif
        try {
            $data = json_decode($fileContents, true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
        } catch (\JsonException $ex) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Le fichier de données JSON [$taxAdminDataFilename] n'a pu être exploité correctement", 2, $ex);
        }
        // le JSON doit être un objet {...}
        if (!is_array($data)) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Le fichier de données JSON [$taxAdminDataFilename] ne contient pas un objet JSON", 3);
        }
        // construction de l'objet à partir du tableau associatif
        return self::fromArray($data);
    }

    // construction à partir d'un tableau associatif [nom => valeur]
    public static function fromArray(array $data): self
    {
        // les clés présentes doivent être exactement celles attendues
        $attendues = [...self::TABLEAUX, ...self::CONSTANTES];
        $manquante = array_first(array_diff($attendues, array_keys($data)));
        if ($manquante !== null) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("L'attribut [$manquante] de [TaxAdminData] n'a pas été initialisé", 4);
        }
        $inconnue = array_first(array_diff(array_keys($data), $attendues));
        if ($inconnue !== null) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("L'attribut [$inconnue] n'existe pas dans [TaxAdminData]", 5);
        }
        // on vérifie et on convertit chaque valeur
        $valeurs = [];
        foreach (self::TABLEAUX as $clé) {
            // un tableau non vide de réels >= 0
            if (!is_array($data[$clé]) || !array_is_list($data[$clé]) || count($data[$clé]) === 0) {
                throw new ExceptionImpots("La valeur de l'attribut [$clé] est invalide", 6);
            }
            $valeurs[$clé] = array_map(fn(mixed $valeur): float => self::check($clé, $valeur), $data[$clé]);
        }
        // les trois tableaux doivent avoir la même taille
        $taille = count($valeurs["limites"]);
        if (count($valeurs["coeffR"]) !== $taille || count($valeurs["coeffN"]) !== $taille) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Les tableaux [limites, coeffR, coeffN] n'ont pas la même taille", 7);
        }
        foreach (self::CONSTANTES as $clé) {
            // un réel >= 0
            $valeurs[$clé] = self::check($clé, $data[$clé]);
        }
        // construction de l'objet : les clés du tableau deviennent des arguments nommés
        return new self(...$valeurs);
    }

    // vérifie qu'une valeur est un nombre réel positif ou nul et le rend sous forme de [float]
    private static function check(string $clé, mixed $value): float
    {
        // on accepte 1551, 1551.78, "1551" mais pas "xx", true, null, -3...
        if ((is_int($value) || is_float($value) || (is_string($value) && is_numeric($value)))
            && (float) $value >= 0) {
            return (float) $value;
        }
        throw new ExceptionImpots("La valeur de l'attribut [$clé] est invalide", 6);
    }

    // chaîne JSON de l'objet
    public function __toString(): string
    {
        return json_encode(get_object_vars($this), JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
    }
}

Comments

  • line 9: the class is [readonly]: all its properties are read-only. Once constructed, a [TaxAdminData] object can no longer be modified: it can be shared safely among all parts of the application. It is also [final]: it cannot be extended;
  • lines 12-24: two private class constants gather the names of the properties expected in the data. Since PHP 8.3, a class constant can be typed (here [array]);
  • lines 27-43: the constructor uses parameter promotion: each parameter becomes a public property with the same name and the same type. The properties have the names of the JSON file's keys. This is an important point that greatly simplifies writing the code, as we will see. The tax brackets are arrays ([array]), the calculation constants are reals ([float]). In PHP 7, properties could not be typed (the PHP 7 course regretted this): they can be since PHP 7.4;
  • line 27: the constructor is private: you cannot write [new TaxAdminData(...)] outside the class. A [TaxAdminData] object can only be obtained through the static methods [fromJsonFile] and [fromArray], which check the validity of the data. We are thus assured that every [TaxAdminData] object contains valid data. In PHP, a class can have only one constructor. Static methods that build an object, sometimes called "named constructors", provide several ways of building an object. The PHP 7 course used instance methods [setFromJsonFile] called on an empty object: [(new TaxAdminData())->setFromJsonFile(...)]. This is impossible with an immutable object;
  • lines 47-67: the [fromJsonFile] method builds a [TaxAdminData] object from the JSON file whose name is passed to it. Its return type [self] designates the class itself;
  • lines 50-53: we read the content of the file. If this is not possible, we throw an [ExceptionImpots] exception. It will propagate up to the main script;
  • lines 56-60: we decode the JSON content of the file. With the [JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR] option (PHP 7.3), the [json_decode] function throws a [JsonException] exception when the JSON is invalid, instead of silently returning [null]. Note the named argument [flags:], which avoids giving a value to the third parameter [depth] of [json_decode]. The [JsonException] exception is wrapped in an [ExceptionImpots]: the calling code has only one exception type to handle but can retrieve the original cause with [$ex->getPrevious()];
  • lines 62-64: a file containing, for example, only the number 12 is valid JSON: we must check that we did get an array;
  • line 66: the rest of the work is delegated to the [fromArray] method. This method is public: it can be used in a later version where the tax administration data will come from a database;
  • lines 73-81: we check that the keys of the [$data] array are exactly the expected names. [[...self::TABLEAUX, ...self::CONSTANTES]] creates an array containing the elements of both arrays. The [array_diff] function returns the elements of the first array that are absent from the second, and the [array_first] function (PHP 8.5) the first element of an array, or [null] if the array is empty. We thus detect a missing key and then an unknown key. This is the most frequent error: a typo in a property name in the [taxadmindata.json] file. In the PHP 7 course, the loop [$this->$key = $value] silently created a dynamic property bearing the wrong name. Since PHP 8.2, the creation of dynamic properties is deprecated, and it is forbidden in a [readonly] class;
  • lines 84-90: each of the three arrays must be a non-empty list ([array_is_list] function, PHP 8.1) all of whose elements are non-negative reals. The [array_map] function applies the [check] method to each of the elements;
  • lines 92-95: the three tax bracket arrays must have the same size;
  • lines 96-99: each of the calculation constants must be a non-negative real;
  • line 101: the [$valeurs] array has as keys the names of the constructor's parameters. The [...] operator applied to an array with string keys turns each element into a named argument (PHP 8.1): this line is equivalent to [new self(limites: $valeurs["limites"], coeffR: $valeurs["coeffR"], ...)]. This is where the choice of identical names for the JSON keys and the class properties simplifies the code;
  • lines 105-113: the [check] method checks that a value [$value] of unknown type ([mixed]) is a non-negative number. Depending on what is written in the JSON file, the value read may be an integer (1551), a real (1551.78), a string convertible to a number ("1551"), a non-convertible string ("xx"), a boolean... The [is_numeric] function returns [true] for a string representing a number. The PHP 7 course performed this check with a regular expression and returned a [stdClass] object indicating whether there had been an error. Here, an error causes an exception and the method simply returns the number as a [float];
  • line 116: the [__toString] method returns the JSON string of the object's properties. The [get_object_vars] function returns an associative array [property name => value].

docs.title: 8.3.1. Why are there no more getters and setters?
docs.text:
The PHP 7 course declared the properties private and wrote a getter and a setter for each of them (26 methods), generated automatically by the NetBeans IDE. The setters were "fluent": they returned the [$this] object, which made it possible to chain calls [$data->setLimites($limites)->setCoeffR($coeffR)].

With PHP 8, this code no longer has any reason to exist:

  • getters were used to read private properties. [readonly] properties can safely be public since they cannot be modified: we write [$taxAdminData->plafondQfDemiPart] instead of [$taxAdminData->getPlafondQfDemiPart()];
  • setters were used to initialize the object and allowed values to be checked. An immutable object is initialized once and for all by its constructor, and the checking is done by the [fromJsonFile] and [fromArray] methods;
  • typed properties guarantee the type of values. The PHP 7 course noted that the statement [$this->plafondQfDemiPart = 'abcd'] was possible: with a [float] property and [declare(strict_types=1)], it causes a [TypeError] error.

The [test-taxadmindata.php] script checks how the [TaxAdminData] class works:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres et des résultats des fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// inclusion des classes
require_once __DIR__ . "/ExceptionImpots.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/TaxAdminData.php";

// un objet valide
$taxAdminData = TaxAdminData::fromJsonFile("taxadmindata.json");
print "$taxAdminData\n";
print "plafondQfDemiPart=" . $taxAdminData->plafondQfDemiPart . "\n";
// l'objet est immuable
try {
    $taxAdminData->plafondQfDemiPart = 2000;
} catch (\Error $ex) {
    print $ex::class . " : " . $ex->getMessage() . "\n";
}
// le constructeur est privé
try {
    $taxAdminData = new TaxAdminData([], [], []);
} catch (\Error $ex) {
    print $ex::class . " : " . $ex->getMessage() . "\n";
}

// des données incorrectes
$valides = json_decode(file_get_contents("taxadmindata.json"), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
$tests = [
    // fichier inexistant
    fn() => TaxAdminData::fromJsonFile("xx.json"),
    // fichier qui n'est pas du JSON
    fn() => TaxAdminData::fromJsonFile("taxpayersdata.txt"),
    // clé manquante
    fn() => TaxAdminData::fromArray(array_diff_key($valides, ["plafondQfDemiPart" => 0])),
    // clé inconnue (faute de frappe)
    fn() => TaxAdminData::fromArray(["plafondQFDemiPart" => 1551] + $valides),
    // valeur non numérique
    fn() => TaxAdminData::fromArray(["plafondQfDemiPart" => "xx"] + $valides),
    // valeur négative dans un tableau
    fn() => TaxAdminData::fromArray(["coeffR" => [0, 0.14, -0.3, 0.41, 0.45]] + $valides),
    // tableaux de tailles différentes
    fn() => TaxAdminData::fromArray(["limites" => [9964, 27519, 73779, 0]] + $valides),
];
foreach ($tests as $test) {
    try {
        $test();
    } catch (ExceptionImpots $ex) {
        print "ExceptionImpots n° {$ex->getCode()} : {$ex->getMessage()}\n";
    }
}
// une valeur "1551" est acceptée et convertie en réel
$taxAdminData = TaxAdminData::fromArray(["plafondQfDemiPart" => "1551"] + $valides);
var_dump($taxAdminData->plafondQfDemiPart);

Comments

  • line 14: construction of a valid [TaxAdminData] object from the [taxadmindata.json] file;
  • line 15: the object is inserted into a string: its [__toString] method is called;
  • line 19: attempt to modify a read-only property;
  • line 25: attempt to use the private constructor;
  • line 31: the associative array of valid data;
  • lines 32-47: an array of arrow functions, each building a [TaxAdminData] object from incorrect data. The incorrect data are obtained by modifying a copy of the [$valides] array. With the [+] operator on two arrays, it is the elements of the left-hand array that win in case of a common key. The [array_diff_key] function returns the first array minus the keys present in the second;
  • lines 48-54: each function is executed and the expected exception is displayed;
  • line 56: a numeric string is accepted and converted to a real.

Results:

> php test-taxadmindata.php
{"limites":[9964,27519,73779,156244,0],"coeffR":[0,0.14,0.3,0.41,0.45],"coeffN":[0,1394.96,5798,13913.69,20163.45],"plafondQfDemiPart":1551,"plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction":21037,"plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction":42074,"valeurReducDemiPart":3797,"plafondDecoteCelibataire":1196,"plafondDecoteCouple":1970,"plafondImpotCouplePourDecote":2627,"plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote":1595,"abattementDixPourcentMax":12502,"abattementDixPourcentMin":437}
plafondQfDemiPart=1551
Error : Cannot modify readonly property Application\TaxAdminData::$plafondQfDemiPart
Error : Call to private Application\TaxAdminData::__construct() from global scope
ExceptionImpots n° 1 : Le fichier des données [xx.json] n'existe pas
ExceptionImpots n° 2 : Le fichier de données JSON [taxpayersdata.txt] n'a pu être exploité correctement
ExceptionImpots n° 4 : L'attribut [plafondQfDemiPart] de [TaxAdminData] n'a pas été initialisé
ExceptionImpots n° 5 : L'attribut [plafondQFDemiPart] n'existe pas dans [TaxAdminData]
ExceptionImpots n° 6 : La valeur de l'attribut [plafondQfDemiPart] est invalide
ExceptionImpots n° 6 : La valeur de l'attribut [coeffR] est invalide
ExceptionImpots n° 7 : Les tableaux [limites, coeffR, coeffN] n'ont pas la même taille
float(1551)
  • line 2: the JSON string of the object. Note that reals without a fractional part (1551.0) are written without it (1551) by the [json_encode] function;
  • lines 4-5: the two [Error] errors caused by modifying a [readonly] property and by calling a private constructor. These are programming errors, not data errors: they are not turned into [ExceptionImpots];
  • lines 6-12: all the incorrect data are detected, each with a different message and error code;
  • line 13: the string "1551" has been converted to a real.

docs.title: 8.4. The [InterfaceImpots] interface
docs.text:
We now define the following [InterfaceImpots] interface [InterfaceImpots.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

interface InterfaceImpots
{
    // récupérer les données de l'administration fiscale permettant le calcul de l'impôt
    // peut lancer l'exception ExceptionImpots
    public function getTaxAdminData(): TaxAdminData;

    // l'interface sait calculer un impôt
    public function calculerImpot(string $marié, int $enfants, int $salaire): array;

    // l'interface sait exploiter des données dans des fichiers texte
    // $taxPayersFileName : fichier des données contribuables sous la forme statut marital, nombre d'enfants, salaire annuel
    // $resultsFileName : fichier des résultats sous la forme statut marital, nombre d'enfants, salaire annuel, montant de l'impôt...
    // $errorsFileName : fichier des erreurs rencontrées
    // peut lancer l'exception ExceptionImpots
    public function executeBatchImpots(string $taxPayersFileName, string $resultsFileName, string $errorsFileName): void;
}

Comments

  • line 8: the interface for calculating taxes. It too is in the [Application] namespace;
  • line 12: the [getTaxAdminData] method will acquire the tax administration data into an object of the [TaxAdminData] type that we have just presented. Since these data may be in a file, a database or even on the network, the [getTaxAdminData] method may fail to obtain the data. In that case, it will throw an exception of type [ExceptionImpots]. This is the standard way in object-oriented programming to report an error encountered in a method or a constructor;
  • line 15: the [calculerImpot] method will calculate the tax of a taxpayer;
  • line 22: the [executeBatchImpots] method will calculate the tax of several taxpayers:
    • [$taxPayersFileName] is the name of the text file containing the taxpayers' data;
    • [$resultsFileName] is the name of the text file containing the amount of tax for these taxpayers;
    • [$errorsFileName] is the name of the text file containing the errors encountered while processing these files.

The content of the taxpayers' text file [taxpayersdata.txt] is as follows:

oui,2,55555
oui,2,50000
oui,3,50000
non,2,100000
non,3x,100000
non,3,100000
oui,3,100000
oui,5,100000x
oui,5,100000
non,0,100000
oui,2,30000
non,0,200000
oui,3,200000

Note that lines 5 and 8 contain erroneous elements. The other eleven lines are the eleven taxpayers of the table of official figures.

docs.title: 8.5. The [Utilitaires] class
docs.text:
We also define a [Utilitaires] class in a [Utilitaires.php] file:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// une classe de fonctions utilitaires : elle n'est ni instanciable, ni dérivable
final class Utilitaires
{
    // constructeur privé : la classe ne peut être instanciée
    private function __construct()
    {
    }

    public static function cutNewLineChar(string $ligne): string
    {
        // on supprime la marque de fin de ligne de $ligne si elle existe
        // (\r\n sous Windows, \n sous Unix)
        return rtrim($ligne, "\r\n");
    }
}

Comments

  • line 9: the [Utilitaires] class is also placed in the [Application] namespace. It contains only static methods: there is no reason to instantiate it or to extend it. The PHP 7 course declared it abstract to prevent its instantiation, regretting that PHP refuses to declare it both [final] and [abstract]. This is still the case. Today's practice is to declare it [final] (not extendable) and to give it a private constructor (not instantiable from outside);
  • line 16: the [cutNewLineChar] method removes the possible end-of-line mark from the text passed to it as a parameter. It is a static method, which means it will be called in the form [Utilitaires::cutNewLineChar($ligne)]. Its code is that of the function of the same name in version 2.

docs.title: 8.6. The [AbstractBaseImpots] abstract class
docs.text:
The [InterfaceImpots] interface will be implemented by the following abstract class [AbstractBaseImpots] [AbstractBaseImpots.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// une classe abstraite qui implémente l'interface [InterfaceImpots]
abstract class AbstractBaseImpots implements InterfaceImpots
{
    // les données de l'administration fiscale
    private ?TaxAdminData $taxAdminData = null;

    // données nécessaires au calcul de l'impôt : les classes dérivées savent où les trouver
    #[\Override]
    abstract public function getTaxAdminData(): TaxAdminData;

    // calcul de l'impôt
    // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[\Override]
    public function calculerImpot(string $marié, int $enfants, int $salaire): array
    {
        // $marié : oui, non
        // $enfants : nombre d'enfants
        // $salaire : salaire annuel
        // $this->taxAdminData : données de l'administration fiscale
        //
        // on récupère les données de l'administration fiscale si ce n'est déjà fait
        $this->taxAdminData ??= $this->getTaxAdminData();
        // calcul de l'impôt avec enfants
        $result1 = $this->calculerImpot2($marié, $enfants, $salaire);
        $impot1 = $result1["impôt"];
        // calcul de l'impôt sans les enfants
        if ($enfants !== 0) {
            $result2 = $this->calculerImpot2($marié, 0, $salaire);
            $impot2 = $result2["impôt"];
            // application du plafonnement du quotient familial
            $plafondDemiPart = $this->taxAdminData->plafondQfDemiPart;
            if ($enfants < 3) {
                // plafondQfDemiPart euros pour les 2 premiers enfants
                $impot2 = $impot2 - $enfants * $plafondDemiPart;
            } else {
                // plafondQfDemiPart euros pour les 2 premiers enfants, le double pour les suivants
                $impot2 = $impot2 - 2 * $plafondDemiPart - ($enfants - 2) * 2 * $plafondDemiPart;
            }
        } else {
            $impot2 = $impot1;
            $result2 = $result1;
        }
        // on prend l'impôt le plus fort avec le taux et la surcôte qui vont avec
        if ($impot1 > $impot2) {
            $impot = $impot1;
            $taux = $result1["taux"];
            $surcôte = $result1["surcôte"];
        } else {
            $surcôte = $impot2 - $impot1 + $result2["surcôte"];
            $impot = $impot2;
            $taux = $result2["taux"];
        }
        // calcul d'une éventuelle décôte
        $décôte = $this->getDecote($marié, $salaire, $impot);
        $impot -= $décôte;
        // calcul d'une éventuelle réduction d'impôts
        $réduction = $this->getRéduction($marié, $salaire, $enfants, $impot);
        $impot -= $réduction;
        // résultat
        return [
            "impôt" => (int) floor($impot),
            "surcôte" => (int) $surcôte,
            "décôte" => (int) $décôte,
            "réduction" => (int) $réduction,
            "taux" => $taux,
        ];
    }

Comments

  • line 9: the [AbstractBaseImpots] class implements the [InterfaceImpots] interface;
  • line 12: the tax administration data will be placed in the private property [$taxAdminData]. Its type [?TaxAdminData] means "a [TaxAdminData] object or the value [null]". Its initial value is [null];
  • line 16: the [getTaxAdminData] method of the interface. We do not yet know how to define it: we have seen one case where the tax administration data were taken from a JSON file (version 2). We will see another case where the data will have to be fetched from a database. It will be up to the derived classes to define the content of the [getTaxAdminData] method. The method is therefore declared abstract, which forces the class itself to be declared abstract. This declaration is optional: an abstract class that implements an interface is not required to redeclare the methods it does not implement. It does, however, make the code more readable. The [#[\Override]] attribute (PHP 8.3) indicates that the method is that of an interface or of a parent class: if we get its name wrong, PHP reports the error;
  • lines 21-73: the tax calculation function already encountered in versions 1 and 2. Its parameters have changed: version 2 received the associative array [$taxAdminData] as its first parameter, version 3 uses the [$this->taxAdminData] property. The 1st difference between these two solutions is a difference in the visibility of the tax data:
    • in version 2, the associative array [$taxAdminData] did not have global visibility. It was therefore passed as a parameter to all the tax calculation functions;
    • in version 3, the [$this->taxAdminData] property is visible in all the methods of the class. It is therefore no longer passed as a parameter;
  • a second difference comes from the fact that version 3 replaces functions with class methods. Each method call is now made with an expression [$this->méthode(...)] (line 31, line 61);
  • line 29: a third difference is that when the [calculerImpot] method starts its work, it does not know whether the [$taxAdminData] property it needs has been initialized. Indeed, the class has no constructor that would initialize it. It is therefore up to the [calculerImpot] method to do so with the help of the [getTaxAdminData] method. The [??=] operator (PHP 7.4) assigns the right-hand value to the left-hand variable only if the latter is [null]. The line is equivalent to [if ($this->taxAdminData === null) { $this->taxAdminData = $this->getTaxAdminData(); }];
  • line 38: the tax administration data are read directly from the public read-only properties of the [TaxAdminData] object;
  • apart from these differences, the tax calculation method remains what it was in the previous versions.

The private tax calculation methods are as follows:

    // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    private function calculerImpot2(string $marié, int $enfants, float $salaire): array
    {
        // nombre de parts
        $nbParts = match ($marié) {
            "oui" => $enfants / 2 + 2,
            "non" => $enfants / 2 + 1,
        };
        // 1 part par enfant à partir du 3e
        if ($enfants >= 3) {
            // une demi-part de + pour chaque enfant à partir du 3e
            $nbParts += 0.5 * ($enfants - 2);
        }
        // revenu imposable
        $revenuImposable = $this->getRevenuImposable($salaire);
        // surcôte
        $surcôte = floor($revenuImposable - 0.9 * $salaire);
        // pour des pbs d'arrondi
        if ($surcôte < 0) {
            $surcôte = 0;
        }
        // quotient familial
        $quotient = $revenuImposable / $nbParts;
        // les tranches d'imposition (des copies des tableaux de l'objet)
        $limites = $this->taxAdminData->limites;
        $coeffR = $this->taxAdminData->coeffR;
        $coeffN = $this->taxAdminData->coeffN;
        // est mis à la fin du tableau limites pour arrêter la boucle qui suit
        $limites[count($limites) - 1] = $quotient;
        // calcul de l'impôt
        $i = 0;
        while ($quotient > $limites[$i]) {
            $i++;
        }
        // maintenant on peut calculer l'impôt
        $impôt = floor($revenuImposable * $coeffR[$i] - $nbParts * $coeffN[$i]);
        // résultat
        return ["impôt" => $impôt, "surcôte" => $surcôte, "taux" => $coeffR[$i]];
    }

    // revenuImposable=salaireAnnuel-abattement
    // l'abattement a un min et un max
    private function getRevenuImposable(float $salaire): float
    {
        // abattement de 10% du salaire, borné par un minimum et un maximum
        $abattement = 0.1 * $salaire;
        $abattement = min($abattement, $this->taxAdminData->abattementDixPourcentMax);
        $abattement = max($abattement, $this->taxAdminData->abattementDixPourcentMin);
        // revenu imposable
        $revenuImposable = $salaire - $abattement;
        // résultat
        return floor($revenuImposable);
    }

    // calcule une décôte éventuelle
    private function getDecote(string $marié, float $salaire, float $impots): float
    {
        // au départ, une décôte nulle
        $décôte = 0;
        // montant maximal d'impôt pour avoir la décôte
        $plafondImpôtPourDécôte = $marié === "oui"
            ? $this->taxAdminData->plafondImpotCouplePourDecote
            : $this->taxAdminData->plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote;
        if ($impots < $plafondImpôtPourDécôte) {
            // montant maximal de la décôte
            $plafondDécôte = $marié === "oui"
                ? $this->taxAdminData->plafondDecoteCouple
                : $this->taxAdminData->plafondDecoteCelibataire;
            // décôte théorique
            $décôte = $plafondDécôte - 0.75 * $impots;
            // la décôte ne peut dépasser le montant de l'impôt
            if ($décôte > $impots) {
                $décôte = $impots;
            }
            // pas de décôte < 0
            if ($décôte < 0) {
                $décôte = 0;
            }
        }
        // résultat
        return ceil($décôte);
    }

    // calcule une réduction éventuelle
    private function getRéduction(string $marié, float $salaire, int $enfants, float $impots): float
    {
        // le plafond des revenus pour avoir droit à la réduction de 20%
        $plafondRevenuPourRéduction = $marié === "oui"
            ? $this->taxAdminData->plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction
            : $this->taxAdminData->plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction;
        $plafondRevenuPourRéduction += $enfants * $this->taxAdminData->valeurReducDemiPart;
        if ($enfants > 2) {
            $plafondRevenuPourRéduction += ($enfants - 2) * $this->taxAdminData->valeurReducDemiPart;
        }
        // revenu imposable
        $revenuImposable = $this->getRevenuImposable($salaire);
        // réduction
        $réduction = 0;
        if ($revenuImposable < $plafondRevenuPourRéduction) {
            // réduction de 20%
            $réduction = 0.2 * $impots;
        }
        // résultat
        return ceil($réduction);
    }

Comments

  • lines 80-83: the [match] expression (PHP 8.0) is an advantageous replacement for the [if / else] of version 2. It compares the value [$marié] with the values of its arms using the identity operator [===] and returns the value of the matching arm. If no arm matches, it throws an [UnhandledMatchError] error: a marital status other than "oui" or "non" will not go unnoticed;
  • lines 100-102: the tax bracket arrays are copied into local variables. In PHP, assigning an array creates a copy: modifying [$limites] at line 104 does not affect the [readonly] property of the [TaxAdminData] object (which would in any case be an error);
  • lines 122-123: the [min] and [max] functions replace the two [if] statements of version 2: the allowance can neither exceed [abattementDixPourcentMax] nor be less than [abattementDixPourcentMin];
  • the rest of the code is that of version 2, where the expression [$taxAdminData["PLAFOND_DECOTE_COUPLE"]] has become [$this->taxAdminData->plafondDecoteCouple]. A typo in a property name is now reported by the [VS Code] editor ([PHP Intelephense] extension) as soon as the code is written, which was not the case for a typo in an array key.

The [executeBatchImpots] method is as follows:

    // calcul de l'impôt en mode batch
    // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[\Override]
    public function executeBatchImpots(string $taxPayersFileName, string $resultsFileName, string $errorsFileName): void
    {
        // les trois fichiers ne sont pas encore ouverts
        $errors = $results = $data = false;
        // pas mal d'erreurs peuvent se produire dès qu'on gère des fichiers
        try {
            // ouverture du fichier des erreurs
            $errors = fopen($errorsFileName, "w");
            if ($errors === false) {
                throw new ExceptionImpots("Impossible de créer le fichier des erreurs [$errorsFileName]", 10);
            }
            // ouverture du fichier des résultats
            $results = fopen($resultsFileName, "w");
            if ($results === false) {
                throw new ExceptionImpots("Impossible de créer le fichier des résultats [$resultsFileName]", 11);
            }
            // ouverture du fichier des données contribuables
            $data = is_readable($taxPayersFileName) ? fopen($taxPayersFileName, "r") : false;
            if ($data === false) {
                throw new ExceptionImpots("Impossible d'ouvrir en lecture les déclarations des contribuables [$taxPayersFileName]", 12);
            }
            // on exploite la ligne courante du fichier des données contribuables
            // qui a la forme statut marital, nombre d'enfants, salaire annuel
            $num = 0;         // n° ligne courante
            $nbErreurs = 0;   // nbre d'erreurs rencontrées
            while (($ligne = fgets($data, 100)) !== false) {
                // une ligne de plus
                $num++;
                // on enlève l'éventuelle marque de fin de ligne
                $ligne = Utilitaires::cutNewLineChar($ligne);
                // on ignore les lignes vides
                if (trim($ligne) === "") {
                    continue;
                }
                // la ligne doit avoir 3 champs marié,enfants,salaire
                $champs = array_map(trim(...), explode(",", $ligne));
                $erreur = count($champs) !== 3;
                if (!$erreur) {
                    [$marié, $enfants, $salaire] = $champs;
                    // le statut marital doit être oui ou non
                    $marié = strtolower($marié);
                    // le nombre d'enfants et le salaire doivent être des entiers positifs ou nuls
                    $erreur = !in_array($marié, ["oui", "non"], true)
                        || !preg_match('/^\d+$/', $enfants)
                        || !preg_match('/^\d+$/', $salaire);
                }
                // erreur ?
                if ($erreur) {
                    fputs($errors, "la ligne [$num] du fichier [$taxPayersFileName] est erronée\n");
                    $nbErreurs++;
                    continue;
                }
                // on calcule l'impôt
                $result = $this->calculerImpot($marié, (int) $enfants, (int) $salaire);
                // on inscrit le résultat dans le fichier des résultats
                $result = ["marié" => $marié, "enfants" => (int) $enfants, "salaire" => (int) $salaire] + $result;
                fputs($results, json_encode($result, JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR) . "\n");
            }
            // des erreurs ?
            if ($nbErreurs > 0) {
                throw new ExceptionImpots("Il y a eu $nbErreurs ligne(s) erronée(s) : voir le fichier [$errorsFileName]", 15);
            }
        } finally {
            // on ferme les fichiers qui ont été ouverts
            foreach ([$data, $results, $errors] as $fichier) {
                if ($fichier !== false) {
                    fclose($fichier);
                }
            }
        }
    }

Comments on the code

  • line 185: the method receives three parameters:
    • [$taxPayersFileName]: the name of the text file containing the taxpayers' data. Each line of text contains the data of one taxpayer in the form: marital status (oui / non), number of children, annual salary, for example [oui,2,55555];
    • [$resultsFileName]: the name of the text file that will contain the results. Each line of text will be the JSON string of one taxpayer's results, for example [{"marié":"oui","enfants":2,"salaire":50000,"impôt":1384,"surcôte":0,"décôte":384,"réduction":347,"taux":0.14}];
    • [$errorsFileName]: the name of the errors text file, for example [la ligne [5] du fichier [taxpayersdata.txt] est erronée] (meaning that line 5 of the file is erroneous);
  • line 188: the variables of the three files are initialized to [false] (file not open). This will let us know, in the [finally] clause, which files have been opened;
  • line 190: because a number of operations may throw an exception, a [try / finally] structure surrounds all the code of the method;
  • lines 192-204: the three files are opened. An exception is thrown as soon as an opening fails, with a different error code for each case;
  • line 210: the lines of the [$data] file are read one by one, at most 100 characters at a time (all lines are shorter than 100 characters);
  • line 214: we use the static method [Utilitaires::cutNewLineChar] to remove the possible end-of-line mark;
  • lines 216-218: empty lines (for example at the end of the file) are ignored;
  • line 220: we split the line on the comma and remove the spaces surrounding each field. [trim(...)] is the "first-class callable" syntax (PHP 8.1): it designates the [trim] function itself, without calling it;
  • line 221: the line must have exactly three fields. The PHP 7 course wrote directly [list($marié, $enfants, $salaire) = explode(",", $ligne)]: with a line having only two fields, PHP 8 emits an "Undefined array key 2" warning;
  • lines 227-229: the validity of the three elements is checked: the marital status must be oui or non, the number of children and the salary must be non-negative integers (a sequence of digits, regular expression [/^\d+$/]). The third parameter [true] of [in_array] requests a strict [===] comparison;
  • lines 232-236: we do not throw an exception if the line is erroneous; instead we write an error message to the [$errors] text file and move on to the next line;
  • line 238: if the line read is valid, the tax calculation is performed. We get a result in the form of an associative array [impôt, surcôte, décôte, réduction, taux];
  • line 240: to the result obtained, we prepend the keys [marié, enfants, salaire];
  • line 241: the result is written to the [$results] text file as its JSON string. The [JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR] option makes the [json_encode] function throw a [JsonException] exception rather than return [false] if encoding fails;
  • lines 244-246: at the end of processing the [$data] file, we look at the number of erroneous lines encountered. If there is at least one, we throw an exception;
  • lines 247-254: whatever the way the execution of the method ends (normally or through an exception), the [finally] clause is executed: the files that were opened are closed. The PHP 7 course used a [try / catch / finally] structure whose [catch] clause merely rethrew the exception. It is useless: a [try / finally] structure without [catch] lets the exception propagate after executing the [finally] clause. Moreover, the PHP 7 course closed the three files without checking that they had been opened: in PHP 8, [fclose(false)] causes a [TypeError] error.

docs.title: 8.7. The [ImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile] class
docs.text:
The abstract class [AbstractBaseImpots] does not implement the [getTaxAdminData] method of the [InterfaceImpots] interface. We must therefore define it in a derived class. We do so in the following derived class [ImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// une classe qui prend les données de l'administration fiscale dans un fichier JSON
class ImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile extends AbstractBaseImpots
{
    // les données de l'administration fiscale
    private readonly TaxAdminData $taxAdminData;

    // le constructeur
    public function __construct(string $jsonFileName)
    {
        // on initialise $this->taxAdminData à partir du fichier JSON
        // peut lancer une exception ExceptionImpots
        $this->taxAdminData = TaxAdminData::fromJsonFile($jsonFileName);
    }

    // rend les données permettant le calcul de l'impôt
    #[\Override]
    public function getTaxAdminData(): TaxAdminData
    {
        return $this->taxAdminData;
    }
}

Comments

  • line 9: the [ImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile] class extends the abstract class [AbstractBaseImpots]. It must define the [getTaxAdminData] method that its parent class did not define;
  • line 12: the [$taxAdminData] property will contain the tax administration data. It is read-only: it is initialized once and for all by the constructor. Note that the parent class also has a private property [$taxAdminData]: the two properties are distinct, since a private property is visible only in the class that declares it;
  • lines 15-20: the constructor receives as its only parameter the name of the JSON file containing the tax data;
  • line 19: an object of type [TaxAdminData] is created from the JSON file. This operation may throw an exception of type [ExceptionImpots]. It will propagate up to the main script [main.php];
  • lines 23-27: we give a body to the [getTaxAdminData] method that the parent class had not defined. Here, it suffices to return the [$this->taxAdminData] property initialized by the constructor.

docs.title: 8.8. The [main.php] script
docs.text:
These classes and interface are used by the following [main.php] script:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres et des résultats des fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// inclusion des interfaces et classes
require_once __DIR__ . "/ExceptionImpots.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/TaxAdminData.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/Utilitaires.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/InterfaceImpots.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/AbstractBaseImpots.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/ImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile.php";

// définition des constantes
const TAXPAYERSDATA_FILENAME = "taxpayersdata.txt";
const RESULTS_FILENAME = "resultats.txt";
const ERRORS_FILENAME = "errors.txt";
const TAXADMINDATA_FILENAME = "taxadmindata.json";

try {
    // on crée un objet [ImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile]
    $impots = new ImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile(TAXADMINDATA_FILENAME);
    // on exécute le batch des impôts
    $impots->executeBatchImpots(TAXPAYERSDATA_FILENAME, RESULTS_FILENAME, ERRORS_FILENAME);
} catch (ExceptionImpots $ex) {
    // on affiche l'erreur
    print "Erreur n° {$ex->getCode()} : {$ex->getMessage()}\n";
}
// fin
print "Terminé\n";

Comments

  • line 4: we enforce strict compliance with the types of function parameters;
  • line 7: the [main.php] script is also placed in the [Application] namespace;
  • lines 10-15: we load the files of the classes and interfaces used by the script. Note that here we have not used a [use] statement to declare the fully qualified name of the classes used by the script. It is indeed unnecessary because the script and the classes are in the same [Application] namespace. Note also the loading order: a parent class or an interface must be loaded before the class that extends or implements it;
  • lines 18-21: the names of the files used in the script. These names are relative: the files are looked for in the current folder, the one from which the script is executed;
  • line 25: an [ImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile] object is created. This may cause an exception if the JSON file is missing or incorrect;
  • line 27: we execute the [executeBatchImpots] method, which will calculate the taxes for all the taxpayers in the [TAXPAYERSDATA_FILENAME] file. The results will be put in the [RESULTS_FILENAME] file and any errors in the [ERRORS_FILENAME] file;
  • lines 28-31: in case of error, we display the error's code and message. The expression [{$ex->getCode()}] lets you insert the result of a method call into a string.
