docs.title: 4.3.3. Conclusion
docs.text: The tax calculation algorithm, even in supposedly simple cases, is complex. We will not come back to it. Over the versions, its core will remain the same despite a few changes in presentation. We will then comment only on the latter.

docs.title: 4.4.1. The changes
docs.text:
In the previous version, the data needed to calculate the tax were hard-coded in the form of constants and arrays. This method is to be avoided. In the new version, these data are externalized in the JSON file [taxadmindata.json] placed next to the script:

version-02
├── main.php
├── resultats.txt
├── taxadmindata.json
└── taxpayersdata.txt

The content of the file [taxadmindata.json] is as follows:

{
    "limites": [9964, 27519, 73779, 156244, 0],
    "coeffR": [0, 0.14, 0.3, 0.41, 0.45],
    "coeffN": [0, 1394.96, 5798, 13913.69, 20163.45],
    "PLAFOND_QF_DEMI_PART": 1551,
    "PLAFOND_REVENUS_CELIBATAIRE_POUR_REDUCTION": 21037,
    "PLAFOND_REVENUS_COUPLE_POUR_REDUCTION": 42074,
    "VALEUR_REDUC_DEMI_PART": 3797,
    "PLAFOND_DECOTE_CELIBATAIRE": 1196,
    "PLAFOND_DECOTE_COUPLE": 1970,
    "PLAFOND_IMPOT_COUPLE_POUR_DECOTE": 2627,
    "PLAFOND_IMPOT_CELIBATAIRE_POUR_DECOTE": 1595,
    "ABATTEMENT_DIXPOURCENT_MAX": 12502,
    "ABATTEMENT_DIXPOURCENT_MIN": 437
}

It contains the three arrays [limites, coeffR, coeffN] and the constants of version 1, with the same names.

The new version [version-02/main.php] is as follows (the functions that are not shown have the same code as in version 1, apart from the [$taxAdminData] parameter):

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres et des résultats des fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// définition des constantes
$TAXPAYERSDATA = "taxpayersdata.txt";
$RESULTATS = "resultats.txt";
$TAXADMINDATA = "taxadmindata.json";

// on récupère le contenu du fichier des données fiscales
$fileContents = is_readable($TAXADMINDATA) ? file_get_contents($TAXADMINDATA) : false;
$erreur = false;
$message = "";
// erreur ?
if ($fileContents === false) {
    // on note l'erreur
    $erreur = true;
    $message = "Le fichier des données [$TAXADMINDATA] n'existe pas";
}

if (!$erreur) {
    // le contenu du fichier est-il du JSON valide ?
    if (json_validate($fileContents)) {
        // on récupère le code JSON du fichier des données fiscales dans un tableau associatif
        $taxAdminData = json_decode($fileContents, true);
    } else {
        // on note l'erreur
        $erreur = true;
        $message = "Le fichier de données JSON [$TAXADMINDATA] n'a pu être exploité correctement";
    }
}

// erreur ?
if ($erreur) {
    // affichage d'un msg d'erreur puis arrêt
    print "$message\n";
    exit;
}

// ouverture fichier des résultats
$résultats = fopen($RESULTATS, "w");
if ($résultats === false) {
    print "Impossible de créer le fichier des résultats [$RESULTATS]\n";
    // sortie
    exit;
}

// ouverture fichier des données contribuables
$taxpayersdata = is_readable($TAXPAYERSDATA) ? fopen($TAXPAYERSDATA, "r") : false;
if ($taxpayersdata === false) {
    print "Impossible d'ouvrir le fichier des contribuables [$TAXPAYERSDATA]\n";
    // sortie
    exit;
}

// on exploite la ligne courante du fichier des données
while (($ligne = fgets($taxpayersdata, 100)) !== false) {
    // on enlève l'éventuelle marque de fin de ligne
    $ligne = cutNewLineChar($ligne);
    // on récupère les 3 champs marié,enfants,salaire qui forment $ligne
    [$marié, $enfants, $salaire] = explode(",", $ligne);
    $marié = strtolower($marié);
    $enfants = (int) $enfants;
    $salaire = (int) $salaire;
    // on calcule l'impôt
    $result = calculImpot($taxAdminData, $marié, $enfants, $salaire);
    // on inscrit le résultat dans le fichier des résultats
    $result = ["marié" => $marié, "enfants" => $enfants, "salaire" => $salaire] + $result;
    fputs($résultats, json_encode($result, JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE) . "\n");
    // donnée suivante
}
// on ferme les fichiers
fclose($taxpayersdata);
fclose($résultats);
print "Les résultats ont été enregistrés dans le fichier [$RESULTATS]\n";

// fin
exit;

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function cutNewLineChar(string $ligne): string
{
    // on supprime la marque de fin de ligne de $ligne si elle existe
    // (\r\n sous Windows, \n sous Unix)
    return rtrim($ligne, "\r\n");
}

// calcul de l'impôt
// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function calculImpot(array $taxAdminData, string $marié, int $enfants, float $salaire): array
{
    // $marié : oui, non
    // $enfants : nombre d'enfants
    // $salaire : salaire annuel
    // $taxAdminData : données de l'administration fiscale
    //
    // calcul de l'impôt avec enfants
    $result1 = calculImpot2($taxAdminData, $marié, $enfants, $salaire);
    $impot1 = $result1["impôt"];
    // calcul de l'impôt sans les enfants
    if ($enfants !== 0) {
        $result2 = calculImpot2($taxAdminData, $marié, 0, $salaire);
        $impot2 = $result2["impôt"];
        // application du plafonnement du quotient familial
        if ($enfants < 3) {
            // PLAFOND_QF_DEMI_PART euros pour les 2 premiers enfants
            $impot2 = $impot2 - $enfants * $taxAdminData["PLAFOND_QF_DEMI_PART"];
        } else {
            // PLAFOND_QF_DEMI_PART euros pour les 2 premiers enfants, le double pour les suivants
            $impot2 = $impot2 - 2 * $taxAdminData["PLAFOND_QF_DEMI_PART"] - ($enfants - 2) * 2 * $taxAdminData["PLAFOND_QF_DEMI_PART"];
        }
    } else {
        $impot2 = $impot1;
        $result2 = $result1;
    }
    // on prend l'impôt le plus fort avec le taux et la surcôte qui vont avec
    if ($impot1 > $impot2) {
        $impot = $impot1;
        $taux = $result1["taux"];
        $surcôte = $result1["surcôte"];
    } else {
        $surcôte = $impot2 - $impot1 + $result2["surcôte"];
        $impot = $impot2;
        $taux = $result2["taux"];
    }
    // calcul d'une éventuelle décôte
    $décôte = getDecote($taxAdminData, $marié, $salaire, $impot);
    $impot -= $décôte;
    // calcul d'une éventuelle réduction d'impôts
    $réduction = getRéduction($taxAdminData, $marié, $salaire, $enfants, $impot);
    $impot -= $réduction;
    // résultat
    return [
        "impôt" => (int) floor($impot),
        "surcôte" => (int) $surcôte,
        "décôte" => (int) $décôte,
        "réduction" => (int) $réduction,
        "taux" => $taux,
    ];
}

Comments:

  • line 9: the name of the JSON file of the tax administration's data;
  • lines 12-20: we try to read the content of the JSON file named [$TAXADMINDATA]. The [file_get_contents] function returns the whole content of a file in the form of a string, and [false] on failure;
  • lines 22-32: if the file was read successfully, we check with the [json_validate] function (PHP 8.3) that it does contain valid JSON, then its content is decoded into the associative array [$taxAdminData];
  • lines 35-39: if an error occurred in one of the two previous operations, an error message is written to the console and the program stops;
  • line 67: the difference from version 1 is that here the tax administration's data (arrays and constants) are in the associative array [$taxAdminData], whereas in version 1 they were in global arrays and constants. It is the global nature of these constants that makes the difference between the two versions:
    • in version 1, the constants were known in all the functions of [main.php];
    • to achieve the same result in version 2, the associative array [$taxAdminData] must be passed as a parameter to all the functions that need it: [calculImpot], [calculImpot2], [getRevenuImposable], [getDecote] and [getRéduction];
  • line 91: the [calculImpot] function receives the array [$taxAdminData] as its first parameter. The arrays [limites, coeffR, coeffN] are no longer parameters: they are in [$taxAdminData];
  • lines 108-111: where global constants were used, the content of the array [$taxAdminData] received as a parameter is now used.

The [calculImpot2] function retrieves the tax brackets from the array [$taxAdminData] in the same way:

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function calculImpot2(array $taxAdminData, string $marié, int $enfants, float $salaire): array
{
    // $marié : oui, non
    // $enfants : nombre d'enfants
    // $salaire : salaire annuel
    // $taxAdminData : données de l'administration fiscale
    //
    // nombre de parts
    if ($marié === "oui") {
        $nbParts = $enfants / 2 + 2;
    } else {
        $nbParts = $enfants / 2 + 1;
    }
    // 1 part par enfant à partir du 3e
    if ($enfants >= 3) {
        // une demi-part de + pour chaque enfant à partir du 3e
        $nbParts += 0.5 * ($enfants - 2);
    }
    // revenu imposable
    $revenuImposable = getRevenuImposable($taxAdminData, $salaire);
    // surcôte
    $surcôte = floor($revenuImposable - 0.9 * $salaire);
    // pour des pbs d'arrondi
    if ($surcôte < 0) {
        $surcôte = 0;
    }
    // quotient familial
    $quotient = $revenuImposable / $nbParts;
    // les tranches d'imposition
    $limites = $taxAdminData["limites"];
    $coeffR = $taxAdminData["coeffR"];
    $coeffN = $taxAdminData["coeffN"];
    // est mis à la fin du tableau limites pour arrêter la boucle qui suit
    $limites[count($limites) - 1] = $quotient;
    // calcul de l'impôt
    $i = 0;
    while ($quotient > $limites[$i]) {
        $i++;
    }
    // du fait qu'on a placé $quotient à la fin du tableau $limites, la boucle précédente
    // ne peut déborder du tableau $limites
    // maintenant on peut calculer l'impôt
    $impôt = floor($revenuImposable * $coeffR[$i] - $nbParts * $coeffN[$i]);
    // résultat
    return ["impôt" => $impôt, "surcôte" => $surcôte, "taux" => $coeffR[$i]];
}
  • lines 173-175: the three arrays of tax brackets are retrieved from the dictionary [$taxAdminData]. The rest of the code is unchanged.

The other functions are rewritten in the same way. For example, the [getDecote] function:

// calcule une décôte éventuelle
function getDecote(array $taxAdminData, string $marié, float $salaire, float $impots): float
{
    // au départ, une décôte nulle
    $décôte = 0;
    // montant maximal d'impôt pour avoir la décôte
    $plafondImpôtPourDécôte = $marié === "oui" ? $taxAdminData["PLAFOND_IMPOT_COUPLE_POUR_DECOTE"] : $taxAdminData["PLAFOND_IMPOT_CELIBATAIRE_POUR_DECOTE"];
    if ($impots < $plafondImpôtPourDécôte) {
        // montant maximal de la décôte
        $plafondDécôte = $marié === "oui" ? $taxAdminData["PLAFOND_DECOTE_COUPLE"] : $taxAdminData["PLAFOND_DECOTE_CELIBATAIRE"];
        // décôte théorique
        $décôte = $plafondDécôte - 0.75 * $impots;
        // la décôte ne peut dépasser le montant de l'impôt
        if ($décôte > $impots) {
            $décôte = $impots;
        }
        // pas de décôte < 0
        if ($décôte < 0) {
            $décôte = 0;
        }
    }
    // résultat
    return ceil($décôte);
}

Execution produces the following output:

> php main.php
Les résultats ont été enregistrés dans le fichier [resultats.txt]

and the following [resultats.txt] file:

The results obtained are the same as those obtained in the previous version.

docs.title: 4.4.2. Conclusion
docs.text:
Version 2 is much more flexible than version 1. If, in another year, the tax calculation algorithm remains the same, only the tax brackets and the calculation constants change. It is then enough to update the file [taxadmindata.json]. With version 1, you have to go into the code to modify the tax brackets and the calculation constants. Yet the people who have to change the values of the tax brackets and calculation constants probably do not have access to the algorithm's code.

Version 2 nevertheless has a flaw: the array [$taxAdminData] must be passed to all the functions, and nothing guarantees that it contains all the expected keys. A typo in a key of the JSON file would only be detected at calculation time. Version 3 will store these data in an object of a class [TaxAdminData] whose properties are declared and typed.

docs.title: 5. Classes
docs.text:
Vocabulary: a class (keyword [class]) is a PHP type. A variable of this type is called an object. An object is an instance (a copy) of a class.

It is in this chapter that the evolution of PHP between versions 7 and 8 is most visible. PHP 8 brought a series of new features that make writing classes more concise and safer: typed attributes, constructor parameter promotion, read-only attributes ([readonly]), enumerations ([enum]), property hooks and asymmetric visibility (PHP 8.4), cloning with modification (PHP 8.5)... We introduce them as the examples progress, keeping the progression of the PHP 7 course: we start from the most rudimentary class and arrive at the class written according to current best practices.

docs.title: 5.1. The script tree
docs.text:

docs.title: 5.2. Can any variable become an object with attributes?
docs.text:
In PHP 7, you could write [$obj1->attr1 = "un";] on a non-existent variable [$obj1]: PHP would then silently (with a mere warning) create an object of type [stdClass] with the attribute [attr1]. This is no longer possible in PHP 8. The script [classes-01.php] is as follows:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// en PHP 8, une variable inexistante ne devient plus un objet par magie
try {
    $obj0->attr1 = "un";
} catch (\Error $e) {
    print "Erreur : " . $e->getMessage() . "\n";
}
// un objet générique doit être créé explicitement
$obj1 = new \stdClass();
// un objet [stdClass] peut recevoir des attributs créés dynamiquement
$obj1->attr1 = "un";
$obj1->attr2 = 100;
// affiche l'objet
print "objet1=[$obj1->attr1,$obj1->attr2]\n";
// modifie l'objet
$obj1->attr2 += 100;
// affiche l'objet
print "objet1=[$obj1->attr1,$obj1->attr2]\n";
// copie la valeur de objet1 (adresse de l'objet pointé) dans objet2
// les deux variables sont alors différentes mais pointent sur le même objet
$obj2 = $obj1;
// modifie obj2
$obj2->attr2 = 0;
// affiche les deux objets
print "objet1=[$obj1->attr1,$obj1->attr2]\n";
print "objet2=[$obj2->attr1,$obj2->attr2]\n";
// change l'objet pointé par obj1
$obj1 = new \stdClass();
print "obj1 :\n";
print_r($obj1);
print "obj2 :\n";
print_r($obj2);
// affecte la référence (l'adresse) de objet2 à objet3
// $obj2 et $obj3 sont alors une seule et même variable
$obj3 = &$obj2;
print "obj2 :\n";
print_r($obj2);
print "obj3 :\n";
print_r($obj3);
// modifie obj3
$obj3->attr2 = 10;
// affiche les deux objets
print "objet2=[$obj2->attr1,$obj2->attr2]\n";
print "objet3=[$obj3->attr1,$obj3->attr2]\n";
// change l'objet pointé par obj2
$obj2 = new \stdClass();
$obj2->attr3 = "deux";
$obj2->attr4 = 20;
// affiche les deux objets $obj2 et $obj3
print "obj2 :\n";
print_r($obj2);
print "obj3 :\n";
print_r($obj3);

// un objet est-il un dictionnaire ?
try {
    print count($obj3) . "\n";
} catch (\TypeError $e) {
    print "Erreur : " . $e->getMessage() . "\n";
}
// le nombre d'attributs s'obtient avec [get_object_vars]
print "nombre d'attributs : " . count(get_object_vars($obj3)) . "\n";
// un objet peut être parcouru avec [foreach]
foreach ($obj3 as $attribut => $valeur) {
    print "obj3[$attribut]=$valeur\n";
}
// un tableau associatif peut être transformé en objet [stdClass] et inversement
$obj4 = (object) ["nom" => "Langevin", "age" => 48];
print "obj4=[$obj4->nom,$obj4->age]\n";
print_r((array) $obj4);
// fin
exit;

We will study the [try / catch] structure in the chapter on exceptions. For now, just remember that it makes it possible to catch the error and continue executing the script;
  • line 13: a generic object must be created explicitly with the [new] operator. The predefined class [stdClass] is an empty class;
  • lines 15-16: the notation [$obj->attr] designates the attribute [attr] of the object [$obj]. If it does not exist, it is created: it is said to be a dynamic attribute. The [stdClass] class is made for this: you can add as many attributes to it as you like;
  • line 25: the expression [$obj2 = $obj1], when [$obj1] is an object, is a copy of references: [$obj2] and [$obj1] are references (addresses) to the same object. The object itself can be modified through either reference;
  • lines 27-30: aim to show that [$obj1] and [$obj2] are two different variables pointing to the same object. [$obj2 = $obj1] copied the value of [$obj1] into the variable [$obj2] (operation 1 below). The value of [$obj1] is the address of an object. Thus [$obj1] and [$obj2] point to the same object. When you manipulate a variable [$obj] that points to an object, PHP manipulates the object pointed to. From the diagram below, we can see that the object pointed to can be modified either through [$obj1] or through [$obj2]. This is what lines 5 and 6 of the results show;

  • line 39: the expression [$obj3 = &$obj2] makes [$obj2] and [$obj3] be at the same address [1 below]. One could say that the two variables are aliases of the same memory location. They both point to an object, Object A below [2];
  • line 50: the operation [$obj2 = new \stdClass()] creates a new object, Object B [3 below], and the address of this new object is assigned to the variable [$obj2] [4]. Since [$obj2] and [$obj3] are two aliases of the same memory location, [$obj3] also points to the new object Object B. This is what lines 31-42 of the results show;

  • line 61: is an object a dictionary? In PHP 7, the [count] function accepted an object (with a warning) and returned 1, which made no sense. In PHP 8, it throws a [TypeError] error: [count] only accepts arrays or objects implementing the [Countable] interface (line 43 of the results);
  • line 66: the [get_object_vars] function returns the attributes of an object in the form of an associative array. Its number of elements is the number of attributes of the object;
  • lines 68-69: an object can be traversed with [foreach], like a dictionary. The keys are the names of the attributes and the values are the values of those attributes. So an object has similarities with a dictionary but is not one. In PHP 7, this traversal was done with the [each] function, which has since been removed;
  • lines 72-74: the conversion operator [(object)] transforms an associative array into a [stdClass] object and the [(array)] operator does the reverse.

docs.title: 5.3. A Personne class without declared attributes
docs.text:
In PHP 7, a class could use attributes it had not declared: you just had to write [$p->prenom = "Paul";] to create the attribute [prenom] in the object [$p], as is done with [stdClass]. These dynamic attributes on objects of an ordinary class have been deprecated since PHP 8.2: each creation of such an attribute produces the message "Deprecated: Creation of dynamic property Personne::$prenom is deprecated". They will disappear in a future version of PHP. The reason is simple: a typo in the name of an attribute ([$p->prenon = "Paul"]) silently created a new attribute instead of reporting the error.

There are three exceptions to this rule:

  • the [stdClass] class, which we have just used, still accepts dynamic attributes;
  • a class preceded by the attribute [#[\AllowDynamicProperties]] also accepts them. This attribute was designed to facilitate the migration of old code. We will not use it in this course;
  • a class that defines the magic methods [__get] and [__set] decides for itself what to do with an undeclared attribute.

It is this third solution that the script [classes-02.php] presents:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

class Personne
{
    // les attributs ne sont pas déclarés un par un :
    // ils sont rangés dans un tableau privé
    private array $attributs = [];

    // appelée lors de l'écriture d'un attribut non déclaré : $p->x = valeur
    public function __set(string $nom, mixed $valeur): void
    {
        $this->attributs[$nom] = $valeur;
    }

    // appelée lors de la lecture d'un attribut non déclaré : $p->x
    public function __get(string $nom): mixed
    {
        return $this->attributs[$nom] ?? null;
    }

    // appelée par isset($p->x)
    public function __isset(string $nom): bool
    {
        return isset($this->attributs[$nom]);
    }

    // méthode
    public function identite(): string
    {
        // utilise des attributs qui n'ont pas été déclarés
        return "[$this->prenom,$this->nom,$this->age]";
    }
}

// test
// les attributs sont créés par la méthode magique [__set]
$p = new Personne();
$p->prenom = "Paul";
$p->nom = "Langevin";
$p->age = 48;
// appel d'une méthode
print "personne=" . $p->identite() . "\n";
// isset
print "isset(\$p->age) : " . var_export(isset($p->age), true) . "\n";
print "isset(\$p->adresse) : " . var_export(isset($p->adresse), true) . "\n";
// fin
exit;

Results:

> php classes-02.php
personne=[Paul,Langevin,48]
isset($p->age) : true
isset($p->adresse) : false

Comments

  • lines 6-38: define a class [Personne]. A class is a mold from which objects are created. It groups together attributes and functions called methods;
  • line 10: the only declared attribute of the class is a private array (we will soon see the meaning of the [private] keyword). It is this array that will store the "undeclared" attributes;
  • lines 13-16: the magic method [__set] is called automatically by PHP when you write to an attribute that does not exist (or is not accessible). It receives the name of the attribute and the value to assign to it. Here, it stores this value in the array [$attributs]. Methods whose name begins with two underscores are called magic methods: you do not call them explicitly; PHP calls them;
  • lines 19-22: the magic method [__get] is called when you read an attribute that does not exist. It returns the stored value or [null]. The [??] operator returns its left operand if it exists and is not [null], otherwise its right operand;
  • line 25: the magic method [__isset] is called by the [isset] function;
  • line 31: the [identite] method uses three attributes not declared in the class. The keyword [$this] designates the object to which the method is applied. Each read [$this->prenom] triggers a call to [__get];
  • line 40: an object [$p] of type [Personne] is created. The keyword [new] is used to create a new object. The operation returns a reference to the created object (hence an address). Various forms are possible: [new Personne()], [new Personne], [new personne]. The class name is case-insensitive;
  • lines 41-43: the three attributes needed by the [identite] method are created in the object [$p] by the [__set] method;
  • line 45: the [identite] method of the [Personne] class is applied to the object [$p]. In the code of the [identite] method, [$this] references the same object as [$p].

This technique has its uses (configuration objects, encapsulation of data read from a file), but it is not the normal way to write a class. In an ordinary class, you declare its attributes.

docs.title: 5.4. The Personne class with declared attributes
docs.text:
The script [classes-03.php] is as follows:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

class Personne
{
    // attributs de la classe, publics et typés
    public string $prenom;
    public string $nom;
    public int $age;

    // méthode
    public function identite(): string
    {
        return "[$this->prenom,$this->nom,$this->age]";
    }
}

// test
// les attributs sont publics
$p = new Personne();
$p->prenom = "Paul";
$p->nom = "Langevin";
$p->age = 48;
// appel d'une méthode
print "personne=" . $p->identite() . "\n";
// un attribut typé n'accepte que des valeurs de son type
try {
    $p->age = "quarante-huit";
} catch (\TypeError $e) {
    print "Erreur 1 : " . $e->getMessage() . "\n";
}
// un attribut typé non initialisé ne peut pas être lu
$p2 = new Personne();
try {
    print "personne=" . $p2->identite() . "\n";
} catch (\Error $e) {
    print "Erreur 2 : " . $e->getMessage() . "\n";
}
// fin
exit;

Results:

> php classes-03.php
personne=[Paul,Langevin,48]
Erreur 1 : Cannot assign string to property Personne::$age of type int
Erreur 2 : Typed property Personne::$prenom must not be accessed before initialization

Comments

  • lines 9-11: the class's attributes are explicitly declared. The keyword [public] means that they are accessible from outside the class. In PHP 7, the course used the keyword [var], inherited from PHP 4, which is a synonym of [public] and is no longer used today;
  • each attribute is preceded by its type: [string] for the first name and the last name, [int] for the age. These are typed attributes, introduced in PHP 7.4. The possible types are those of function parameters: [int], [float], [string], [bool], [array], a class or interface name, a nullable type [?string], a union type [int|float]...;
  • line 30: a typed attribute only accepts values of its type. Any other value causes a [TypeError] error (line 3 of the results);
  • lines 35-37: a typed attribute without a default value is in the "uninitialized" state as long as nothing has been assigned to it. Reading it causes an error (line 4 of the results). Untyped attributes, on the other hand, are [null] by default. This is a first reason to initialize all the attributes of an object as soon as it is created: that is the role of the constructor.

docs.title: 5.5. The Personne class with a constructor
docs.text:
The previous examples showed exotic [Personne] classes such as could be found in PHP 4. It is not advisable to follow these examples. We now present a [Personne] class [classes-04.php] that corresponds to classic best practices, found in all object-oriented languages (Java, C#...):

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

class Personne
{
    // attributs de la classe
    private string $prenom;
    private string $nom;
    private int $age;

    // getters et setters
    public function getPrenom(): string
    {
        return $this->prenom;
    }

    public function getNom(): string
    {
        return $this->nom;
    }

    public function getAge(): int
    {
        return $this->age;
    }

    public function setPrenom(string $prenom): void
    {
        $this->prenom = $prenom;
    }

    public function setNom(string $nom): void
    {
        $this->nom = $nom;
    }

    public function setAge(int $age): void
    {
        $this->age = $age;
    }

    // constructeur
    public function __construct(string $prenom, string $nom, int $age)
    {
        // on passe par les set
        $this->setPrenom($prenom);
        $this->setNom($nom);
        $this->setAge($age);
    }

    // méthode toString
    public function __toString(): string
    {
        return "[$this->prenom,$this->nom,$this->age]";
    }
}

// test
// création d'un objet Personne
$p = new Personne("Paul", "Langevin", 48);
// identité de cette personne
print "personne=$p\n";
// on change l'âge
$p->setAge(14);
// identité de la personne
print "personne=$p\n";
// une classe ayant une méthode [__toString] implémente l'interface [Stringable]
print "Stringable : " . var_export($p instanceof \Stringable, true) . "\n";
// un attribut privé n'est pas accessible de l'extérieur de la classe
try {
    print $p->nom;
} catch (\Error $e) {
    print "Erreur : " . $e->getMessage() . "\n";
}
// fin
exit;

Results:

> php classes-04.php
personne=[Paul,Langevin,48]
personne=[Paul,Langevin,14]
Stringable : true
Erreur : Cannot access private property Personne::$nom

Comments

  • line 4: we ask for the declared types of function parameters to be strictly respected. Without this declaration, PHP would try to convert a value of the wrong type (for example the string ["48"] into the integer [48]);
  • lines 6-60: the [Personne] class;
  • lines 9-11: the private ([private]) attributes of the class. These attributes are visible only inside the class. The other keywords that can be used are:
    • [public]: makes the attribute a public attribute visible from outside the class;
    • [protected]: makes the attribute a protected attribute visible from inside the class and from the classes derived from it;
  • because the attributes are private, they cannot be accessed from outside the class. So we cannot write [$p->nom = "Landru"]: we are outside the [Personne] class and the attribute [nom] is private. The lines 72-74 check this: reading [$p->nom] causes an error (line 5 of the results). To initialize the private attributes of the object [$p], there are two ways:
    • use the public [set] and [get] methods (the names of these methods can be anything) of lines 14-39. We will then write: [$p->setNom("Landru")];
    • use the constructor of lines 45-50. We will then write: [$p = new Personne("Michel", "Landru", 44)]. This form automatically calls the method of the [Personne] class named [__construct];
  • line 64: this line displays the person [$p] in the form of a string. To do so, the method of the [Personne] class named [__toString] (line 54) is used;
  • line 70: since PHP 8.0, any class that defines a [__toString] method automatically implements the predefined interface [Stringable] (we will study interfaces in the next chapter). The [instanceof] operator tests whether an object is of a given type. A function can thus declare a parameter of type [string|Stringable]: it then accepts a string or any object convertible into a string;
  • all the methods of the class have been prefixed with the keyword [public], which indicates that the method is visible outside the class. The other keywords that can be used are, as for attributes and with the same meaning, [private] and [protected]. Without an explicit visibility keyword, the method is implicitly [public]. The PSR-12 style rules, which the scripts of this course follow, require the visibility always to be written explicitly.

docs.title: 5.6. Constructor parameter promotion
docs.text:
The previous class is verbose: each attribute is named four times (declaration, constructor parameter, assignment in the constructor, getter). Since PHP 8.0, constructor parameter promotion makes it possible to declare and initialize an attribute directly in the constructor's parameter list. The script [classes-22.php] shows this:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

class Personne
{
    // constructeur avec promotion des paramètres :
    // chaque paramètre précédé d'une visibilité devient un attribut de la classe
    public function __construct(
        private string $prenom,
        private string $nom,
        private int $age = 0,
    ) {
        // rien d'autre à faire : les attributs sont déjà initialisés
    }

    // getters
    public function getPrenom(): string
    {
        return $this->prenom;
    }

    public function getNom(): string
    {
        return $this->nom;
    }

    public function getAge(): int
    {
        return $this->age;
    }

    // setter
    public function setAge(int $age): void
    {
        $this->age = $age;
    }

    // méthode toString
    public function __toString(): string
    {
        return "[$this->prenom,$this->nom,$this->age]";
    }
}

// test
// appel classique : les arguments sont passés dans l'ordre des paramètres
$p1 = new Personne("Paul", "Langevin", 48);
print "p1=$p1\n";
// arguments nommés : l'ordre n'a plus d'importance
$p2 = new Personne(nom: "Lefur", age: 70, prenom: "Sylvie");
print "p2=$p2\n";
// le paramètre [age] a une valeur par défaut : on peut l'omettre
$p3 = new Personne(prenom: "Steve", nom: "Boer");
print "p3=$p3\n";
// les attributs promus sont de vrais attributs
var_dump($p3);
// fin
exit;

Results:

> php classes-22.php
p1=[Paul,Langevin,48]
p2=[Sylvie,Lefur,70]
p3=[Steve,Boer,0]
object(Personne)#3 (3) {
  ["prenom":"Personne":private]=>
  string(5) "Steve"
  ["nom":"Personne":private]=>
  string(4) "Boer"
  ["age":"Personne":private]=>
  int(0)
}

Comments

  • lines 10-14: each constructor parameter preceded by a visibility keyword ([private], [protected], [public]) is "promoted": PHP declares an attribute with the same name and the same type and assigns it the value of the parameter. These three lines replace the attribute declarations and assignments of the previous class;
  • line 13: a promoted parameter can have a default value. The comma after the last parameter has been allowed since PHP 8.0: it makes it easier to add a parameter later;
  • line 15: the body of the constructor can contain code (checks, for example). Here, there is nothing to do;
  • line 52: named arguments (PHP 8.0) make it possible to pass the arguments in any order, designating them by the name of the parameter. The code is more readable, especially when a function has many parameters;
  • line 55: the parameter [age] is omitted: it takes its default value;
  • line 58: the [var_dump] function shows that the promoted attributes are real private attributes of the class (lines 5-12 of the results).

docs.title: 5.7. The Personne class with validity checks in the constructor
docs.text:
A class's constructor is the right place to check that the object's initialization values are correct. But an object can also be initialized by its [set] methods or equivalent. To avoid putting the same checks in two different places, they can be put in the [set] methods. If an initialization value of an object turns out to be incorrect, an exception will be thrown. Here is an example.

First, the definition of the [Personne] class is moved into its own file [Personne.php]:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Exemples;

// classe Personne
class Personne
{
    // attributs de la classe
    private string $prenom;
    private string $nom;
    private int $age;

    // getters et setters
    public function getPrenom(): string
    {
        return $this->prenom;
    }

    public function getNom(): string
    {
        return $this->nom;
    }

    public function getAge(): int
    {
        return $this->age;
    }

    public function setPrenom(string $prénom): void
    {
        // le prénom doit être non vide
        $prénom = trim($prénom);
        if ($prénom === "") {
            throw new \Exception("Le prénom doit être non vide");
        }
        $this->prenom = $prénom;
    }

    public function setNom(string $nom): void
    {
        // le nom doit être non vide
        $nom = trim($nom);
        if ($nom === "") {
            throw new \Exception("Le nom doit être non vide");
        }
        $this->nom = $nom;
    }

    public function setAge(int $âge): void
    {
        // l'âge doit être valide
        if ($âge < 0) {
            throw new \Exception("L'âge doit être un entier positif ou nul");
        }
        $this->age = $âge;
    }

    // constructeur
    public function __construct(string $prenom, string $nom, int $age)
    {
        // on passe par les set
        $this->setPrenom($prenom);
        $this->setNom($nom);
        $this->setAge($age);
    }

    // méthode faisant office de second constructeur
    public function initWithPersonne(Personne $p): void
    {
        // initialise l'objet courant avec une personne $p
        $this->__construct($p->prenom, $p->nom, $p->age);
    }

    // méthode statique de fabrication (constructeur nommé)
    public static function fromPersonne(Personne $p): self
    {
        // crée une nouvelle personne copie de la personne $p
        return new self($p->prenom, $p->nom, $p->age);
    }

    // méthode toString
    public function __toString(): string
    {
        return "[$this->prenom,$this->nom,$this->age]";
    }
}

Comments

  • line 4: we ask for the type of function parameters to be respected when it is declared;
  • line 7: defines a namespace. The full (so-called qualified) name of the [Personne] class is then [\Exemples\Personne]. Note the [\] character at the start of the qualified name: this makes it an absolute qualified name. If this character is absent, it is a relative qualified name (relative to the current namespace). Thus, if two classes A and B belong to the same namespace E, in the code of class A, class B can be reached with the relative notation B. If class A belongs to namespace E1 and B to namespace E2, in the code of A, B will be reached with the absolute notation [\E2\B]. Defining a class inside a namespace is not mandatory but it is good practice: two libraries can then each define a [Personne] class without conflict;
  • namespaces often correspond to the file tree. Thus class A of a namespace E1 is often in a file [E1/A.php]. This is the PSR-4 convention used by the [Composer] tool to load classes automatically, which we will use in later chapters. The [PHP Intelephense] extension of [VS Code] does not enforce it. The file tree and the namespace must not be confused: the fully qualified name of a class uses a namespace and has nothing to do with the location of the class's PHP file in the tree. Here, the class [\Exemples\Personne] is in the file [scripts-console/classes/Personne.php];
  • lines 13-15: the three private attributes of the class;
  • lines 33-41: initialization of the attribute [prenom] and check of the initialization value;
  • line 36: the function [trim($chaine)] removes the spaces at the beginning and end of [$chaine]. Thus [trim(" abcd ")] is the string ["abcd"] and [trim(" ")] is the empty string. Note that a variable name can contain accented characters;
  • line 37: if the first name is empty, an exception is thrown (line 38); otherwise the first name is stored (line 40). To throw an exception, the predefined class [Exception] has been used here. We are obliged here to use its absolute name [\Exception]. If we use its relative name [Exception], this class will be looked for in the current namespace, i.e. the [Exemples] namespace of the [Personne] class. The PHP interpreter would thus look for a class with the absolute name [\Exemples\Exception], which does not exist;
  • lines 63-69: the constructor goes through the [set] methods to initialize the attributes: the checks are written only once;
  • the methods line 72 and line 79 are presented in the next section.

The [Personne] class is used by the following script [classes-05.php]:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// inclusion de la définition de la classe Personne
require_once __DIR__ . "/Personne.php";
// pour démonstration
print __DIR__ . "/Personne.php\n";

// nom qualifié de la classe Personne
use Exemples\Personne;

// test
// création d'un objet Personne
$p = new Personne("Paul", "Langevin", 48);
// identité de cette personne
print "Exemple1, personne=$p\n";
// création d'un objet Personne erroné
try {
    $p = new Personne("xx", "yy", "zz");
} catch (\Exception $e1) {
    print "Exemple2, erreur : " . $e1->getMessage() . "\n";
} catch (\TypeError $e2) {
    print "Exemple2, erreur : " . $e2->getMessage() . "\n";
}
// création d'un objet Personne erroné
try {
    $p = new Personne("", "yy", 10);
} catch (\Exception $e1) {
    print "Exemple3, erreur : " . $e1->getMessage() . "\n";
} catch (\TypeError $e2) {
    print "Exemple3, erreur : " . $e2->getMessage() . "\n";
}

// fin
exit;

Results:

> php classes-05.php
.../php8-oct-2026/scripts-console/classes/Personne.php
Exemple1, personne=[Paul,Langevin,48]
Exemple2, erreur : Exemples\Personne::__construct(): Argument #3 ($age) must be of type int, string given, called in .../php8-oct-2026/scripts-console/classes/classes-05.php on line 21
Exemple3, erreur : Le prénom doit être non vide

Comments

  • line 7: the script is going to use the [Personne] class. The PHP interpreter must then be told where it can find the definition of this class. This is the role of the [include fichier] and [require fichier] statements. The difference between the two statements is as follows: if the [include fichier] statement encounters errors while loading [fichier], an error of level [E_WARNING] is emitted but execution continues, whereas [require], in the same case, generates a fatal error and the script's execution stops. Each of the two statements has a variant, [include_once] and [require_once]. These two variants make it possible to handle the case of multiple inclusions of the same file. One can imagine here a project made up of several PHP scripts, several of which reference the [Personne] class. Their execution will then cause the file [Personne.php] to be included several times and cause an error, because a class cannot be defined twice. The solution is to use the [_once] variants, which ensure that the file will be included only once in the project's overall script;
  • the [__DIR__] constant is a PHP constant that designates the full name of the folder containing the script that contains the [__DIR__] constant. line 9 displays it (line 2 of the results). On the reader's machine, you will get something like [C:\laragon\www\php8-oct-2026\scripts-console\classes/Personne.php]. In a file path, the [/] and [\] signs can be used interchangeably under Windows. Using [__DIR__] makes the script independent of the current folder at the time it is executed;
  • line 12: the script [classes-05.php] has no namespace. When the code uses the relative name [Personne], it is looked for in the root namespace [\] and will therefore not be found. There are two solutions to this problem:
    • use the full name of the class [\Exemples\Personne];
    • use the [use] statement, which indicates that, in the code that follows, the name [Personne] designates the class [\Exemples\Personne]. In a [use] statement, the name is always absolute: the initial [\] is unnecessary (this is the recommended form). The statement is equivalent to [use Exemples\Personne as Personne;], which says that the alias [Personne] designates the class [\Exemples\Personne];
  • the [use] statement lets the interpreter know that the class [Personne] is in reality the class [\Exemples\Personne]. That said, where will the interpreter find the code of this class? It is the [require_once] statement that tells it. The two statements have very different roles: [use] works on names, [require_once] loads a file;
  • line 16: a [Personne] object is created. It is the [__construct] method of the [Personne] class that will be implicitly executed here;
  • line 18: displays the person [$p]. To be displayed, the value of the variable [$p] must be transformed into a string. Implicitly, it is the [Personne::__toString] method that is then executed. It must therefore return a string;
  • we saw that the constructor of the [Personne] class could throw an exception of type [\Exception]. This exception must therefore be handled. So the creation of a person should always be surrounded by a [try / catch] structure, as in lines 20-34. Here an error is deliberately produced by passing an age that is not an integer. In this particular case, the error is thrown by the PHP interpreter and not by the code of the [Personne] class. Indeed, the signature of the [Personne::__construct] method is [__construct(string $prenom, string $nom, int $age)]. The parameter [age] passed to the constructor must therefore be of type integer. If it is not, the PHP interpreter throws an error of type [TypeError]. Furthermore, the [set] methods of the [Personne] class throw an exception of type [\Exception]. As the constructor that calls them has no [try / catch] structure, the exception goes up one level, to the code that called the constructor, i.e. the code of the script [classes-05.php]. Ultimately, the script [classes-05.php] can receive two types of error: [\Exception] or [\TypeError]. For this reason, the [try] structure has two [catch] clauses to handle the two types of error separately. When the developer is sure that certain errors cannot occur, they will not use the corresponding [catch] clauses. Here they are systematically used purely for demonstration purposes;
  • line 22: you can write either [Exception] or [\Exception]. The first version uses the relative name of the class, relative to the script's namespace. The script has none. Its namespace is then the root of the namespaces: [\]. So writing [Exception] here amounts to writing [\Exception]. It is preferable to use the absolute name of PHP's predefined classes in a script that has no namespace of its own. That way, if you decide to give this script a namespace, the absolute class names remain valid, whereas in the other case, the change of namespace will cause errors on the relative class names;
  • line 23: when there is an exception, the [Exception::getMessage] method makes it possible to obtain the exception's error message. The same goes for an error of type [TypeError]. In the [Personne::setPrenom] method, we wrote [throw new \Exception("Le prénom doit être non vide")]. It is this message ("the first name must not be empty") that the [getMessage] method retrieves in example 3 (line 5 of the results);
  • line 4 of the results: the message of the [TypeError] error. Since PHP 8.0, it designates the faulty parameter by its number and by its name: "Argument #3 ($age) must be of type int, string given". PHP 8's error messages are more precise than those of PHP 7.

docs.title: 5.8. Adding a method acting as a second constructor
docs.text:
In PHP, it is not possible to have several constructors with different parameters that would make it possible to build an object in various ways. Instead, you can use methods that act as constructors. The [Personne] class has two:

    public function initWithPersonne(Personne $p): void
    {
        // initialise l'objet courant avec une personne $p
        $this->__construct($p->prenom, $p->nom, $p->age);
    }

    // méthode statique de fabrication (constructeur nommé)
    public static function fromPersonne(Personne $p): self
    {
        // crée une nouvelle personne copie de la personne $p
        return new self($p->prenom, $p->nom, $p->age);
    }

Comments

  • lines 72-76: the [initWithPersonne] method makes it possible to assign to the current object the values of the attributes of another [Personne] object. Here, it calls the constructor [__construct], but this is not mandatory. It could initialize the attributes of the [Personne] class itself. Note that a method of the [Personne] class has access to the private attributes of all [Personne] objects, not only to those of [$this];
  • lines 79-83: the [fromPersonne] method is another way of doing things, more common today. It is a static method (keyword [static]): it does not apply to an object but to the class. It is called with the notation [Personne::fromPersonne($p)]. It creates a new object with [new self(...)]: the keyword [self] designates the class in which the code is written, here [Personne]. The return type [self] indicates that the method returns an object of this class. Such a method is called a named constructor or factory method. We will come back to static methods a little further on.

The new [Personne] class is used by the following script [classes-06.php]:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// inclusion de la définition de la classe Personne
require_once __DIR__ . "/Personne.php";
// déclaration du nom qualifié de la classe Personne
use Exemples\Personne;

// test
// création d'un objet Personne
try {
    $p = new Personne("Paul", "Langevin", 48);
} catch (\Exception $e) {
    print "erreur : " . $e->getMessage() . "\n";
    exit;
}
// identité de cette personne
print "personne=$p\n";
// création d'une seconde personne
try {
    $p2 = new Personne("Laure", "Adeline", 67);
} catch (\Exception $e) {
    print "erreur : " . $e->getMessage() . "\n";
    exit;
}
// initialisation de la première avec les valeurs de la seconde
try {
    $p->initWithPersonne($p2);
} catch (\Exception $e) {
    print "erreur : " . $e->getMessage() . "\n";
    exit;
}
// vérification
print "personne=$p\n";

// création d'une troisième personne avec le constructeur nommé
$p3 = Personne::fromPersonne($p2);
print "personne=$p3\n";
// $p3 et $p2 sont deux objets différents ayant les mêmes valeurs
print "même objet : " . var_export($p3 === $p2, true) . "\n";
print "mêmes valeurs : " . var_export($p3 == $p2, true) . "\n";
// fin
exit;

Results:

> php classes-06.php
personne=[Paul,Langevin,48]
personne=[Laure,Adeline,67]
personne=[Laure,Adeline,67]
même objet : false
mêmes valeurs : true

Comments

  • line 17, line 26, line 33: it is common, after an exception, to have to stop the execution of a console script if the error encountered is unrecoverable. This is not the case in a web script: the script's execution is not stopped; an error page is displayed instead. If you are in a function, it is not the [exit] statement that will be used but [return]: you do not stop the execution of the script ([exit]) but leave the function ([return]) after having set an error;
  • line 39: call of the named constructor;
  • line 42: the [===] operator applied to two objects returns true if they are the same object (same address). [$p3] and [$p2] are two distinct objects (line 5 of the results);
  • line 43: the [==] operator applied to two objects of the same class returns true if their attributes have the same values (line 6 of the results). The [var_export] function returns a PHP representation of its parameter, here [true] or [false].

docs.title: 5.9. Validity checks with property hooks (PHP 8.4)
docs.text:
The previous [Personne] class protects its attributes by making them private and forcing outside code to go through [get] and [set] methods. PHP 8.4 offers another solution: property hooks. A public attribute can be accompanied by a [set] hook, code executed each time the attribute is written, and a [get] hook, code executed each time it is read. You thus keep the simple form [$p->age = 49] while retaining control over the values. This is what the script [classes-23.php] shows:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

class Personne
{
    // attribut public avec un crochet [set] : la validation est faite à chaque écriture
    public string $prenom {
        set(string $value) {
            $value = trim($value);
            if ($value === "") {
                throw new \InvalidArgumentException("Le prénom doit être non vide");
            }
            $this->prenom = $value;
        }
    }

    public string $nom {
        set(string $value) {
            $value = trim($value);
            if ($value === "") {
                throw new \InvalidArgumentException("Le nom doit être non vide");
            }
            $this->nom = $value;
        }
    }

    // sans paramètre explicite, la valeur reçue s'appelle [$value]
    public int $age {
        set {
            if ($value < 0) {
                throw new \InvalidArgumentException("L'âge doit être un entier positif ou nul");
            }
            $this->age = $value;
        }
    }

    // attribut virtuel : il n'a qu'un crochet [get] et n'occupe aucune place dans l'objet
    public string $identite {
        get => "[$this->prenom,$this->nom,$this->age]";
    }

    // constructeur : les affectations passent par les crochets [set]
    public function __construct(string $prenom, string $nom, int $age)
    {
        $this->prenom = $prenom;
        $this->nom = $nom;
        $this->age = $age;
    }
}

// test
$p = new Personne(" Paul ", "Langevin", 48);
print "personne=$p->identite\n";
// les attributs sont publics : on les lit et on les écrit directement
$p->age = 49;
print "âge=$p->age\n";
// mais l'écriture passe toujours par le crochet [set]
foreach (["prenom" => "  ", "age" => -4] as $attribut => $valeur) {
    try {
        $p->$attribut = $valeur;
    } catch (\InvalidArgumentException $e) {
        print "Erreur : " . $e->getMessage() . "\n";
    }
}
// un attribut virtuel sans crochet [set] ne peut être écrit
try {
    $p->identite = "?";
} catch (\Error $e) {
    print "Erreur : " . $e->getMessage() . "\n";
}
// l'objet est resté valide
print "personne=$p->identite\n";
var_dump($p);

Results:

> php classes-23.php
personne=[Paul,Langevin,48]
âge=49
Erreur : Le prénom doit être non vide
Erreur : L'âge doit être un entier positif ou nul
Erreur : Property Personne::$identite is read-only
personne=[Paul,Langevin,49]
object(Personne)#1 (3) {
  ["prenom"]=>
  string(4) "Paul"
  ["nom"]=>
  string(8) "Langevin"
  ["age"]=>
  int(49)
}

Comments

  • lines 9-17: the public attribute [prenom] is followed by a block in braces that contains its hooks. Here, there is only a [set] hook;
  • line 10: the [set] hook receives the value to be assigned to the attribute. It cleans it with [trim], checks it and throws an exception if it is incorrect;
  • line 15: inside its hooks, [$this->prenom] designates the attribute's memory location: the value is stored there. Everywhere else, [$this->prenom] goes through the hooks;
  • line 13: an exception of type [\InvalidArgumentException] is thrown, a predefined class derived from [\Exception] and more precise than it: it signals an invalid argument. We will present PHP's predefined exceptions in the chapter on exceptions;
  • line 31: when the [set] hook does not declare a parameter, the value received is available in the implicit variable [$value], and its type is that of the attribute;
  • lines 40-42: an attribute that has only a [get] hook and never refers to its own memory location is a virtual attribute: it is computed on each read and takes up no space in the object. The notation [get => expression] is a shorthand for a [get] hook that returns the value of the expression;
  • lines 45-50: the constructor assigns the attributes: these assignments go through the [set] hooks. The checks are therefore performed at construction time as well as on any later modification, without [set] methods;
  • line 54: the first name [" Paul "] is cleaned by the [set] hook;
  • line 57: the attribute [age] is modified directly, but through its [set] hook;
  • lines 60-66: we try to assign invalid values. The notation [$p->$attribut] uses the content of the variable [$attribut] as the attribute name. The [set] hooks throw their exceptions (lines 4-5 of the results);
  • line 69: the virtual attribute [identite] has no [set] hook: it is read-only (line 6 of the results);
  • line 75: the object has kept valid values. [var_dump] shows only three attributes: the virtual attribute [identite] does not exist in memory.

Property hooks have long existed in other languages (C#, Kotlin, Swift). They avoid writing getters and setters "just in case": you start with a simple public attribute and add a hook the day a check becomes necessary, without changing the code that uses the class.

docs.title: 5.10. Asymmetric visibility (PHP 8.4)
docs.text:
It often happens that an attribute must be readable by everyone but modifiable only by the class itself. People used to write a private attribute and a public getter. PHP 8.4 makes it possible to give different visibilities to the reading and the writing of an attribute: this is asymmetric visibility. The script [classes-24.php] puts it into practice with a bank account:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

class CompteBancaire
{
    // visibilité asymétrique : lecture publique, écriture privée
    public private(set) float $solde = 0.0;

    // la promotion de paramètre accepte aussi la visibilité asymétrique
    public function __construct(public private(set) string $titulaire)
    {
    }

    // seules les méthodes de la classe peuvent modifier le solde
    public function deposer(float $montant): void
    {
        if ($montant <= 0) {
            throw new \InvalidArgumentException("Le montant doit être positif");
        }
        $this->solde += $montant;
    }

    public function retirer(float $montant): void
    {
        if ($montant <= 0 || $montant > $this->solde) {
            throw new \InvalidArgumentException("Retrait de $montant impossible");
        }
        $this->solde -= $montant;
    }
}

// test
$compte = new CompteBancaire("Paul Langevin");
$compte->deposer(100);
$compte->retirer(30);
// lecture directe des attributs, sans getter
print "{$compte->titulaire} : {$compte->solde} euros\n";
// l'écriture depuis l'extérieur de la classe est interdite
try {
    $compte->solde = 1_000_000;
} catch (\Error $e) {
    print "Erreur : " . $e->getMessage() . "\n";
}
// la classe garde le contrôle de la validité du solde
try {
    $compte->retirer(500);
} catch (\InvalidArgumentException $e) {
    print "Erreur : " . $e->getMessage() . "\n";
}
print "{$compte->titulaire} : {$compte->solde} euros\n";

Results:

> php classes-24.php
Paul Langevin : 70 euros
Erreur : Cannot modify private(set) property CompteBancaire::$solde from global scope
Erreur : Retrait de 500 impossible
Paul Langevin : 70 euros

Comments

  • line 9: the attribute [solde] is public for reading ([public]) and private for writing ([private(set)]). Outside code can read [$compte->solde] but only the class's methods can modify it. You can also write [protected(set)]: derived classes can then modify the attribute;
  • line 12: asymmetric visibility is also possible for a promoted parameter;
  • lines 17-25: the [deposer] and [retirer] methods are the only means of modifying the balance. They check the validity of the operations;
  • line 39: the attributes are read directly, without a getter. The [{$expression}] notation inside a double-quoted string makes it possible to insert an expression more complex than a simple variable;
  • line 42: writing the balance from outside the class causes an error (line 3 of the results). The [_] character can be used as a thousands separator in a numeric literal (PHP 7.4);
  • line 48: the withdrawal is refused by the [retirer] method (line 4 of the results). The balance has not changed (line 5).

docs.title: 5.11. Read-only attributes and classes ([readonly])
docs.text:
An object whose state can no longer change after its construction is said to be immutable. Immutable objects greatly simplify programming: they can be shared between several parts of the code without fear that one of those parts will modify them. PHP 8.1 introduced read-only attributes (keyword [readonly]): such an attribute can only be initialized once, from inside the class. PHP 8.2 introduced read-only classes: all their attributes are then [readonly]. The script [classes-25.php] presents an immutable [Personne] class:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// classe en lecture seule : tous ses attributs sont [readonly]
final readonly class Personne
{
    public function __construct(
        public string $prenom,
        public string $nom,
        public int $age,
    ) {
        if ($age < 0) {
            throw new \InvalidArgumentException("L'âge doit être un entier positif ou nul");
        }
    }

    // « modifier » un objet immuable = créer une copie modifiée
    public function avecAge(int $age): static
    {
        // clone avec modification d'attributs (PHP 8.5)
        return clone($this, ["age" => $age]);
    }

    public function __toString(): string
    {
        return "[$this->prenom,$this->nom,$this->age]";
    }
}

// test
$p1 = new Personne("Paul", "Langevin", 48);
print "p1=$p1\n";
// un attribut [readonly] est initialisé une fois pour toutes
try {
    $p1->age = 49;
} catch (\Error $e) {
    print "Erreur 1 : " . $e->getMessage() . "\n";
}
// on ne peut pas non plus ajouter d'attributs à une classe [readonly]
try {
    $p1->adresse = "Paris";
} catch (\Error $e) {
    print "Erreur 2 : " . $e->getMessage() . "\n";
}
// une nouvelle personne, copie de la première avec un autre âge
$p2 = $p1->avecAge(49);
print "p1=$p1\n";
print "p2=$p2\n";

Results:

> php classes-25.php
p1=[Paul,Langevin,48]
Erreur 1 : Cannot modify readonly property Personne::$age
Erreur 2 : Cannot create dynamic property Personne::$adresse
p1=[Paul,Langevin,48]
p2=[Paul,Langevin,49]

Comments

  • line 7: the class is declared [readonly]: its three promoted attributes are read-only. The keyword [final], which we will study soon, forbids deriving from the class;
  • lines 10-12: the attributes are public: they can be read directly, without a getter. They cannot be modified: a getter would serve no purpose;
  • line 14: the constructor checks the validity of the age. An immutable object must be valid from its construction, since it will no longer change;
  • lines 20-24: "modifying" an immutable object consists of creating a modified copy of that object. This is what the [avecAge] method does. Its return type [static] (PHP 8.0) means "an object of the class on which the method was called". The difference from [self] only appears with derived classes: if a derived class inherits the method, the type [static] designates the derived class;
  • line 23: the [clone] operator creates a copy of the object [$this]. Since PHP 8.5, [clone] can be used like a function and receive as its second parameter an array of attributes to modify in the copy (clone with). Before PHP 8.5, you had to go through the magic method [__clone] or rebuild the object with [new];
  • line 37: modifying a [readonly] attribute causes an error (line 3 of the results);
  • line 43: a [readonly] class does not accept dynamic attributes either: this is an error and not a mere deprecation warning (line 4 of the results);
  • line 48: [$p2] is a new person; [$p1] has not changed (lines 5-6 of the results).

In the following chapters, we will often use [readonly] classes to represent data (the tax administration's tax data, the results of a tax calculation...).

docs.title: 5.12. An array of [Personne] objects
docs.text:
The following example [classes-07.php] shows that we can have arrays of objects:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

require_once __DIR__ . "/Personne.php";
use Exemples\Personne;

// test
// création d'un tableau d'objets Personne
// pour faciliter la compréhension du code, on ne gère pas l'éventuelle exception
$groupe = [new Personne("Paul", "Langevin", 48), new Personne("Sylvie", "Lefur", 70)];

// identité de ces personnes
for ($i = 0; $i < count($groupe); $i++) {
    print "groupe[$i]=$groupe[$i]\n";
}

// fin
exit;

Results:

> php classes-07.php
groupe[0]=[Paul,Langevin,48]
groupe[1]=[Sylvie,Lefur,70]

Comments

  • line 12: creation of an array of 2 people;
  • line 15: traversal of the array;
  • line 16: [$groupe[$i]] is an object of type [Personne]. The [Personne::__toString] method is used to display it.

docs.title: 5.13. Creating a class derived from the Personne class
docs.text:
In a file [Enseignant.php], we create the following [Enseignant] class:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Exemples;

// une classe dérivée de Personne
class Enseignant extends Personne
{
    // attribut : discipline enseignée
    private string $discipline;

    // getter et setter
    public function getDiscipline(): string
    {
        return $this->discipline;
    }

    public function setDiscipline(string $discipline): void
    {
        $this->discipline = $discipline;
    }

    // constructeur
    public function __construct(string $prénom, string $nom, int $âge, string $discipline)
    {
        // attributs parent
        parent::__construct($prénom, $nom, $âge);
        // autres attributs
        $this->setDiscipline($discipline);
    }

    // redéfinition de la méthode __toString de la classe parent
    #[\Override]
    public function __toString(): string
    {
        return "[" . parent::__toString() . ",$this->discipline]";
    }
}

Comments

  • line 7: the [Enseignant] class also belongs to the [Exemples] namespace;
  • line 10: the [Enseignant] class derives ([extends]) from the [Personne] class. The derived class [Enseignant] inherits the attributes and methods of its parent class;
  • line 13: the [Enseignant] class adds a new attribute [discipline] of its own;
  • line 27: the constructor of the [Enseignant] class receives 4 parameters:
    • 3 to initialize its parent class (first name, last name, age), line 30;
    • 1 for its own initialization (subject), line 32;
  • line 30: the derived class has access to the methods and constructors of its parent class through the keyword [parent::]. Here the parameters (first name, last name, age) are passed to the constructor of the parent class;
  • line 36: [#[\Override]] is a PHP attribute (PHP 8.3). An attribute, written between [#[] and []], is a piece of information attached to a class, a method, a parameter... that PHP or other tools can exploit. This one declares that the method that follows overrides a method of the parent class. If this is not the case (typo in the method name, method removed from the parent class...), PHP reports a fatal error. We will see an example a little further on;
  • lines 37-40: the [__toString] method of the derived class uses the [__toString] method of the parent class.

The [Enseignant] class is used by the following script [classes-08.php]:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// inclusion de la définition des deux classes
require_once __DIR__ . "/Personne.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/Enseignant.php";
// déclaration des deux classes utilisées
use Exemples\Personne;
use Exemples\Enseignant;

// test
// création d'un tableau d'objets Personne et dérivés
// pour la simplicité de l'exemple, on ne gère pas les exceptions
$groupe = [new Enseignant("Paul", "Langevin", 48, "anglais"), new Personne("Sylvie", "Lefur", 70)];

// identité de ces personnes
for ($i = 0; $i < count($groupe); $i++) {
    print "groupe[$i]=$groupe[$i]\n";
}
// fin
exit;

Results:

> php classes-08.php
groupe[0]=[[Paul,Langevin,48],anglais]
groupe[1]=[Sylvie,Lefur,70]

Comments

  • lines 7-8: we need to tell the PHP interpreter where the two classes [Enseignant, Personne] are. The order is important: the parent class [Personne] must be known at the moment the [Enseignant] class is defined;
  • lines 10-11: declaration of the full names of the two classes. This will allow us to designate them in the code simply by their name, without their namespace prefix;
  • line 16: we create an array containing an object of type [Enseignant] and an object of type [Personne];
  • lines 19-21: display the elements of the array;
  • line 20: the [__toString] method of each element [$groupe[$i]] will be called. The [Personne] class has a [__toString] method. The [Enseignant] class has two: that of its parent class and its own. One may wonder which one will be called. Execution shows that it is the one of the [Enseignant] class that was called. It is always so: when a method is called on an object, it is looked for in the following order: in the object's class, in its parent class if it has one, then in the parent class of the parent class, and so on. The search stops as soon as the method has been found.

docs.title: 5.14. Creating a second class derived from the Personne class
docs.text:
The following example creates a class [Etudiant] derived from the [Personne] class, in the file [Etudiant.php]:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Exemples;

// une seconde classe dérivée de Personne
class Etudiant extends Personne
{
    // attribut : formation suivie
    private string $formation;

    // getter et setter
    public function getFormation(): string
    {
        return $this->formation;
    }

    public function setFormation(string $formation): void
    {
        $this->formation = $formation;
    }

    // constructeur
    public function __construct(string $prénom, string $nom, int $âge, string $formation)
    {
        // attributs parent
        parent::__construct($prénom, $nom, $âge);
        // autres attributs
        $this->setFormation($formation);
    }

    // redéfinition de la méthode __toString de la classe parent
    #[\Override]
    public function __toString(): string
    {
        return "[" . parent::__toString() . ",$this->formation]";
    }
}

This class is used by the following script [classes-09.php]:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// inclusion et déclaration des classes utilisées par le script
require_once __DIR__ . "/Personne.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/Enseignant.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/Etudiant.php";
use Exemples\{Personne, Enseignant, Etudiant};

// test
// création d'un tableau d'objets Personne et dérivés
// pour faciliter la compréhension de l'exemple, on ne gère pas les exceptions
$groupe = [
    new Enseignant("Paul", "Langevin", 48, "anglais"),
    new Personne("Sylvie", "Lefur", 70),
    new Etudiant("Steve", "Boer", 23, "iup2 qualité"),
];

// identité de ces personnes
foreach ($groupe as $i => $personne) {
    print "groupe[$i]=$personne (" . $personne::class . ")\n";
}
// fin
exit;

Results:

> php classes-09.php
groupe[0]=[[Paul,Langevin,48],anglais] (Exemples\Enseignant)
groupe[1]=[Sylvie,Lefur,70] (Exemples\Personne)
groupe[2]=[[Steve,Boer,23],iup2 qualité] (Exemples\Etudiant)

Comments

  • line 10: a single [use] statement can declare several classes of the same namespace by grouping them in braces;
  • line 22: the array is traversed with [foreach], which gives both the index [$i] and the element [$personne];
  • line 23: the notation [$objet::class] (PHP 8.0) returns the full name of the object's class. It replaces the [get_class] function, whose use without a parameter has been deprecated since PHP 8.3.

docs.title: 5.15. Relationship between the constructor of a derived class and that of the parent class
docs.text:
In some object-oriented languages, the constructor of a derived class automatically calls that of its parent class. The following code [classes-16.php] shows that this is not the case with PHP:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

class Classe1
{
    // constructeur
    public function __construct()
    {
        print "constructeur de la classe Classe1\n";
    }
}

class Classe2 extends Classe1
{
    // constructeur
    public function __construct()
    {
        // le constructeur de la classe parent n'est pas appelé implicitement
        print "constructeur de la classe Classe2\n";
    }
}

class Classe3 extends Classe1
{
    // constructeur
    public function __construct()
    {
        // appel explicite du constructeur de la classe parent
        parent::__construct();
        // code propre à Classe3
        print "constructeur de la classe Classe3\n";
    }
}

class Classe4 extends Classe1
{
    // pas de constructeur : c'est celui de la classe parent qui est utilisé
}

// tests
print "test1---------\n";
new Classe2();
print "test2---------\n";
new Classe3();
print "test3---------\n";
new Classe4();

Results:

> php classes-16.php
test1---------
constructeur de la classe Classe2
test2---------
constructeur de la classe Classe1
constructeur de la classe Classe3
test3---------
constructeur de la classe Classe1

Comments

  • lines 15-23: the constructor of [Classe2] does not call that of its parent class: the latter is not executed (line 3 of the results);
  • line 31: the constructor of [Classe3] explicitly calls that of its parent class (lines 5-6 of the results);
  • lines 37-40: the [Classe4] class has no constructor. It then inherits that of its parent class, which is executed (line 8 of the results).

docs.title: 5.16. Overriding a method of the parent class
docs.text:
We have already seen that a method of the parent class could be overridden in a child class. Thus the [__toString] method of the [Personne] class was overridden in the child classes [Enseignant] and [Etudiant]. The script [classes-13.php] illustrates the concept again:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// classe principale
class Classe1
{
    public function f(): int
    {
        return 1;
    }

    public function g(): int
    {
        return 2;
    }
}

// classe dérivée
class Classe2 extends Classe1
{
    // on redéfinit la fonction f de la classe parent
    #[\Override]
    public function f(): int
    {
        return parent::f() + 10;
    }
}

// code
$c2 = new Classe2();
print $c2->f() . "\n";
print $c2->g() . "\n";
$c1 = new Classe1();
print $c1->f() . "\n";

Results:

> php classes-13.php
11
2
1

Comments

  • lines 7-18: the [Classe1] class defines two methods f and g;
  • lines 21-29: the [Classe2] class extends the [Classe1] class and overrides its method f. The [#[\Override]] attribute documents this override;
  • line 32: creates an object [$c2] of type [Classe2];
  • line 33: calls the method f of the object [$c2]. As it exists in the [Classe2] class, it is executed. It in turn calls the method f of the parent class with the notation [parent::f()];
  • line 34: calls the method g of the object [$c2]. As it does not exist in the [Classe2] class, it is looked for in the parent class, where it is found and executed;
  • line 35: creates an object [$c1] of type [Classe1];
  • line 36: calls the method f of the object [$c1]. It is the method f of the [Classe1] class that is executed.

Let us now see the value of the [#[\Override]] attribute. In the script [classes-10.php], the developer wanted to override the method f but got the name wrong:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// classe principale
class Classe1
{
    public function f(): int
    {
        return 1;
    }
}

// classe dérivée
class Classe2 extends Classe1
{
    // on croit redéfinir la méthode f de la classe parent
    // mais on s'est trompé de nom : l'attribut [Override] le détecte
    #[\Override]
    public function F2(): int
    {
        return parent::f() + 10;
    }
}

// code
$c2 = new Classe2();
print $c2->f() . "\n";

Results:

> php classes-10.php

Fatal error: Classe2::F2() has #[\Override] attribute, but no matching parent method exists in .../php8-oct-2026/scripts-console/classes/classes-10.php on line 21
Stack trace:
#0 {main}

Without the [#[\Override]] attribute, the method [F2] would simply be a new method of [Classe2] and the script would display [1] without reporting the slightest anomaly: the error would go unnoticed. With the attribute, PHP rejects the class as soon as it is loaded (line 3 of the results). In the rest of the course, we will systematically use [#[\Override]] on overridden methods.

docs.title: 5.17. Passing an object as a function parameter
docs.text:
Consider the following script [classes-14.php]:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// classe principale
class Classe1
{
    public function f(): int
    {
        return 1;
    }

    public function g(): int
    {
        return 2;
    }
}

// classe dérivée
class Classe2 extends Classe1
{
    // on redéfinit la fonction f de la classe parent
    #[\Override]
    public function f(): int
    {
        return parent::f() + 10;
    }
}

// le paramètre de la fonction est de type Classe1 ou dérivé
function doSomething(Classe1 $c1): void
{
    print $c1->f() + $c1->g() . "\n";
}

// code
// on crée un objet de type Classe2 dérivé de Classe1
$c2 = new Classe2();
// on appelle doSomething avec un objet de type Classe2
doSomething($c2);
// un objet d'un autre type est refusé
try {
    doSomething(new \stdClass());
} catch (\TypeError $e) {
    print "Erreur : " . $e->getMessage() . "\n";
}

Results:

> php classes-14.php
13
Erreur : doSomething(): Argument #1 ($c1) must be of type Classe1, stdClass given, called in .../php8-oct-2026/scripts-console/classes/classes-14.php on line 44

Comments

  • lines 7-18: the [Classe1] class;
  • lines 21-29: a class [Classe2] derived from [Classe1];
  • line 32: a function that expects a parameter of type [Classe1]. When the expected type is a class, the actual parameter can be an object of the expected type or of a derived type;
  • line 41: the [doSomething] function is called with a parameter of type [Classe2], whereas it is the type [Classe1] that is expected. This is accepted since [Classe2] derives from [Classe1] (line 2 of the results);
  • line 44: a [stdClass] object is not of type [Classe1]: the call causes a [TypeError] error (line 3 of the results).

docs.title: 5.18. Abstract classes
docs.text:
An abstract class is an incomplete class that cannot be instantiated. It must necessarily be derived to be usable.

What is an abstract class for? Sometimes there are classes that share one or more methods but differ in other methods or other attributes. It is then desirable to gather everything they have in common in a parent class. So far, we have no need for an abstract class. But suppose the child classes differ only in a method M: the signature of the method would be the same in all the child classes but its implementation would differ. To force the child classes to implement method M:

  • we declare the signature of method M in the parent class. As the parent class does not know how to implement it, the method is prefixed with the keyword [abstract]: this means that the implementation of method M is deferred to the child classes;
  • because the parent class is not fully implemented, it too is declared abstract with the same keyword [abstract]. This means that the class can no longer be instantiated. A child class that defines the implementation of method M must be created for the body of the parent class to be usable.

Here is an example [classes-15.php]:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres de fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// classe principale abstraite
abstract class Classe1
{
    // méthode connue de toutes les classes dérivées
    public function f(): int
    {
        return 1;
    }

    // méthode g abstraite - sera définie par les classes dérivées
    abstract public function g(): int;
}

// classe dérivée
class Classe2 extends Classe1
{
    // la méthode g de la classe parent doit être définie
    #[\Override]
    public function g(): int
    {
        return parent::f() + 10;
    }
}

// classe dérivée
class Classe3 extends Classe1
{
    // la méthode g de la classe parent doit être définie
    #[\Override]
    public function g(): int
    {
        return parent::f() + 20;
    }

    // on peut redéfinir la méthode f de la classe parent
    #[\Override]
    public function f(): int
    {
        return 2;
    }
}

// code
$c2 = new Classe2();
print $c2->f() . "\n";
print $c2->g() . "\n";
$c3 = new Classe3();
print $c3->f() . "\n";
print $c3->g() . "\n";
// une classe abstraite ne peut être instanciée
try {
    new Classe1();
} catch (\Error $e) {
    print "Erreur : " . $e->getMessage() . "\n";
}

Results:

> php classes-15.php
1
11
2
21
Erreur : Cannot instantiate abstract class Classe1

Comments

  • lines 7-17: the [Classe1] class is abstract because it does not know how to implement the method g of line 16. It must therefore necessarily be derived to be usable;
  • lines 20-28: the [Classe2] class extends the [Classe1] class and defines the method g of its parent class. The [#[\Override]] attribute also applies to the implementation of an abstract method;
