docs.title: 16.4.6. Example 6
docs.text:
PHP has an extension called [curl] that makes the capabilities of the [curl] tool available in a PHP program. It is enabled in [Laragon]'s PHP: you can check this with the [php -m] command, which lists the loaded extensions. If it were not, you would need to uncomment the [extension=curl] line in the [php.ini] file.

We are going to write a script [http-02.php] that will use the following JSON configuration file [config-http-02.json]:

{
    "localhost": {
        "timeout": 5,
        "url": "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-console/inet/http/pages"
    },
    "localhost-https": {
        "timeout": 5,
        "url": "https://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-console/inet/http/pages/bonjour.html",
        "verify-peer": false
    }
}

Each element of the [clé => valeur] dictionary has the following structure:

  • key: a name that will be used to name the file in which the document will be saved;
  • value is a dictionary with the following keys:
    • timeout: maximum time to wait for the server's response. Beyond that, the client will disconnect;
    • url: URL of the requested document;
    • verify-peer: should the server's certificate (HTTPS) be verified? True by default.

The code of the [http-02.php] script is as follows:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// client HTTP écrit avec l'extension [curl] de PHP
// sait parler HTTPS, suivre les redirections et recevoir un document envoyé par morceaux

// constantes
const CONFIG_FILE_NAME = "config-http-02.json";

// on récupère la configuration
$config = json_decode(file_get_contents(CONFIG_FILE_NAME), true);

// obtenir le texte HTML des URL du fichier de configuration
foreach ($config as $site => $infos) {
    // lecture de l'URL du site $site
    $résultat = getUrl($site, $infos["url"], $infos["timeout"], $infos["verify-peer"] ?? true);
    // affichage résultat
    print "$résultat\n";
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function getUrl(string $site, string $url, int $timeout, bool $verifyPeer = true): string
{
    // lit l'URL $url et la stocke dans le fichier output/$site.html
    //
    // suivi
    print "Client : début de la communication avec le serveur [$site] ----------------------------\n";
    // initialisation d'une session cURL : depuis PHP 8.0, [curl_init] rend un objet [CurlHandle]
    $curl = curl_init($url);
    if ($curl === false) {
        return "Erreur lors de l'initialisation de la session cURL pour le site [$site]";
    }
    // options de curl
    $options = [
        // mode verbose : les échanges client / serveur sont affichés...
        CURLOPT_VERBOSE => true,
        // ... sur la sortie standard (par défaut, c'est la sortie d'erreur)
        CURLOPT_STDERR => STDOUT,
        // nouvelle connexion - pas de cache
        CURLOPT_FRESH_CONNECT => true,
        // timeout de la requête (en secondes)
        CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => $timeout,
        CURLOPT_CONNECTTIMEOUT => $timeout,
        // vérifier ou non la validité du certificat du serveur (HTTPS)
        CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER => $verifyPeer,
        CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST => $verifyPeer ? 2 : 0,
        // suivre les redirections
        CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION => true,
        // récupération du document demandé sous la forme d'une chaîne de caractères
        CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
    ];
    // paramétrage de curl
    curl_setopt_array($curl, $options);
    // exécution de la requête
    $pageContent = curl_exec($curl);
    // la session cURL est fermée automatiquement quand l'objet $curl disparaît
    // ([curl_close] est inutile depuis PHP 8.0 et obsolète depuis PHP 8.5)
    //
    // exploitation du résultat
    if ($pageContent === false) {
        // il y a eu une erreur de communication
        return "Erreur de communication avec le serveur [$site] : " . curl_error($curl);
    }
    // enregistrement du résultat dans output/$site.html
    if (!is_dir("output")) {
        mkdir("output");
    }
    if (file_put_contents("output/$site.html", $pageContent) === false) {
        return "Erreur lors de la création du fichier [output/$site.html]";
    }
    // retour avec succès
    return "Fin de la communication avec le serveur [$site]. Vérifiez le fichier [output/$site.html]";
}

Comments:

  • line 12: we use the configuration file to create the [$config] dictionary;
  • line 15: we loop over the list of sites found in the configuration;
  • line 17: for each site, we call the [getUrl] function, which will download the URL [$infos["url"]] with a timeout [$infos["timeout"]];
  • line 30: we start a [curl] session. [curl_init] does not yet connect to the web server. Since PHP 8.0, it returns an object of the [CurlHandle] class (and no longer a resource), which will be a parameter for all subsequent [curl] functions. If the session initialization fails, the function returns the boolean [false];
  • lines 35-52: the [$options] dictionary will configure the [curl] connection to the server:
    • [CURLOPT_VERBOSE]: displays the client / server exchanges, like the [--verbose] option of the [curl] tool. [CURLOPT_STDERR] sends them to the standard output [STDOUT] rather than to the error output, which keeps the displays in order;
    • [CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER] and [CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST]: verification of the server's certificate and of the name it contains;
    • [CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION]: follow redirections, like the [--location] option;
    • [CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER]: return the document received as a string;
  • line 54: the connection options are passed to the [$curl] object;
  • line 56: connection to the requested URL with the defined options. Because of the [CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true] option, the [curl_exec] function returns the document sent by the server as a string, stripped of the chunk sizes if it was sent in chunks. The [curl_exec] function returns the boolean [false] if the connection fails. The [curl_error] function then gives the cause of the error;
  • line 57: the PHP 7 course closed the session with the [curl_close] function. Since PHP 8.0, this function no longer does anything: the session is closed when the [CurlHandle] object is no longer used. It has been deprecated since PHP 8.5;
  • line 69: we save the page received in a local file.

When we run the [http-02.php] script, we get the following console results:

*   Certificate level 0: Public key type RSA (2048/112 Bits/secBits), signed using sha256WithRSAEncryption
* using HTTP/1.x
> GET /php8-oct-2026/scripts-console/inet/http/pages/bonjour.html HTTP/1.1

We get the same exchanges as with the [curl] tool: the lines beginning with [>] are sent to the server, those beginning with [<] are received from the server, those beginning with [*] are information from [curl]. The redirection was followed and the HTTPS connection was established.

docs.title: 16.4.7. Conclusion
docs.text: In this section, we have discovered the HTTP protocol and written a script [http-02.php] capable of downloading a URL from the web. In the next chapter, we will use the [HttpClient] component of the Symfony framework for this.

docs.title: 16.5. The SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) protocol
16.5.1. Introduction
docs.text:
In this chapter:

  • [Serveur B] will be a local SMTP server that we will install;
  • [Client A] will be an SMTP client in various forms:
    • the [tcp-client.php] client, to discover the SMTP protocol;
    • a PHP script replaying the SMTP protocol discovered with [tcp-client.php];
    • a PHP script using the [Symfony Mailer] library, which can send all kinds of emails.

docs.title: 16.5.2. Installing a test SMTP server: [Mailpit]
docs.text:
The PHP 7 course installed the [hMailServer] mail server, which is no longer maintained, and configured it to relay emails through Gmail's SMTP server. Instead, we will use [Mailpit] (https://mailpit.axllent.org), a free tool designed for developers:

  • it is an SMTP server that accepts all the emails sent to it, whatever the sender and recipient, but does not deliver them: it keeps them. We can therefore send emails to any address without any risk of bothering anyone;
  • it offers a web interface for reading the emails received;
  • it also offers a POP3 server, which we will use to read emails programmatically;
  • it is a single executable, with no installation.

[Mailpit] can be downloaded from the page https://github.com/axllent/mailpit/releases. On Windows, take the [mailpit-windows-amd64.zip] file of the most recent version and copy the [mailpit.exe] file it contains into the [inet/mailpit] folder of the course code. This folder already contains the following files:

mailpit
├── mailpit.bat
├── mailpit-securise.bat
├── pop3-users.txt
├── relay.yml
└── smtp-users.txt

The [pop3-users.txt] file defines the users of [Mailpit]'s POP3 server in the form [utilisateur:mot de passe] (user:password). There is only one:

guest:guest

The [mailpit.bat] file starts [Mailpit] with this users file:

@echo off
rem instance principale de Mailpit : SMTP sur le port 1025, POP3 sur le port 1110, interface web sur le port 8025
"%~dp0mailpit.exe" --pop3-auth-file "%~dp0pop3-users.txt"
  • [%~dp0] refers to the folder of the [.bat] file: [mailpit.bat] can therefore be launched from any folder, for example by double-clicking on it in Windows Explorer;
  • the [--pop3-auth-file] option enables [Mailpit]'s POP3 server.

You can also type the command directly in a terminal opened in the [inet/mailpit] folder: [.\mailpit.exe --pop3-auth-file pop3-users.txt]. [Mailpit] then displays log lines indicating that it offers three services:

  • an SMTP server on port 1025 (the standard port of the SMTP protocol is port 25, but ports below 1024 are often reserved or blocked);
  • a POP3 server on port 1110 (the standard port is port 110);
  • a web interface at the URL [http://localhost:8025].

The terminal must remain open as long as you want to use [Mailpit]: the [Ctrl-C] key combination stops it. The emails received are kept in memory as long as [Mailpit] is running. We will meet [Mailpit] again in the following versions of the tax calculation server, which will send emails to their administrator.

The second file, [mailpit-securise.bat], starts a second instance of [Mailpit], which we will use later to study secure connections:

@echo off
rem instance securisee de Mailpit : SMTP avec STARTTLS et authentification obligatoires sur le port 1587,
rem interface web en HTTPS sur le port 8026, relais des messages vers l instance principale (port 1025)
"%~dp0mailpit.exe" --smtp 0.0.0.0:1587 --listen 0.0.0.0:8026 --ui-tls-cert sans:localhost --ui-tls-key sans:localhost --smtp-tls-cert sans:localhost --smtp-tls-key sans:localhost --smtp-require-starttls --smtp-auth-file "%~dp0smtp-users.txt" --smtp-relay-config "%~dp0relay.yml" --smtp-relay-all
  • [--smtp 0.0.0.0:1587]: the SMTP server of this instance listens on port 1587;
  • [--listen 0.0.0.0:8026 --ui-tls-cert sans:localhost --ui-tls-key sans:localhost]: its web interface is on port 8026 (port 8025 is taken by the first instance), over HTTPS;
  • [--smtp-tls-cert sans:localhost --smtp-tls-key sans:localhost]: [Mailpit] creates a self-signed certificate for the [localhost] machine itself. This certificate allows it to encrypt the exchanges with its clients;
  • [--smtp-require-starttls]: clients must encrypt the connection (the STARTTLS command, which we will see) before sending an email;
  • [--smtp-auth-file smtp-users.txt]: clients must authenticate with one of the accounts in the [smtp-users.txt] file. There is only one, [guest@localhost] with the password [guest];
  • [--smtp-relay-config relay.yml --smtp-relay-all]: the emails received are relayed to the SMTP server defined in [relay.yml], i.e. to the first instance of [Mailpit] (localhost, port 1025):
# relais SMTP de l'instance « sécurisée » de Mailpit (port 1587)
# vers l'instance principale (port 1025)
host: localhost
port: 1025

This second instance plays the role that a public SMTP server such as Gmail's ([smtp.gmail.com], port 587) would play, which also requires an encrypted connection and authentication. We will use it with a Gmail account when the time comes, for those who have one.

Let's start the first instance of [Mailpit] and open its web interface [http://localhost:8025] with a browser:

We will see this page fill up as we go through the examples.

docs.title: 16.5.3. The SMTP protocol
docs.text:
We are going to discover the SMTP protocol with the following environment:

  • client A will be the generic TCP client [tcp-client.php];
  • server B will be [Mailpit]'s SMTP server;
  • client A will ask server B to deliver an email to the user [guest@localhost];
  • we will check with [Mailpit]'s web interface that the email was indeed received.

In a terminal opened in the [inet/utilitaires] folder, we start the client and type the SMTP protocol commands:

> php tcp-client.php --quit bye localhost 1025
Client [127.0.0.1:50072] connecté au serveur [localhost:1025]
Tapez vos commandes (bye pour arrêter) :
<-- [220 vm Mailpit ESMTP Service ready]
EHLO localhost
<-- [250-vm greets localhost]
<-- [250-SIZE 52428800]
<-- [250-ENHANCEDSTATUSCODES]
<-- [250-8BITMIME]
<-- [250 SMTPUTF8]
MAIL FROM: <guest@localhost>
<-- [250 2.1.0 Ok]
RCPT TO: <guest@localhost>
<-- [250 2.1.5 Ok]
DATA
<-- [354 Start mail input; end with <CR><LF>.<CR><LF>]
Subject: test
From: guest@localhost
To: guest@localhost

ligne 1
ligne 2
.
<-- [250 2.0.0 Ok: queued as 0d0daBzXhAGBiM8Aw3oxZ7]
QUIT
<-- [221 2.0.0 vm Mailpit ESMTP Service closing transmission channel]
Perte de la connexion avec le serveur...
Fin du client
  • [php tcp-client.php --quit bye localhost 1025]: we connect to port 1025 of the local machine, where [Mailpit]'s SMTP service operates. The [--quit bye] argument indicates that the user will leave the program by typing the [bye] command. Without this argument, the program's end command is [quit]. But [QUIT] is also an SMTP protocol command. We must therefore avoid this ambiguity;
  • [220 vm Mailpit ESMTP Service ready]: as soon as the connection is made, the server sends its welcome message. Code [220] indicates that the server is ready. [vm] is the name of the machine running [Mailpit]: you will get the name of your computer;
  • [EHLO localhost]: the client sends the [EHLO nom-de-la-machine-cliente] command (client machine name). The server replies with a series of lines of the form [250-xx], the last one having the form [250 xx] (a space and not a hyphen after the code). Code [250] indicates the success of the command sent by the client. The following lines indicate the SMTP protocol extensions the server knows, for example the maximum size of a message [SIZE];
  • [MAIL FROM: <guest@localhost>]: the client indicates the sender of the message, and the server accepts it (code 250);
  • [RCPT TO: <guest@localhost>]: the client indicates the recipient of the message. There could be several [RCPT TO] commands for several recipients;
  • [DATA]: this command tells the server that the client is going to send the content of the message. The server replies with code [354] and indicates how to end the message;
  • the client then sends a list of lines of text ending with a line containing only a single dot. The message may begin with [Subject:, From:, To:] lines to define respectively the subject of the message, the sender and the recipient. These headers must be followed by an empty line, then comes the text of the message;
  • [250 2.0.0 Ok: queued as ...]: once the server has received the line containing only a single dot, it queues the message for delivery;
  • [QUIT]: the client tells the server that it has finished. The server replies with code [221], then closes the connection, which the client detects.

Let's check in [Mailpit]'s web interface that the user [guest@localhost] has indeed received the message:

We find the sender [From], the recipient [To], the subject [Subject] and the text of the message. The [Headers] tab displays all the message headers and the [Raw] tab the raw text received by [Mailpit].

Our [tcp-client.php] client managed to send the message. We have the basics to create an SMTP client written in PHP.

docs.title: 16.5.4. A basic SMTP client written in PHP
docs.text:
We are going to reproduce in PHP what we have just learned about the SMTP protocol.

The [inet/smtp/smtp-01.php] script is configured by the following JSON file [config-smtp-01.json]:

{
    "mail to localhost via localhost": {
        "smtp-server": "localhost",
        "smtp-port": 1025,
        "from": "guest@localhost",
        "to": "guest@localhost",
        "subject": "to localhost via localhost",
        "message": "ligne 1\nligne 2\nligne 3"
    },
    "mail to gmail via localhost": {
        "smtp-server": "localhost",
        "smtp-port": 1025,
        "from": "guest@localhost",
        "to": "php8parlexemple@gmail.com",
        "subject": "to gmail via localhost",
        "message": "ligne 1\nligne 2\nligne 3"
    },
    "mail via a secure server": {
        "smtp-server": "localhost",
        "smtp-port": 1587,
        "from": "guest@localhost",
        "to": "guest@localhost",
        "subject": "via a secure server",
        "message": "ligne 1\nligne 2\nligne 3"
    }
}

[config-smtp-01.json] is a dictionary each of whose elements has the form [nom => infos]. The [infos] value is itself a dictionary with the following keys and values:

  • [smtp-server]: the name of the SMTP server to use;
  • [smtp-port]: the port number of the SMTP service;
  • [from]: the sender of the message;
  • [to]: the recipient of the message;
  • [subject]: the subject of the message;
  • [message]: the message to send.

There are three sends:

  • the 1st uses [Mailpit]'s SMTP server to send an email to the user [guest@localhost];
  • the 2nd uses the same server to send an email to a Gmail address. [Mailpit] will keep this email without delivering it;
  • the 3rd uses the second instance of [Mailpit], the one on port 1587, which requires an encrypted connection. So [mailpit-securise.bat] must have been launched.

The code [smtp-01.php] of the SMTP client is as follows:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// client SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) permettant d'envoyer un message
// protocole de communication SMTP client-serveur
// -> client se connecte sur le port du serveur SMTP (25, 587, 1025...)
// <- serveur lui envoie un message de bienvenue
// -> client envoie la commande EHLO nom de sa machine
// <- serveur répond OK ou non
// -> client envoie la commande MAIL FROM: <expéditeur>
// <- serveur répond OK ou non
// -> client envoie la commande RCPT TO: <destinataire>
// <- serveur répond OK ou non
// -> client envoie la commande DATA
// <- serveur répond OK ou non
// -> client envoie toutes les lignes de son message et termine avec une ligne contenant le
// seul caractère .
// <- serveur répond OK ou non
// -> client envoie la commande QUIT
// <- serveur répond OK ou non
// les réponses du serveur ont la forme xxx texte où xxx est un nombre à 3 chiffres. Tout
// nombre xxx >= 400 signale une erreur.
// La réponse peut comporter plusieurs lignes de la forme xxx-texte, sauf la dernière
// qui a la forme xxx texte (espace après le code)
// les lignes de texte échangées doivent se terminer par les caractères CR (13) et LF (10)

// les paramètres de l'envoi des courriers
const CONFIG_FILE_NAME = "config-smtp-01.json";

// on récupère la configuration
$mails = json_decode(file_get_contents(CONFIG_FILE_NAME), true);

// envoi des courriers
foreach ($mails as $name => $infos) {
    // suivi
    print "Envoi du mail [$name]\n";
    // envoi du courrier
    $résultat = sendmail($infos, verbose: true);
    // affichage résultat
    print "$résultat\n";
}
// fin
print "Terminé\n";

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function sendmail(array $infos, bool $verbose = true): string
{
    // envoie le message décrit par [$infos]
    // si $verbose=true, fait un suivi des échanges client-serveur
    //
    // le nom de la machine cliente
    $client = gethostname();
    // ouverture d'une connexion avec le serveur SMTP
    $connexion = @stream_socket_client("tcp://{$infos["smtp-server"]}:{$infos["smtp-port"]}", $numErreur, $erreur);
    if ($connexion === false) {
        return "Échec de la connexion au serveur [{$infos["smtp-server"]}:{$infos["smtp-port"]}] : $erreur";
    }
    // $connexion représente un flux de communication bidirectionnel
    // entre le client (ce programme) et le serveur SMTP contacté
    try {
        // après la connexion, le serveur envoie un message de bienvenue qu'on lit
        sendCommand($connexion, "", $verbose);
        // commande EHLO
        sendCommand($connexion, "EHLO $client", $verbose);
        // commande MAIL FROM:
        sendCommand($connexion, "MAIL FROM: <{$infos["from"]}>", $verbose);
        // commande RCPT TO:
        sendCommand($connexion, "RCPT TO: <{$infos["to"]}>", $verbose);
        // commande DATA
        sendCommand($connexion, "DATA", $verbose);
        // le message : des entêtes (From, To, Subject), une ligne vide, le texte
        // et une ligne réduite à un point
        // les fins de ligne du texte doivent être \r\n
        $texte = str_replace("\n", "\r\n", $infos["message"]);
        // une ligne du texte qui commence par un point doit commencer par deux points
        $texte = preg_replace('/^\./m', '..', $texte);
        $data = "From: {$infos["from"]}\r\nTo: {$infos["to"]}\r\nSubject: {$infos["subject"]}\r\n\r\n$texte\r\n.";
        sendCommand($connexion, $data, $verbose);
        // commande QUIT
        sendCommand($connexion, "QUIT", $verbose);
        return "Message envoyé";
    } catch (RuntimeException $ex) {
        // le serveur a signalé une erreur
        return "Erreur : " . $ex->getMessage();
    } finally {
        // dans tous les cas, on ferme la connexion
        fclose($connexion);
    }
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function sendCommand($connexion, string $commande, bool $verbose): void
{
    // envoie $commande dans le canal $connexion et lit la réponse du serveur
    // mode verbeux si $verbose=true
    // lance une RuntimeException si le serveur signale une erreur
    //
    // envoi de la commande si elle n'est pas vide
    if ($commande !== "") {
        fwrite($connexion, "$commande\r\n");
        if ($verbose) {
            affiche($commande, 1);
        }
    }
    // lecture de la réponse : des lignes [xxx-texte] terminées par une ligne [xxx texte]
    do {
        $réponse = fgets($connexion);
        if ($réponse === false) {
            throw new RuntimeException("le serveur a fermé la connexion");
        }
        if ($verbose) {
            affiche($réponse, 2);
        }
    } while (substr($réponse, 3, 1) === "-");
    // code de la réponse
    $code = (int) substr($réponse, 0, 3);
    // erreur renvoyée par le serveur ?
    if ($code >= 400) {
        throw new RuntimeException(rtrim(substr($réponse, 4)));
    }
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function affiche(string $échange, int $sens): void
{
    // affiche $échange à l'écran
    // si $sens=1 affiche --> [$échange] (avec des fins de ligne \n à la place de \r\n)
    // si $sens=2 affiche <-- [$échange] sans les caractères de fin de ligne \r\n
    print match ($sens) {
        1 => "--> [" . str_replace("\r\n", "\n", $échange) . "]\n",
        2 => "<-- [" . rtrim($échange, "\r\n") . "]\n",
    };
}

Comments:

  • line 32: we use the configuration file. The 2nd parameter [true] of [json_decode] requests associative arrays rather than objects;
  • line 35: we loop over the elements of the [$mails] dictionary. Each element has the form [name => infos], where [name] is any name and [infos] a dictionary containing the information needed to send an email;
  • line 39: sending the email is handled by the [sendmail] function, which takes two parameters:
    • $infos: the dictionary containing the information needed for sending;
    • $verbose: a boolean indicating whether or not the client / server exchanges should be displayed on the console. Note the named argument [verbose: true] (PHP 8.0), which makes the call more readable than a plain [true];
  • line 53: the name of the client machine, used by the EHLO command;
  • line 55: opening a connection with the SMTP server. The PHP 7 course used the [fsockopen] function, which is still available. [stream_socket_client] is more general: it is the one we used in [tcp-client.php];
  • lines 61-86: the [sendmail] function sends the various commands an SMTP client must send: reading the welcome message, EHLO, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO, DATA, the message, QUIT. Each command is sent by the [sendCommand] function, which throws a [RuntimeException] exception if the server replies with an error code. All the commands are therefore in a [try] block: the first error takes us into the [catch] block, which returns the error message. The [finally] block is executed in all cases: that is where we close the connection. The code is thus much shorter than that of the PHP 7 course, which tested the result of each command;
  • lines 75-78: preparing the message. The lines of the message must end with \r\n. If a line of the text contains only a dot, the server will think the message is finished. To avoid this, the SMTP protocol requires the client to double the dot that begins a line: the server will remove this extra dot. The regular expression [/^\./m] (m option: multiline) denotes a dot at the beginning of a line;
  • line 93: the [sendCommand] function is responsible for sending the client's commands to the SMTP server and reading the response. It takes three parameters:
    • [$connexion]: the connection linking the client to the server;
    • [$commande]: the command to send. If it is empty, nothing is sent: we just read a response (the case of the welcome message);
    • [$verbose]: if true, the client / server exchanges are displayed on the console;
  • lines 107-115: reading all the lines of the response. Each line has the form [XXX-YYY], where XXX is a numeric code, except the last line of the response, which has the form [XXX YYY] (no - character). The [do ... while] loop therefore stops when the 4th character of the line is not a hyphen;
  • line 119: if the numeric code XXX is greater than or equal to 400, the server has returned an error (4xx codes signal temporary errors, 5xx codes permanent errors);
  • line 125: the [affiche] function uses a [match] expression to choose the text to display according to the direction of the exchange.

Running the script gives the following console results:

> php smtp-01.php
Envoi du mail [mail to localhost via localhost]
<-- [220 vm Mailpit ESMTP Service ready]
--> [EHLO vm]
<-- [250-vm greets vm]
<-- [250-SIZE 52428800]
<-- [250-ENHANCEDSTATUSCODES]
<-- [250-8BITMIME]
<-- [250 SMTPUTF8]
--> [MAIL FROM: <guest@localhost>]
<-- [250 2.1.0 Ok]
--> [RCPT TO: <guest@localhost>]
<-- [250 2.1.5 Ok]
--> [DATA]
<-- [354 Start mail input; end with <CR><LF>.<CR><LF>]
--> [From: guest@localhost
To: guest@localhost
Subject: to localhost via localhost

ligne 1
ligne 2
ligne 3
.]
<-- [250 2.0.0 Ok: queued as 5SoJJqMUYg3ZrkBqoVKLQo]
--> [QUIT]
<-- [221 2.0.0 vm Mailpit ESMTP Service closing transmission channel]
Message envoyé
Envoi du mail [mail to gmail via localhost]
<-- [220 vm Mailpit ESMTP Service ready]
--> [EHLO vm]
<-- [250-vm greets vm]
<-- [250-SIZE 52428800]
<-- [250-ENHANCEDSTATUSCODES]
<-- [250-8BITMIME]
<-- [250 SMTPUTF8]
--> [MAIL FROM: <guest@localhost>]
<-- [250 2.1.0 Ok]
--> [RCPT TO: <php8parlexemple@gmail.com>]
<-- [250 2.1.5 Ok]
--> [DATA]
<-- [354 Start mail input; end with <CR><LF>.<CR><LF>]
--> [From: guest@localhost
To: php8parlexemple@gmail.com
Subject: to gmail via localhost

ligne 1
ligne 2
ligne 3
.]
<-- [250 2.0.0 Ok: queued as 78JcBpdQn6ACCrBcnniPz3]
--> [QUIT]
<-- [221 2.0.0 vm Mailpit ESMTP Service closing transmission channel]
Message envoyé
Envoi du mail [mail via a secure server]
<-- [220 vm Mailpit ESMTP Service ready]
--> [EHLO vm]
<-- [250-vm greets vm]
<-- [250-SIZE 52428800]
<-- [250-STARTTLS]
<-- [250-AUTH LOGIN PLAIN]
<-- [250-ENHANCEDSTATUSCODES]
<-- [250-8BITMIME]
<-- [250 SMTPUTF8]
--> [MAIL FROM: <guest@localhost>]
<-- [530 5.7.0 Must issue a STARTTLS command first]
Erreur : 5.7.0 Must issue a STARTTLS command first
Terminé
  • the first two sends go well;
  • the third fails: after the [MAIL FROM] command, the server on port 1587 sends an error code 530 with the message [Must issue a STARTTLS command first]. Note that in its response to the EHLO command, it announced the [STARTTLS] extension and the [AUTH LOGIN PLAIN] authentication. The SMTP client must first encrypt the connection (STARTTLS command) and then authenticate (AUTH command). Our client did not do so and is therefore rejected. Gmail's SMTP server ([smtp.gmail.com], port 587) responds in exactly the same way.

[Mailpit]'s web interface shows the emails received. Note that the email intended for [php8parlexemple@gmail.com] is indeed there: [Mailpit] did not forward it to Gmail.

docs.title: 16.5.5. A second SMTP client written with the [Symfony Mailer] library
docs.text:
The previous client has at least two shortcomings:

  • it cannot use a secure connection if the server requires one;
  • it cannot attach files to the message.

In our new script, we are going to use the [Symfony Mailer] library (https://symfony.com/doc/current/mailer.html). The PHP 7 course used the [SwiftMailer] library, which has not been maintained since 2021: [Symfony Mailer] is its successor, written by the same team. The library was installed with the course's other dependencies by the [composer install] command (see the [composer.json] file at the root of the [php8-oct-2026] folder) and is in the [vendor/symfony/mailer] folder. It uses the [symfony/mime] component, which can build messages of any form.

The [inet/smtp/smtp-02.php] script will use the following JSON configuration file [config-smtp-02.json]:

{
    "mail to localhost via localhost": {
        "smtp-server": "localhost",
        "smtp-port": 1025,
        "from": "guest@localhost",
        "to": "guest@localhost",
        "subject": "test-localhost",
        "message": "ligne 1\nligne 2\nligne 3",
        "tls": false,
        "attachments": [
            "/attachments/Hello from Symfony Mailer.docx",
            "/attachments/Hello from Symfony Mailer.pdf",
            "/attachments/Hello from Symfony Mailer.odt",
            "/attachments/Cours-Tutoriels-Serge-Tahé-1568x268.png",
            "/attachments/test-localhost.eml"
        ]
    },
    "mail to localhost via a secure server": {
        "smtp-server": "localhost",
        "smtp-port": 1587,
        "from": "guest@localhost",
        "to": "guest@localhost",
        "subject": "test-secure-server",
        "message": "ligne 1\nligne 2\nligne 3",
        "tls": true,
        "user": "guest@localhost",
        "password": "guest",
        "verify-peer": false,
        "attachments": [
            "/attachments/Hello from Symfony Mailer.pdf"
        ]
    },
    "mail to gmail via gmail": {
        "enabled": false,
        "smtp-server": "smtp.gmail.com",
        "smtp-port": 587,
        "from": "php8parlexemple@gmail.com",
        "to": "php8parlexemple@gmail.com",
        "subject": "test-gmail-via-gmail",
        "message": "ligne 1\nligne 2\nligne 3",
        "tls": true,
        "user": "php8parlexemple@gmail.com",
        "password": "mot de passe d'application",
        "verify-peer": true,
        "attachments": [
            "/attachments/Hello from Symfony Mailer.docx",
            "/attachments/Hello from Symfony Mailer.pdf",
            "/attachments/Hello from Symfony Mailer.odt",
            "/attachments/Cours-Tutoriels-Serge-Tahé-1568x268.png",
            "/attachments/test-localhost.eml"
        ]
    }
}

We find the same entries as in the [config-smtp-01.json] file, with additional entries:

  • [tls]: when [true], indicates that a secure and authenticated connection with the SMTP server must be used. In that case, the following entries must be added:
    • [user]: the name of the user authenticating the connection;
    • [password]: their password;
    • [verify-peer]: should the certificate sent by the server be verified? This must be done with a public server. With our test server, whose certificate is self-signed, it must be set to [false];
  • [attachments]: gives the names of the files to attach to the email. They are in the [smtp/attachments] folder;
  • [enabled]: when [false], disables the send. This is the case of the 3rd send, which uses Gmail's SMTP server.

To use Gmail's SMTP server, you need a Gmail account (replace [php8parlexemple@gmail.com] with your address) on which 2-Step Verification is enabled, and you must create an "app password" for it in the [Security] section of Google account management. This 16-letter password replaces the account password in applications such as ours. Put it in the [password] entry and set [enabled] to [true].

The code of the [smtp-02.php] script is as follows:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// client SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) écrit avec la bibliothèque [Symfony Mailer]
// sait utiliser une connexion sécurisée et joindre des fichiers au message

// dépendances
require_once __DIR__ . "/../../../vendor/autoload.php";

use Symfony\Component\Mailer\Mailer;
use Symfony\Component\Mailer\Transport;
use Symfony\Component\Mime\Email;

// les paramètres de l'envoi des courriers : le fichier de configuration
// peut être passé en argument (php smtp-02.php config.json)
$configFileName = $argv[1] ?? "config-smtp-02.json";

// on récupère la configuration
$mails = json_decode(file_get_contents($configFileName), true);

// envoi des courriers
foreach ($mails as $name => $infos) {
    // envoi désactivé dans la configuration ?
    if (($infos["enabled"] ?? true) === false) {
        print "Envoi du mail [$name] désactivé\n";
        continue;
    }
    // suivi
    print "Envoi du mail [$name]\n";
    // envoi du courrier
    $résultat = sendmail($name, $infos);
    // affichage résultat
    print "$résultat\n";
}
// fin
print "Terminé\n";

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function sendmail(string $name, array $infos): string
{
    // envoie $infos["message"] au serveur SMTP $infos["smtp-server"] sur le port $infos["smtp-port"]
    // si $infos["tls"] est vrai, la connexion est sécurisée et authentifiée
    // le mail est envoyé de la part de $infos["from"]
    // pour le destinataire $infos["to"]
    // les documents $infos["attachments"] sont joints au message
    // le message a le sujet $infos["subject"]
    //
    try {
        // création du message
        $email = (new Email())
            // expéditeur
            ->from($infos["from"])
            // destinataire (il peut y en avoir plusieurs : to(a, b, c), cc(...), bcc(...))
            ->to($infos["to"])
            // sujet du message
            ->subject($infos["subject"])
            // texte du message
            ->text($infos["message"])
            // variante HTML du texte
            ->html("<b>" . str_replace("\n", "<br/>", $infos["message"]) . "</b>");
        // pièces jointes
        foreach ($infos["attachments"] as $attachment) {
            // chemin de la pièce jointe
            $fileName = __DIR__ . $attachment;
            // on vérifie que le fichier existe
            if (file_exists($fileName)) {
                // on joint le document au message
                $email->attachFromPath($fileName);
            } else {
                print "La pièce jointe [$fileName] n'existe pas\n";
            }
        }
        // le transport du message : un DSN (Data Source Name) de la forme
        // smtp://utilisateur:motdepasse@serveur:port?options
        $dsn = "smtp://{$infos["smtp-server"]}:{$infos["smtp-port"]}";
        if ($infos["tls"]) {
            // connexion sécurisée (STARTTLS) et authentifiée
            $verifyPeer = ($infos["verify-peer"] ?? true) ? 1 : 0;
            $dsn = sprintf("smtp://%s:%s@%s:%d?require_tls=1&verify_peer=%d",
                rawurlencode($infos["user"]), rawurlencode($infos["password"]),
                $infos["smtp-server"], $infos["smtp-port"], $verifyPeer);
        }
        // le gestionnaire de l'envoi
        $mailer = new Mailer(Transport::fromDsn($dsn));
        // envoi du message
        $mailer->send($email);
        // fin
        return "Message [$name] envoyé";
    } catch (Throwable $ex) {
        // erreur
        return "Erreur lors de l'envoi du message [$name] : " . $ex->getMessage();
    }
}

Comments:

  • line 9: we load the [vendor/autoload.php] file created by Composer. This file loads the class definition files of the libraries as soon as these classes are first used. It saves us from writing as many [require] statements as there are [Symfony Mailer] classes and interfaces we are going to use. The path is relative to the script's folder ([__DIR__]): the script works wherever the [php8-oct-2026] folder is located;
  • lines 11-13: the [Symfony Mailer] classes are in namespaces. The [use] statements allow us to refer to them by their short names;
  • line 17: the configuration file can be passed as an argument to the script; otherwise, it is [config-smtp-02.json];
  • line 25: a send is disabled if its [enabled] entry is [false]. The [??] operator returns [true] if the entry is missing;
  • line 40: the new [sendmail] function, which has two parameters:
    • [$name], which is used to distinguish the messages from one another;
    • [$infos]: the information needed to send the message to its recipient;
  • lines 51-61: we define the message using the [Email] class. Its methods return the object itself, which allows them to be chained:
    • [from] sets the sender of the message;
    • [to] sets the recipient of the message;
    • [subject] sets the subject of the message;
    • [text] sets the body of the message;
    • [html] sets an HTML variant of the message. Here, we change the end-of-line markers into HTML [<br/>] tags and put the whole thing in bold. When the message has variants, email readers display the user's preferred variant;
  • lines 63-72: the [attachFromPath] method attaches a file to the message. The file's MIME type (application/pdf...) is deduced from its extension;
  • lines 76-82: once the message to send has been defined, we must define how to send it. [Symfony Mailer] describes the message transport with a string called a DSN (Data Source Name), of the form [smtp://utilisateur:motdepasse@serveur:port?options]. For a secure connection, we add the user and their password, encoded with [rawurlencode] (the @ character of [guest@localhost] becomes %40), and two options: [require_tls=1] requires the connection to be encrypted and [verify_peer=0] disables verification of the server's certificate. Note that [Symfony Mailer] uses the STARTTLS command on its own when the server announces it;
  • line 85: the [Mailer] class sends the messages. We must pass it the chosen transport, created from the DSN by the static method [Transport::fromDsn];
  • line 87: the message is sent;
  • line 90: the library throws an exception as soon as something goes wrong.

When we run the [smtp-02.php] script (with both instances of [Mailpit] running), we get the following console results:

> php smtp-02.php
Envoi du mail [mail to localhost via localhost]
Message [mail to localhost via localhost] envoyé
Envoi du mail [mail to localhost via a secure server]
Message [mail to localhost via a secure server] envoyé
Envoi du mail [mail to gmail via gmail] désactivé
Terminé

[Mailpit]'s web interface shows the two messages. The [test-secure-server] message went through the secure instance, which relayed it to the main instance. Here is the [test-localhost] message:

  • at the top right, the [Attachments (5)] badge indicates the five attachments, whose thumbnails can be seen at the bottom of the page;
  • the [HTML] tab displays the HTML variant of the message (in bold), the [Text] tab its text variant.

The [Raw] tab shows the raw text of the message received. Here it is, with the lines encoding the content of the attachments removed:

Return-Path: <guest@localhost>

--jM982j4q

 name="=?utf-8?Q?Cours-Tutoriels-Serge-Tah=C3=A9-1568x268=2Epng?="

  • [Return-Path] and [Received]: these headers were added by [Mailpit] when it received the message. Each server a message passes through adds a [Received] header;
  • [From], [To], [Subject]: the sender, the recipient and the subject;
  • [Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=...]: the message is made up of several parts, separated by [--boundary] lines. The last one is followed by the [--boundary--] line. This is the MIME (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions) format;
  • the 1st part is itself of type [multipart/alternative]: it contains two variants of the message, in [text/plain] and in [text/html]. They are encoded in [quoted-printable], an encoding that leaves ASCII characters readable and encodes the others (é becomes =C3=A9);
  • next come the five attachments ([Content-Disposition: attachment]), encoded in [base64], an encoding that turns any binary content into lines of ASCII characters;
  • the file name [Cours-Tutoriels-Serge-Tahé-1568x268.png] contains the character [é]. It is encoded in two ways: [name="=?utf-8?Q?...?="] (so-called RFC 2047 encoding) and [filename*=utf-8''...%C3%A9...] (so-called RFC 2231 encoding). We will come across them again when reading emails;
  • the last attachment, of type [message/rfc822], is itself an email: the [test-localhost.eml] file, which also has attachments.

Finally, let's look at two classic errors. The [config-smtp-02-erreurs.json] file describes two sends to the secure instance: the first verifies the server's certificate ([verify-peer] set to [true]), the second uses a wrong password:

{
    "certificat du serveur vérifié": {
        "smtp-server": "localhost",
        "smtp-port": 1587,
        "from": "guest@localhost",
        "to": "guest@localhost",
        "subject": "test-erreurs",

        "tls": true,
        "user": "guest@localhost",
        "password": "guest",
        "verify-peer": true,
        "attachments": []
    },
    "mauvais mot de passe": {
        "smtp-server": "localhost",
        "smtp-port": 1587,
        "from": "guest@localhost",
        "to": "guest@localhost",
        "subject": "test-erreurs",
        "message": "ligne 1\nligne 2\nligne 3",
        "tls": true,
        "user": "guest@localhost",
        "password": "xx",
        "verify-peer": false,
        "attachments": []
    }
}

Let's run the script with this configuration file, using the command [php smtp-02.php config-smtp-02-erreurs.json]:

> php smtp-02.php config-smtp-02-erreurs.json
Envoi du mail [certificat du serveur vérifié]
Erreur lors de l'envoi du message [certificat du serveur vérifié] : Unable to connect with STARTTLS: stream_socket_enable_crypto(): SSL operation failed with code 1. OpenSSL Error messages:
error:0A000086:SSL routines::certificate verify failed
Envoi du mail [mauvais mot de passe]
Erreur lors de l'envoi du message [mauvais mot de passe] : Failed to authenticate on SMTP server with username "guest@localhost" using the following authenticators: "LOGIN", "PLAIN". Authenticator "LOGIN" returned "Expected response code "235" but got code "535", with message "535 5.7.8 Authentication credentials invalid".". Authenticator "PLAIN" returned "Expected response code "235" but got code "535", with message "535 5.7.8 Authentication credentials invalid".".
Terminé
  • 1st send: [Mailpit]'s self-signed certificate was not issued by a known certificate authority. Its verification fails and the client refuses to continue: this is what protects a client against a server impersonating another. With [smtp.gmail.com], whose certificate is valid, verification succeeds;
  • 2nd send: the server rejects the authentication with error code 535.

docs.title: 16.6. The POP3 (Post Office Protocol) and IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) protocols
16.6.1. Introduction
docs.text:
Two protocols exist for reading the emails stored in a mail server:

  • the POP3 (Post Office Protocol) protocol, historically the 1st protocol but now little used;
  • the IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) protocol, a more recent protocol than POP3 and the most widely used today.

To discover these protocols, we are going to use the following architecture:

  • [Serveur B] will be:
    • for POP3, [Mailpit]'s POP3 server (port 1110);
    • for IMAP, an IMAP server. This can be Gmail's ([imap.gmail.com], port 993), with the Gmail account and app password mentioned for the SMTP protocol. The results presented here were obtained with a local IMAP server, the open source [Dovecot] server (https://www.dovecot.org), on which there is a user [guest@localhost] with the password [guest]. We placed the emails sent by our SMTP scripts in its INBOX mailbox. With Gmail, you will get results of the same form;
  • [Client A] will be a POP3 / IMAP client in various forms:
    • the [tcp-client.php] client, to discover the POP3 and IMAP protocols;
    • a PHP script replaying the POP3 protocol discovered with [tcp-client.php];
    • PHP scripts using POP3 and IMAP classes that we will write, then the [zbateson/mail-mime-parser] library to analyze the messages.

The PHP 7 course used the [imap_*] functions of PHP's [imap] extension, which could speak IMAP as well as POP3. This extension, which relied on a C library abandoned years ago, was removed from PHP 8.4. We are therefore going to write the POP3 and IMAP clients we need ourselves, with PHP's socket functions. This is an opportunity to gain a good understanding of these two protocols.

docs.title: 16.6.2. Discovering the POP3 protocol
docs.text:
First, we use the [smtp-01.php] script to send two emails: one to [guest@localhost], the other to [php8parlexemple@gmail.com] (the 3rd send fails, as we have seen). [Mailpit]'s POP3 server presents all the emails received by [Mailpit] in a single mailbox, whatever their recipients. To read it, you must log in with a user from the [pop3-users.txt] file, here [guest] with the password [guest].

Let's see with the [tcp-client.php] client how this mailbox can be read:

> php tcp-client.php --quit bye localhost 1110
Client [127.0.0.1:47492] connecté au serveur [localhost:1110]
Tapez vos commandes (bye pour arrêter) :
<-- [+OK Mailpit POP3 server]
USER guest
<-- [+OK]
PASS guest
<-- [+OK signed in]
LIST
<-- [+OK 2 messages (688 octets)]
<-- [1 352]
<-- [2 336]
<-- [.]
RETR 1
<-- [+OK 352 octets]
<-- [Message-ID: <73n0AqT1QxqOYmrcWH5gK7@mailpit>]
<-- [Return-Path: <guest@localhost>]
<-- [Received: from vm (localhost [127.0.0.1])]
<-- [        by vm (Mailpit) with SMTP]
<-- [        for <php8parlexemple@gmail.com>; Thu, 1 Oct 2026 17:14:31 +0200 (CEST)]
<-- [From: guest@localhost]
<-- [To: php8parlexemple@gmail.com]
<-- [Subject: to gmail via localhost]
<-- []
<-- [ligne 1]
<-- [ligne 2]
<-- [ligne 3]
<-- []
<-- [.]
DELE 1
<-- [+OK message marked for deletion]
LIST
<-- [+OK 1 messages (336 octets)]
<-- [2 336]
<-- [.]
DELE 2
<-- [+OK message marked for deletion]
LIST
<-- [+OK 0 messages (0 octets)]
<-- [.]
QUIT
<-- [+OK goodbye]
Perte de la connexion avec le serveur...
Fin du client
  • [php tcp-client.php --quit bye localhost 1110]: the POP3 server usually works with port 110. Here, it is [Mailpit]'s port 1110;
  • [USER guest]: the [USER] command is used to define the user whose mailbox we want to read;
  • [PASS guest]: the [PASS] command is used to define their password;
  • [LIST]: the [LIST] command requests the list of messages in the user's mailbox. The server replies with the number of messages and their total size, then with one [n° taille] (number size) line per message;
  • [RETR 1]: the [RETR] command asks to see the message whose number is passed. We find the [From], [To], [Subject] headers sent by [smtp-01.php], and headers added by [Mailpit]. [Mailpit] presents the messages from the most recent to the oldest: message no. 1 is the last one received;
  • [DELE 1]: the [DELE] command marks the message whose number is passed as "to be deleted". The message no longer appears in the list;
  • [QUIT]: the [QUIT] command tells the server that we have finished. It is at this point that the server deletes the marked messages. The two messages have disappeared from [Mailpit]'s web interface.

The server's response can take several forms:

  • a single line beginning with [+OK] to indicate that the client's previous command succeeded;
  • a single line beginning with [-ERR] to indicate that the client's previous command failed;
  • several lines where:
    • the 1st line begins with [+OK];
    • the last line consists of a single dot.

docs.title: 16.6.3. A basic script implementing the POP3 protocol
docs.text:
Since the POP3 protocol has the same structure as the SMTP protocol, the [inet/imap/pop3-01.php] script is a port of the [smtp-01.php] script. It has the following configuration file [config-pop3-01.json]:

{
    "localhost:1110": {
        "server": "localhost",
        "port": 1110,
        "user": "guest",
        "password": "guest",
        "maxmails": 5
    }
}
  • lines 3-4: the POP3 server queried is [Mailpit]'s server;
  • lines 5-6: the user and their password;
  • line 7: we will read at most 5 emails.

The [pop3-01.php] script is as follows:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// client POP3 (Post Office Protocol) permettant de lire les messages d'une boîte à lettres
// protocole de communication POP3 client-serveur
// -> client se connecte sur le port du serveur POP3 (110, 1110...)
// <- serveur lui envoie un message de bienvenue
// -> client envoie la commande USER utilisateur
// <- serveur répond OK ou non
// -> client envoie la commande PASS mot_de_passe
// <- serveur répond OK ou non
// -> client envoie la commande LIST
// <- serveur répond OK ou non. Si OK envoie la liste [n° taille] des messages
// -> client envoie la commande RETR n° pour chacun des messages
// <- serveur répond OK ou non. Si OK envoie le contenu du message demandé
// -> client envoie la commande DELE n° pour supprimer un message
// <- serveur répond OK ou non
// -> client envoie la commande QUIT pour terminer le dialogue avec le serveur
// <- serveur répond OK ou non
// les réponses du serveur ont la forme +OK texte ou -ERR texte
// La réponse peut comporter plusieurs lignes. Alors la dernière est constituée d'un unique point
// les lignes de texte échangées doivent se terminer par les caractères CR (13) et LF (10)

// les paramètres de lecture des boîtes à lettres
const CONFIG_FILE_NAME = "config-pop3-01.json";

// on récupère la configuration
$mailboxes = json_decode(file_get_contents(CONFIG_FILE_NAME), true);

// lecture des boîtes à lettres
foreach ($mailboxes as $name => $infos) {
    // suivi
    print "Lecture de la boîte à lettres [$name]\n";
    // lecture de la boîte à lettres
    $résultat = readmail($infos, verbose: true);
    // affichage résultat
    print "$résultat\n";
}
// fin
print "Terminé\n";

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function readmail(array $infos, bool $verbose = true): string
{
    // lit au plus $infos["maxmails"] messages de la boîte à lettres décrite par [$infos]
    // chaque message est supprimé après sa lecture
    // si $verbose=true, fait un suivi des échanges client-serveur
    //
    // ouverture d'une connexion avec le serveur POP3
    $connexion = @stream_socket_client("tcp://{$infos["server"]}:{$infos["port"]}", $numErreur, $erreur);
    if ($connexion === false) {
        return "Échec de la connexion au serveur [{$infos["server"]}:{$infos["port"]}] : $erreur";
    }
    try {
        // après la connexion, le serveur envoie un message de bienvenue qu'on lit
        sendCommand($connexion, "", $verbose);
        // commande USER
        sendCommand($connexion, "USER {$infos["user"]}", $verbose);
        // commande PASS
        sendCommand($connexion, "PASS {$infos["password"]}", $verbose);
        // commande LIST : la 1re ligne de la réponse a la forme [+OK n messages...]
        $réponse = sendCommand($connexion, "LIST", $verbose, multiligne: true);
        preg_match('/^\+OK (\d+)/', $réponse[0], $champs);
        $nbMessages = (int) ($champs[1] ?? 0);
        // on boucle sur les messages
        for ($i = 1; $i <= min($nbMessages, $infos["maxmails"]); $i++) {
            // commande RETR : le message est dans les lignes 1 à n-1 de la réponse
            sendCommand($connexion, "RETR $i", $verbose, multiligne: true);
            // commande DELE
            sendCommand($connexion, "DELE $i", $verbose);
        }
        // commande QUIT : c'est elle qui fait supprimer les messages marqués par DELE
        sendCommand($connexion, "QUIT", $verbose);
        return "Lecture terminée";
    } catch (RuntimeException $ex) {
        // le serveur a signalé une erreur
        return "Erreur : " . $ex->getMessage();
    } finally {
        // dans tous les cas, on ferme la connexion
        fclose($connexion);
    }
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function sendCommand($connexion, string $commande, bool $verbose, bool $multiligne = false): array
{
    // envoie $commande dans le canal $connexion et rend les lignes de la réponse
    // mode verbeux si $verbose=true
    // si $multiligne=true, la réponse se termine par une ligne réduite à un point
    // lance une RuntimeException si le serveur signale une erreur
    //
    // envoi de la commande si elle n'est pas vide
    if ($commande !== "") {
        fwrite($connexion, "$commande\r\n");
        if ($verbose) {
            affiche($commande, 1);
        }
    }
    // lecture de la 1re ligne de la réponse
    $ligne = lireLigne($connexion, $verbose);
    // erreur ?
    if (str_starts_with($ligne, "-ERR")) {
        throw new RuntimeException(substr($ligne, 5));
    }
    $réponse = [$ligne];
    // réponse sur plusieurs lignes ?
    if ($multiligne) {
        while (($ligne = lireLigne($connexion, $verbose)) !== ".") {
            // une ligne du message qui commence par un point a été envoyée
            // avec un point supplémentaire : on l'enlève
            $réponse[] = str_starts_with($ligne, "..") ? substr($ligne, 1) : $ligne;
        }
    }
    return $réponse;
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function lireLigne($connexion, bool $verbose): string
{
    // lit une ligne envoyée par le serveur et la rend sans les caractères \r\n
    $ligne = fgets($connexion);
    if ($ligne === false) {
        throw new RuntimeException("le serveur a fermé la connexion");
    }
    $ligne = rtrim($ligne, "\r\n");
    if ($verbose) {
        affiche($ligne, 2);
    }
    return $ligne;
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function affiche(string $échange, int $sens): void
{
    // affiche $échange à l'écran
    // si $sens=1 affiche --> [$échange]
    // si $sens=2 affiche <-- [$échange]
    print match ($sens) {
        1 => "--> [$échange]\n",
        2 => "<-- [$échange]\n",
    };
}

Comments

As we said, [pop3-01.php] is a port of the [smtp-01.php] script, which we have already commented on. We will only comment on the main differences:

  • line 44: the [readmail] function is responsible for reading the emails in the mailbox. The information needed to connect to this mailbox is in the [$infos] dictionary;
  • line 51: opening a connection with the POP3 server;
  • line 57: reading the welcome message sent by the server;
  • lines 59-61: we send the [USER] and [PASS] commands to identify the user whose emails we want;
  • lines 63-65: we send the [LIST] command to find out how many emails there are in the mailbox. The [sendCommand] function now returns the lines of the response. In the 1st line of its response to the LIST command, the server indicates how many messages there are. We get this with a regular expression. [$champs[1] ?? 0] is 0 if the regular expression found nothing;
  • lines 67-71: we loop over the messages. For each of them we issue two commands:
    • RETR i: to retrieve message no. i;
    • DELE i: to delete it once it has been read;
  • line 74: we send the [QUIT] command to tell the server that we have finished;
  • line 86: the [$multiligne] parameter indicates whether the expected response has several lines, the last one consisting of a single dot. This is the case for the [LIST] and [RETR] commands. An error is signaled by a 1st line beginning with [-ERR] (PHP 8.0's [str_starts_with] function);
  • lines 110-112: as with SMTP, the server doubles the dot that begins a line of the message. The client must remove this extra dot.

We again send two emails with [smtp-01.php], then run [pop3-01.php]:

  • the ability to talk to a secure server;
  • the ability to read a message's attachments.

Before giving it these, let's discover the IMAP protocol.

docs.title: 16.6.4. Discovering the IMAP protocol
docs.text:
The IMAP protocol is richer than the POP3 protocol. The server manages several mailboxes per user (INBOX, Sent, Trash...) and remembers the state of messages: read, answered, to be deleted... These states are called flags. Above all, the client can ask the server for the structure of a message and download only part of it.

Each client command is preceded by a tag chosen by the client, for example [A1]. The server replies with lines beginning with an asterisk [*], then with a line beginning with the command's tag, followed by [OK] (success), [NO] (failure) or [BAD] (incorrect command).

Public IMAP servers only accept connections that are encrypted from the start, on port 993. With Gmail, we would start the TCP client with the [--tls] option: [php tcp-client.php --tls --quit bye imap.gmail.com 993]. Our local server also accepts unencrypted connections on the standard port 143, which is handy for discovery. We sent two emails with the [smtp-02.php] script ([config-smtp-02.json] configuration) and they were placed in the INBOX mailbox of the user [guest@localhost]. Here is a dialogue with the IMAP server:

> php tcp-client.php --quit bye localhost 143
