Résultats(/^\s*([+-]?)\s*(\d+\.\d*|\.\d+|\d+)\s*/, + 4)
champs[0]= + 4
champs[1]=+
champs[2]=4

Comments:

Here we use regular expressions to retrieve the various fields of a string. Regular expressions make it possible to go beyond the limits of the [explode] function. The principle is to compare a string with another string called a pattern, using the [preg_match] function: [$correspond = preg_match($modèle, $chaîne, $champs)] (line 48). The [preg_match] function returns the integer 1 if the pattern can be found in the string, 0 otherwise. If so, [$champs[0]] represents the substring matching the pattern. Furthermore, if the pattern contains subpatterns in parentheses, [$champs[1]] is the piece of [$chaîne] matching the 1st subpattern, [$champs[2]] is the piece of [$chaîne] matching the 2nd subpattern, and so on. Let us go back to the script:

  • line 10: the pattern designates a sequence of one or more (+) digits (\d) located anywhere in a string. Furthermore, the pattern defines a subpattern enclosed in parentheses;
  • line 12: the pattern /(\d+)/ is compared with the string "xyz1234abcd". We see that the substring 1234 matches the pattern. We will therefore have [$champs[0]] equal to "1234". Furthermore, the pattern has a subpattern in parentheses. We will have [$champs[1]="1234"];
  • line 13: the pattern /(\d+)/ is compared with the string "12 34". We see that the substrings 12 and 34 match the pattern. The comparison stops at the first substring matching the pattern. We will therefore have [$champs[0]=12] and [$champs[1]=12];
  • line 14: the pattern /(\d+)/ is compared with the string "abcd". No match is found;
  • line 51: [preg_match] returns an integer (and [false] in case of an error in the pattern): we compare it strictly with 1.

Let us spell out the patterns used in the rest of the code:

$modèle = "/^(.*?)(\d+)(.*?)$/";

matches the start of the string (^), then 0 or more (*) arbitrary characters (.), then 1 or more (+) digits, then again 0 or more (*) arbitrary characters (.). The pattern (.*) designates 0 or more arbitrary characters. Such a pattern will match any string. Thus, in the pattern /^(.*)(\d+)(.*)$/, the first subpattern (.*) would absorb all the digits except the last, the only one left to the subpattern (\d+). The pattern (.*?)(\d+), on the other hand, designates 0 or more arbitrary characters up to the next subpattern (?), here \d+. So the digits are no longer absorbed by the pattern (.*). The pattern above therefore matches [start of string (^), a sequence of arbitrary characters (.*?), a sequence of one or more digits (\d+), a sequence of arbitrary characters (.*?), the end of the string ($)].

$modèle = "/^\s*(\d\d)\/(\d\d)\/(\d\d)\s*$/";

matches [start of string (^), a sequence of 0 or more whitespace characters (\s*), 2 digits (\d\d), the / character (\/), 2 digits, /, 2 digits, a sequence of 0 or more whitespace characters (\s*), the end of the string ($)].

$modèle = "/^\s*([+-]?)\s*(\d+\.\d*|\.\d+|\d+)\s*/";

matches [start of string (^), 0 or more whitespace characters (\s*), a + or - sign ([+-]) present 0 or 1 time (?), a sequence of 0 or more whitespace characters (\s*), 1 or more digits followed by a decimal point followed by zero or more digits (\d+\.\d*) or (|) a decimal point (\.) followed by one or more digits (\d+) or (|) one or more digits (\d+), a sequence of 0 or more whitespace characters (\s*)]. The PHP 7 course wrote [+|-]: inside square brackets, the | character has no special meaning, and this pattern also accepted the | sign in front of a number. [+-] is the correct form.

Note: the term [whitespace] in regular expressions designates a set of characters: blank, line feed \n, tab \t, carriage return \r, form feed \f…

docs.title: 3.8.1. Parameter passing modes
docs.text:
The script [bases-12.php] is as follows:

<?php

// mode de passage des paramètres d'une fonction
// respect strict du type des paramètres
declare(strict_types=1);

function f(int &$i, int $j): void
{
    // $i sera obtenu par référence
    // $j sera obtenu par valeur
    $i++;
    $j++;
    print "f[i,j]=[$i,$j]\n";
}

// tests
$i = 0;
$j = 0;
// $i et $j sont passés à la fonction f
f($i, $j);
print "test[i,j]=[$i,$j]\n";

Results:

> php bases-12.php
f[i,j]=[1,1]
test[i,j]=[1,0]

Comments:

The code above shows the two modes of passing parameters to a function. Let us take the following example:

function f(int &$a, int $b): void
{
    …
}

// programme principal
$i = 10;
$j = 20;
f($i, $j);
  • line 1: defines the formal parameters [$a] and [$b] of the function [f]. The function manipulates these two formal parameters;
  • line 9: call of function [f] with two actual parameters [$i] and [$j]. The links between the formal parameters ([$a], [$b]) and the actual parameters ([$i], [$j]) are defined by lines 1 and 9:
    • [&$a]: the & sign indicates that the formal parameter [$a] will take as its value the address of the actual parameter [$i]. In other words, [$a] and [$i] are two references to the same memory location. Manipulating the formal parameter [$a] amounts to manipulating the actual parameter [$i]. This is what the execution of the code shows. This passing mode is suited to output parameters. It is called passing by reference;
    • [$b]: the formal parameter [$b] will take as its value that of the actual parameter [$j]. This is passing by value. The formal and actual parameters are two different variables. Manipulating the formal parameter [$b] has no effect on the actual parameter [$j]. This is what the execution of the code shows. This passing mode is suited to input parameters.

Consider the function [échange] (swap), which accepts two formal parameters [$a] and [$b]. The function swaps the values of these two parameters. Thus, during a call [échange($i, $j)], the calling code expects the values of the two actual parameters to be swapped. They are therefore output parameters (they are modified). We will therefore write:

function échange(mixed &$a, mixed &$b): void
{
    [$a, $b] = [$b, $a];
}

Note: one might think that passing by reference is also suitable for large data, arrays and dictionaries, to avoid copying them. It is pointless: PHP only actually copies an array passed by value if the function modifies it. We will therefore reserve passing by reference for output parameters.

The following script [bases-13.php] shows other examples:

<?php

// mode de passage des paramètres
// pas de declare(strict_types=1) dans ce script : on est en mode « coercitif »

function f(&$i, $j)
{
    // $i sera obtenu par référence
    // $j sera obtenu par valeur
    $i++;
    $j++;
    print "f[i,j]=[$i,$j]\n";
}

function g(int &$i, int $j): void
{
    // $i sera obtenu par référence
    // $j sera obtenu par valeur
    $i++;
    $j++;
    print "g[i,j]=[$i,$j]\n";
}

// tests
$i = 0;
$j = 0;
// $i et $j sont passés à la fonction f
f($i, $j);
print "test[i,j]=[$i,$j]\n";
// $i et $j sont passés à la fonction g
g($i, $j);
print "test[i,j]=[$i,$j]\n";
// on passe des paramètres de type float à f
$a = 5.0;
$b = 6.2;
f($a, $b);
print "test[a,b]=[$a,$b]\n";
// on passe des paramètres de type float à g
$a = 5.0;
$b = 6.0;
g($a, $b);
print "test[a,b]=[$a,$b]\n";

Comments:

  • line 4: unlike all the other scripts of the course, this script does not have the [declare(strict_types=1)] statement: PHP operates in "coercive" mode;
  • lines 6-13: the function [f] studied in the previous section, but the parameters have not been typed;
  • lines 15-22: the function [g] does the same thing as function [f], but the type of the expected parameters is specified. Two parameters of type [int] are expected. We want to see what happens when the actual parameter passed to the function does not have the type it expects;
  • lines 25-26: [$i] and [$j] are two integers;
  • line 28: call of function [f] with parameters of the expected type;
  • line 31: call of function [g] with parameters of the expected type;
  • lines 34-35: the variables [$a] and [$b] are of type [float];
  • line 36: call of function [f] with parameters of type [float];
  • lines 39-41: call of function [g] with parameters of type [float], which is not the expected type.

Results:

> php bases-13.php
f[i,j]=[1,1]
test[i,j]=[1,0]
g[i,j]=[2,1]
test[i,j]=[2,0]
f[i,j]=[6,7.2]
test[a,b]=[6,6.2]
g[i,j]=[6,7]
test[a,b]=[6,6]
  • function [f], whose parameters are not typed, accepted the two parameters of type [float] and worked with them: [$i] is 6.0, displayed as 6, and [$j] is 7.2;
  • function [g] accepted the two parameters of type [float] but transformed them into type [int]. This can be seen from the variable [$a], passed by reference, which has become the integer 6.

The real numbers 5.0 and 6.0 have no decimal part: converting them to integers loses no information. What would happen with the real number 5.3? In PHP 7, it was silently converted into the integer 5. Since PHP 8.1, this conversion, which loses information, is reported as deprecated: it will become an error in a future version of PHP.

Let us now do the same thing in strict mode. The script [bases-13b.php] is identical to the script [bases-13.php] except that it begins with the statement:

declare(strict_types=1);

This statement indicates that the types of the formal parameters must be respected. If they are not, an error is reported. The execution results then become:

> php bases-13b.php
f[i,j]=[1,1]
test[i,j]=[1,0]
g[i,j]=[2,1]
test[i,j]=[2,0]
f[i,j]=[6,7.2]
test[a,b]=[6,6.2]

Fatal error: Uncaught TypeError: g(): Argument #1 ($i) must be of type int, float given, called in .../php8-oct-2026/scripts-console/bases/bases-13b.php on line 42 and defined in .../php8-oct-2026/scripts-console/bases/bases-13b.php:16
Stack trace:
#0 .../php8-oct-2026/scripts-console/bases/bases-13b.php(42): g(5.0, 6.0)
#1 {main}
  thrown in .../php8-oct-2026/scripts-console/bases/bases-13b.php on line 16

The PHP interpreter threw a [TypeError] error to indicate that the 1st parameter passed to function [g] did not have the right type: g(): Argument #1 ($i) must be of type int, float given. The message indicates the line of the faulty call (42) and that of the function's definition (16). As this error is not caught (there is no [try / catch]), the script stops. It is recommended to be strict about parameter types whenever possible, in order to detect errors in function calls: this is why all the course scripts begin with [declare(strict_types=1)].

docs.title: 3.8.2. Function parameters in PHP 8
docs.text:
PHP 8 has greatly enriched the declaration and calling of functions. The script [bases-14.php] presents these new features:

<?php

// les paramètres des fonctions en PHP 8
declare(strict_types=1);

// 1 - paramètres avec valeur par défaut
function salutation(string $nom, string $formule = "Bonjour", bool $majuscules = false): string
{
    $message = "$formule $nom";
    return $majuscules ? strtoupper($message) : $message;
}

print salutation("Pierre") . "\n";
print salutation("Pierre", "Bonsoir") . "\n";
// 2 - arguments nommés (PHP 8.0) : on peut sauter un paramètre et les donner dans n'importe quel ordre
print salutation("Pierre", majuscules: true) . "\n";
print salutation(majuscules: true, formule: "Salut", nom: "Paul") . "\n";
// les fonctions prédéfinies acceptent aussi les arguments nommés
print str_pad(string: "7", length: 3, pad_string: "0", pad_type: STR_PAD_LEFT) . "\n";

// 3 - type union (PHP 8.0) : le paramètre peut être de l'un des types listés
function double(int|float $nombre): int|float
{
    return 2 * $nombre;
}

var_dump(double(4));
var_dump(double(4.5));

// 4 - type nullable : ?string est équivalent à string|null
function longueur(?string $chaîne): int
{
    // l'opérateur ?? rend son opérande droit si l'opérande gauche est null
    return strlen($chaîne ?? "");
}

print "longueur(\"abc\")=" . longueur("abc") . ", longueur(null)=" . longueur(null) . "\n";

// 5 - type mixed (PHP 8.0) et expression match (PHP 8.0)
function décrire(mixed $valeur): string
{
    // match compare avec === et rend une valeur
    return match (true) {
        is_int($valeur), is_float($valeur) => "le nombre $valeur",
        is_string($valeur) => "la chaîne [$valeur]",
        is_bool($valeur) => "le booléen " . ($valeur ? "true" : "false"),
        is_array($valeur) => "un tableau de " . count($valeur) . " élément(s)",
        default => "une valeur de type " . get_debug_type($valeur),
    };
}

foreach ([12, 3.5, "abc", false, [1, 2], null] as $valeur) {
    print décrire($valeur) . "\n";
}

// match sur une valeur
$enfants = 3;
$parts = match ($enfants) {
    0 => 0.0,
    1, 2 => $enfants * 0.5,
    default => 1 + ($enfants - 2) * 1.0,
};
print "$enfants enfant(s) apportent $parts part(s)\n";

// 6 - nombre variable de paramètres (variadique) et opérateur ... (spread)
function somme(int|float ...$nombres): int|float
{
    // $nombres est un tableau
    return array_sum($nombres);
}

print "somme()=" . somme() . "\n";
print "somme(1, 2, 3)=" . somme(1, 2, 3) . "\n";
$valeurs = [10, 20, 30.5];
// le tableau est « étalé » en paramètres effectifs
print "somme(...\$valeurs)=" . somme(...$valeurs) . "\n";
// l'opérateur ... permet aussi de fusionner des tableaux
$tous = [0, ...$valeurs, 40];
print "tous=[" . implode(",", $tous) . "]\n";

Results:

> php bases-14.php
Bonjour Pierre
Bonsoir Pierre
BONJOUR PIERRE
SALUT PAUL
007
int(8)
float(9)
longueur("abc")=3, longueur(null)=0
le nombre 12
le nombre 3.5
la chaîne [abc]
le booléen false
un tableau de 2 élément(s)
une valeur de type null
3 enfant(s) apportent 2 part(s)
somme()=0
somme(1, 2, 3)=6
somme(...$valeurs)=60.5
tous=[0,10,20,30.5,40]

Comments:

  • line 7: the parameters [$formule] and [$majuscules] have a default value. They can be omitted from the call (line 13), in which case they take their default value;
  • line 10: the ternary operator [condition ? valeur1 : valeur2] returns [valeur1] if the condition is true, [valeur2] otherwise;
  • line 16: named arguments (PHP 8.0). The actual parameter is preceded by the name of the formal parameter followed by :. This makes it possible to give a value to the 3rd parameter without giving the 2nd, which keeps its default value;
  • line 17: with named arguments, the order of the parameters no longer matters. The code gains in readability: [majuscules: true] is more meaningful than an isolated [true];
  • line 19: PHP's predefined functions also accept named arguments. Their names are those of the php.net documentation;
  • line 22: the union type [int|float] (PHP 8.0) indicates that the parameter can be an [int] or a [float]. The same goes for the result;
  • line 31: the type [?string] is a nullable type: the parameter is a string or the value [null]. It is a shorthand for [string|null]. Beware: in PHP 7, people often wrote [string $chaîne = null] to obtain the same effect. This form ("implicit nullable") has been deprecated since PHP 8.4: you must write [?string $chaîne = null];
  • line 34: the [??] operator already encountered: if [$chaîne] is [null], the empty string is used. Indeed, since PHP 8.1, passing [null] to a non-nullable parameter of a predefined function, as here [strlen(null)], is deprecated;
  • line 40: the parameter of type [mixed] accepts any value, including [null];
  • lines 43-49: the [match] expression (PHP 8.0). It compares the value in parentheses with the values to the left of the => arrows and returns the value to the right of the first arrow whose comparison succeeds. With [match (true)], conditions are written on the left: the first true condition wins. Several values can be separated by commas (line 44). [default] designates all other cases;
  • line 48: the [get_debug_type] function (PHP 8.0) returns the name of a value's type as it is written in code: int, float, string, null, or the name of an object's class. [gettype], for its part, returned historical names such as integer or double;
  • lines 58-62: [match] applied to a value. Here the variable [$enfants] is compared with the values 0, then 1 and 2, otherwise it is the [default] case. Unlike the [switch] statement, which [match] advantageously replaces, the comparison is done with [===], [match] is an expression that returns a value, and there is no [break] statement to forget. If no branch fits and there is no [default], [match] throws an [UnhandledMatchError] error;
  • line 66: [int|float ...$nombres] is a variadic parameter: the function accepts any number of actual parameters (even none), which PHP gathers in the array [$nombres]. A variadic parameter is always the last one;
  • line 76: the [...] (spread) operator placed in front of an array in a call "spreads" the array: its elements become the actual parameters of the function. [somme(...$valeurs)] is equivalent to [somme(10, 20, 30.5)];
  • line 78: the same operator makes it possible to insert the elements of one array into another array.

docs.title: 3.8.3. Results returned by a function
docs.text:
The script [bases-15.php] is as follows:

<?php

// types en mode strict
declare(strict_types=1);

// résultats rendus par une fonction
// une fonction peut rendre plusieurs valeurs dans un tableau
[$res1, $res2, $res3] = f1(10);
print "[$res1,$res2,$res3]\n";
$res = f1(10);
for ($i = 0; $i < count($res); $i++) {
    print "f1 : res[$i]=$res[$i]\n";
}
// un tableau associatif peut aussi être « déstructuré »
["min" => $min, "max" => $max] = minMax([4, -2, 17, 8]);
print "minMax : [min=$min,max=$max]\n";

// une fonction peut rendre un objet
$res = f2(10);
print "f2 : [$res->res1,$res->res2,$res->res3]\n";
// objet de quelle nature ?
print "nature de l'objet : ";
var_dump($res);

// on fait la même chose avec la fonction f3
$res = f3(10);
print "f3 : [$res->res1,$res->res2,$res->res3]\n";
// objet de quelle nature ?
print "nature de l'objet : ";
var_dump($res);

// une fonction peut rendre un objet ou null
$res = f4(10);
// l'opérateur nullsafe ?-> rend null au lieu de provoquer une erreur si $res est null
print "f4(10) : res1=" . ($res?->res1 ?? "aucun") . "\n";
$res = f4(-10);
print "f4(-10) : res1=" . ($res?->res1 ?? "aucun") . "\n";

// fin
exit;

// fonction f1
function f1(int $valeur): array
{
    // rend un tableau ($valeur+1,$valeur+2,$valeur+3)
    return [$valeur + 1, $valeur + 2, $valeur + 3];
}

// fonction minMax
function minMax(array $nombres): array
{
    // rend un tableau associatif
    return ["min" => min($nombres), "max" => max($nombres)];
}

// fonction f2
function f2(int $valeur): object
{
    // rend un objet ($valeur+1,$valeur+2,$valeur+3)
    // obtenu en transformant un tableau associatif en objet
    return (object) ["res1" => $valeur + 1, "res2" => $valeur + 2, "res3" => $valeur + 3];
}

// fonction f3 - fait la même chose que la fonction f2
function f3(int $valeur): object
{
    // rend un objet ($valeur+1,$valeur+2,$valeur+3)
    $res = new stdClass();
    $res->res1 = $valeur + 1;
    $res->res2 = $valeur + 2;
    $res->res3 = $valeur + 3;
    // rend l'objet
    return $res;
}

// fonction f4 - rend un objet si $valeur est positive, null sinon
function f4(int $valeur): ?object
{
    return $valeur >= 0 ? f3($valeur) : null;
}

Results:

> php bases-15.php
[11,12,13]
f1 : res[0]=11
f1 : res[1]=12
f1 : res[2]=13
minMax : [min=-2,max=17]
f2 : [11,12,13]
nature de l'objet : object(stdClass)#1 (3) {
  ["res1"]=>
  int(11)
  ["res2"]=>
  int(12)
  ["res3"]=>
  int(13)
}
f3 : [11,12,13]
nature de l'objet : object(stdClass)#2 (3) {
  ["res1"]=>
  int(11)
  ["res2"]=>
  int(12)
  ["res3"]=>
  int(13)
}
f4(10) : res1=11
f4(-10) : res1=aucun

Comments:

  • the program above shows that a PHP function can return a set of results rather than a single one, in the form of an array or an object. The notion of object is explained in a later chapter;
  • lines 43-47: the function [f1] returns several values in the form of an array ([array]);
  • line 8: the returned array is destructured into three variables;
  • line 15: destructuring also works with an associative array: for each variable, you indicate the key of the value to retrieve. The [minMax] function does indeed return a dictionary (line 53). The predefined functions [min] and [max] return the smallest and the largest element of an array;
  • lines 57-62: the function [f2] returns several values in the form of an object ([object]). It obtains it by converting an associative array into an object with the [(object)] operator: each key of the array becomes a property of the object;
  • lines 65-74: the function [f3] does the same thing as function [f2], but it explicitly creates an object of type [stdClass] (line 68), then adds properties to it. Attribute A of an object O is written [$O->A];
  • line 23: the [var_dump] function gives access to the nature of the object and to its content. In the results, we see that the object is of type [stdClass], that its property [res1] is of type integer and has the value 11, and so on. The number #1 or #2 following the type is an internal object number;
  • line 77: the result type [?object] indicates that the function [f4] returns an object or [null];
  • lines 35-37: the nullsafe operator [?->] (PHP 8.0). If [$res] is [null], the expression [$res?->res1] is [null] instead of causing an error; the [??] operator then replaces [null] with "aucun" (none). Here the [??] operator alone would suffice, because it does not report the absence of the property. The [?->] operator will show its full value with objects and their methods: [$client?->getAdresse()?->getVille()].

Note: the PHP 7 course presented a function that wrote [$res->res1 = ...] without having created the object [$res]. PHP 7 then created a default [stdClass] object with a mere warning. Since PHP 8.0, this is a fatal error (Attempt to assign property on null): an object must always be created before being used.

docs.title: 3.8.4. Functions are values too
docs.text:
In PHP, a function can be stored in a variable, passed as a parameter to another function or returned as a result. The script [bases-17.php] shows the various ways of writing and using these functions:

<?php

// les fonctions sont aussi des valeurs
declare(strict_types=1);

$nombres = [4, -2, 17, 8, -5];

// 1 - une fonction anonyme affectée à une variable
$carré = function (int $x): int {
    return $x * $x;
};
print "carré(5)=" . $carré(5) . "\n";

// 2 - une fonction anonyme passée en paramètre à une fonction prédéfinie
// array_map applique la fonction à chaque élément du tableau
$carrés = array_map($carré, $nombres);
print "carrés=[" . implode(",", $carrés) . "]\n";

// 3 - une fonction anonyme utilisant une variable extérieure : mot clé use
$seuil = 5;
$grands = array_filter($nombres, function (int $x) use ($seuil): bool {
    return $x > $seuil;
});
print "nombres > $seuil : [" . implode(",", $grands) . "]\n";

// 4 - la fonction fléchée (PHP 7.4) : une seule expression, variables extérieures capturées automatiquement
$positifs = array_filter($nombres, fn(int $x): bool => $x >= 0);
print "positifs=[" . implode(",", $positifs) . "]\n";
// tri avec une fonction de comparaison : l'opérateur <=> rend -1, 0 ou 1
$triés = $nombres;
usort($triés, fn(int $a, int $b): int => $b <=> $a);
print "tri décroissant=[" . implode(",", $triés) . "]\n";

// 5 - recherche dans un tableau (PHP 8.4)
print "premier négatif : " . array_find($nombres, fn(int $x): bool => $x < 0) . "\n";
print "au moins un > 10 : " . var_export(array_any($nombres, fn(int $x): bool => $x > 10), true) . "\n";
print "tous > -10 : " . var_export(array_all($nombres, fn(int $x): bool => $x > -10), true) . "\n";

// 6 - la syntaxe callable de première classe (PHP 8.1) : nomFonction(...)
$majuscules = strtoupper(...);
print $majuscules("bonjour") . "\n";
$noms = ["dupont", "durand", "martin"];
print "noms=[" . implode(",", array_map(ucfirst(...), $noms)) . "]\n";

// 7 - l'opérateur pipe |> (PHP 8.5) : le résultat de gauche est passé à la fonction de droite
$résultat = "  Bonjour tout le monde  "
    |> trim(...)
    |> strtolower(...)
    |> (fn(string $s): string => str_replace(" ", "-", $s));
print "résultat=[$résultat]\n";
// équivalent sans l'opérateur pipe
$résultat = str_replace(" ", "-", strtolower(trim("  Bonjour tout le monde  ")));
print "résultat=[$résultat]\n";

Results:

> php bases-17.php
carré(5)=25
carrés=[16,4,289,64,25]
nombres > 5 : [17,8]
positifs=[4,17,8]
tri décroissant=[17,8,4,-2,-5]
premier négatif : -2
au moins un > 10 : true
tous > -10 : true
BONJOUR
noms=[Dupont,Durand,Martin]
résultat=[bonjour-tout-le-monde]
résultat=[bonjour-tout-le-monde]

Comments:

  • lines 9-11: an anonymous (nameless) function is assigned to the variable [$carré]. Note the final ;: this is an assignment;
  • line 12: the function is called through the variable;
  • line 16: the predefined function [array_map] applies the function passed as 1st parameter to each element of the array passed as 2nd parameter, and returns the array of results;
  • lines 21-23: the predefined function [array_filter] returns the elements of the array for which the function passed as 2nd parameter returns [true]. An anonymous function does not know the variables of the surrounding code: the keyword [use ($seuil)] gives it access to the variable [$seuil]. Note that [array_filter] keeps the keys of the retained elements; this has no effect here because [implode] only uses the values;
  • line 27: an arrow function (PHP 7.4): [fn(paramètres) => expression]. It contains only one expression, whose value is the function's result. It automatically has (read) access to the variables of the surrounding code: no need for [use]. It is the most concise form for small functions passed as parameters;
  • line 31: the [usort] function sorts an array using a comparison function that receives two elements [$a] and [$b] and returns a negative, zero or positive number depending on whether [$a] must be placed before, at the same rank as, or after [$b]. The [<=>] ("spaceship") operator returns precisely -1, 0 or 1. By writing [$b <=> $a] instead of [$a <=> $b], we obtain a descending sort. Note that [usort] modifies the array passed to it (passing by reference): we have therefore sorted a copy [$triés] of the array [$nombres];
  • line 35: the [array_find], [array_any] and [array_all] functions were introduced in PHP 8.4. [array_find] returns the first element for which the function returns [true] (or [null] if there is none), [array_any] returns [true] if at least one element satisfies the condition, [array_all] if all of them satisfy it;
  • line 40: the first-class callable syntax (PHP 8.1): [nomFonction(...)], with literally three dots between the parentheses, does not call the function but returns the function itself, in the form of a [Closure] object. It can then be used like an anonymous function;
  • line 43: the predefined function [ucfirst] (first letter in uppercase) is passed to [array_map];
  • lines 46-49: the pipe operator [|>] (PHP 8.5). The expression [valeur |> fonction] calls the function with the value as its only parameter. The calls are chained from left to right, in the order in which they are read: leading and trailing spaces are removed with [trim], the text is converted to lowercase with [strtolower], then the spaces are replaced by hyphens. An arrow function used with [|>] must be enclosed in parentheses;
  • line 52: the same thing without the pipe operator. The functions are nested and are read from the inside out, in the reverse of the execution order.

docs.title: 3.9. Text files
docs.text:
The script [bases-16.php] is as follows:

<?php

// respect strict du type des paramètres des fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// exploitation séquentielle d'un fichier texte
// celui-ci est un ensemble de lignes de la forme login:pwd:uid:gid:infos:dir:shell
// chaque ligne est mise dans un dictionnaire sous la forme login => [uid, gid, infos, dir, shell]
// on fixe le nom du fichier
$INFOS = "infos.txt";
// on l'ouvre en création
$fic = fopen($INFOS, "w");
if ($fic === false) {
    print "Erreur d'ouverture du fichier $INFOS en écriture\n";
    exit;
}
// on génère un contenu arbitraire
for ($i = 0; $i < 100; $i++) {
    fputs($fic, "login$i:pwd$i:uid$i:gid$i:infos$i:dir$i:shell$i\n");
}
// on ferme le fichier
fclose($fic);

// on l'exploite - fgets garde la marque de fin de ligne
// cela permet de ne pas récupérer une chaîne vide lors de la lecture d'une ligne blanche
// on l'ouvre en lecture
$fic = fopen($INFOS, "r");
if ($fic === false) {
    print "Erreur d'ouverture du fichier $INFOS en lecture\n";
    exit;
}

// le dictionnaire des informations
$dico = [];
// les lignes font moins de 1000 caractères
// la lecture de la ligne s'arrête sur la marque de fin de ligne
// ou celle de fin de fichier
while (($ligne = fgets($fic, 1000)) !== false) {
    // on supprime la marque de fin de ligne si elle existe
    $ligne = cutNewLineChar($ligne);
    // on met la ligne dans un tableau
    $infos = explode(":", $ligne);
    // on récupère le login
    $login = array_shift($infos);
    // on néglige le pwd
    array_shift($infos);
    // on crée une entrée dans le dictionnaire
    $dico[$login] = $infos;
}
// on le ferme
fclose($fic);

// exploitation du dictionnaire
afficheInfos($dico, "login10");
afficheInfos($dico, "X");

// une autre façon de lire un fichier texte : la fonction file
$lignes = file($INFOS, FILE_IGNORE_NEW_LINES);
print "le fichier $INFOS a " . count($lignes) . " lignes, la dernière est [" . array_last($lignes) . "]\n";

// fin
exit;

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function afficheInfos(array $dico, string $clé): void
{
    // affiche la valeur associée à clé dans le dictionnaire $dico si elle existe
    if (isset($dico[$clé])) {
        // valeur existe - est-ce un tableau ?
        $valeur = $dico[$clé];
        if (is_array($valeur)) {
            print "[$clé," . implode(":", $valeur) . "]\n";
        } else {
            // $valeur n'est pas un tableau
            print "[$clé,$valeur]\n";
        }
    } else {
        // $clé n'est pas une clé du dictionnaire $dico
        print "la clé [$clé] n'existe pas\n";
    }
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function cutNewLineChar(string $ligne): string
{
    // on supprime la marque de fin de ligne de $ligne si elle existe
    // (\n sous Unix, \r\n sous Windows)
    return rtrim($ligne, "\r\n");
}

The file [infos.txt] created by the script:

login0:pwd0:uid0:gid0:infos0:dir0:shell0
login1:pwd1:uid1:gid1:infos1:dir1:shell1
login2:pwd2:uid2:gid2:infos2:dir2:shell2
…
login98:pwd98:uid98:gid98:infos98:dir98:shell98
login99:pwd99:uid99:gid99:infos99:dir99:shell99

The results:

> php bases-16.php
[login10,uid10:gid10:infos10:dir10:shell10]
la clé [X] n'existe pas
le fichier infos.txt a 100 lignes, la dernière est [login99:pwd99:uid99:gid99:infos99:dir99:shell99]

Comments:

  • line 12: [fopen(nom_fichier, "w")] opens the file [nom_fichier] for writing (w=write). If the file does not exist, it is created. If it exists, it is emptied. The file is created in the current folder, the one from which the script was launched. If creation fails, [fopen] emits a warning and returns the value [false];
  • line 13: the result of [fopen] is tested by comparing it strictly with [false];
  • line 19: [fputs($fic, $chaîne)] writes [$chaîne] to the file [$fic]. Here the string ends with the end-of-line mark [\n];
  • line 22: [fclose($fic)] closes the file [$fic];
  • line 27: [fopen(nom_fichier, "r")] opens the file [nom_fichier] for reading (r=read). If opening fails (the file does not exist, for example), [fopen] returns the value [false];
  • line 34: the dictionary is initialized as empty before being filled. PHP would create the array on the first assignment [$dico[$login] = ...], but if the file were empty, the variable would not exist and using it would cause a warning;
  • line 38: [fgets($fic, 1000)] reads the next line of the file, up to 1000 characters. In the operation [while (($ligne = fgets($fic, 1000)) !== false) {...}], there are two successive operations: 1) [$ligne = fgets(...)] 2) [while ($ligne !== false)]. After the last character of the file has been read, the [fgets] function returns the value [false] and the [while] loop stops. The [fgets] function here tries to read at most 1000 characters but stops as soon as an end-of-line mark is encountered. Here, since all lines have fewer than 1000 characters, [fgets] reads one line of text, end-of-line mark included. The PHP 7 course wrote [while ($ligne = fgets($fic, 1000))]: the loop would have stopped prematurely on a last line reduced to "0", with no end-of-line mark, because the string "0" is converted to [false]. The strict comparison [!== false] avoids this trap;
  • line 40: the [cutNewLineChar] function removes any end-of-line characters;
  • line 44: the function [array_shift($tableau)] removes the 1st element of [$tableau] and returns it as its result;
  • line 46: here the result returned by [array_shift] is ignored;
  • line 58: another way to read a text file. The [file] function returns the array of all the lines of the file. With the [FILE_IGNORE_NEW_LINES] option, the end-of-line marks are removed. This is simpler than the [fgets] loop, but the whole file is loaded into memory: for a very large file, reading line by line remains preferable;
  • line 71: the function [is_array($variable)] returns [true] if [$variable] is an array, [false] otherwise;
  • line 84: the end-of-line mark is the string "\r\n" on Windows systems, "\n" on Unix systems. The function [rtrim($chaîne, $caractères)] removes from the end of [$chaîne] all the characters present in [$caractères], here \r and \n. Without a second parameter, [rtrim] removes all "whitespace" (blank, tab, end of line…); the [trim] function does the same thing at both ends of the string.

docs.title: 3.10. JSON encoding / decoding
docs.text:
The [scripts-console/json] folder contains the scripts of this section:

json
├── famille.json
├── json-01.php
├── json-02.php
└── json-03.php

JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) encoding / decoding is something we will use intensively in the exercise that serves as the common thread of the document. The scripts [json-01.php, json-02.php, json-03.php] explain what you need to know for what follows.

The script [json-01.php] is as follows:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

$array1 = ["nom" => "séléné", "prénom" => "bénédicte", "âge" => 34];
// encodage JSON du tableau array1 avec caractères Unicode échappés
print "encodage JSON du tableau array1 avec caractères Unicode échappés\n";
$json1 = json_encode($array1);
print "json1=$json1\n";
// encodage JSON du tableau array1 avec caractères Unicode non échappés
print "encodage JSON du tableau array1 avec caractères Unicode non échappés\n";
$json2 = json_encode($array1, JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE);
print "json2=$json2\n";
// décodage JSON dans tableau associatif
print "décodage JSON de json2 dans tableau associatif\n";
$array2 = json_decode($json2, true);
var_dump($array2);
foreach ($array2 as $key => $value) {
    print "$key:$value\n";
}
// décodage JSON dans objet
print "décodage JSON de json2 dans objet stdClass\n";
$objet2 = json_decode($json2);
var_dump($objet2);
print "prénom=$objet2->prénom\n";
print "nom=$objet2->nom\n";
print "âge=$objet2->âge\n";

Results:

> php json-01.php
encodage JSON du tableau array1 avec caractères Unicode échappés
json1={"nom":"s\u00e9l\u00e9n\u00e9","pr\u00e9nom":"b\u00e9n\u00e9dicte","\u00e2ge":34}
encodage JSON du tableau array1 avec caractères Unicode non échappés
json2={"nom":"séléné","prénom":"bénédicte","âge":34}
décodage JSON de json2 dans tableau associatif
array(3) {
  ["nom"]=>
  string(9) "séléné"
  ["prénom"]=>
  string(11) "bénédicte"
  ["âge"]=>
  int(34)
}
nom:séléné
prénom:bénédicte
âge:34
décodage JSON de json2 dans objet stdClass
object(stdClass)#1 (3) {
  ["nom"]=>
  string(9) "séléné"
  ["prénom"]=>
  string(11) "bénédicte"
  ["âge"]=>
  int(34)
}
prénom=bénédicte
nom=séléné
âge=34

Comments:

  • line 8: the [json_encode] function transforms its parameter into a JSON string. In the string produced, the accented characters é and â have been replaced by their Unicode code, which begins with \u;
  • line 12: we do the same thing again, this time asking for the Unicode characters to be kept as they are. The resulting JSON string is much more readable;
  • lines 16-20: we perform the reverse operation. A JSON string is transformed into an associative array: this is the role of the 2nd parameter [true] of [json_decode]. The results show that we have indeed retrieved an associative array;
  • lines 23-27: without the [true] parameter, [json_decode] transforms the JSON string into an object of type [stdClass]. Attribute A of an object O is written [$O->A].

Multi-level arrays can be encoded in JSON, as the following script [json-02.php] shows:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

$array = [
    "nom" => "séléné", "prénom" => "bénédicte", "âge" => 34,
    "mari" => ["nom" => "icariù", "prénom" => "ignacio", "âge" => 35],
    "enfants" => [
        ["prénom" => "angèle", "age" => 8],
        ["prénom" => "andré", "age" => 2],
    ],
];
// encodage JSON du tableau à plusieurs niveaux
print "encodage JSON d'un tableau à plusieurs niveaux\n";
$json = json_encode($array, JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE);
print "json=$json\n";
// le même encodage, présenté de façon lisible
print "encodage JSON avec l'option JSON_PRETTY_PRINT\n";
print json_encode($array["mari"], JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_PRETTY_PRINT) . "\n";

Results:

> php json-02.php
encodage JSON d'un tableau à plusieurs niveaux
json={"nom":"séléné","prénom":"bénédicte","âge":34,"mari":{"nom":"icariù","prénom":"ignacio","âge":35},"enfants":[{"prénom":"angèle","age":8},{"prénom":"andré","age":2}]}
encodage JSON avec l'option JSON_PRETTY_PRINT
{
    "nom": "icariù",
    "prénom": "ignacio",
    "âge": 35
}

Comments:

In the JSON string:

  • non-associative arrays (lists) are enclosed in square brackets [];
  • associative arrays are enclosed in braces {}.

line 19: the options of [json_encode] are combined with the | (bitwise OR) operator. The [JSON_PRETTY_PRINT] option produces a JSON string indented over several lines, which is more readable.

The script [json-03.php] shows how to use the following JSON file [famille.json]:

{
    "épouse": {
        "nom": "séléné",
        "prénom": "bénédicte",
        "âge": 34
    },
    "mari": {
        "nom": "icariù",
        "prénom": "ignacio",
        "âge": 35
    },
    "enfants": [
        {
            "prénom": "angèle",
            "age": 8
        },
        {
            "prénom": "andré",
            "age": 2
        }
    ]
}

The script [json-03.php] is as follows:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// lecture du fichier JSON
$json = file_get_contents("famille.json");
// le contenu lu est-il du JSON valide ? (PHP 8.3)
if ($json === false || !json_validate($json)) {
    print "Le fichier [famille.json] est absent ou ne contient pas du JSON valide\n";
    exit;
}
// décodage JSON en objet
$famille1 = json_decode($json);
print "----famille1\n";
var_dump($famille1);
// décodage JSON en tableau associatif
print "----famille2\n";
$famille2 = json_decode($json, true);
var_dump($famille2);

Comments:

  • line 6: the [file_get_contents] function reads the content of the file named [famille.json] and puts it in the variable [$json]. It returns [false] if reading fails;
  • line 8: the [json_validate] function (PHP 8.3) returns [true] if the string passed as parameter is valid JSON. Previously, you had to decode the string and then consult the [json_last_error] function;
  • lines 13-19: the string is then decoded into an object and then into an associative array.

Results:

> php json-03.php
----famille1
object(stdClass)#2 (3) {
  ["épouse"]=>
  object(stdClass)#1 (3) {
    ["nom"]=>
    string(9) "séléné"
    ["prénom"]=>
    string(11) "bénédicte"
    ["âge"]=>
    int(34)
  }
  ["mari"]=>
  object(stdClass)#3 (3) {
    ["nom"]=>
    string(7) "icariù"
    ["prénom"]=>
    string(7) "ignacio"
    ["âge"]=>
    int(35)
  }
  ["enfants"]=>
  array(2) {
    [0]=>
    object(stdClass)#4 (2) {
      ["prénom"]=>
      string(7) "angèle"
      ["age"]=>
      int(8)
    }
    [1]=>
    object(stdClass)#5 (2) {
      ["prénom"]=>
      string(6) "andré"
      ["age"]=>
      int(2)
    }
  }
}
----famille2
array(3) {
  ["épouse"]=>
  array(3) {
    ["nom"]=>
    string(9) "séléné"
    ["prénom"]=>
    string(11) "bénédicte"
    ["âge"]=>
    int(34)
  }
  ["mari"]=>
  array(3) {
    ["nom"]=>
    string(7) "icariù"
    ["prénom"]=>
    string(7) "ignacio"
    ["âge"]=>
    int(35)
  }
  ["enfants"]=>
  array(2) {
    [0]=>
    array(2) {
      ["prénom"]=>
      string(7) "angèle"
      ["age"]=>
      int(8)
    }
    [1]=>
    array(2) {
      ["prénom"]=>
      string(6) "andré"
      ["age"]=>
      int(2)
    }
  }
}
  • the first part of the results shows the object resulting from decoding the JSON file [famille.json]: the JSON objects have become [stdClass] objects, the JSON list of children has become a PHP array;
  • the second part shows the associative array resulting from the same decoding: all the JSON objects have become associative arrays.

docs.title: 20. Practical exercise – version 10
docs.text: The previous version showed that the tax data, shared by all users of the application, should be stored in a memory with [application] scope. We are going to use a Redis server (https://redis.io) to implement it.

docs.title: 20.1. Redis
docs.text:
Redis is a server that keeps data in memory in the form of [key, value] pairs. It is very fast and widely used by web applications as a cache, i.e. as a memory for data that are expensive to obtain. The memory with [application] scope will be implemented by a Redis server. The PHP scripts that need this application memory will be clients of this server:

  • in [1], a PHP script sends a command to the Redis server, for example to ask it for the value associated with a key;
  • in [2], the Redis server replies.

The Redis server lives independently of the PHP scripts: the data entrusted to it remain available from one request to the next, and for all users of the application.

docs.title: 20.2. Installing Redis
docs.text: [Laragon] comes with a Redis server that is not enabled by default. It is enabled in [Laragon]'s preferences ([Preferences] menu, [Services & Ports] tab) by ticking the [Redis] box. We keep port [6379], which Redis clients use by default. The Redis server is then started along with [Laragon]'s other services (Apache, MySQL...) by the [Start All] button.

docs.title: 20.3. The Redis command-line client
docs.text:
The Redis server can be queried from the command line. We open a [Laragon] terminal and type the [redis-cli] command, which starts the Redis server's command-line client. The client then displays the prompt [127.0.0.1:6379>]: it is connected to the Redis server of the local machine (IP address 127.0.0.1), on port 6379. Here is a working session:

> redis-cli
127.0.0.1:6379> command count
(integer) 240
127.0.0.1:6379> set titre "PHP 8 par l'exemple"
OK
127.0.0.1:6379> get titre
"PHP 8 par l'exemple"
127.0.0.1:6379> exists titre
(integer) 1
127.0.0.1:6379> del titre
(integer) 1
127.0.0.1:6379> get titre
(nil)
127.0.0.1:6379> exists titre
(integer) 0
127.0.0.1:6379> quit
  • line 3: the Redis client has more than 200 commands for talking to the server. One of them, [command count], displays their exact number for the version used;
  • lines 4-7: we will only present the ones we will need in our PHP application. We are going to use Redis for a single thing: associating a value with a key in Redis's memory. This is done with the Redis command [set clé valeur] (set key value). The value can then be retrieved with the [get clé] command. That is all we will need;
  • lines 8-9: the [exists] command checks whether a key exists: it returns 1 if the key exists, 0 otherwise;
  • lines 10-11: the [del] command deletes a key;
  • lines 12-13: if we ask for the value of a non-existent key, we get the value [nil], indicating that the key was not found;
  • line 16: to leave the Redis client, we type the [quit] command.

It may be necessary to empty Redis's entire memory. This is done with the [flushdb] command.

docs.title: 20.4. Installing a Redis client for PHP
docs.text:
We now need a Redis client for PHP. There are two main ones:

  • the PHP extension [phpredis], written in C, which must be added to the PHP configuration;
  • the [Predis] library (https://github.com/predis/predis), written in PHP, which is installed with [Composer].

Like the PHP 7 course, we will use [Predis], in its version 3. It appears in the [composer.json] file of the [php8-oct-2026] folder and was installed with the course's other libraries by the [composer install] command. It is found in the [vendor/predis/predis] folder. [Composer]'s class loader takes care of it: unlike in the PHP 7 course, there is no longer a [predis/autoload.php] file to include, nor a [Predis\Autoloader::register] method to call.

docs.title: 20.5. Server code
docs.text:
The version 10 server consists of the following files:

scripts-web/impots/version-10
├── Data
│   ├── .htaccess
│   ├── config-server.json
│   └── logs.txt
└── impots-server.php

The configuration file [config-server.json] changes as follows:

{
    "databaseFilename": "../version-08/Data/database-mysql.json",
    "dependencies": [
        "../../../scripts-console/impots/version-05/Entities/ExceptionImpots.php",
        "../../../scripts-console/impots/version-05/Entities/TaxAdminData.php",
        "../../../scripts-console/impots/version-05/Entities/Database.php",
        "../../../scripts-console/impots/version-05/Utilities/Utilitaires.php",
        "../version-08/Dao/InterfaceServerDao.php",
        "../version-08/Dao/ServerDao.php",
        "../version-09/Dao/ServerDaoWithSession.php",
        "../version-08/Metier/InterfaceServerMetier.php",
        "../version-08/Metier/ServerMetier.php",
        "../version-09/Utilities/Logger.php",
        "../version-09/Utilities/SendAdminMail.php"
    ],
    "users": [
        {
            "login": "admin",
            "passwd": "admin"
        }
    ],
    "adminMail": {
        "smtp-server": "localhost",
        "smtp-port": 1025,
        "from": "guest@localhost",
        "to": "guest@localhost",
        "subject": "plantage du serveur de calcul d'impôts",
        "tls": false,
        "attachments": []
    },
    "logsFilename": "Data/logs.txt",
    "redis": {
        "scheme": "tcp",
        "host": "127.0.0.1",
        "port": 6379
    }
}

Comments

  • lines 3-15: version 10 brings nothing new apart from the [impots-server.php] script. It uses elements of versions 5, 8 and 9;
  • lines 32-37: the parameters for connecting to the Redis server: the protocol (tcp), the machine and the port. These are [Predis]'s default values, but it is better to write them in the configuration: if the Redis server changes machine or port, only the configuration needs to be modified.

The code of the server [impots-server.php] changes as follows:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres et des résultats des fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// dépendances Symfony
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;
// dépendances Predis
use Predis\Client as RedisClient;
use Predis\PredisException;
// alias de classe : la couche [dao] de la version 9 est utilisée avec Redis
use Application\ServerDaoWithSession as ServerDaoWithRedis;

// les erreurs de PHP ne sont pas envoyées au client (elles vont dans le journal du serveur web)
ini_set("display_errors", "0");

// le dossier racine du serveur : les chemins du fichier de configuration sont relatifs à ce dossier
const ROOT_DIRECTORY = __DIR__;
// chemin du fichier de configuration
const CONFIG_FILENAME = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/Data/config-server.json";

// on récupère la configuration
$config = json_decode(file_get_contents(CONFIG_FILENAME), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);

// on inclut les dépendances nécessaires au script
require_once ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/../../../vendor/autoload.php";
foreach ($config["dependencies"] as $dependency) {
    require_once ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/$dependency";
}

// session : elle ne contient plus que l'identifiant de l'utilisateur authentifié
$session = new Session();
$session->start();

// création du fichier des logs
try {
    $logger = new Logger(ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["logsFilename"]);
} catch (ExceptionImpots $ex) {
    // erreur 500 sans logs - le message ne doit pas révéler l'arborescence des fichiers du serveur
    $message = "Echec lors de la création du fichier de logs [{$config["logsFilename"]}]";
    doInternalServerError($message, $config["adminMail"]);
    // terminé
    exit;
}

// 1er log
$logger->write("---nouvelle requête");

// on récupère la requête courante
$request = Request::createFromGlobals();
// authentification seulement la 1re fois
if (!$session->has("user")) {
    // log
    $logger->write("Authentification en cours…");
    // les identifiants envoyés par le client (null s'il n'en a pas envoyé)
    $requestUser = $request->getUser();
    $requestPassword = $request->getPassword();
    // l'utilisateur fait-il partie des utilisateurs autorisés ?
    $trouvé = $requestUser !== null && $requestPassword !== null
        && array_any(
            $config["users"],
            fn(array $user): bool => $user["login"] === $requestUser && hash_equals($user["passwd"], $requestPassword)
        );
    if (!$trouvé) {
        // pas trouvé - code 401
        sendResponse(
            ["erreur" => "Echec de l'authentification [$requestUser]"],
            Response::HTTP_UNAUTHORIZED,
            ["WWW-Authenticate" => 'Basic realm="Serveur de calcul des impots"'],
            $logger
        );
        // terminé
        exit;
    }
    // on note dans la session qu'on a authentifié l'utilisateur
    $session->set("user", $requestUser);
    // log
    $logger->write("Authentification réussie [$requestUser]");
} else {
    // log
    $logger->write("Authentification prise en session…");
}

// on a un utilisateur valide - on vérifie les paramètres reçus
$erreurs = [];
// on doit avoir une requête GET avec trois paramètres
if ($request->getMethod() !== "GET" || $request->query->count() !== 3) {
    $erreurs[] = "Méthode GET requise avec les seuls paramètres [marié, enfants, salaire]";
}
// le statut marital
if (!$request->query->has("marié")) {
    $erreurs[] = "paramètre marié manquant";
} else {
    $marié = strtolower(trim($request->query->getString("marié")));
    if (!in_array($marié, ["oui", "non"], true)) {
        $erreurs[] = "paramètre marié [$marié] invalide";
    }
}
// le nombre d'enfants et le salaire : des nombres entiers >= 0
$valeurs = [];
foreach (["enfants", "salaire"] as $paramètre) {
    if (!$request->query->has($paramètre)) {
        $erreurs[] = "paramètre $paramètre manquant";
        continue;
    }
    $valeur = trim($request->query->getString($paramètre));
    if (preg_match('/^\d+$/', $valeur) !== 1) {
        $erreurs[] = "paramètre $paramètre [$valeur] invalide";
    } else {
        $valeurs[$paramètre] = (int) $valeur;
    }
}
// autres paramètres dans la requête ?
foreach (array_diff(array_keys($request->query->all()), ["marié", "enfants", "salaire"]) as $paramètre) {
    $erreurs[] = "paramètre [$paramètre] invalide";
}
// erreurs ?
if ($erreurs !== []) {
    // on envoie un code d'erreur 400 au client
    sendResponse(["erreurs" => $erreurs], Response::HTTP_BAD_REQUEST, [], $logger);
    // terminé
    exit;
}
// log
[$enfants, $salaire] = [$valeurs["enfants"], $valeurs["salaire"]];
$logger->write("paramètres ['marié'=>$marié, 'enfants'=>$enfants, 'salaire'=>$salaire] valides");

// on a tout ce qu'il faut pour travailler
// la mémoire de portée [application] : un serveur Redis
try {
    // le client Redis
    $redis = new RedisClient($config["redis"]);
    // on se connecte tout de suite au serveur pour savoir s'il est là
    $redis->connect();
} catch (PredisException $ex) {
    // erreur 500
    doInternalServerError("[redis], {$ex->getMessage()}", $config["adminMail"], $logger);
    // terminé
    exit;
}
// création de la couche [dao]
$json = $redis->get("taxAdminData");
if ($json === null) {
    // les données fiscales sont prises dans la base de données
    $logger->write("données fiscales prises en base de données");
    try {
        // construction de la couche [dao]
        $dao = new ServerDaoWithRedis(ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["databaseFilename"]);
        // on met la chaîne JSON des données fiscales dans la mémoire de portée [application]
        $redis->set("taxAdminData", (string) $dao->getTaxAdminData());
    } catch (ExceptionImpots $ex) {
        // erreur 500
        doInternalServerError("[dao], {$ex->getMessage()}", $config["adminMail"], $logger, $redis);
        // terminé
        exit;
    }
} else {
    // les données fiscales sont prises dans la mémoire de portée [application]
    $taxAdminData = TaxAdminData::fromArray(json_decode($json, true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR));
    // instanciation de la couche [dao]
    $dao = new ServerDaoWithRedis($taxAdminData);
    // log
    $logger->write("données fiscales prises dans Redis");
}
// création de la couche [métier]
$métier = new ServerMetier($dao);
// calcul de l'impôt
$result = $métier->calculerImpot($marié, $enfants, $salaire);
// on rend la réponse
sendResponse($result, Response::HTTP_OK, [], $logger, $redis);
// fin
exit;

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
// erreur fatale : un mail à l'administrateur et une réponse 500 au client
function doInternalServerError(
    string $message,
    array $adminMail,
    ?Logger $logger = null,
    ?RedisClient $redis = null
): void {
    // le message d'erreur d'un pilote de SGBD peut ne pas être codé en UTF-8 (Windows-1252 sous Windows)
    if (!mb_check_encoding($message, "UTF-8")) {
        $message = mb_convert_encoding($message, "UTF-8", "Windows-1252");
    }
    // on envoie un mail à l'administrateur
    // [SendAdminMail] intercepte toutes les exceptions et les logue lui-même
    (new SendAdminMail($adminMail, $logger))->send($message);
    // on envoie un code d'erreur 500 au client
    sendResponse(["erreur" => $message], Response::HTTP_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, [], $logger, $redis);
}

// envoi de la réponse HTTP au client
// $result : le tableau à envoyer, sous la forme ["réponse" => $result]
// $statusCode : le statut HTTP de la réponse
// $headers : des entêtes HTTP à ajouter à la réponse
// $logger : le journal de l'application (null s'il n'a pu être créé)
// $redis : le client Redis (null s'il n'a pas encore été créé)
function sendResponse(
    array $result,
    int $statusCode,
    array $headers = [],
    ?Logger $logger = null,
    ?RedisClient $redis = null
): void {
    // la réponse JSON
    $response = new JsonResponse(null, $statusCode, $headers);
    $response->setEncodingOptions(JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_PRESERVE_ZERO_FRACTION);
    $response->setData(["réponse" => $result]);
    // envoi
    $response->send();
    // log
    $logger?->write($response->getContent());
    // fermeture de la connexion au serveur Redis
    $redis?->disconnect();
}

Comments

  • lines 15-16: the [Predis] classes we use. The [Predis\Client] class is the Redis client. We give it the alias [RedisClient], which is more meaningful in our code. [PredisException] is the parent class of all exceptions thrown by [Predis];
  • line 18: we give the alias [ServerDaoWithRedis] to the [ServerDaoWithSession] class of version 9 to reflect the change in the server script's implementation. The [ServerDaoWithSession] class knows how to build the [dao] layer from tax data that have already been acquired: it does not matter to it whether they come from a session or from a Redis server;
  • lines 38-39: the session is kept. Here we have two pieces of information to remember:
    • the fact that the user has authenticated correctly. This information has [session] scope: it is tied to a specific user and is not valid for other users. It stays in the session;
    • the tax authority data. This information has [application] scope: it is not tied to a specific user but is valid for all users. It goes into the Redis server;
  • lines 135-145: creation of the [Predis] client that will communicate with the Redis server, with the connection parameters from the configuration file:
    • line 140: we connect the client to the server immediately to find out whether it is responding;
    • if the connection to the Redis server fails, we send an error response to the client and an email to the application administrator. The error message is prefixed with [[redis]] to indicate where the error comes from;
  • line 148: we ask the Redis server for the value of the [taxAdminData] key. The [Predis] client offers a method for each Redis command: the [get] method sends the [get taxAdminData] command. It returns the value of the key, or [null] if it does not exist;
  • line 149: if the key is not found, the tax data are taken from the database;
  • line 156: the [taxAdminData] key is placed in Redis's memory, associated with the JSON string of the [TaxAdminData] object obtained from the [dao] layer. The [set] method expects a string for the key's value. The [(string)] cast calls the [__toString] method of the [TaxAdminData] class, which returns the object's JSON string. The PHP 7 script let PHP perform this conversion implicitly; with [declare(strict_types=1)], it is better to write it;
  • line 159: if reading the database fails, a 500 response and an email to the administrator, the message being prefixed with [[dao]];
  • lines 164-169: the [taxAdminData] key is in Redis's memory. We know that its value is the JSON string of a [TaxAdminData] object:
    • line 165: we decode the JSON string into an associative array, then the static method [TaxAdminData::fromArray] of version 5 builds the [TaxAdminData] object from this array, checking its data;
    • line 167: the [dao] layer is instantiated with these data;
  • lines 182-187: the [doInternalServerError] function has one more parameter, the Redis client, which it passes on to the [sendResponse] function. When a function has many parameters, they are written one per line;
  • line 221: the [sendResponse] function closes the connection to the Redis server, if it was opened.

docs.title: 20.8. Viewing the contents of the Redis server
docs.text:
We have seen that the Redis server could be managed from the command line. The [get taxAdminData] command shows the value of the [taxAdminData] key: we recognize the JSON string of an object of type [TaxAdminData]:

> redis-cli get taxAdminData
"{\"limites\":[9964,27519,73779,156244,0],\"coeffR\":[0,0.14,0.3,0.41,0.45],\"coeffN\":[0,1394.96,5798,13913.69,20163.45],\"plafondQfDemiPart\":1551,\"plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction\":21037,\"plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction\":42074,\"valeurReducDemiPart\":3797,\"plafondDecoteCelibataire\":1196,\"plafondDecoteCouple\":1970,\"plafondImpotCouplePourDecote\":2627,\"plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote\":1595,\"abattementDixPourcentMax\":12502,\"abattementDixPourcentMin\":437}"

[redis-cli] displays the string in double quotes, preceding each of the double quotes it contains with a [\] character.

The Redis server can also be managed through a graphical interface. The official tool is [Redis Insight] (https://redis.io/insight), free and available for Windows. Once connected to the server [127.0.0.1:6379], it displays the list of keys stored by the server. By clicking on the [taxAdminData] key, we see its value, which the tool can display as a JSON object. We can also delete a key there, add another one, or run [redis-cli] commands in a built-in console.

docs.title: 22. Practical exercise – version 11
docs.text:
It is still common for web services to send their response as an XML document rather than a JSON document:

  • the JSON document is lighter, but you need instructions to understand it;
  • the XML document is more verbose, but it is self-documenting. It can be understood at a glance.

We modify the client / server application of version 10 so that the server now sends an XML document as its response to its clients. We thus put the previous chapter into practice.

docs.title: 22.1. The server
docs.text:
This architecture will be implemented by the following files:

scripts-web/impots/version-11
├── Data
│   ├── .htaccess
│   ├── config-server.json
│   └── logs.txt
├── Utilities
│   ├── XmlUtilitaires.php
│   └── testXml.php
└── impots-server.php

docs.title: 22.1.1. The [XmlUtilitaires] class
docs.text:
The PHP 7 course added to the [Utilitaires] class a [getXmlForArrayOfAttributes] method that returned the XML document of an array. Our server already uses the [Utilitaires] class of version 5 (for the [Database] class): we create a new class [XmlUtilitaires]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// des fonctions utilitaires pour le format XML : la classe n'est ni instanciable, ni dérivable
final class XmlUtilitaires
{
    // constructeur privé : la classe ne peut être instanciée
    private function __construct()
    {
    }

    // rend le document XML d'un tableau [$data] : l'élément racine s'appelle [$racine]
    // les clés du tableau deviennent des noms d'éléments, les valeurs leur contenu
    public static function arrayToXml(array $data, string $racine): string
    {
        // un document XML vide (nouvelle API DOM de PHP 8.4)
        $document = \Dom\XMLDocument::createEmpty();
        // le document sera indenté
        $document->formatOutput = true;
        // l'élément racine et ses descendants
        $document->append(self::element($document, $racine, $data));
        // le texte XML du document
        return $document->saveXml();
    }

    // rend l'élément XML [<$nom>$valeur</$nom>]
    private static function element(\Dom\XMLDocument $document, string $nom, mixed $valeur): \Dom\Element
    {
        $element = $document->createElement($nom);
        if (is_array($valeur)) {
            // un tableau : chaque élément du tableau devient un élément fils (appel récursif)
            foreach ($valeur as $clé => $sousValeur) {
                // les éléments d'une liste (clés 0, 1, 2...) s'appellent [item]
                $element->append(self::element($document, is_int($clé) ? "item" : $clé, $sousValeur));
            }
        } else {
            // une valeur simple devient le texte de l'élément (les caractères <, >, & sont codés par DOM)
            $element->textContent = match (true) {
                is_bool($valeur) => $valeur ? "true" : "false",
                default => (string) $valeur,
            };
        }
        return $element;
    }
}

Comments

  • line 9: like the [Utilitaires] class of version 5, the class has only static methods. It is [final] and its constructor is private: it can be neither extended nor instantiated;
  • line 18: the static method [arrayToXml] returns the XML document of the array [$data] passed as a parameter. The second parameter is the name of the document's root element;
  • line 21: we use PHP 8.4's new DOM API, presented in the previous chapter. The static method [createEmpty] creates an empty XML document. The PHP 7 script used [SimpleXML], which can also build a document, but less well: you had to encode the special characters of the text yourself with the [htmlspecialchars] function;
  • line 23: the document produced will be indented, which makes it more readable;
  • line 25: we add to the document its root element, built by the [element] method;
  • line 27: the [saveXml] method returns the XML text of the document;
  • line 31: the private method [element] returns the XML element named [$nom] representing the value [$valeur];
  • line 33: the document's [createElement] method creates the element;
  • lines 34-38: if the value is an array, each of its elements becomes a child element, built by a recursive call to the [element] method. The array keys become the names of the child elements. The keys of a list are the integers 0, 1, 2..., which cannot be XML element names: these elements are then called [item]. The PHP 7 script called them [i0], [i1], [i2]...;
  • lines 40-45: otherwise, the value becomes the element's text, assigned to its [textContent] property. The characters [<], [>] and [&] in the text are encoded by DOM ([<], [>], [&]). Booleans are written [true] and [false]; other values are converted to character strings. The [match (true)] expression chooses the first branch whose condition is true.

We write the following test script [testXml.php]:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres et des résultats des fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// dépendance
require_once __DIR__ . "/XmlUtilitaires.php";

use Application\XmlUtilitaires;

// un tableau associatif
$array = [
    "nom" => "amédée",
    "prénom" => "sylvain",
    "âge" => 40,
    "enfants" => [
        ["nom" => "amédée", "prénom" => "béatrice", "âge" => 6],
        ["nom" => "amédée", "prénom" => "bertrand", "âge" => 4],
    ],
    "remarque" => "<marié> & heureux",
];
// la réponse est un document XML
header("Content-Type: application/xml; charset=utf-8");
print XmlUtilitaires::arrayToXml($array, "personne");
  • lines 12-21: an associative array containing a list and a text containing XML special characters;
  • line 23: the [header] function sets the HTTP [Content-Type] header of the response: it is an XML document;
  • line 24: the XML document of the array, with root element [personne], is sent to the client.

Let's request the URL [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-11/Utilities/testXml.php] with [curl]:

> curl http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-11/Utilities/testXml.php
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<personne>
  <nom>amédée</nom>
  <prénom>sylvain</prénom>
  <âge>40</âge>
  <enfants>
    <item>
      <nom>amédée</nom>
      <prénom>béatrice</prénom>
      <âge>6</âge>
    </item>
    <item>
      <nom>amédée</nom>
      <prénom>bertrand</prénom>
      <âge>4</âge>
    </item>
  </enfants>
  <remarque><marié> & heureux</remarque>
</personne>
  • lines 7-18: the [enfants] list and its two [item] elements;
  • line 19: the characters [<], [>] and [&] have been encoded.

A browser displays the same document as a tree:

Note that [Chrome] has decoded the text of the [remarque] element.

docs.title: 22.1.2. The server script
docs.text:
The server script [impots-server.php] must be modified, as well as its configuration file [config-server.json]:

{
    "databaseFilename": "../version-08/Data/database-mysql.json",
    "dependencies": [
        "../../../scripts-console/impots/version-05/Entities/ExceptionImpots.php",
        "../../../scripts-console/impots/version-05/Entities/TaxAdminData.php",
        "../../../scripts-console/impots/version-05/Entities/Database.php",
        "../../../scripts-console/impots/version-05/Utilities/Utilitaires.php",
        "../version-08/Dao/InterfaceServerDao.php",
        "../version-08/Dao/ServerDao.php",
        "../version-09/Dao/ServerDaoWithSession.php",
        "../version-08/Metier/InterfaceServerMetier.php",
        "../version-08/Metier/ServerMetier.php",
        "../version-09/Utilities/Logger.php",
        "../version-09/Utilities/SendAdminMail.php",
        "Utilities/XmlUtilitaires.php"
    ],
  • line 15: we include the new [XmlUtilitaires] class. The rest of the configuration is that of version 10.

The changes to the server script are the following:

}

// envoi de la réponse HTTP au client
// $result : le tableau à envoyer, sous la forme du document XML <réponse>...</réponse>
// $statusCode : le statut HTTP de la réponse
// $headers : des entêtes HTTP à ajouter à la réponse
// $logger : le journal de l'application (null s'il n'a pu être créé)
// $redis : le client Redis (null s'il n'a pas encore été créé)
function sendResponse(
    array $result,
    int $statusCode,
    array $headers = [],
    ?Logger $logger = null,
    ?RedisClient $redis = null
): void {
    // la réponse XML
    $response = new Response(XmlUtilitaires::arrayToXml($result, "réponse"), $statusCode, $headers);
    $response->headers->set("Content-Type", "application/xml; charset=utf-8");
    // envoi
    $response->send();
    // log en JSON, plus concis que le XML
    $logger?->write(json_encode(
        ["réponse" => $result],
        JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_PRESERVE_ZERO_FRACTION
    ));
    // fermeture de la connexion au serveur Redis
    $redis?->disconnect();
}

Comments

  • the [JsonResponse] class is no longer used: the response is a plain [Response];
  • line 212: the server's response is now the XML document, with root element [réponse], of the [$result] array;
  • line 213: we indicate that the response is a UTF-8 encoded XML document;
  • lines 217-220: the response is recorded in the logs as JSON, which is more concise than XML.

The rest of the script is unchanged. Since all responses go through the [sendResponse] function, it is enough to modify that function for all responses, including error responses, to be XML documents.

Test

Let's request the URL [https://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-11/impots-server.php?marié=oui&enfants=2&salaire=60000] with [curl]:

docs.title: 22.2. The client
docs.text:
We now turn to the client side of the application.

This architecture will be implemented by the following files:

scripts-console/impots/version-11
├── Dao
│   └── ClientDao.php
├── Data
│   ├── config-client-ko.json
│   ├── config-client.json
│   ├── errors.json
│   ├── results.json
│   └── taxpayersdata.json
├── Main
│   └── MainImpotsClient.php
└── Tests
    └── ClientMetierTest.php

In the new version, only the following change:

  • the configuration file [config-client.json];
  • the client's [dao] layer.

docs.title: 22.2.1. The [dao] layer
docs.text:
The [ClientDao] class of version 9 is modified to take into account the new format of the response. We use [SimpleXML] to process it:

        try {
            // on fait la requête au serveur
            $response = $this->httpClient->request("GET", $this->urlServer, $options);
            // le statut, les entêtes et le document XML de la réponse, même en cas d'erreur (paramètre false)
            $statusCode = $response->getStatusCode();
            $headers = $response->getHeaders(false);
            $contenu = $response->getContent(false);
        } catch (ExceptionInterface $ex) {
            // le serveur n'a pu être joint
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Erreur de communication avec le serveur ({$ex->getMessage()})", 40, $ex);
        }
        // logs
        // print "$contenu\n";
        // le serveur envoie le document XML <réponse>...</réponse>
        // les options LIBXML_NOERROR et LIBXML_NOWARNING évitent les avertissements de PHP si le XML est invalide
        $xml = simplexml_load_string($contenu, options: LIBXML_NOERROR | LIBXML_NOWARNING);
        if ($xml === false || $xml->getName() !== "réponse") {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Réponse du serveur invalide [$contenu]", 41);
        }
        // erreur ?
        if ($statusCode !== 200) {
            // on lance une exception dont le message est la réponse du serveur, convertie en JSON (plus concis),
            // complétée par son statut HTTP
            $réponse = json_decode(json_encode($xml, JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
            $message = json_encode(
                ["statut HTTP" => $statusCode] + $réponse,
                JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR
            );
            throw new ExceptionImpots($message, 42);
        }
        // on récupère le cookie de session s'il n'est pas encore connu
        if ($this->sessionCookie === null) {
            foreach ($headers["set-cookie"] ?? [] as $cookie) {
                if (preg_match('/^PHPSESSID=(.+?);/', $cookie, $champs) === 1) {
                    $this->sessionCookie = "PHPSESSID=$champs[1]";
                }
            }
        }
        // on rend la réponse : le tableau [impôt, surcôte, décôte, réduction, taux]
        // dans le document XML, toutes les valeurs sont des textes : on les convertit dans leur type
        return [
            "impôt" => (int) $xml->impôt,
            "surcôte" => (int) $xml->surcôte,
            "décôte" => (int) $xml->décôte,
            "réduction" => (int) $xml->réduction,
            "taux" => (float) $xml->taux,
        ];
    }
}

Comments

  • line 63: the server's response is read. It is an XML document [<réponse>…</réponse>];
  • line 72: the [simplexml_load_string] function parses the XML document received and returns a [SimpleXMLElement] object representing its root element, or [false] if the document is not a valid XML document. By default, the [libxml] library used by [SimpleXML] also reports errors in the document as PHP warnings: the [LIBXML_NOERROR] and [LIBXML_NOWARNING] options suppress them. They are passed through the named argument [options], which avoids writing the [class_name] parameter that precedes it in the function's signature;
  • line 73: the [getName] method returns the name of the root element, which must be [réponse];
  • lines 77-85: in case of error, the exception message will be the JSON string of the server's response rather than the XML string received, because the JSON string is more concise. To obtain the associative array of the XML response, we use a classic trick: the [json_encode] function can turn a [SimpleXMLElement] object into JSON, and [json_decode] then turns this JSON into an array. The exception message thus has the same form as in the previous versions;
  • lines 97-103: we return the array of results. The child elements of the [réponse] element are reached as properties of the [$xml] object ([$xml->impôt]). In an XML document, all values are text: unlike JSON, XML does not distinguish between integers, real numbers and character strings. We therefore convert each value to the type expected by the [métier] layer with the [(int)] and [(float)] operators. The PHP 7 client returned the values as character strings.

Test

If we run the client with a correct environment (database, authentication, logs, Redis), we get the usual results:

> php MainImpotsClient.php
Les résultats ont été enregistrés dans le fichier [Data/results.json]
Terminé

Check the files [taxpayersdata.json, results.json, errors.json] in the [Data] folder: the [results.json] file is identical to that of the previous versions. On the server side, the logs are the following:
