docs.title: 13. Practical exercise – version 5
docs.text:
We have already written several versions of this exercise. The last version used a layered architecture:

The [dao] layer implements an [InterfaceDao] interface. We built one class implementing this interface:

  • [DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile], which fetched the tax data from a JSON file.

We are going to implement the [InterfaceDao] interface with a new class [DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase] that will fetch the tax administration's data from a MySQL database.

docs.title: 13.1. Creating the [dbimpots-2019] database
docs.text:
Following the example of the previous chapter, we build a MySQL database named [dbimpots-2019] whose owner will be the user [admimpots] with the password [mdpimpots]. This database will have two tables:

  • the [tbtranches] table will contain the tax brackets;
  • the [tbconstantes] table will contain the constants used in the tax calculation.

The PHP 7 course created the database, the user and the tables with the [phpMyAdmin] wizard, then exported the resulting structure to an SQL file. We take the opposite route: we write the SQL script [dbimpots-2019.sql] directly, placed in the [Data] folder of version 5:

-- base de données [dbimpots-2019] de l'application de calcul de l'impôt - SGBD MySQL
-- à exécuter par l'administrateur [root] du SGBD :
--   mysql -u root < dbimpots-2019.sql
-- la base, ses tables et son utilisateur sont recréés s'ils existent déjà

-- la base de données
DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS `dbimpots-2019`;
CREATE DATABASE `dbimpots-2019` CHARACTER SET utf8mb4;

-- son propriétaire [admimpots] de mot de passe [mdpimpots]
DROP USER IF EXISTS 'admimpots'@'localhost';
CREATE USER 'admimpots'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY 'mdpimpots';
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON `dbimpots-2019`.* TO 'admimpots'@'localhost';

-- les tables sont créées dans la base [dbimpots-2019]
USE `dbimpots-2019`;

-- la table des tranches d'impôt
CREATE TABLE tbtranches (
    id INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
    limites DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    coeffr DECIMAL(6, 2) NOT NULL,
    coeffn DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)
);

-- la table des constantes de calcul de l'impôt
CREATE TABLE tbconstantes (
    id INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
    plafondQfDemiPart DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    valeurReducDemiPart DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    plafondDecoteCelibataire DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    plafondDecoteCouple DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    plafondImpotCouplePourDecote DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    abattementDixPourcentMax DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    abattementDixPourcentMin DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)
);

Comments

  • line 7: the [dbimpots-2019] database is deleted if it exists. The script can thus be run again to regenerate the database if it has been destroyed or corrupted. The database name contains a hyphen: it must be surrounded by backquotes ` so that MySQL does not take it for a subtraction;
  • line 8: creation of the database with the [utf8mb4] character set;
  • lines 11-13: the user [admimpots] with the password [mdpimpots] is (re)created. It has all privileges on the [dbimpots-2019] database;
  • line 16: the following statements apply to the [dbimpots-2019] database;
  • lines 19-25: the [tbtranches] table has four columns:
    • [id] is an integer, the table's primary key, and will be auto-incremented by the DBMS ([AUTO_INCREMENT]). This means that MySQL will manage the primary key values itself at insertion time: it will assign the value 1 to the primary key of the first insertion, then 2 to the next one, and so on;
    • [limites] is a decimal number with 10 digits, 2 of them after the decimal point ([DECIMAL(10, 2)]). It will contain the elements of the [limites] column of the tax brackets;
    • [coeffr] is a decimal number with 6 digits, 2 of them after the decimal point. It will contain the elements of the [coeffR] column of the tax brackets;
    • [coeffn] is a decimal number with 10 digits, 2 of them after the decimal point. It will contain the elements of the [coeffN] column of the tax brackets;
  • lines 28-41: the [tbconstantes] table has a primary key [id] and one decimal column per tax calculation constant. It will have only one row.

The [DECIMAL] type stores numbers exactly, unlike the real types [FLOAT] and [DOUBLE], which store an approximate binary value: 0.14 is stored exactly as 0.14.

This script is run in the [Laragon] terminal, opened in the [version-05/Data] folder, with the command:

mysql -u root < dbimpots-2019.sql

If all goes well, nothing is displayed. We check the result by connecting as [admimpots]:

> mysql -u admimpots -pmdpimpots dbimpots-2019 -e "show tables"
mysql: [Warning] Using a password on the command line interface can be insecure.
+-------------------------+
| Tables_in_dbimpots-2019 |
+-------------------------+
| tbconstantes            |
| tbtranches              |
+-------------------------+

> mysql -u admimpots -pmdpimpots dbimpots-2019 -e "describe tbtranches"
mysql: [Warning] Using a password on the command line interface can be insecure.
+---------+---------------+------+-----+---------+----------------+
| Field   | Type          | Null | Key | Default | Extra          |
+---------+---------------+------+-----+---------+----------------+
| id      | int           | NO   | PRI | NULL    | auto_increment |
| limites | decimal(10,2) | NO   |     | NULL    |                |
| coeffr  | decimal(6,2)  | NO   |     | NULL    |                |
| coeffn  | decimal(10,2) | NO   |     | NULL    |                |
+---------+---------------+------+-----+---------+----------------+
  • line 6: the [id] column is the primary key (PRI) and its values are managed by MySQL (auto_increment).

You can of course also open and run the [dbimpots-2019.sql] script in [HeidiSQL] or [phpMyAdmin], and examine the structure of the tables there.

docs.title: 13.2. Code organization
docs.text:
To better show the role of the various PHP scripts we write, we are going to organize the code of version 5 into folders:

version-05
├── Dao
│   ├── DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase.php
│   ├── DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database.php
│   ├── InterfaceDao.php
│   ├── InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database.php
│   └── TraitDao.php
├── Data
│   ├── database.json
│   ├── dbimpots-2019.sql
│   ├── errors.json
│   ├── resultats.json
│   ├── taxadmindata.json
│   └── taxpayersdata.json
├── Entities
│   ├── Database.php
│   ├── ExceptionImpots.php
│   ├── TaxAdminData.php
│   └── TaxPayerData.php
├── Main
│   ├── MainCalculateImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInMySQLDatabase.php
│   └── MainTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2MySQLDatabase.php
├── Metier
│   ├── InterfaceMetier.php
│   └── Metier.php
├── Tests
│   ├── data
│   │   ├── database-incomplet.json
│   │   └── database-mdp-errone.json
│   ├── DaoTest.php
│   └── MetierTest.php
└── Utilities
    └── Utilitaires.php
  • [Entities]: the application's entities, the objects exchanged between layers;
  • [Utilities]: the application's utilities;
  • [Data]: the data used or produced by the application, and the database's SQL script. We decide here to use only JSON files for text files. They have several advantages:
    • they are recognized by many tools;
    • these tools provide syntax highlighting. Moreover, JSON notation has rules, and when they are not followed, the tools report it. For example, an error that is hard to spot in a basic text file is the use of the capital letter O instead of the digit zero. If in the JSON file we inadvertently write ["plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction": 42O74], [VS Code] underlines the value 42O74 in red, since it is neither a number nor a quoted string, and the [Problems] tab displays the error. The developer's attention is drawn to the mistake and they can fix it;
  • [Dao]: the interfaces, trait and classes of the [dao] layer;
  • [Metier]: the interface and the class of the [métier] layer. The PHP 7 course named this folder [Métier]. We avoid accented characters in folder and file names: they cause problems when files move from one system to another (zip archives, Git repositories…);
  • [Main]: the main scripts of version 5;
  • [Tests]: the [PHPUnit] tests of version 5.

Version 5 has two distinct goals:

  • populate the MySQL database [dbimpots-2019] with the contents of the JSON file [Data/taxadmindata.json];
  • implement the tax calculation with tax data now coming from the MySQL database [dbimpots-2019].

We will deal with these two goals separately.

docs.title: 13.3.1. Goal
docs.text:
The [Data/taxadmindata.json] file contains the tax administration's data. It is the one from version 4:

{
    "limites": [9964, 27519, 73779, 156244, 0],
    "coeffR": [0, 0.14, 0.3, 0.41, 0.45],
    "coeffN": [0, 1394.96, 5798, 13913.69, 20163.45],
    "plafondQfDemiPart": 1551,
    "plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction": 21037,
    "plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction": 42074,
    "valeurReducDemiPart": 3797,
    "plafondDecoteCelibataire": 1196,
    "plafondDecoteCouple": 1970,
    "plafondImpotCouplePourDecote": 2627,
    "plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote": 1595,
    "abattementDixPourcentMax": 12502,
    "abattementDixPourcentMin": 437
}

Our goal is to transfer this data into the MySQL database [dbimpots-2019] created earlier.

docs.title: 13.3.2. The entities
docs.text:
The entities are the objects exchanged between the application's layers. Three of them come from version 4 and are reused without any modification:

  • the exception [ExceptionImpots];
  • the [readonly] class [TaxAdminData] holding the tax administration's data, built by its static methods [fromJsonFile] and [fromArray];
  • the [readonly] class [TaxPayerData] holding a taxpayer's data and the results of their tax calculation.

We add a fourth one, the [Database] entity, which describes the database.

docs.title: 13.3.2.1. Why no [BaseEntity] base class?
docs.text:
At this point the PHP 7 course introduced a parent class [BaseEntity] from which all the entities derived. It relied on a rule: an entity's attributes have the same names as the keys of the JSON file it encapsulates. [BaseEntity] could then initialize any entity from a JSON file or an associative array with the loop:

foreach ($arrayOfAttributes as $key => $value) {
  $this->$key = $value;
}

The entities' attributes were declared [protected] (untyped) so that the parent class could modify them, and each entity added its getters and setters. We do not reuse this solution:

  • the loop above silently creates a dynamic attribute when a key in the JSON file is misspelled. This has been deprecated since PHP 8.2, and is forbidden for [readonly] classes;
  • the entities could be modified by any layer, through their setters or the [setFromArrayOfAttributes] method. Our entities are immutable: a layer cannot accidentally modify an object it has received from another;
  • the rule "same names in the JSON and in the class" is still ours, but PHP 8 exploits it directly: the expression [new self(...$tableau)] turns the array's keys into named arguments of the constructor (PHP 8.1). PHP then checks that no key is missing, that none is unknown and that each value has the right type. There is no longer any common code to factor out into a parent class.

Finally, version 4 already gave the [TaxAdminData] class the [fromArray] method. We will see that it is enough to build a [TaxAdminData] object from the data read from the database. An important consequence is that the [métier] layer of version 4 will be reused without modification: in the PHP 7 course, changing the entities had forced changes to the [métier] layer.

docs.title: 13.3.2.2. The [Database] entity
docs.text:
The [Database] entity will encapsulate the data of the following JSON file [Data/database.json]:

{
    "dsn": "mysql:host=localhost;dbname=dbimpots-2019;charset=utf8mb4",
    "id": "admimpots",
    "pwd": "mdpimpots",
    "tableTranches": "tbtranches",
    "colId": "id",
    "colLimites": "limites",
    "colCoeffR": "coeffr",
    "colCoeffN": "coeffn",
    "tableConstantes": "tbconstantes",
    "colPlafondQfDemiPart": "plafondQfDemiPart",
    "colPlafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction": "plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction",
    "colPlafondRevenusCouplePourReduction": "plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction",
    "colValeurReducDemiPart": "valeurReducDemiPart",
    "colPlafondDecoteCelibataire": "plafondDecoteCelibataire",
    "colPlafondDecoteCouple": "plafondDecoteCouple",
    "colPlafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote": "plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote",
    "colPlafondImpotCouplePourDecote": "plafondImpotCouplePourDecote",
    "colAbattementDixPourcentMax": "abattementDixPourcentMax",
    "colAbattementDixPourcentMin": "abattementDixPourcentMin"
}

Its attributes describe the characteristics of the MySQL database [dbimpots-2019]:

AttributeRoledsnthe database's DSNidthe database ownerpwdits passwordtableTranchesthe name of the table containing the tax bracketscolId / colLimites / colCoeffR / colCoeffNthe names of the columns of the [tableTranches] tabletableConstantesthe name of the table containing the tax calculation constantscolPlafondQfDemiPart / colPlafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction / colPlafondRevenusCouplePourReduction / colValeurReducDemiPart / colPlafondDecoteCelibataire / colPlafondDecoteCouple / colPlafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote / colPlafondImpotCouplePourDecote / colAbattementDixPourcentMax / colAbattementDixPourcentMinthe names of the columns of the [tableConstantes] table containing the tax calculation constants

Why name the tables and columns when we already know their names and they are not likely to change? After the MySQL DBMS, we are going to use the PostgreSQL DBMS to store the tax administration's data. Now, PostgreSQL column and table names do not follow the same rules as MySQL ones. We will have to use other names. The same is true for other DBMSs. If we want code that is portable across DBMSs, it is therefore better to use parameters rather than hard-coded table and column names. Compared with the PHP 7 course, we have added the [colId] attribute, the name of the primary key column of the brackets table: we will need it to read the brackets back in the order in which they were inserted.

The [Database] class is the following [Entities/Database.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// la description de la base de données des données fiscales : un objet immuable
final readonly class Database
{
    // les constantes de calcul de l'impôt : chacune a sa colonne dans la table [tableConstantes]
    public const array CONSTANTES = [
        "plafondQfDemiPart",
        "plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction",
        "plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction",
        "valeurReducDemiPart",
        "plafondDecoteCelibataire",
        "plafondDecoteCouple",
        "plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote",
        "plafondImpotCouplePourDecote",
        "abattementDixPourcentMax",
        "abattementDixPourcentMin",
    ];

    // constructeur privé : on passe obligatoirement par la méthode [fromJsonFile]
    private function __construct(
        // connexion à la base
        public string $dsn,
        public string $id,
        #[\SensitiveParameter] public string $pwd,
        // la table des tranches d'impôt et ses colonnes
        public string $tableTranches,
        public string $colId,
        public string $colLimites,
        public string $colCoeffR,
        public string $colCoeffN,
        // la table des constantes de calcul et ses colonnes
        public string $tableConstantes,
        public string $colPlafondQfDemiPart,
        public string $colPlafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction,
        public string $colPlafondRevenusCouplePourReduction,
        public string $colValeurReducDemiPart,
        public string $colPlafondDecoteCelibataire,
        public string $colPlafondDecoteCouple,
        public string $colPlafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote,
        public string $colPlafondImpotCouplePourDecote,
        public string $colAbattementDixPourcentMax,
        public string $colAbattementDixPourcentMin,
    ) {
    }

    // construction à partir d'un fichier JSON dont les clés sont les noms des attributs
    public static function fromJsonFile(string $databaseFilename): self
    {
        // peut lancer une exception [ExceptionImpots]
        $data = Utilitaires::lireFichierJson($databaseFilename);
        // le JSON doit être un objet {...}
        if (!is_array($data) || array_is_list($data)) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Le fichier [$databaseFilename] ne contient pas un objet JSON", 20);
        }
        try {
            // les clés du tableau deviennent des arguments nommés du constructeur
            return new self(...$data);
        } catch (\Error $ex) {
            // clé inconnue, clé manquante, valeur qui n'est pas une chaîne...
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Le fichier [$databaseFilename] est incorrect ({$ex->getMessage()})", 21, $ex);
        }
    }

    // les noms des colonnes des constantes de calcul : [nom de la constante => nom de la colonne]
    public function colonnesConstantes(): array
    {
        $colonnes = [];
        foreach (self::CONSTANTES as $constante) {
            // la colonne de la constante [plafondQfDemiPart] est dans l'attribut [colPlafondQfDemiPart]
            $colonnes[$constante] = $this->{"col" . ucfirst($constante)};
        }
        return $colonnes;
    }
}

Comments

  • line 9: like [TaxAdminData], the [Database] class is immutable and cannot be extended;
  • lines 12-23: the names of the ten tax calculation constants. They are also the names of the attributes of the [TaxAdminData] class;
  • lines 26-50: the private constructor declares, through promotion, a public attribute of type [string] for each key of the [database.json] file, with the same name;
  • line 30: the PHP 8.2 attribute [#[\SensitiveParameter]] marks the parameter as sensitive. If an exception is thrown while the constructor is running, the password value will not appear in the exception's call stack (stack trace), which is often written to log files: it is replaced there by a [SensitiveParameterValue] object;
  • lines 53-68: the static method [fromJsonFile] builds a [Database] object from a JSON file:
    • line 56: reading and decoding the JSON file are delegated to the [Utilitaires] class presented later. They may throw an [ExceptionImpots] exception;
    • line 58: the JSON must be an object, hence an associative array and not a list;
    • line 63: the keys of the [$data] array become named arguments of the constructor. If a key is missing, PHP throws an [ArgumentCountError] error; if a key is unknown, an [Error] error ("Unknown named parameter"); if a value is not a string, a [TypeError] error. These three errors derive from the [Error] class;
    • lines 64-66: we catch the error and turn it into an [ExceptionImpots] with code 21, keeping the original error ([$ex]) as the previous exception. The PHP error message, included in the message, says precisely what is wrong;
  • lines 71-79: the [colonnesConstantes] method returns the associative array [constant name => column name]. For the constant [plafondQfDemiPart], the column name is in the [colPlafondQfDemiPart] attribute. The [ucfirst] function capitalizes the first letter of a string, and the syntax [$this->{"col" . ucfirst($constante)}] designates the attribute whose name is the value of the expression in braces. This method will save us from writing nearly identical code ten times in the [dao] layer.

docs.title: 13.3.2.3. The [Utilitaires] class
docs.text:
Version 4 used the [Utilitaires] class to remove the end-of-line marker from the lines of a text file. We now use only JSON files: the [Utilitaires] class now groups together the reading and writing of JSON files [Utilities/Utilitaires.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// une classe de fonctions utilitaires : elle n'est ni instanciable, ni dérivable
final class Utilitaires
{
    // constructeur privé : la classe ne peut être instanciée
    private function __construct()
    {
    }

    // lit un fichier JSON et rend son contenu décodé (les objets JSON deviennent des tableaux associatifs)
    public static function lireFichierJson(string $fileName): mixed
    {
        // on récupère le contenu du fichier
        $contenu = is_readable($fileName) ? file_get_contents($fileName) : false;
        if ($contenu === false) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Le fichier [$fileName] n'existe pas ou ne peut être lu", 15);
        }
        // on décode le JSON
        try {
            return json_decode($contenu, true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
        } catch (\JsonException $ex) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Le fichier [$fileName] ne contient pas du JSON valide ({$ex->getMessage()})", 16, $ex);
        }
    }

    // enregistre une valeur au format JSON dans un fichier texte (créé s'il n'existe pas, écrasé sinon)
    public static function écrireFichierJson(string $fileName, mixed $data): void
    {
        // JSON indenté, caractères accentués non échappés, réels toujours écrits avec un point décimal (0.0)
        $json = json_encode($data, JSON_PRETTY_PRINT | JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_PRESERVE_ZERO_FRACTION | JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
        if (@file_put_contents($fileName, "$json\n") === false) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Erreur lors de l'enregistrement de données dans le fichier [$fileName]", 14);
        }
    }
}

Comments

  • lines 17-30: the [lireFichierJson] method reads a JSON file and returns its decoded contents, of any type ([mixed]): a JSON object gives an associative array, a JSON array a list. The code is the one we wrote in the [TaxAdminData::fromJsonFile] method of version 3. Errors are reported by an [ExceptionImpots] with code 15 (unreadable file) or 16 (invalid JSON);
  • lines 33-40: the [écrireFichierJson] method saves a value in JSON format to a text file. The [json_encode] options are combined with the [|] operator:
    • [JSON_PRETTY_PRINT] produces indented JSON that is easy to read;
    • [JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE] writes accented characters as they are (marié) instead of their code (mari\u00e9);
    • [JSON_PRESERVE_ZERO_FRACTION] writes the real number 0.0 as 0.0 and not 0: this distinguishes reals from integers in the file produced;
    • [JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR] makes [json_encode] throw a [JsonException] if the value cannot be encoded as JSON.

docs.title: 13.3.3. The [dao] layer
docs.text:
Now we can write the code that will transfer the data from the JSON file [taxadmindata.json] into the tables [tbtranches, tbconstantes] of the MySQL database [dbimpots-2019]. We will adopt the following architecture:

The [dao] layer will implement the following [InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database] interface [Dao/InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// l'interface de la couche [dao] de transfert des données fiscales dans une base de données
interface InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database
{
    // enregistre les données de l'administration fiscale dans la base de données
    // lance une exception [ExceptionImpots] en cas d'erreur
    public function transferAdminData2Database(): void;
}
  • line 13: the role of the [transferAdminData2Database] method is to store the tax administration's data in a database.

The [InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database] interface will be implemented by the following [DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database] class [Dao/DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// transfert des données de l'administration fiscale d'un fichier JSON vers une base de données
class DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database implements InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database
{
    // la description de la base de données cible
    private readonly Database $database;
    // les données de l'administration fiscale
    private readonly TaxAdminData $taxAdminData;

    // le constructeur
    public function __construct(string $databaseFilename, string $taxAdminDataFilename)
    {
        // peuvent lancer une exception [ExceptionImpots]
        $this->database = Database::fromJsonFile($databaseFilename);
        $this->taxAdminData = TaxAdminData::fromJsonFile($taxAdminDataFilename);
    }

    // transfère les données fiscales dans la base de données
    #[\Override]
    public function transferAdminData2Database(): void
    {
        $database = $this->database;
        try {
            // on ouvre la connexion à la base de données
            $connexion = \PDO::connect($database->dsn, $database->id, $database->pwd);
            // on démarre une transaction
            $connexion->beginTransaction();
            // on remplit la table des tranches d'impôt
            $this->fillTableTranches($connexion);
            // on remplit la table des constantes
            $this->fillTableConstantes($connexion);
            // on termine la transaction sur un succès
            $connexion->commit();
        } catch (\PDOException $ex) {
            // y a-t-il une transaction en cours ?
            if (isset($connexion) && $connexion->inTransaction()) {
                // on termine la transaction sur un échec
                $connexion->rollBack();
            }
            // on remonte l'erreur au code appelant sous la forme d'une exception [ExceptionImpots]
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Erreur d'accès à la base de données ({$ex->getMessage()})", 30, $ex);
        }
        // la connexion est fermée lorsque la variable [$connexion] disparaît, à la fin de la méthode
    }

Comments

Here we use what we learned in the chapter on MySQL.

  • line 9: the [DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database] class implements the [InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database] interface;
  • line 12: the [$database] attribute is the [Database] object encapsulating the data of the [database.json] file;
  • line 14: the [$taxAdminData] attribute is the [TaxAdminData] object encapsulating the data of the [taxadmindata.json] file;
  • lines 17-22: the constructor receives as parameters the names of the files [database.json, taxadmindata.json] and initializes the two attributes. If one of the files is incorrect, an [ExceptionImpots] exception propagates to the calling code;
  • line 26: we implement the single method of the [InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database] interface;
  • line 31: we open the connection to the database. Note the notation [\PDO] to designate PHP's [PDO] class. Indeed, since we are in the [Application] namespace, if we simply wrote [PDO], this relative name would be prefixed with the current namespace and would therefore designate the class [Application\PDO], which does not exist. The [PDO::connect] method returns a [Pdo\Mysql] object here, since the DSN begins with [mysql:]. Nothing in this class depends on MySQL: it is the DSN, read from the [database.json] file, that determines the DBMS used;
  • lines 33-39: we fill the tables [tbtranches, tbconstantes] within a transaction. The [fillTableTranches] and [fillTableConstantes] methods throw a [PDOException] as soon as something goes wrong. In that case, execution continues in the [catch] clause and the database remains in its initial state: there is no risk of ending up with a filled [tbtranches] table and an empty [tbconstantes] table;
  • lines 40-47: the case where an exception was thrown by the code. If a transaction is in progress, it is rolled back. Then we throw an exception of type [ExceptionImpots], with code 30, with the message of the original exception, which becomes the previous exception. The calling code thus has only one type of exception to handle;
  • line 49: the PHP 7 course closed the connection in a [finally] clause with the statement [$connexion = NULL]. This is unnecessary: the local variable [$connexion] disappears at the end of the method, and the connection with it.

The code of the [fillTableTranches] method is the following:

    // remplissage de la table des tranches d'impôt
    private function fillTableTranches(\PDO $connexion): void
    {
        // raccourcis
        $database = $this->database;
        $taxAdminData = $this->taxAdminData;
        // on vide la table au cas où il y aurait quelque chose dedans
        $connexion->exec("delete from $database->tableTranches");
        // on prépare les insertions
        $statement = $connexion->prepare(
            "insert into $database->tableTranches ($database->colLimites, $database->colCoeffR, $database->colCoeffN)"
            . " values (:limites, :coeffR, :coeffN)"
        );
        // on exécute l'ordre préparé avec les valeurs de chaque tranche d'impôt
        foreach ($taxAdminData->limites as $i => $limite) {
            $statement->execute([
                "limites" => $limite,
                "coeffR" => $taxAdminData->coeffR[$i],
                "coeffN" => $taxAdminData->coeffN[$i],
            ]);
        }
    }

Comments

  • line 53: the [fillTableTranches] method receives an open connection as a parameter. We also know that a transaction has been started on this connection;
  • lines 56-57: two shortcuts to avoid writing [$this->database] and [$this->taxAdminData] throughout the code. These are copies of object references, not copies of the objects themselves;
  • line 59: we delete the current contents of the brackets table. The table name is inserted into the string with the syntax ["$database->tableTranches"]: PHP replaces the expression with the value of the attribute;
  • lines 61-64: we prepare the insertion of rows into the table. Here we use the table and column names provided by the [$database] attribute. Table and column names cannot be parameters of a prepared statement: only values can. This is why they are inserted into the text of the SQL statement. They come from a configuration file and not from a user: there is no risk of SQL injection;
  • lines 66-72: we execute the prepared insert statement as many times as necessary, once per tax bracket. [$i] is the bracket number, which serves as an index into the [coeffR] and [coeffN] arrays.

The code of the [fillTableConstantes] method is the following:

    // remplissage de la table des constantes
    private function fillTableConstantes(\PDO $connexion): void
    {
        // raccourci
        $database = $this->database;
        // on vide la table au cas où il y aurait quelque chose dedans
        $connexion->exec("delete from $database->tableConstantes");
        // [nom de la constante => nom de la colonne]
        $colonnes = $database->colonnesConstantes();
        // les paramètres de l'ordre préparé portent les noms des constantes : :plafondQfDemiPart, ...
        $paramètres = array_map(fn(string $constante): string => ":$constante", array_keys($colonnes));
        $statement = $connexion->prepare(
            "insert into $database->tableConstantes (" . implode(", ", $colonnes) . ")"
            . " values (" . implode(", ", $paramètres) . ")"
        );
        // les valeurs des paramètres : [nom de la constante => valeur de la constante]
        $valeurs = [];
        foreach (array_keys($colonnes) as $constante) {
            $valeurs[$constante] = $this->taxAdminData->$constante;
        }
        // on exécute l'ordre préparé : une seule ligne est insérée
        $statement->execute($valeurs);
    }

Comments

  • line 76: the [fillTableConstantes] method also receives an open connection in which a transaction is in progress;
  • line 81: the [tbconstantes] table is emptied;
  • line 83: the array [constant name => column name], for example [["plafondQfDemiPart" => "plafondQfDemiPart", ...]];
  • line 85: the names of the prepared statement's parameters: [[":plafondQfDemiPart", ...]]. These are the names of the constants preceded by a colon;
  • lines 86-89: preparation of the SQL insert statement. The [implode] function builds the list of columns and the list of parameters, separated by commas. We obtain the statement [insert into tbconstantes (plafondQfDemiPart, ...) values (:plafondQfDemiPart, ...)]. The PHP 7 course wrote this statement out in full, column by column, over some twenty lines;
  • lines 91-94: the array of parameter values [constant name => value]. The syntax [$this->taxAdminData->$constante] designates the attribute of the [TaxAdminData] object whose name is the value of the variable [$constante];
  • line 96: execution of the insert statement. There is only one row to insert.

docs.title: 13.3.4. The main script
docs.text:
The main script [Main/MainTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2MySQLDatabase.php] relies on the [dao] layer to perform the data transfer:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres et des résultats des fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// inclusion des interfaces et classes nécessaires au transfert
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/ExceptionImpots.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/TaxAdminData.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/Database.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Utilities/Utilitaires.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database.php";

// définition des constantes
const DATABASE_CONFIG_FILENAME = __DIR__ . "/../Data/database.json";
const TAXADMINDATA_FILENAME = __DIR__ . "/../Data/taxadmindata.json";

try {
    // création de la couche [dao]
    $dao = new DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database(DATABASE_CONFIG_FILENAME, TAXADMINDATA_FILENAME);
    // transfert des données dans la base
    $dao->transferAdminData2Database();
    print "Les données de l'administration fiscale ont été transférées dans la base de données\n";
} catch (ExceptionImpots $ex) {
    // on affiche l'erreur
    print "Erreur n° {$ex->getCode()} : {$ex->getMessage()}\n";
}
// fin
print "Terminé\n";

Comments

  • lines 10-15: loading of the classes and interfaces needed for the transfer. The paths are relative to the script's folder ([Main]): [__DIR__ . "/../Entities"] designates the neighboring [Entities] folder;
  • lines 18-19: the paths of the two JSON files, also relative to the script's folder. The PHP 7 course used paths relative to the current folder (["../Data/database.json"]): the script only worked if it was launched from the [Main] folder;
  • line 23: we instantiate the [dao] layer, passing the names of the two JSON files to the constructor;
  • line 25: we perform the data transfer;
  • lines 27-29: we display the exception's code and message. The PHP 7 course used the [utf8_encode] function here, deprecated since PHP 8.2 and unnecessary since all our messages are in UTF-8.

When we run this script in a terminal opened in the [Main] folder, we get the following result:

> php MainTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2MySQLDatabase.php
Les données de l'administration fiscale ont été transférées dans la base de données
Terminé

and the following contents in the database:

> mysql -u admimpots -pmdpimpots dbimpots-2019 -e "select * from tbtranches"
mysql: [Warning] Using a password on the command line interface can be insecure.
+----+-----------+--------+----------+
| id | limites   | coeffr | coeffn   |
+----+-----------+--------+----------+
|  1 |   9964.00 |   0.00 |     0.00 |
|  2 |  27519.00 |   0.14 |  1394.96 |
|  3 |  73779.00 |   0.30 |  5798.00 |
|  4 | 156244.00 |   0.41 | 13913.69 |
|  5 |      0.00 |   0.45 | 20163.45 |
+----+-----------+--------+----------+
  • [id] column: the values assigned by MySQL to the primary key. Numbering starts at 1. If the script is run again, the rows are deleted and then reinserted, and MySQL continues the numbering (6, 7…): an auto-incremented key value is never reused;
  • the numbers have two decimal places, in accordance with the [DECIMAL(10, 2)] type of the columns.

The [\G] option at the end of the SQL statement displays each row vertically, one column per screen line, which is more readable for a table with many columns:

> mysql -u admimpots -pmdpimpots dbimpots-2019 -e "select * from tbconstantes\G"
mysql: [Warning] Using a password on the command line interface can be insecure.
*************************** 1. row ***************************
                                    id: 1
                     plafondQfDemiPart: 1551.00
plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction: 21037.00
     plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction: 42074.00
                   valeurReducDemiPart: 3797.00
              plafondDecoteCelibataire: 1196.00
                   plafondDecoteCouple: 1970.00
     plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote: 1595.00
          plafondImpotCouplePourDecote: 2627.00
              abattementDixPourcentMax: 12502.00
              abattementDixPourcentMin: 437.00

docs.title: 13.4.1. Architecture
docs.text:
Version 4 of the tax calculation application used a layered architecture:

The [dao] layer implements an [InterfaceDao] interface. The [DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile] class of version 4 fetched the tax data from a JSON file. We are going to implement the [InterfaceDao] interface with a new class [DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase] that will fetch the tax administration's data from the MySQL database. The [dao] layer, as before, will write the results and errors to text files and will also find the taxpayers' data in a text file. Only this time, these text files will be JSON files. Moreover, we know that if we keep respecting the [InterfaceDao] interface, the [métier] layer will not need to be modified.

docs.title: 13.4.2. The [TaxPayerData] entity
docs.text:
The [TaxPayerData] class of version 4 encapsulates a taxpayer's data [marié, enfants, salaire] and the results of their tax calculation [impôt, surcôte, décôte, réduction, taux]. It is reused as is. The taxpayers' data is now in the following JSON file [Data/taxpayersdata.json]:

    },

    {

    },

The keys of the JSON objects are the names of the attributes of the [TaxPayerData] class. Note:

  • line 8: taxpayer no. 1 (numbering starts at 0) is erroneous: all three of their data items are invalid;
  • line 14: the number of children of taxpayer no. 2 is given as a character string. We will accept it;
  • the eleven other taxpayers are those of the tax administration's official tests, used since version 1.

docs.title: 13.4.3.1. The [InterfaceDao] interface
docs.text:
The [InterfaceDao] interface of version 4 is reused without modification [Dao/InterfaceDao.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// l'interface de la couche [dao]
// toutes les méthodes lancent une exception [ExceptionImpots] en cas d'erreur irrécupérable
interface InterfaceDao
{
    // lecture des données contribuables
    // les lignes erronées sont signalées dans le fichier texte [$errorsFilename]
    /** @return TaxPayerData[] */
    public function getTaxPayersData(string $taxPayersFilename, string $errorsFilename): array;

    // lecture des données de l'administration fiscale (tranches d'impôt et constantes)
    public function getTaxAdminData(): TaxAdminData;

    // enregistrement des résultats
    /** @param TaxPayerData[] $taxPayersData */
    public function saveResults(string $resultsFilename, array $taxPayersData): void;
}

The [getTaxPayersData] and [saveResults] methods receive file names: nothing there says whether they are basic text files or JSON files. The interface therefore remains valid.

docs.title: 13.4.3.2. The [TraitDao] trait
docs.text:
The [TraitDao] trait implements the [getTaxPayersData] and [saveResults] methods of the [InterfaceDao] interface. Since we have moved from basic text files to JSON files, we need to rewrite it [Dao/TraitDao.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// implémentation des méthodes de [InterfaceDao] qui travaillent avec des fichiers JSON
trait TraitDao
{
    // lecture des données contribuables dans un fichier JSON
    #[\Override]
    public function getTaxPayersData(string $taxPayersFilename, string $errorsFilename): array
    {
        // le contenu du fichier : un tableau d'objets {marié, enfants, salaire}
        // peut lancer une exception [ExceptionImpots]
        $contribuables = Utilitaires::lireFichierJson($taxPayersFilename);
        if (!is_array($contribuables) || !array_is_list($contribuables)) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Le fichier [$taxPayersFilename] ne contient pas un tableau JSON", 17);
        }
        // tableau des données contribuables
        $taxPayersData = [];
        // tableau des erreurs
        $errors = [];
        // on vérifie chacun des contribuables
        foreach ($contribuables as $numéro => $contribuable) {
            $erreurs = $this->check($contribuable);
            if ($erreurs === []) {
                // un contribuable de plus
                $taxPayersData[] = new TaxPayerData(
                    strtolower(trim($contribuable["marié"])),
                    (int) $contribuable["enfants"],
                    (int) $contribuable["salaire"]
                );
            } else {
                // une erreur de plus : on note le numéro du contribuable erroné dans le tableau JSON
                $errors[] = ["numéro" => $numéro, "erreurs" => $erreurs];
            }
        }
        // on enregistre les erreurs dans un fichier JSON
        Utilitaires::écrireFichierJson($errorsFilename, $errors);
        // résultat de la fonction
        return $taxPayersData;
    }

    // vérification des données d'un contribuable : rend la liste des attributs erronés
    private function check(mixed $contribuable): array
    {
        // le contribuable doit être un objet JSON
        if (!is_array($contribuable)) {
            return [["contribuable" => $contribuable]];
        }
        $erreurs = [];
        // le statut marital doit être oui ou non
        $marié = $contribuable["marié"] ?? null;
        if (!is_string($marié) || !in_array(strtolower(trim($marié)), ["oui", "non"], true)) {
            $erreurs[] = ["marié" => $marié];
        }
        // le nombre d'enfants et le salaire doivent être des entiers positifs ou nuls
        // donnés sous la forme d'un nombre (2) ou d'une chaîne ("2")
        foreach (["enfants", "salaire"] as $clé) {
            $valeur = $contribuable[$clé] ?? null;
            $valide = (is_int($valeur) && $valeur >= 0)
                || (is_string($valeur) && preg_match('/^\s*\d+\s*$/', $valeur) === 1);
            if (!$valide) {
                $erreurs[] = [$clé => $valeur];
            }
        }
        return $erreurs;
    }

    // enregistrement des résultats dans un fichier JSON
    #[\Override]
    public function saveResults(string $resultsFilename, array $taxPayersData): void
    {
        // les objets [TaxPayerData] sont transformés en objets JSON à partir de leurs attributs publics
        Utilitaires::écrireFichierJson($resultsFilename, $taxPayersData);
    }
}

Comments

  • lines 13-44: the [getTaxPayersData] method receives as parameters:
    • [$taxPayersFilename]: the name of the JSON file of taxpayer data [taxpayersdata.json];
    • [$errorsFilename]: the name of the JSON error file [errors.json];
  • line 17: the contents of the JSON file of taxpayer data are decoded into the [$contribuables] array. If the JSON file turns out to be unusable, an [ExceptionImpots] exception is thrown;
  • line 18: the contents must be a JSON array, hence a PHP list. Otherwise, an exception with code 17 is thrown;
  • line 22: the [$taxPayersData] array will contain the taxpayers' data encapsulated in [TaxPayerData] objects;
  • line 24: errors will be accumulated in the [$errors] array;
  • lines 26-39: construction of the [$taxPayersData] array. Before being encapsulated in a [TaxPayerData] object, the data is checked by the [check] method, which returns the list of erroneous attributes, empty if the data is correct:
    • lines 30-34: the case where the data is valid. A new [TaxPayerData] object is built and added to the [$taxPayersData] array. The marital status is converted to lowercase, the number of children and the salary to integers: [(int) "2"] is 2;
    • line 37: the case where the data is invalid. We record in the error the index of the erroneous taxpayer in the JSON array so that the user can find it, then the error is added to the [$errors] array;
  • line 41: the errors encountered are saved to the JSON file [$errorsFilename]. The PHP 7 course wrote one JSON string per error, one per line: with several errors, the file was not a valid JSON file. We write a JSON array of the errors;
  • line 43: we return the array of [TaxPayerData] objects built: that was the purpose of the method;
  • lines 47-70: the private method [check] checks the validity of a taxpayer's data. The [$contribuable] parameter is of type [mixed]: an element of the JSON array can be anything (an object, a number, a string…). The method accumulates the erroneous attributes in the [$erreurs] array in the form of arrays [erroneous attribute => value]:
    • line 50: the element must be a JSON object;
    • line 55: the [??] operator (null coalescing) returns the value of [$contribuable["marié"]] if it exists and is not [null], and [null] otherwise. This avoids the warning that a missing key would trigger;
    • lines 56-58: the marital status must be a string equal to oui or non (yes or no), ignoring case and spaces;
    • lines 61-68: the number of children and the salary must be non-negative integers, given as a JSON number (2) or a string ("2"). A string must consist of digits, possibly surrounded by spaces: this is what the regular expression [/^\s*\d+\s*$/] checks. Note the comparison [preg_match(...) === 1]: the [preg_match] function returns 1 if the string matches the pattern, 0 otherwise, and [false] on error;
  • lines 74-78: the implementation of the [saveResults] method of the [InterfaceDao] interface. The array of [TaxPayerData] objects is saved directly in JSON format: the [json_encode] function turns an object into a JSON object whose keys are the names of its public attributes. The PHP 7 course built the JSON string of the array "by hand", concatenating the JSON strings of the objects separated by commas and adding the square brackets.

docs.title: 13.4.3.3. The [DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase] class
docs.text:
The [DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase] class implements the [InterfaceDao] interface as follows [Dao/DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// une couche [dao] qui trouve les données de l'administration fiscale dans une base de données
class DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase implements InterfaceDao
{
    // le trait implémente les méthodes [getTaxPayersData] et [saveResults] de l'interface
    use TraitDao;

    // la description de la base de données
    private readonly Database $database;
    // l'objet de type [TaxAdminData] qui contient les données de l'administration fiscale
    private readonly TaxAdminData $taxAdminData;

    // le constructeur
    public function __construct(string $databaseFilename)
    {
        // la description de la base de données - peut lancer une exception [ExceptionImpots]
        $this->database = Database::fromJsonFile($databaseFilename);
        $database = $this->database;
        try {
            // on ouvre la connexion à la base de données
            // les lignes lues seront rendues sous la forme de tableaux associatifs [colonne => valeur]
            $connexion = \PDO::connect(
                $database->dsn,
                $database->id,
                $database->pwd,
                [\PDO::ATTR_DEFAULT_FETCH_MODE => \PDO::FETCH_ASSOC]
            );
            // on démarre une transaction
            $connexion->beginTransaction();
            // on lit la table des tranches d'impôt
            $tranches = $this->getTranches($connexion);
            // on lit la table des constantes
            $constantes = $this->getConstantes($connexion);
            // on termine la transaction sur un succès
            $connexion->commit();
        } catch (\PDOException $ex) {
            // y a-t-il une transaction en cours ?
            if (isset($connexion) && $connexion->inTransaction()) {
                // on termine la transaction sur un échec
                $connexion->rollBack();
            }
            // on remonte l'erreur au code appelant sous la forme d'une exception [ExceptionImpots]
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Erreur d'accès à la base de données ({$ex->getMessage()})", 30, $ex);
        }
        // construction de l'objet [TaxAdminData] : les données lues sont vérifiées
        $this->taxAdminData = TaxAdminData::fromArray([...$tranches, ...$constantes]);
    }

Comments

  • line 6: we keep the namespace already used for the application's other classes;
  • line 9: the [DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase] class implements the [InterfaceDao] interface;
  • line 12: we import the [TraitDao] trait. We know that this trait implements part of the interface. The only method left to implement is the [getTaxAdminData] method, which simply returns the private attribute [$taxAdminData]. We conclude that the constructor will have to initialize this attribute. That is its only role;
  • line 20: the constructor receives as its only parameter the name of the JSON file [database.json] that defines the MySQL database [dbimpots-2019];
  • line 23: the JSON file is used to create a [Database] object stored in the [$database] attribute. If the JSON file could not be processed correctly, an [ExceptionImpots] exception is thrown;
  • lines 28-33: we open the connection to the database. The 4th parameter sets the default read mode for rows: associative arrays [column => value];
  • line 35: we start a transaction. It is not essential, since only two SQL statements will be executed, statements that do not modify the database. We do it nonetheless to isolate ourselves from the other users of the database: both tables are read in the same state, even if another program modifies them at the same moment;
  • line 37: the tax brackets table [tbtranches] is read by the private method [getTranches]. It returns the array [["limites" => [...], "coeffR" => [...], "coeffN" => [...]]];
  • line 39: the calculation constants table [tbconstantes] is read by the private method [getConstantes]. It returns the array [constant name => value];
  • line 41: if we reach this line, everything went well. We therefore commit the transaction;
  • lines 42-49: if we get here, an exception occurred. We therefore roll back the transaction if one was in progress. Then, to have uniform exceptions, we rethrow the error in the form of an [ExceptionImpots] exception with code 30;
  • line 52: the expression [[...$tranches, ...$constantes]] merges the two associative arrays into one, which has exactly the thirteen keys expected by the [TaxAdminData::fromArray] method. That method checks the data read from the database, just as it checked the data from the JSON file, and converts it to reals. The PHP 7 course initialized the [TaxAdminData] object attribute by attribute, with ten setter calls.

The [getTranches] method is the following:

    // lecture de la table des tranches d'impôt
    // rend le tableau ["limites" => [...], "coeffR" => [...], "coeffN" => [...]]
    private function getTranches(\PDO $connexion): array
    {
        // raccourci
        $database = $this->database;
        // on prépare puis on exécute la requête SELECT
        $statement = $connexion->prepare(
            "select $database->colLimites, $database->colCoeffR, $database->colCoeffN"
            . " from $database->tableTranches order by $database->colId"
        );
        $statement->execute();
        // toutes les lignes en une fois : un tableau de tableaux associatifs
        $tranches = $statement->fetchAll();
        // on extrait chaque colonne du résultat
        return [
            "limites" => array_column($tranches, $database->colLimites),
            "coeffR" => array_column($tranches, $database->colCoeffR),
            "coeffN" => array_column($tranches, $database->colCoeffN),
        ];
    }

Comments

  • line 57: the method receives as a parameter an open connection in which a transaction is in progress;
  • lines 62-65: the SELECT statement is prepared and then executed. The [order by] clause on the primary key guarantees that the brackets are read back in the order in which they were inserted. The PHP 7 course did not have this clause and relied on the order in which MySQL returned the rows, which is not guaranteed;
  • line 68: all the result rows are read at once. We obtain an array of associative arrays, for example [[["limites" => "9964.00", "coeffr" => "0.00", "coeffn" => "0.00"], ...]]. Note that the values of [DECIMAL] columns are returned as character strings: PHP has no exact decimal type, and the driver does not convert them to [float], which would lose exactness. The [TaxAdminData::fromArray] method will do the conversion;
  • lines 70-74: the [array_column] function extracts a column from an array of associative arrays: [array_column($tranches, "limites")] returns [["9964.00", "27519.00", ...]].

The private method [getConstantes] is the following:

    // lecture de la table des constantes de calcul
    // rend le tableau [nom de la constante => valeur]
    private function getConstantes(\PDO $connexion): array
    {
        // [nom de la constante => nom de la colonne]
        $colonnes = $this->database->colonnesConstantes();
        // on prépare puis on exécute la requête SELECT
        $statement = $connexion->prepare(
            "select " . implode(", ", $colonnes) . " from {$this->database->tableConstantes}"
        );
        $statement->execute();
        // on exploite le résultat - 1 seule ligne ici - [false] si la table est vide
        $ligne = $statement->fetch() ?: [];
        // [nom de la constante => valeur de sa colonne] (null si la table est vide)
        return array_map(fn(string $colonne): mixed => $ligne[$colonne] ?? null, $colonnes);
    }

Comments

  • line 82: the array [constant name => column name];
  • lines 84-86: the SELECT statement for the ten columns is prepared and then executed. Note the braces in [{$this->database->tableConstantes}]: without them, PHP would only interpret [$this->database] in the string;
  • line 89: the table has only one row, read by the [fetch] method, which returns [false] if there is no row. The [?:] operator returns its left operand if it evaluates to true, and its right operand otherwise: [$ligne] is therefore an empty array if the table is empty;
  • line 91: for each constant, we look up the value of its column in [$ligne]. The [array_map] function applied to a single array preserves its keys: we obtain the array [constant name => value]. If the table is empty, all the values are [null] and the [TaxAdminData::fromArray] method will report an invalid value.

Note that the class does not depend on the MySQL DBMS. It is the [database.json] file that determines the DBMS used, through the database's DSN.

docs.title: 13.4.4. The [métier] layer
docs.text:
• we have just implemented the [dao] layer [3];
  • because we respected the [InterfaceDao] interface, the [métier] layer [2] can remain unchanged. The PHP 7 course nevertheless had to modify it, because it had also changed the entities exchanged between the layers: the [executeBatchImpots] method used the setters of the version 4 [TaxPayerData] class, which had disappeared. Here, the entities have not changed.

The [InterfaceMetier] interface and the [Metier] class of version 4 are therefore reused without any modification in the [Metier] folder. Let us recall the [executeBatchImpots] method:

    // calcul des impôts en mode batch
    // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    #[\Override]
    public function executeBatchImpots(string $taxPayersFileName, string $resultsFileName, string $errorsFileName): void
    {
        // on laisse remonter les exceptions qui proviennent de la couche [dao]
        // on récupère les données contribuables
        $taxPayersData = $this->dao->getTaxPayersData($taxPayersFileName, $errorsFileName);
        // on calcule l'impôt de chacun des contribuables
        $results = array_map(
            fn(TaxPayerData $taxPayerData): TaxPayerData => $taxPayerData->avecRésultats(
                $this->calculerImpot($taxPayerData->marié, $taxPayerData->enfants, $taxPayerData->salaire)
            ),
            $taxPayersData
        );
        // enregistrement des résultats
        $this->dao->saveResults($resultsFileName, $results);
    }
}
  • line 192: the [métier] layer does not know that the taxpayers' data now comes from a JSON file: it asks the [dao] layer for the data and receives an array of [TaxPayerData] objects, as in version 4;
  • line 201: likewise, it is unaware that the results are saved in JSON format.

docs.title: 13.4.5. The main script
docs.text:
• we have just implemented the [dao] [3] and [métier] [2] layers;
  • all that remains is to write the main script [1].

The main script [Main/MainCalculateImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInMySQLDatabase.php] is similar to that of version 4:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres et des résultats des fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// inclusion des interfaces et classes
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/ExceptionImpots.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/TaxAdminData.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/TaxPayerData.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/Database.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Utilities/Utilitaires.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/InterfaceDao.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/TraitDao.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Metier/InterfaceMetier.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Metier/Metier.php";

// définition des constantes
const DATABASE_CONFIG_FILENAME = __DIR__ . "/../Data/database.json";
const TAXPAYERSDATA_FILENAME = __DIR__ . "/../Data/taxpayersdata.json";
const RESULTS_FILENAME = __DIR__ . "/../Data/resultats.json";
const ERRORS_FILENAME = __DIR__ . "/../Data/errors.json";

try {
    // création de la couche [dao]
    $dao = new DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase(DATABASE_CONFIG_FILENAME);
    // création de la couche [métier]
    $métier = new Metier($dao);
    // calcul de l'impôt en mode batch
    $métier->executeBatchImpots(TAXPAYERSDATA_FILENAME, RESULTS_FILENAME, ERRORS_FILENAME);
    print "Les résultats ont été enregistrés dans le fichier [resultats.json]\n";
} catch (ExceptionImpots $ex) {
    // on affiche l'erreur
    print "Erreur n° {$ex->getCode()} : {$ex->getMessage()}\n";
}
// fin
print "Terminé\n";

Comments

  • lines 10-19: loading of all the files needed for the tax calculation;
  • lines 22-25: the names of the application's various JSON files;
  • line 29: construction of the [dao] layer;
  • line 31: construction of the [métier] layer;
  • line 33: call to the [executeBatchImpots] method of the [métier] layer.

The results

> php MainCalculateImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInMySQLDatabase.php
Les résultats ont été enregistrés dans le fichier [resultats.json]
Terminé

docs.title: 13.5. [PHPUnit] tests
docs.text: As was done for version 4, we are going to write [PHPUnit] tests for version 5. They are in the [version-05/Tests] folder.

docs.title: 13.5.1. Testing the [dao] layer
docs.text:
The [Tests/DaoTest.php] test is the following:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres et des résultats des fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms des tests
namespace Application\Tests;

// les classes testées
use Application\DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase;
use Application\DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database;
use Application\ExceptionImpots;
use Application\InterfaceDao;
use Application\TaxAdminData;
use Application\TaxPayerData;
// les classes de PHPUnit
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

// chargement des classes de la couche [dao]
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/ExceptionImpots.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/TaxAdminData.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/TaxPayerData.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/Database.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Utilities/Utilitaires.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/InterfaceDao.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/TraitDao.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database.php";

final class DaoTest extends TestCase
{
    // le dossier des données de la version 5
    private const string DATA = __DIR__ . "/../Data";
    // la couche [dao] testée
    private InterfaceDao $dao;
    // un fichier temporaire pour les erreurs
    private string $errorsFilename;

    // exécutée avant chaque test
    #[\Override]
    protected function setUp(): void
    {
        // création de la couche [dao]
        $this->dao = new DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase(self::DATA . "/database.json");
        // un fichier temporaire
        $this->errorsFilename = tempnam(sys_get_temp_dir(), "errors");
    }

    // exécutée après chaque test
    #[\Override]
    protected function tearDown(): void
    {
        // suppression du fichier temporaire
        unlink($this->errorsFilename);
    }

    // les données de l'administration fiscale lues dans la base de données
    public function testTaxAdminData(): void
    {
        $taxAdminData = $this->dao->getTaxAdminData();
        // constantes de calcul
        $this->assertSame(1551.0, $taxAdminData->plafondQfDemiPart);
        $this->assertSame(21037.0, $taxAdminData->plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction);
        $this->assertSame(42074.0, $taxAdminData->plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction);
        $this->assertSame(3797.0, $taxAdminData->valeurReducDemiPart);
        $this->assertSame(1196.0, $taxAdminData->plafondDecoteCelibataire);
        $this->assertSame(1970.0, $taxAdminData->plafondDecoteCouple);
        $this->assertSame(1595.0, $taxAdminData->plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote);
        $this->assertSame(2627.0, $taxAdminData->plafondImpotCouplePourDecote);
        $this->assertSame(12502.0, $taxAdminData->abattementDixPourcentMax);
        $this->assertSame(437.0, $taxAdminData->abattementDixPourcentMin);
        // tranches de l'impôt
        $this->assertSame([9964.0, 27519.0, 73779.0, 156244.0, 0.0], $taxAdminData->limites);
        $this->assertSame([0.0, 0.14, 0.30, 0.41, 0.45], $taxAdminData->coeffR);
        $this->assertSame([0.0, 1394.96, 5798.0, 13913.69, 20163.45], $taxAdminData->coeffN);
    }

    // le transfert du fichier JSON vers la base, puis la relecture de la base
    public function testTransfert(): void
    {
        // transfert
        (new DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database(self::DATA . "/database.json", self::DATA . "/taxadmindata.json"))
            ->transferAdminData2Database();
        // relecture de la base par une nouvelle couche [dao]
        $dao = new DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase(self::DATA . "/database.json");
        // la base contient les données du fichier JSON
        $this->assertEquals(TaxAdminData::fromJsonFile(self::DATA . "/taxadmindata.json"), $dao->getTaxAdminData());
    }

    // des descriptions de la base de données incorrectes
    public static function basesInvalides(): array
    {
        // [nom du fichier, code d'erreur attendu]
        return [
            "fichier inexistant" => ["inexistant.json", 15],
            "clé manquante" => ["database-incomplet.json", 21],
            "mot de passe erroné" => ["database-mdp-errone.json", 30],
        ];
    }

    #[DataProvider("basesInvalides")]
    public function testBasesInvalides(string $fichier, int $code): void
    {
        // on attend une exception [ExceptionImpots] avec un code précis
        $this->expectException(ExceptionImpots::class);
        $this->expectExceptionCode($code);
        // construction d'une couche [dao] avec une description de base incorrecte
        new DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase(__DIR__ . "/data/$fichier");
    }

    // les données des contribuables lues dans un fichier JSON
    public function testTaxPayersData(): void
    {
        $taxPayersData = $this->dao->getTaxPayersData(self::DATA . "/taxpayersdata.json", $this->errorsFilename);
        // 11 contribuables corrects
        $this->assertCount(11, $taxPayersData);
        $this->assertContainsOnlyInstancesOf(TaxPayerData::class, $taxPayersData);
        // le premier et le dernier
        $this->assertEquals(new TaxPayerData("oui", 2, 55555), $taxPayersData[0]);
        $this->assertEquals(new TaxPayerData("oui", 3, 200000), $taxPayersData[10]);
        // le contribuable n° 1 du fichier JSON est erroné
        $erreurs = json_decode(file_get_contents($this->errorsFilename), true);
        $this->assertSame([
            ["numéro" => 1, "erreurs" => [["marié" => "ouix"], ["enfants" => "2x"], ["salaire" => "55555x"]]],
        ], $erreurs);
    }

    // un fichier des contribuables inexistant
    public function testTaxPayersDataInexistant(): void
    {
        $this->expectException(ExceptionImpots::class);
        $this->expectExceptionCode(15);
        $this->dao->getTaxPayersData(self::DATA . "/inexistant.json", $this->errorsFilename);
    }
}

Comments

  • lines 21-30: definition of the test environment. We load the files of the two [dao] layers of version 5: the transfer one and the tax calculation one;
  • lines 43-49: before each test, we build the [dao] layer with the [Data/database.json] file, as the main script does;
  • line 60: the [testTaxAdminData] method is identical to that of version 4. But this time, the data tested has been read from the database;
  • lines 81-90: we test the transfer from the JSON file to the database, then read the database back with a new [dao] layer. The [TaxAdminData] object obtained must be equal ([assertEquals]) to the one built from the JSON file. This test assumes that the transfer has indeed put the data of the [taxadmindata.json] file back into the database: it does not modify the data expected by the other tests;
  • lines 93-101: three incorrect descriptions of the database: a non-existent file (code 15), a [database-incomplet.json] file missing the [colCoeffN] key (code 21), a [database-mdp-errone.json] file with a wrong password (code 30). The last two files are in the [Tests/data] folder;
  • lines 104-111: we check that a [dao] layer built with an incorrect description throws an [ExceptionImpots] exception with the right error code;
  • lines 114-128: reading the taxpayers' data from the JSON file. We check the number of taxpayers obtained and the contents of the first and last ones, then the exact contents of the error file;
  • line 131: a non-existent taxpayers file must cause an exception with code 15.
