docs.title: 18.3.1. The entities exchanged between layers
docs.text:
The client's entities have all been described and already used in version 5:

  • the [ExceptionImpots] exception;
  • a taxpayer's data [TaxPayerData].

Like the server, the client loads them from the version 5 folder, together with the [Utilitaires] class and the [TraitDao] trait.

docs.title: 18.3.2. The [dao] layer
docs.text:
The [dao] layer implements the following [InterfaceClientDao] interface:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// l'interface de la couche [dao] du client
// toutes les méthodes lancent une exception [ExceptionImpots] en cas d'erreur
interface InterfaceClientDao
{
    // lecture des données contribuables
    // les données erronées sont signalées dans le fichier JSON [$errorsFilename]
    /** @return TaxPayerData[] */
    public function getTaxPayersData(string $taxPayersFilename, string $errorsFilename): array;

    // calcul de l'impôt d'un contribuable par le serveur
    // rend le tableau [impôt, surcôte, décôte, réduction, taux]
    public function calculerImpot(string $marié, int $enfants, int $salaire): array;

    // enregistrement des résultats
    /** @param TaxPayerData[] $taxPayersData */
    public function saveResults(string $resultsFilename, array $taxPayersData): void;
}
  • line 15: the [getTaxPayersData] method loads into memory the taxpayers' data from the JSON file [$taxPayersFilename]. If there are errors, they are recorded in the JSON file [$errorsFilename];
  • line 19: the [calculerImpot] method calculates a taxpayer's tax;
  • line 23: the [saveResults] method saves to the [$resultsFilename] file the data of the [$taxPayersData] array, which represent the results of several tax calculations.

The [getTaxPayersData] and [saveResults] methods are those of the [InterfaceDao] interface of version 5. The [InterfaceClientDao] interface is implemented by the following [ClientDao] class:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// dépendances Symfony
use Symfony\Component\HttpClient\HttpClient;
use Symfony\Contracts\HttpClient\Exception\ExceptionInterface;
use Symfony\Contracts\HttpClient\HttpClientInterface;

// la couche [dao] du client : un client HTTP du serveur de calcul de l'impôt
class ClientDao implements InterfaceClientDao
{
    // le trait de la version 5 implémente les méthodes [getTaxPayersData] et [saveResults] de l'interface
    use TraitDao;

    // le client HTTP
    private readonly HttpClientInterface $httpClient;

    // constructeur
    // $urlServer : l'URL du serveur de calcul de l'impôt
    // $user : l'utilisateur qui fait les requêtes, tableau [login, passwd]
    // $httpClientOptions : des options supplémentaires du client HTTP (verify_peer, verify_host...)
    public function __construct(
        private readonly string $urlServer,
        #[\SensitiveParameter] array $user,
        array $httpClientOptions = [],
    ) {
        // le client HTTP : les identifiants de l'utilisateur seront envoyés avec chaque requête
        $this->httpClient = HttpClient::create([
            ...$httpClientOptions,
            "auth_basic" => [$user["login"], $user["passwd"]],
        ]);
    }

    // calcul de l'impôt par le serveur
    #[\Override]
    public function calculerImpot(string $marié, int $enfants, int $salaire): array
    {
        try {
            // on fait la requête au serveur
            $response = $this->httpClient->request("GET", $this->urlServer, [
                "query" => [
                    "marié" => $marié,
                    "enfants" => $enfants,
                    "salaire" => $salaire,
                ],
            ]);
            // le statut de la réponse
            $statusCode = $response->getStatusCode();
            // le document JSON de la réponse, même si le statut est un code d'erreur (paramètre false)
            $json = $response->getContent(false);
        } catch (ExceptionInterface $ex) {
            // le serveur n'a pu être joint
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Erreur de communication avec le serveur ({$ex->getMessage()})", 40, $ex);
        }
        // logs
        // print "$json\n";
        // le serveur envoie la chaîne JSON d'un tableau ["réponse" => qqChose]
        try {
            $réponse = json_decode($json, true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR)["réponse"] ?? null;
        } catch (\JsonException $ex) {
            $réponse = null;
        }
        if (!is_array($réponse)) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Réponse du serveur invalide [$json]", 41);
        }
        // erreur ?
        if ($statusCode !== 200) {
            // on lance une exception dont le message est la réponse du serveur complétée par son statut HTTP
            $message = json_encode(
                ["statut HTTP" => $statusCode] + $réponse,
                JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR
            );
            throw new ExceptionImpots($message, 42);
        }
        // on rend la réponse : le tableau [impôt, surcôte, décôte, réduction, taux]
        return $réponse;
    }
}

Comments

  • line 17: we insert the [TraitDao] trait of version 5, which implements the [getTaxPayersData] and [saveResults] methods. So only the [calculerImpot] method remains to be implemented;
  • line 20: the [Symfony] HTTP client, of the [HttpClientInterface] interface type;
  • lines 26-30: the constructor of the [ClientDao] class receives three parameters:
    • the URL [$urlServer] of the tax calculation server. This is a parameter promoted to an attribute (constructor property promotion);
    • the [$user] array with keys [login] and [passwd], which defines the user making the requests. The [#[\SensitiveParameter]] attribute (PHP 8.2) asks PHP to hide the value of this parameter in the stack traces displayed in the event of an error: the password will not appear in them;
    • additional options for the HTTP client;
  • lines 32-35: we create the HTTP client once and for all, with the options received, to which we add the [auth_basic] option: the user's credentials will be sent with every request. The [...] operator copies the elements of the [$httpClientOptions] array into the options array. The PHP 7 client created a new HTTP client for each request;
  • line 40: the [calculerImpot] method receives the three parameters to send to the tax calculation server;
  • lines 44-50: the server is queried with the three parameters it expects. The [query] option adds these parameters to the URL, after encoding them ([marié] becomes [mari%C3%A9]);
  • line 54: we retrieve the server's JSON response. If we do not pass the [false] parameter to the [getContent] method, then, if the status of the server's response indicates an error (codes 3xx-5xx), the HTTP client throws an exception as soon as we try to get the content of the response. Here, whatever the HTTP status of the response, we want access to its content, which explains the error;
  • lines 55-57: if the server could not be reached, the HTTP client throws an exception of type [ExceptionInterface]. We turn it into an [ExceptionImpots] exception: in this way the client's upper layers only have one type of exception to handle;
  • line 60: in development mode, we can display the server's JSON response;
  • lines 63-68: the server's response is the JSON string of an array [["réponse" => qqChose]]. We retrieve the [qqChose]. If the document received is not JSON (for example an Apache HTML error page), we throw an [ExceptionImpots] exception;
  • lines 71-77: if the HTTP status code is not 200, the server has run into a problem. We then throw an exception of type [ExceptionImpots] whose message is the server's JSON response plus the HTTP code of the response. The [+] operator merges two associative arrays;
  • line 80: we return the result, which is an associative array with the keys [impôt, surcôte, décôte, réduction, taux].

docs.title: 18.3.3. The [métier] layer
docs.text:
The [métier] layer [8] implements the following [InterfaceClientMetier] interface:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// l'interface de la couche [métier] du client
interface InterfaceClientMetier
{
    // calcul de l'impôt d'un contribuable
    // rend le tableau [impôt, surcôte, décôte, réduction, taux]
    public function calculerImpot(string $marié, int $enfants, int $salaire): array;

    // calcul des impôts en mode batch
    // peut lancer une exception [ExceptionImpots] remontant de la couche [dao]
    public function executeBatchImpots(string $taxPayersFileName, string $resultsFileName, string $errorsFileName): void;
}
  • line 13: the [calculerImpot] method calculates the tax;
  • line 17: the [executeBatchImpots] method calculates the tax of the taxpayers whose data are in the [$taxPayersFileName] file, puts the results obtained in the [$resultsFileName] file and the errors encountered in the [$errorsFileName] file.

These are the two methods of the [InterfaceMetier] interface of version 5. The [InterfaceClientMetier] interface is implemented by the following [ClientMetier] class:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// la couche [métier] du client : le calcul de l'impôt est fait par le serveur
class ClientMetier implements InterfaceClientMetier
{
    // la couche [dao] est injectée par le constructeur
    public function __construct(private readonly InterfaceClientDao $clientDao)
    {
    }

    // calcul de l'impôt : il est délégué à la couche [dao] qui interroge le serveur
    #[\Override]
    public function calculerImpot(string $marié, int $enfants, int $salaire): array
    {
        return $this->clientDao->calculerImpot($marié, $enfants, $salaire);
    }

    // calcul des impôts en mode batch
    #[\Override]
    public function executeBatchImpots(string $taxPayersFileName, string $resultsFileName, string $errorsFileName): void
    {
        // on laisse remonter les exceptions qui proviennent de la couche [dao]
        // on récupère les données contribuables
        $taxPayersData = $this->clientDao->getTaxPayersData($taxPayersFileName, $errorsFileName);
        // on calcule l'impôt de chacun des contribuables
        $results = array_map(
            fn(TaxPayerData $taxPayerData): TaxPayerData => $taxPayerData->avecRésultats(
                $this->calculerImpot($taxPayerData->marié, $taxPayerData->enfants, $taxPayerData->salaire)
            ),
            $taxPayersData
        );
        // enregistrement des résultats
        $this->clientDao->saveResults($resultsFileName, $results);
    }
}

Comments

  • line 12: the constructor of the [ClientMetier] class receives as a parameter a reference to the [dao] layer;
  • lines 18-20: the tax calculation is delegated to the [dao] layer;
  • lines 25-38: the [executeBatchImpots] method is that of the [Metier] class of version 5.

docs.title: 18.3.4. The main script
docs.text:
The client script [Main/MainImpotsClient.php] implements the [console] layer [9]. It is configured by the following JSON file [Data/config-client.json]:

{
    "urlServer": "https://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-08/impots-server.php",
    "user": {
        "login": "admin",
        "passwd": "admin"
    },
    "httpClientOptions": {
        "verify_peer": false,
        "verify_host": false
    },
    "taxPayersDataFilename": "Data/taxpayersdata.json",
    "resultsFilename": "Data/results.json",
    "errorsFilename": "Data/errors.json",
    "dependencies": [
        "../version-05/Entities/ExceptionImpots.php",
        "../version-05/Entities/TaxPayerData.php",
        "../version-05/Utilities/Utilitaires.php",
        "../version-05/Dao/TraitDao.php",
        "Dao/InterfaceClientDao.php",
        "Dao/ClientDao.php",
        "Metier/InterfaceClientMetier.php",
        "Metier/ClientMetier.php"
    ]
}
  • line 2: the secure URL of the tax calculation server;
  • lines 3-6: the user making the requests to the tax calculation server;
  • lines 7-9: the HTTP client's options. As in the previous chapter, we ask the client not to verify the server's self-signed certificate;
  • lines 11-13: the JSON files for the taxpayer data, the results and the errors;
  • lines 14-23: the client's various PHP files. The first four are those of version 5.

The code of the [MainImpotsClient.php] script is as follows:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres et des résultats des fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// le dossier racine du client : les chemins du fichier de configuration sont relatifs à ce dossier
const ROOT_DIRECTORY = __DIR__ . "/..";
// le fichier de configuration du dossier [Data] : 1er argument de la ligne de commande s'il existe
$configFilename = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/Data/" . ($argv[1] ?? "config-client.json");

// on récupère la configuration
$config = json_decode(file_get_contents($configFilename), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);

// on inclut les dépendances nécessaires au script : bibliothèques tierces (Symfony) puis fichiers de l'application
require_once ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/../../../vendor/autoload.php";
foreach ($config["dependencies"] as $dependency) {
    require_once ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/$dependency";
}

// les chemins des fichiers de données
$taxPayersDataFilename = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["taxPayersDataFilename"];
$resultsFilename = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["resultsFilename"];
$errorsFilename = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["errorsFilename"];

// création de la couche [dao]
$clientDao = new ClientDao($config["urlServer"], $config["user"], $config["httpClientOptions"]);
// création de la couche [métier]
$clientMetier = new ClientMetier($clientDao);

// calcul de l'impôt en mode batch
try {
    $clientMetier->executeBatchImpots($taxPayersDataFilename, $resultsFilename, $errorsFilename);
    print "Les résultats ont été enregistrés dans le fichier [{$config["resultsFilename"]}]\n";
} catch (ExceptionImpots $ex) {
    // on affiche l'erreur
    print "Erreur n° {$ex->getCode()} : {$ex->getMessage()}\n";
}
// fin
print "Terminé\n";

Comments

  • line 10: the client's root folder is the parent folder of the [Main] folder;
  • line 12: the configuration file, looked for in the [Data] folder. Its name can be passed as an argument to the script ([php MainImpotsClient.php config-client-ko.json]). Otherwise, it is the [config-client.json] file. We will use this possibility for the error tests;
  • lines 18-21: loading the dependencies: [Composer]'s class loader for Symfony's [HttpClient] library, then the client's files;
  • line 29: creation of the [dao] layer. We pass the layer's constructor the information it expects:
    • the URL of the tax calculation server;
    • the credentials of the user who will make the requests;
    • the HTTP client's options;
  • line 31: creation of the [métier] layer. We pass the layer's constructor a reference to the [dao] layer that has just been created;
  • line 35: we ask the [métier] layer to:
    • calculate the taxes of all the taxpayers in the [taxpayersdata.json] file;
    • put the results in the [results.json] file;
    • put the errors in the [errors.json] file;
  • lines 37-39: all the client's errors, including errors communicating with the server, arrive in the form of an [ExceptionImpots] exception, whose code and message we display.

With the Apache server and the MySQL DBMS running, let's run the client in a terminal opened in the [Main] folder:

> php MainImpotsClient.php
Les résultats ont été enregistrés dans le fichier [Data/results.json]
Terminé

Running the client produces the same results as the previous versions. Check the following files:

  • [Data/taxpayersdata.json]: data of the taxpayers for whom the tax amount is calculated;
  • [Data/results.json]: results for the various taxpayers in the [Data/taxpayersdata.json] file. This file is identical to the [results.json] file of version 7;
  • [Data/errors.json]: the errors that may have been encountered while processing the [Data/taxpayersdata.json] file.

Let's look at the possible error cases. First, an unreachable server. We could stop the Apache server of [Laragon]. Instead, we used the configuration file [config-client-injoignable.json], identical to the [config-client.json] file except for the URL: it refers to port 4443 of the [localhost] machine, on which no server is waiting for requests ([https://localhost:4443/php8-oct-2026/...]). The results in the client's console are then as follows:

> php MainImpotsClient.php config-client-injoignable.json
Erreur n° 40 : Erreur de communication avec le serveur (Failed to connect to localhost port 4443 after 0 ms: Couldn't connect to server for "https://localhost:4443/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-08/impots-server.php?mari%C3%A9=oui&enfants=2&salaire=55555".)
Terminé

The exception thrown by Symfony's HTTP client has been turned by the [dao] layer into an [ExceptionImpots] exception with code 40.

Now let's simulate a failure of the MySQL DBMS, in the same way as before with [curl]. The results in the client's console are then as follows:

> php MainImpotsClient.php
Erreur n° 42 : {"statut HTTP":500,"erreur":"Erreur d'accès à la base de données (SQLSTATE[HY000] [2002] Connection refused)"}
Terminé

Let's restore the DBMS, then use the configuration file [config-client-ko.json], in which the user connecting is unknown to the server:

    "user": {
        "login": "x",
        "passwd": "x"
    },

The results in the client's console are then as follows:

> php MainImpotsClient.php config-client-ko.json
Erreur n° 42 : {"statut HTTP":401,"erreur":"Echec de l'authentification [x]"}
Terminé

docs.title: 18.3.5. [PHPUnit] tests
docs.text:
As was done for the previous versions, we are going to write a [PHPUnit] test for the client's [métier] layer. The [Tests/ClientMetierTest.php] test is as follows:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres et des résultats des fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms des tests
namespace Application\Tests;

// les classes testées
use Application\ClientDao;
use Application\ClientMetier;
use Application\InterfaceClientMetier;
// les classes de PHPUnit
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

// test de la couche [métier] du client : le serveur doit être lancé
final class ClientMetierTest extends TestCase
{
    // le dossier racine du client
    private const string ROOT_DIRECTORY = __DIR__ . "/..";
    // la configuration du client
    private static array $config;
    // la couche [métier] testée
    private InterfaceClientMetier $métier;

    // exécutée une fois, avant le premier test de la classe
    #[\Override]
    public static function setUpBeforeClass(): void
    {
        // on récupère la configuration du client
        self::$config = json_decode(file_get_contents(self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/Data/config-client.json"), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
        // on inclut les dépendances du client (le chargeur de Composer est déjà chargé par PHPUnit)
        foreach (self::$config["dependencies"] as $dependency) {
            require_once self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/$dependency";
        }
    }

    // exécutée avant chaque test
    #[\Override]
    protected function setUp(): void
    {
        // création des couches [dao] et [métier] comme dans le script principal
        $clientDao = new ClientDao(self::$config["urlServer"], self::$config["user"], self::$config["httpClientOptions"]);
        $this->métier = new ClientMetier($clientDao);
    }

Comments

  • lines 29-37: definition of the test environment. We use the same one as the main script [MainImpotsClient.php];
  • lines 41-45: construction of the [dao] and [métier] layers before each test. The [$this->métier] attribute references the [métier] layer;
  • the rest of the test, not reproduced here, is that of the previous versions: the 11 taxpayers from the table of official figures and the [testCalculerImpot] method. Note that the [assertSame] check requires the values returned by the server to have exactly the expected types: integers for the tax, the surcharge, the discount and the reduction, a real number for the rate. This is the case thanks to the server's [JSON_PRESERVE_ZERO_FRACTION] option.

This test is a test of the client, but also, through it, of the server: the Apache server and the MySQL DBMS must be running. The test results are as follows:

 ✔ Calculer impot with data set "couple, 3 enfants, 200000"

OK (11 tests, 22 assertions)

We now have a client / server application. In the next version, we will improve the server: it will use a session, keep a log of its operations and notify its administrator by email in the event of a problem.

docs.title: 19. Practical exercise – version 9
docs.text:
In this version, we are going to improve the server as follows:

  • currently, on every request, the tax authority data are fetched from the database. We are going to use a session:
    • on a user's 1st request, the tax authority data are fetched from the database and put in the session;
    • on subsequent requests from the same user, the tax authority data are fetched from the session. We can hope for a slight gain in execution time, since database queries are expensive;
  • the session will also be used to authenticate the user only once;
  • the server will record the important moments in a text file (logs):
    • successful or failed authentication;
    • whether or not the parameters sent by the client are valid;
    • the result of the tax calculation;
    • the various error cases;
  • in the event of a fatal error, an email will be sent to the application administrator.

The client will also have to be modified to handle the session cookie that the server will send it.

docs.title: 19.1. The server
docs.text:
We now focus on the server part of the application.

This architecture will be implemented by the following files:

scripts-web/impots/version-09
├── Dao
│   └── ServerDaoWithSession.php
├── Data
│   ├── .htaccess
│   ├── config-server.json
│   └── logs.txt
├── Tests
│   └── ServerDaoTest.php
├── Utilities
│   ├── Logger.php
│   └── SendAdminMail.php
└── impots-server.php

The other files are those of versions 5 and 8.

docs.title: 19.1.1.1. The [Logger] class
docs.text:
The [Logger] class will be used to write logs to a text file:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// un journal (logs) dans un fichier texte
final readonly class Logger
{
    // constructeur : le fichier des logs est créé s'il n'existe pas
    public function __construct(private string $logsFilename)
    {
        // on vérifie qu'on peut écrire dans le fichier (ajout d'une chaîne vide)
        if (@file_put_contents($logsFilename, "", FILE_APPEND) === false) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Echec lors de la création du fichier de logs [$logsFilename]", 50);
        }
    }

    // écriture d'un message dans les logs, précédé de la date et de l'heure
    public function write(string $message): void
    {
        $date = (new \DateTimeImmutable())->format("d/m/y H:i:s.v");
        // FILE_APPEND : on écrit à la fin du fichier
        // LOCK_EX : le fichier est verrouillé pendant l'écriture
        file_put_contents($this->logsFilename, "$date : $message\n", FILE_APPEND | LOCK_EX);
    }
}

Comments

  • line 9: the class is [final] (it cannot be derived) and [readonly]: its only attribute, the name of the log file, cannot be modified after the object has been constructed;
  • line 12: the class constructor receives the name of the log file as a parameter;
  • line 15: we check that we can write to the file by appending an empty string to it. The [FILE_APPEND] flag causes the file to be created if it does not exist and its content to be preserved otherwise. The [@] operator prevents PHP from displaying a warning on failure: we handle the error ourselves;
  • line 16: if the write could not be done, an exception is thrown;
  • line 21: the [write] method writes the message [$message] to the log file, preceded by the date and time. The format [d/m/y H:i:s.v] gives the day, the month, the two-digit year, then the hours, minutes, seconds and milliseconds;
  • line 26: the [file_put_contents] function opens the file, appends the line to it and closes it again. There is therefore no longer a [close] method as in the PHP 7 version of the class, which kept the file open between two writes.

The server application may serve several clients simultaneously. Yet there is a single log file for all of them. There is therefore a risk of concurrent access when writing to the file. The PHP 7 course ignored the problem. Here, the [LOCK_EX] flag asks [file_put_contents] to lock the file during the write: if another request wants to write at the same time, it waits until the lock is released. A log line is therefore never mixed with another one. On the other hand, the lines written by two simultaneous requests may be interleaved.

docs.title: 19.1.1.2. The [SendAdminMail] class
docs.text:
The [SendAdminMail] class sends an email to the application administrator if the application crashes:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// dépendances Symfony Mailer
use Symfony\Component\Mailer\Mailer;
use Symfony\Component\Mailer\Transport;
use Symfony\Component\Mime\Email;

// envoi d'un mail à l'administrateur de l'application
final readonly class SendAdminMail
{
    // $config : les informations nécessaires à l'envoi du mail
    // $logger : un journal facultatif pour noter le résultat de l'envoi
    public function __construct(private array $config, private ?Logger $logger = null)
    {
    }

    // envoi du message [$message] à l'administrateur
    // la méthode ne lance pas d'exception : un échec de l'envoi est seulement noté dans les logs
    public function send(string $message): void
    {
        // le mail est envoyé au serveur SMTP $this->config["smtp-server"] sur le port $this->config["smtp-port"]
        // de la part de $this->config["from"] pour le destinataire $this->config["to"]
        // avec le sujet $this->config["subject"] et les pièces jointes $this->config["attachments"]
        // si $this->config["tls"] est vrai, la connexion est sécurisée et authentifiée
        $config = $this->config;
        try {
            // création du message
            $email = (new Email())
                ->from($config["from"])
                ->to($config["to"])
                ->subject($config["subject"])
                ->text($message);
            // pièces jointes
            foreach ($config["attachments"] as $attachment) {
                if (file_exists($attachment)) {
                    $email->attachFromPath($attachment);
                } else {
                    $this->logger?->write("La pièce jointe [$attachment] n'existe pas");
                }
            }
            // le transport du message
            $dsn = "smtp://{$config["smtp-server"]}:{$config["smtp-port"]}";
            if ($config["tls"]) {
                // connexion sécurisée (STARTTLS) et authentifiée
                $verifyPeer = ($config["verify-peer"] ?? true) ? 1 : 0;
                $dsn = sprintf("smtp://%s:%s@%s:%d?require_tls=1&verify_peer=%d",
                    rawurlencode($config["user"]), rawurlencode($config["password"]),
                    $config["smtp-server"], $config["smtp-port"], $verifyPeer);
            }
            // envoi du message
            (new Mailer(Transport::fromDsn($dsn)))->send($email);
            $this->logger?->write("Message [$message] envoyé à {$config["to"]}");
        } catch (\Throwable $ex) {
            // échec de l'envoi
            $this->logger?->write("Erreur lors de l'envoi du message [$message] : {$ex->getMessage()}");
        }
    }
}

Comments

  • lines 9-11: the PHP 7 course used the [SwiftMailer] library, which is no longer maintained. We use [Symfony Mailer], presented in the chapter on network functions;
  • line 18: the constructor receives two parameters:
    • [$config]: an associative array containing all the information needed to send the email;
    • [$logger]: a log in which to record the result of sending the email. The parameter is optional: its default value is [null];
  • line 24: the [send] method sends the message [$message]. The code is that of the [sendmail] function of the [smtp-02.php] script in the chapter on network functions;
  • line 43: the nullsafe operator [?->] (PHP 8.0) only calls the [write] method if [$this->logger] is not [null]. It replaces the [if ($this->logger !== NULL)] test of the PHP 7 script;
  • line 58: the [send] method catches all errors: a failure to send the email is only recorded in the logs. An error while handling an error must not prevent the server from responding to its client.

The associative array [$config] will have the following form:

    "adminMail": {
        "smtp-server": "localhost",
        "smtp-port": 1025,
        "from": "guest@localhost",
        "to": "guest@localhost",
        "subject": "plantage du serveur de calcul d'impôts",
        "tls": false,
        "attachments": []
    },

The email is sent to the [Mailpit] server presented in the chapter on network functions, which listens on port 1025 of the [localhost] machine and keeps all the emails it receives. It must be running ([mailpit.bat] file in the [scripts-console/inet/mailpit] folder).

docs.title: 19.1.2. The [dao] layer
docs.text:
The [dao] layer of version 9 is implemented by the following [ServerDaoWithSession] class:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// une couche [dao] qui peut être construite à partir de données fiscales déjà acquises
class ServerDaoWithSession extends ServerDao
{
    // le constructeur reçoit :
    // - soit le nom du fichier JSON décrivant la base de données : les données fiscales sont lues dans la base
    // - soit les données fiscales elles-mêmes, déjà acquises (en session par exemple)
    public function __construct(string|TaxAdminData $source)
    {
        if ($source instanceof TaxAdminData) {
            // cas le plus simple : les données sont déjà là
            $this->taxAdminData = $source;
        } else {
            // on passe la main à la classe parent qui sait utiliser la base de données
            parent::__construct($source);
        }
    }
}

Comments

  • line 9: the [ServerDaoWithSession] class of version 9 extends the [ServerDao] class of version 8. The [ServerDao] class already knows how to use the database. All we have left to do is handle the case where the tax authority data have already been acquired;
  • line 14: the constructor receives a parameter that can be of two types. The union type [string|TaxAdminData] (PHP 8.0) expresses this:
    • a string: the name of the file containing the information needed to connect to the database, if the tax authority data have not yet been acquired;
    • a [TaxAdminData] object: the tax authority data, if they have already been acquired;
  • lines 16-18: the [instanceof] operator tells us which of the two types was received. If it is the tax data, we store them in the [taxAdminData] attribute inherited from the [ServerDao] class. This is why this attribute was declared [protected readonly] in version 8. The PHP 7 class had a constructor with two parameters, one of which had to be [NULL];
  • line 21: otherwise we hand over to the constructor of the parent class, which fetches the data from the database.

When a web session starts, the [dao] layer will be constructed with the name of the database file. The tax authority data will then be fetched from the database and stored in the session. On subsequent requests in the same session, the [dao] layer will be constructed with the [TaxAdminData] object coming from the session. There will therefore be no database lookup.

docs.title: 19.1.3. The server script
docs.text:
The server script [impots-server.php] is configured by the following JSON file [config-server.json]:

{
    "databaseFilename": "../version-08/Data/database-mysql.json",
    "dependencies": [
        "../../../scripts-console/impots/version-05/Entities/ExceptionImpots.php",
        "../../../scripts-console/impots/version-05/Entities/TaxAdminData.php",
        "../../../scripts-console/impots/version-05/Entities/Database.php",
        "../../../scripts-console/impots/version-05/Utilities/Utilitaires.php",
        "../version-08/Dao/InterfaceServerDao.php",
        "../version-08/Dao/ServerDao.php",
        "Dao/ServerDaoWithSession.php",
        "../version-08/Metier/InterfaceServerMetier.php",
        "../version-08/Metier/ServerMetier.php",
        "Utilities/Logger.php",
        "Utilities/SendAdminMail.php"
    ],
    "users": [
        {
            "login": "admin",
            "passwd": "admin"
        }
    ],
    "adminMail": {
        "smtp-server": "localhost",
        "smtp-port": 1025,
        "from": "guest@localhost",
        "to": "guest@localhost",
        "subject": "plantage du serveur de calcul d'impôts",
        "tls": false,
        "attachments": []
    },
    "logsFilename": "Data/logs.txt"
}
  • line 2: we use the MySQL database description of version 8;
  • lines 3-15: the files of versions 5 and 8, and the three new files of version 9;
  • lines 22-30: the information needed to send an email to the administrator. It now has appropriate JSON types: a number for the port, a boolean for [tls]. The PHP 7 file used strings (["25"], ["FALSE"]);
  • line 31: the log file, relative to the server's [version-09] folder. It is in the [Data] folder, protected by the [.htaccess] file of version 8: the logs must not be readable by everyone.

The server script [impots-server.php] changes as follows:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres et des résultats des fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// dépendances Symfony
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;

// les erreurs de PHP ne sont pas envoyées au client (elles vont dans le journal du serveur web)
ini_set("display_errors", "0");

// le dossier racine du serveur : les chemins du fichier de configuration sont relatifs à ce dossier
const ROOT_DIRECTORY = __DIR__;
// chemin du fichier de configuration
const CONFIG_FILENAME = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/Data/config-server.json";

// on récupère la configuration
$config = json_decode(file_get_contents(CONFIG_FILENAME), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);

// on inclut les dépendances nécessaires au script
require_once ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/../../../vendor/autoload.php";
foreach ($config["dependencies"] as $dependency) {
    require_once ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/$dependency";
}

// session (après le chargement de la classe [TaxAdminData] dont un objet peut être en session)
$session = new Session();
$session->start();

// création du fichier des logs
try {
    $logger = new Logger(ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["logsFilename"]);
} catch (ExceptionImpots $ex) {
    // erreur 500 sans logs - le message ne doit pas révéler l'arborescence des fichiers du serveur
    $message = "Echec lors de la création du fichier de logs [{$config["logsFilename"]}]";
    doInternalServerError($message, $config["adminMail"]);
    // terminé
    exit;
}

// 1er log
$logger->write("---nouvelle requête");

// on récupère la requête courante
$request = Request::createFromGlobals();
// authentification seulement la 1re fois
if (!$session->has("user")) {
    // log
    $logger->write("Authentification en cours…");
    // les identifiants envoyés par le client (null s'il n'en a pas envoyé)
    $requestUser = $request->getUser();
    $requestPassword = $request->getPassword();
    // l'utilisateur fait-il partie des utilisateurs autorisés ?
    $trouvé = $requestUser !== null && $requestPassword !== null
        && array_any(
            $config["users"],
            fn(array $user): bool => $user["login"] === $requestUser && hash_equals($user["passwd"], $requestPassword)
        );
    if (!$trouvé) {
        // pas trouvé - code 401
        sendResponse(
            ["erreur" => "Echec de l'authentification [$requestUser]"],
            Response::HTTP_UNAUTHORIZED,
            ["WWW-Authenticate" => 'Basic realm="Serveur de calcul des impots"'],
            $logger
        );
        // terminé
        exit;
    }
    // on note dans la session qu'on a authentifié l'utilisateur
    $session->set("user", $requestUser);
    // log
    $logger->write("Authentification réussie [$requestUser]");
} else {
    // log
    $logger->write("Authentification prise en session…");
}

// on a un utilisateur valide - on vérifie les paramètres reçus
$erreurs = [];
// on doit avoir une requête GET avec trois paramètres
if ($request->getMethod() !== "GET" || $request->query->count() !== 3) {
    $erreurs[] = "Méthode GET requise avec les seuls paramètres [marié, enfants, salaire]";
}
// le statut marital
if (!$request->query->has("marié")) {
    $erreurs[] = "paramètre marié manquant";
} else {
    $marié = strtolower(trim($request->query->getString("marié")));
    if (!in_array($marié, ["oui", "non"], true)) {
        $erreurs[] = "paramètre marié [$marié] invalide";
    }
}
// le nombre d'enfants et le salaire : des nombres entiers >= 0
$valeurs = [];
foreach (["enfants", "salaire"] as $paramètre) {
    if (!$request->query->has($paramètre)) {
        $erreurs[] = "paramètre $paramètre manquant";
        continue;
    }
    $valeur = trim($request->query->getString($paramètre));
    if (preg_match('/^\d+$/', $valeur) !== 1) {
        $erreurs[] = "paramètre $paramètre [$valeur] invalide";
    } else {
        $valeurs[$paramètre] = (int) $valeur;
    }
}
// autres paramètres dans la requête ?
foreach (array_diff(array_keys($request->query->all()), ["marié", "enfants", "salaire"]) as $paramètre) {
    $erreurs[] = "paramètre [$paramètre] invalide";
}
// erreurs ?
if ($erreurs !== []) {
    // on envoie un code d'erreur 400 au client
    sendResponse(["erreurs" => $erreurs], Response::HTTP_BAD_REQUEST, [], $logger);
    // terminé
    exit;
}
// log
[$enfants, $salaire] = [$valeurs["enfants"], $valeurs["salaire"]];
$logger->write("paramètres ['marié'=>$marié, 'enfants'=>$enfants, 'salaire'=>$salaire] valides");

// on a tout ce qu'il faut pour travailler
// création de la couche [dao]
if (!$session->has("taxAdminData")) {
    // les données fiscales sont prises dans la base de données
    $logger->write("données fiscales prises en base de données");
    try {
        // construction de la couche [dao]
        $dao = new ServerDaoWithSession(ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["databaseFilename"]);
        // on met les données fiscales en session
        $session->set("taxAdminData", $dao->getTaxAdminData());
    } catch (ExceptionImpots $ex) {
        // erreur 500
        doInternalServerError($ex->getMessage(), $config["adminMail"], $logger);
        // terminé
        exit;
    }
} else {
    // les données fiscales sont prises dans la session
    $dao = new ServerDaoWithSession($session->get("taxAdminData"));
    // log
    $logger->write("données fiscales prises en session");
}
// création de la couche [métier]
$métier = new ServerMetier($dao);
// calcul de l'impôt
$result = $métier->calculerImpot($marié, $enfants, $salaire);
// on rend la réponse
sendResponse($result, Response::HTTP_OK, [], $logger);
// fin
exit;

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
// erreur fatale : un mail à l'administrateur et une réponse 500 au client
function doInternalServerError(string $message, array $adminMail, ?Logger $logger = null): void
{
    // le message d'erreur d'un pilote de SGBD peut ne pas être codé en UTF-8 (Windows-1252 sous Windows)
    if (!mb_check_encoding($message, "UTF-8")) {
        $message = mb_convert_encoding($message, "UTF-8", "Windows-1252");
    }
    // on envoie un mail à l'administrateur
    // [SendAdminMail] intercepte toutes les exceptions et les logue lui-même
    (new SendAdminMail($adminMail, $logger))->send($message);
    // on envoie un code d'erreur 500 au client
    sendResponse(["erreur" => $message], Response::HTTP_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, [], $logger);
}

// envoi de la réponse HTTP au client
// $result : le tableau à envoyer, sous la forme ["réponse" => $result]
// $statusCode : le statut HTTP de la réponse
// $headers : des entêtes HTTP à ajouter à la réponse
// $logger : le journal de l'application (null s'il n'a pu être créé)
function sendResponse(array $result, int $statusCode, array $headers = [], ?Logger $logger = null): void
{
    // la réponse JSON
    $response = new JsonResponse(null, $statusCode, $headers);
    $response->setEncodingOptions(JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_PRESERVE_ZERO_FRACTION);
    $response->setData(["réponse" => $result]);
    // envoi
    $response->send();
    // log
    $logger?->write($response->getContent());
}

Comments

  • line 13: we use the [Session] class of [HttpFoundation], presented in the previous chapter;
  • line 16: the errors detected by PHP (warnings, fatal errors...) are not displayed in the document sent to the client. They would corrupt the JSON response it expects. They are still recorded in the web server's error log (Apache's [error.log] file);
  • lines 33-34: we start a session. It is started after the application's files have been loaded: the session may contain a [TaxAdminData] object, and the [TaxAdminData] class must be known when PHP rebuilds the session's objects;
  • lines 37-44: we try to create the log file. If an exception occurs, the [doInternalServerError] function is called without a log (the last parameter is missing). The error message uses the name of the log file given in the configuration: the exception message contains the full path of the file, which would reveal the organization of the server's folders to the client;
  • line 162: the [doInternalServerError] function accepts three parameters:
    • [$message]: the error message;
    • [$adminMail]: the information needed to send an email to the application administrator;
    • [$logger]: the application log, if it could be created;
  • lines 165-166: the error message may come from a DBMS driver and not be encoded in UTF-8 (see version 8);
  • line 170: we send an email to the application administrator;
  • line 172: we send the response to the client with the code [500 Internal Server Error];
  • line 180: the [sendResponse] function sends all responses to the client. Its parameters are:
    • [$result]: the array to send. The server sends the JSON string of the array [["réponse" => $result]];
    • [$statusCode]: the HTTP status of the response;
    • [$headers]: the HTTP headers to add to the response. This is the case of the [WWW-Authenticate] header of the 401 response;
    • [$logger]: the application log;
  • line 183: the constructor of the [JsonResponse] class accepts the data, the status and the headers of the response. The data are set further on by [setData], after choosing the [json_encode] options, which are those of version 8;
  • line 189: the JSON response sent is recorded in the logs;
  • line 48: the 1st log entry of the request;
  • line 53: thanks to the session that has been set up, the client will be authenticated only once:
    • once the client has been authenticated, we put the [user] key in the session, with the user's login as its value line 77;
    • on the same client's next request, the test avoids an authentication that has become unnecessary;
  • lines 67-72: if authentication fails, the 401 response is sent by the [sendResponse] function, with the [WWW-Authenticate] header;
  • lines 86-118: the parameter check is that of version 8;
  • line 126: array destructuring [[$a, $b] = [...]] assigns the two variables [$enfants] and [$salaire] in a single statement. It replaces PHP 7's [list] function;
  • line 131: thanks to the session, the data will be fetched from the database only once:
    • on the first request, the database lookup takes place line 136. The data retrieved are then put in the session, associated with the [taxAdminData] key line 138;
    • on subsequent requests, the [taxAdminData] key is found in the session and the tax data are then passed directly to the [dao] layer line 147;
  • lines 139-143: fetching the tax data from the database may fail. In that case, we send the client a [500 Internal Server Error] code and an email to the administrator;
  • line 156: the rest of the code is that of the previous version, the response being sent by the [sendResponse] function.

Note that the [doInternalServerError] and [sendResponse] functions are defined at the end of the script, after the [exit] statement: PHP knows all the functions defined at the top level of a file before executing its first statement.

docs.title: 19.1.4. [PHPUnit] tests
docs.text:
We will only test the [dao] layer, which is the only one that has changed. The code of the [Tests/ServerDaoTest.php] test is as follows:

<?php

// respect strict des types déclarés des paramètres et des résultats des fonctions
declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms des tests
namespace Application\Tests;

// la classe testée
use Application\ServerDaoWithSession;
// les classes de PHPUnit
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

final class ServerDaoTest extends TestCase
{
    // le dossier racine du serveur
    private const string ROOT_DIRECTORY = __DIR__ . "/..";
    // la configuration du serveur
    private static array $config;

    // exécutée une fois, avant le premier test de la classe
    #[\Override]
    public static function setUpBeforeClass(): void
    {
        // on récupère la configuration du serveur
        self::$config = json_decode(file_get_contents(self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/Data/config-server.json"), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
        // on inclut les dépendances du serveur
        foreach (self::$config["dependencies"] as $dependency) {
            require_once self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/$dependency";
        }
    }

    // les données de l'administration fiscale lues dans la base de données (1re requête d'une session)
    public function testTaxAdminData(): void
    {
        // création de la couche [dao] à partir du fichier décrivant la base de données
        $dao = new ServerDaoWithSession(self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . self::$config["databaseFilename"]);
        $taxAdminData = $dao->getTaxAdminData();
        // constantes de calcul
        $this->assertSame(1551.0, $taxAdminData->plafondQfDemiPart);
        $this->assertSame(21037.0, $taxAdminData->plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction);
        $this->assertSame(42074.0, $taxAdminData->plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction);
        $this->assertSame(3797.0, $taxAdminData->valeurReducDemiPart);
        $this->assertSame(1196.0, $taxAdminData->plafondDecoteCelibataire);
        $this->assertSame(1970.0, $taxAdminData->plafondDecoteCouple);
        $this->assertSame(1595.0, $taxAdminData->plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote);

        $this->assertSame([0.0, 0.14, 0.30, 0.41, 0.45], $taxAdminData->coeffR);
        $this->assertSame([0.0, 1394.96, 5798.0, 13913.69, 20163.45], $taxAdminData->coeffN);

    // les données de l'administration fiscale déjà acquises (requêtes suivantes de la session)
    public function testTaxAdminDataEnSession(): void
    {
        // les données lues en base lors de la 1re requête
        $databaseFilename = self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . self::$config["databaseFilename"];
        $taxAdminData = (new ServerDaoWithSession($databaseFilename))->getTaxAdminData();

        $dao = new ServerDaoWithSession($taxAdminData);

docs.title: 19.2. The client
docs.text:
We now focus on the client part of the application.

This architecture will be implemented by the following files:

scripts-console/impots/version-09
├── Dao
│   └── ClientDao.php
├── Data
│   ├── config-client-ko.json
│   ├── config-client.json

In the new version, only the following change:

  • the configuration file [config-client.json];
  • the client's [dao] layer.

The [MainImpotsClient.php] script is that of version 8.

docs.title: 19.2.1. The [dao] layer
docs.text:
The [dao] layer changes as follows:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// espace de noms
namespace Application;

// dépendances Symfony
use Symfony\Component\HttpClient\HttpClient;
use Symfony\Contracts\HttpClient\Exception\ExceptionInterface;
use Symfony\Contracts\HttpClient\HttpClientInterface;

// la couche [dao] du client : un client HTTP du serveur de calcul de l'impôt qui gère une session
class ClientDao implements InterfaceClientDao
{
    // le trait de la version 5 implémente les méthodes [getTaxPayersData] et [saveResults] de l'interface
    use TraitDao;

    // le client HTTP
    private readonly HttpClientInterface $httpClient;
    // le cookie de session (null tant que le serveur ne l'a pas envoyé)
    private ?string $sessionCookie = null;

    // constructeur
    // $urlServer : l'URL du serveur de calcul de l'impôt
    // $user : l'utilisateur qui fait les requêtes, tableau [login, passwd]
    // $httpClientOptions : des options supplémentaires du client HTTP (verify_peer, verify_host...)
    public function __construct(
        private readonly string $urlServer,
        #[\SensitiveParameter] private readonly array $user,
        array $httpClientOptions = [],
    ) {
        // le client HTTP : les identifiants de l'utilisateur ne seront envoyés qu'avec la 1re requête
        $this->httpClient = HttpClient::create($httpClientOptions);
    }

    // calcul de l'impôt par le serveur
    #[\Override]
    public function calculerImpot(string $marié, int $enfants, int $salaire): array
    {
        // les options de la requête : les paramètres attendus par le serveur
        $options = [
            "query" => [
                "marié" => $marié,
                "enfants" => $enfants,
                "salaire" => $salaire,
            ],
        ];
        if ($this->sessionCookie === null) {
            // pas encore de session : on envoie les identifiants de l'utilisateur
            $options["auth_basic"] = [$this->user["login"], $this->user["passwd"]];
        } else {
            // on envoie le cookie de session : l'utilisateur est déjà authentifié dans cette session
            $options["headers"] = ["Cookie" => $this->sessionCookie];
        }
        try {
            // on fait la requête au serveur
            $response = $this->httpClient->request("GET", $this->urlServer, $options);
            // le statut, les entêtes et le document JSON de la réponse, même en cas d'erreur (paramètre false)
            $statusCode = $response->getStatusCode();
            $headers = $response->getHeaders(false);
            $json = $response->getContent(false);
        } catch (ExceptionInterface $ex) {
            // le serveur n'a pu être joint
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Erreur de communication avec le serveur ({$ex->getMessage()})", 40, $ex);
        }
        // logs
        // print "$json\n";
        // le serveur envoie la chaîne JSON d'un tableau ["réponse" => qqChose]
        try {
            $réponse = json_decode($json, true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR)["réponse"] ?? null;
        } catch (\JsonException $ex) {
            $réponse = null;
        }
        if (!is_array($réponse)) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Réponse du serveur invalide [$json]", 41);
        }
        // erreur ?
        if ($statusCode !== 200) {
            // on lance une exception dont le message est la réponse du serveur complétée par son statut HTTP
            $message = json_encode(
                ["statut HTTP" => $statusCode] + $réponse,
                JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR
            );
            throw new ExceptionImpots($message, 42);
        }
        // on récupère le cookie de session s'il n'est pas encore connu
        if ($this->sessionCookie === null) {
            foreach ($headers["set-cookie"] ?? [] as $cookie) {
                if (preg_match('/^PHPSESSID=(.+?);/', $cookie, $champs) === 1) {
                    $this->sessionCookie = "PHPSESSID=$champs[1]";
                }
            }
        }
        // on rend la réponse : le tableau [impôt, surcôte, décôte, réduction, taux]
        return $réponse;
    }
}

Comments

The change to the [dao] layer consists in now managing a session:

  • line 22: the session cookie. It is [null] as long as the server has not sent it. This attribute is not [readonly]: its value changes after the 1st request;
  • line 30: the user's credentials are now stored in an attribute, since they are no longer sent with every request;
  • line 34: the HTTP client is created without the [auth_basic] option;
  • lines 49-51: on the 1st request, the cookie does not exist: we then make the request to the server, sending the authentication information. This time the [auth_basic] option is an option of the request and not of the HTTP client;
  • lines 52-55: on subsequent requests, we normally have the session cookie. We then send not the authentication information but the cookie, in the HTTP [Cookie] header;
  • line 61: we retrieve the response headers. As with [getContent], the [false] parameter avoids an exception if the status of the response indicates an error;
  • lines 88-94: the server's response to the 1st request includes a session cookie, in a [Set-Cookie] header. We retrieve it as in the previous chapter and store it in the [$sessionCookie] attribute.

We could have kept the old version of the [dao] layer and authenticated on every request, since this has a negligible cost. For teaching purposes, we wanted to recall how an HTTP client can manage a session.

We can see that the tax authority data are always taken from the database and never from the session. Let's go back to the code of the test that was run:

    // exécutée avant chaque test
    #[\Override]
    protected function setUp(): void
    {
        // création des couches [dao] et [métier] comme dans le script principal
        $clientDao = new ClientDao(self::$config["urlServer"], self::$config["user"], self::$config["httpClientOptions"]);
        $this->métier = new ClientMetier($clientDao);
    }
  • line 41: the [setUp] method is executed before each test. A new [ClientDao] is therefore created for each test, with a [null] session cookie. This explains why this client does not benefit from any session: everything happens as if the 11 tests were run by 11 different users.

This example shows us that the session is not the right place to store the tax authority data. These data are common to all users of the application. Yet here, they are duplicated in each of their sessions.

In web programming, three kinds of visibility are distinguished for shared data:

  • data shared by all users of the web application. These are generally read-only data. PHP does not natively have this kind of memory: each request is executed by a script that starts with an empty memory;
  • data shared by the requests of a single client. These data are stored in the session. We then speak of a client session to refer to the client's memory. All of a client's requests have access to this session. They can store information in it and read information from it. In the previous scripts, this session is implemented by the Symfony object [HttpFoundation\Session\Session];
  • request memory, or request context. A user's request may be processed by several successive actions. The request context allows an action 1 to pass information to an action 2. With [HttpFoundation], the request is implemented by the [Request] object and its memory by its [attributes] attribute.

Tools exist to give PHP an application memory. The new version of the practical exercise shows how to use one of them.

docs.title: 21. Processing XML documents
docs.text:
The web services we have written so far exchange JSON data. The XML format (eXtensible Markup Language) was for a long time the most widespread exchange format, and it is still often encountered: SOAP web services, RSS feeds, configuration files, office documents (an [.odt] or [.docx] file is an archive of XML files). PHP offers two APIs for working with it:

  • [SimpleXML]: a very simple API in which the document's elements become object properties;
  • [DOM] (Document Object Model): the standard W3C API, more complete, which also lets you modify a document. PHP 8.4 introduced a new version of it, in the [Dom] namespace, compliant with the current web standard.

The scripts of this chapter are in the [scripts-console/xml] folder:

scripts-console/xml
├── data.xml
├── dom-01.php
└── simplexml-01.php

docs.title: 21.1. The document studied
docs.text:
We consider the following XML file [data.xml]:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>

<tribu>
    <enseignant>
        <personne sexe="M">
            <nom>dupont</nom>
            <prenom>jean</prenom>
            <age>28</age>
            ceci est un commentaire
        </personne>
        <section>27</section>
    </enseignant>
    <etudiant>
        <personne sexe="F">
            <nom>martin</nom>
            <prenom>charline</prenom>
            <age>22</age>
        </personne>
        <formation>dess IAIE</formation>
    </etudiant>
</tribu>

An XML document is a tree of elements:

  • line 1: the prolog, which gives the XML version and the character encoding of the document;
  • lines 3-21: the root element [tribu]. An XML document has one and only one root;
  • lines 4-12: the [enseignant] element, a child of [tribu]. It has two children, [personne] and [section];
  • line 5: the [personne] element has a [sexe] attribute with the value [M];
  • line 9: an element can contain both elements and text (here "ceci est un commentaire", "this is a comment");
  • lines 13-20: the [etudiant] element, with the same structure as [enseignant].

docs.title: 21.2. Working with SimpleXML
docs.text:
We analyze this document with the following script [simplexml-01.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// le fichier XML à exploiter
const FILE_NAME = "data.xml";

// chargement du document XML
$xml = simplexml_load_file(FILE_NAME);
if ($xml === false) {
    print "Le fichier [" . FILE_NAME . "] n'a pu être exploité\n";
    exit(1);
}
// affichage du document
print_r($xml);
// l'attribut [sexe] de la personne enseignante
print_r($xml->enseignant->personne['sexe']);
// valeurs d'éléments et d'attributs, converties en chaînes
$nom = (string) $xml->enseignant->personne->nom;
print "nom=$nom\n";
$sexe = (string) $xml->enseignant->personne['sexe'];
print "sexe=$sexe\n";
$formation = (string) $xml->etudiant->formation;
print "formation=$formation\n";
// existence d'un élément
print "isset(nom)=" . var_export(isset($xml->enseignant->personne->nom), true) . "\n";
print "isset(xx)=" . var_export(isset($xml->enseignant->personne->xx), true) . "\n";
// une conversion en entier
$age = (int) $xml->etudiant->personne->age;
print "âge de l'étudiante=$age\n";
// parcours de tous les éléments <personne> du document avec XPath
foreach ($xml->xpath('//personne') as $personne) {
    print "personne : {$personne->prenom} {$personne->nom} ({$personne['sexe']})\n";
}

Comments

  • line 6: the name of the XML file is a constant. The script is run in its own folder, the one containing [data.xml];
  • line 9: the [simplexml_load_file] function loads the document and returns an object of type [SimpleXMLElement] representing the root element [tribu]. On error (missing file, malformed XML), it returns [false], which we test line 10;
  • line 15: display of the document. [print_r] shows how [SimpleXML] sees the XML tree;
  • line 17: child elements are reached like properties ([$xml->enseignant->personne]), attributes like array keys ([['sexe']]). Note that the root [tribu] does not appear in the code: [$xml] is already that element;
  • line 19: [$xml->enseignant->personne->nom] is not a string but a [SimpleXMLElement] object. The [(string)] cast gives its text. With [declare(strict_types=1)], it is better to perform this conversion explicitly before passing the value to a function that expects a string;
  • line 21: the value of the [sexe] attribute;
  • lines 26-27: [isset] tells whether an element exists. The PHP 7 script displayed the boolean result with [print], which gives [1] for [true] and an empty string for [false]. We use [var_export], which displays [true] or [false];
  • line 29: the [(int)] cast gives the integer value of the element's text;
  • line 32: the [xpath] method evaluates an XPath expression. The expression [//personne] designates all the [personne] elements of the document, at whatever level they are. We get an array of [SimpleXMLElement].

Console results

> php simplexml-01.php
SimpleXMLElement Object
(
    [enseignant] => SimpleXMLElement Object
        (
            [personne] => SimpleXMLElement Object
                (
                    [@attributes] => Array
                        (
                            [sexe] => M
                        )

                    [nom] => dupont
                    [prenom] => jean
                    [age] => 28
                )

            [section] => 27
        )

    [etudiant] => SimpleXMLElement Object
        (
            [personne] => SimpleXMLElement Object
                (
                    [@attributes] => Array
                        (
                            [sexe] => F
                        )

                    [nom] => martin
                    [prenom] => charline
                    [age] => 22
                )

            [formation] => dess IAIE
        )

)
SimpleXMLElement Object
(
    [0] => M
)
nom=dupont
sexe=M
formation=dess IAIE
isset(nom)=true
isset(xx)=false
âge de l'étudiante=22
personne : jean dupont (M)
personne : charline martin (F)
  • lines 2-38: the XML document in the form of an object of type [SimpleXMLElement]. Note that the text [ceci est un commentaire] does not appear: [print_r] shows only elements and attributes;
  • lines 39-42: an attribute is also a [SimpleXMLElement] object;
  • lines 43-48: the values read from the document;
  • lines 49-50: the XPath traversal of the two people.

docs.title: 21.3. Working with PHP 8.4's new DOM API
docs.text:
Since PHP 8.4, the [Dom] namespace offers a new DOM API: the [Dom\XMLDocument] class for XML documents and [Dom\HTMLDocument] for HTML5 documents. It is a welcome replacement for the old [DOMDocument] class (still available): it complies with the current DOM standard and offers the [querySelector] and [querySelectorAll] methods familiar to JavaScript developers. These let you search for elements with CSS selectors.

The [dom-01.php] script works with the same document:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// le même document exploité avec la nouvelle API DOM de PHP 8.4

use Dom\XMLDocument;

// le fichier XML à exploiter
const FILE_NAME = "data.xml";

try {
    // chargement du document XML
    $document = XMLDocument::createFromFile(FILE_NAME);
} catch (Throwable $ex) {
    print "Le fichier [" . FILE_NAME . "] n'a pu être exploité : {$ex->getMessage()}\n";
    exit(1);
}
// l'élément racine
print "racine=" . $document->documentElement->tagName . "\n";
// la 1re personne enseignante, trouvée avec un sélecteur CSS
$personne = $document->querySelector('enseignant > personne');
print "nom=" . $personne->querySelector('nom')->textContent . "\n";
print "sexe=" . $personne->getAttribute('sexe') . "\n";
print "formation=" . $document->querySelector('etudiant > formation')->textContent . "\n";
// un élément absent : querySelector rend null
print "xx existe=" . var_export($personne->querySelector('xx') !== null, true) . "\n";
// toutes les personnes du document
foreach ($document->querySelectorAll('personne') as $personne) {
    // l'opérateur nullsafe ?-> protège d'un élément absent
    $prénom = $personne->querySelector('prenom')?->textContent ?? '?';
    $nom = $personne->querySelector('nom')?->textContent ?? '?';
    print "personne : $prénom $nom ({$personne->getAttribute('sexe')})\n";
}
// modification du document : on change le contenu de l'élément <section> de l'enseignant
$section = $document->querySelector('enseignant > section');
$section->textContent = "26";
// le document modifié, sous forme de texte XML
print $document->saveXml($document->querySelector('enseignant')) . "\n";

Comments

  • line 7: the [XMLDocument] class of the [Dom] namespace;
  • line 14: the static method [createFromFile] loads the document. Unlike [simplexml_load_file], it throws an exception on error;
  • line 20: the [documentElement] property is the root element; [tagName] is its name;
  • line 22: the CSS selector [enseignant > personne] designates a [personne] element that is a direct child of an [enseignant] element. [querySelector] returns the first matching element, or [null] if there is none;
  • line 23: the [textContent] property is the text contained in the element;
  • line 24: the value of an attribute;
  • line 27: a missing element gives [null];
  • line 29: all the [personne] elements of the document;
  • line 31: if the [prenom] element were missing, [querySelector('prenom')] would return [null]. The nullsafe operator [?->] (PHP 8.0) then returns [null] instead of causing an error, and the [??] operator replaces this [null] with ['?'];
  • line 37: the DOM API also lets you modify the document: here, we change the text of the [section] element;
  • line 39: [saveXml] returns the XML text of the document, or of one of its elements if it is passed as a parameter.

Console results

> php dom-01.php
racine=tribu
nom=dupont
sexe=M
formation=dess IAIE
xx existe=false
personne : jean dupont (M)
personne : charline martin (F)
<enseignant>
        <personne sexe="M">
            <nom>dupont</nom>
            <prenom>jean</prenom>
            <age>28</age>
            ceci est un commentaire
        </personne>
        <section>26</section>
    </enseignant>
  • line 16: the modification made by the script.

These two examples do not show all the possibilities of [SimpleXML] and [DOM], but they are enough for us to write a new version of the practical exercise. The PHP documentation describes them in detail: SimpleXML and DOM.

docs.title: 9. Traits
docs.text:
Traits are structures similar to classes. They cannot, however, be instantiated: they are meant to be included in classes. Including a trait in a class has the same effect as if the trait's code had been copied into the class. Code likely to be reused in several classes is placed in a trait.

Traits have existed since PHP 5.4. PHP 8 brought them a few additions that we will present at the end of the chapter: checking of the signature of abstract methods (PHP 8.0), trait constants (PHP 8.2), the [#[\Override]] attribute usable in a trait (PHP 8.3).

docs.title: 9.1. The script tree
docs.text:
The scripts of this chapter are in the [scripts-console/traits] folder:

php8-oct-2026/scripts-console/traits
├── trait-01.php
├── trait-02.php
├── ...
├── trait-09.php
└── trait-10.php

docs.title: 9.2. Including a trait in a class
docs.text:
The [trait-01.php] script shows a basic use of a trait in a class:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

class Class04
{
    // constructeur avec promotion de l'attribut [name]
    public function __construct(private string $name)
    {
    }

    // getter et setter
    public function getName(): string
    {
        return $this->name;
    }

    public function setName(string $name): void
    {
        $this->name = $name;
    }
}

trait Trait04
{
    // attribut
    private string $name;

    // getter et setter
    public function getName(): string
    {
        return $this->name;
    }

    public function setName(string $name): void
    {
        $this->name = $name;
    }
}

class Class05
{
    // inclusion du trait
    use Trait04;

    // constructeur
    public function __construct(string $name)
    {
        $this->name = $name;
    }
}

// test --------------
$class04 = new Class04("Tim");
$class05 = new Class05("Burton");
print $class04->getName() . "\n";
print $class05->getName() . "\n";
// affichage des deux objets
print_r($class04);
print_r($class05);

Comments on the code

  • lines 5-22: definition of the [Class04] class with a [$name] property (promoted by the constructor), its getter and its setter;
  • lines 24-39: we take the code of [Class04] without its constructor and transfer it into the [Trait04] trait. This time the property is declared explicitly, with its type. We do not take the constructor since a trait cannot be instantiated;
  • line 24: it is the [trait] keyword that makes [Trait04] a trait rather than a class;
  • lines 41-51: we define a [Class05] class that includes the code of the [Trait04] trait and adds a constructor to it, to make the class instantiable;
  • line 44: it is the [use] keyword, placed inside the class, that allows a trait to be included in a class. It must not be confused with the [use] statement placed outside any class, which imports a name from a namespace;
  • lines 54-60: tests show that the [Class04] and [Class05] classes work in the same way.

Results

> php trait-01.php
Tim
Burton
Class04 Object
(
    [name:Class04:private] => Tim
)
Class05 Object
(
    [name:Class05:private] => Burton
)

The results in lines 4-11 show that the [Class04] and [Class05] objects have the same content: the trait's private property [$name] has become a private property of the [Class05] class.

Conclusion: using the [use Trait] statement in a class is equivalent to including the code of [Trait] in the class.

docs.title: 9.3. Using the same trait in different classes
docs.text:
A first benefit of the trait seems to be the reuse of the same code (properties + methods) in different classes. We will see, however, that the same goal can be achieved using plain classes.

Sharing a trait between classes is illustrated by the following [trait-02.php] script:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

trait Trait01
{
    // attribut
    private int $id = 0;

    // méthode
    public function doSomething(): void
    {
        print "Trait01::doSomething... ($this->id)\n";
    }
}

class Class02
{
    // inclusion de Trait01
    use Trait01 {
        // la méthode [Trait01::doSomething] est accessible
        // dans la classe sous le nom [doSomethingInTrait]
        Trait01::doSomething as doSomethingInTrait;
    }

    // méthode propre à la classe
    public function doSomething(): void
    {
        // attribut id
        $this->id += 10;
        // utilisation de la méthode de Trait01
        $this->doSomethingInTrait();
        // affichage local
        print "Class02->doSomething\n";
    }
}

class Class03
{
    // inclusion de Trait01
    use Trait01;

    // méthode locale à la classe
    public function doSomethingElse(): void
    {
        // attribut id
        $this->id += 10;
        // utilisation de la méthode de Trait01
        $this->doSomething();
        // affichage local
        print "Class03->doSomethingElse\n";
    }
}

// test01 ----------------
function test01(): void
{
    $class02 = new Class02();
    $class03 = new Class03();
    $class02->doSomething();
    $class03->doSomethingElse();
}

// test01
print "test01-----------------\n";
test01();

Comments

  • lines 5-15: a trait defining a property [$id] and a method [doSomething];
  • the [Trait01] trait is included in two classes, [Class02] (lines 17-36) and [Class03] (lines 38-53);
  • lines 20-24: inclusion of [Trait01] in [Class02]. The inclusion is followed by a [{...}] block that allows the included methods to be adjusted;
  • line 23: this line resolves a conflict: [Trait01] and [Class02] both have a method called [doSomething]. In this case, it is the class's method that wins: the trait's method is hidden. The [as] operator makes the [Trait01::doSomething] method accessible in the class under the name [doSomethingInTrait]. Thus, inside [Class02], we will use the notations:
    • [doSomethingInTrait] to call the [Trait01::doSomething] method;
    • [doSomething] to call the [Class02::doSomething] method;
  • lines 30-32: the [Class02] class uses the property and the method of [Trait01] as if they were its own;
  • lines 38-53: the [Class03] class is similar to the [Class02] class. The inclusion of [Trait01] is simpler here because there is no collision between the methods of [Trait01] and those of [Class03].

Results

> php trait-02.php
test01-----------------
Trait01::doSomething... (10)
Class02->doSomething
Trait01::doSomething... (10)
Class03->doSomethingElse

Note carefully that the [Trait01] trait is not shared between the [Class02] and [Class03] classes. Through the inclusion of [Trait01] in the [Class02] and [Class03] classes, the [$id] property of [Trait01] becomes two different properties, [Class02::$id] and [Class03::$id]. This is what lines 3 and 5 of the results show. If the [$id] property had been shared between the [Class02] and [Class03] classes, we would have had 20 on line 5 instead of 10.

The [trait-03.php] script shows that the same result can be achieved by using a class instead of the trait:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// classe qui remplace le trait
class Class01
{
    // attribut
    private int $id = 0;

    // setter
    public function setId(int $id): void
    {
        $this->id = $id;
    }

    // getter
    public function getId(): int
    {
        return $this->id;
    }

    // méthode
    public function doSomething(): void
    {
        print "Class01::doSomething... ($this->id)\n";
    }
}

class Class02
{
    // une référence sur une instance de Class01, injectée par le constructeur
    public function __construct(private readonly Class01 $class01)
    {
    }

    // méthode propre à la classe
    public function doSomething(): void
    {
        // modification de l'attribut de Class01
        $id = $this->class01->getId();
        $id += 10;
        $this->class01->setId($id);
        // utilisation de la méthode de Class01
        $this->class01->doSomething();
        // affichage local
        print "Class02->doSomething\n";
    }
}

class Class03
{
    // une référence sur une instance de Class01, injectée par le constructeur
    public function __construct(private readonly Class01 $class01)
    {
    }

    // méthode locale à la classe
    public function doSomethingElse(): void
    {
        // modification de l'attribut de Class01
        $id = $this->class01->getId();
        $id += 10;
        $this->class01->setId($id);
        // utilisation de la méthode de Class01
        $this->class01->doSomething();
        // affichage local
        print "Class03->doSomethingElse\n";
    }
}

// test01 ----------------
function test01(): void
{
    // deux objets qui vont accéder à deux instances différentes de [Class01]
    $class02 = new Class02(new Class01());
    $class03 = new Class03(new Class01());
    // vérification
    $class02->doSomething();
    $class03->doSomethingElse();
}

// test02 ----------------
function test02(): void
{
    // instance partagée de [Class01]
    $class01 = new Class01();
    // deux objets qui vont accéder à la même instance de [Class01]
    $class02 = new Class02($class01);
    $class03 = new Class03($class01);
    // vérification
    $class02->doSomething();
    $class03->doSomethingElse();
}

// test01
print "test01-----------------\n";
test01();
// test02
print "test02-----------------\n";
test02();

Comments

  • lines 6-28: the [Class01] class replaces the [Trait01] trait. The code of [Trait01] was incorporated into the code of the [Class02] and [Class03] classes. Here, this will not be the case: it is a reference to a [Class01] object that will be injected into the [Class02] and [Class03] classes. The properties of the [Class01] class will therefore be external to the [Class02] and [Class03] objects. Since the [$id] property is private, a getter and a setter must be provided. This is the 1st difference from the trait: code must be written to access the class's private properties. We could have made the [$id] property public, but this is not advisable: going through a setter to set the value of a property makes it possible to check its validity;
  • line 33: the reference to the [Class01] object is injected into [Class02] through its constructor, thanks to parameter promotion. The PHP 7 course used a [setClass01] setter. Constructor injection is preferable: the [Class02] object is complete as soon as it is constructed and, since the property is [readonly], the reference can no longer be changed;
  • lines 41-45: for any use of the code of [Class01], we must go through the [$this->class01] property;
  • lines 51-70: the [Class03] class is a clone of the [Class02] class except that its method has a different name;
  • lines 73-81: the 1st test. It consists of injecting two different instances of the [Class01] class into the [Class02] and [Class03] objects;
  • lines 84-94: the 2nd test injects the same instance of the [Class01] class into the [Class02] and [Class03] objects.

Results

> php trait-03.php
test01-----------------
Class01::doSomething... (10)
Class02->doSomething
Class01::doSomething... (10)
Class03->doSomethingElse
test02-----------------
Class01::doSomething... (10)
Class02->doSomething
Class01::doSomething... (20)
Class03->doSomethingElse

Comments on the results

  • lines 3-6: we get the same results as with the [Trait01] trait. We conclude that using the trait is not essential here, but that it reduces the code because no methods are needed to access the trait's properties: these are an integral part of the class into which the trait has been incorporated;
  • lines 8-11: because we injected the same [Class01] reference into the [Class02] and [Class03] objects, the [Class01::$id] property has been shared between the two objects. This is why line 10 of the results displays 20 instead of 10 with the trait. We conclude that if properties must be shared between objects, the trait cannot be used and a class must then be used.

docs.title: 9.4. Grouping methods in a trait
docs.text:
In the previous example, the trait had properties and methods. We consider here the case where it contains only methods. The trait then looks like a factoring-out of methods that can be used in different classes. Since the trait here has no property, we will consider the case where the methods it groups together work only on parameters passed to them. This is not mandatory: a trait can work on a property [$this->attribut1] without having this property. It is then up to the classes that use this trait to provide the property [$this->attribut1].

In the case where the trait has only methods that work solely on parameters passed to them, we will show that the trait can be replaced by a class having the same methods as the trait, declared static.

The use of the trait is illustrated by the [trait-04.php] script, which takes the trait of the previous example and removes all its properties:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

trait Trait01
{
    // méthode à partager
    public function doSomething(): void
    {
        print "Trait01::doSomething...\n";
    }
}

class Class02
{
    // inclusion de Trait01
    use Trait01 {
        // la méthode [Trait01::doSomething] est accessible
        // dans la classe sous le nom [doSomethingInTrait]
        Trait01::doSomething as doSomethingInTrait;
    }

    public function doSomething(): void
    {
        // appel de la méthode de Trait01
        $this->doSomethingInTrait();
